Are all of the nodes in the cluster listed? Are they members of the cluster? Is the communications between nodes okay? If the answer to any of these questions is false, contact Digital's customer support organization.

message: unable to set initial sequence number value
cause: A call to the SSN failed to set the sequence number to its initial value, possibly caused by an MC hardware problem.
solution: Verify that the MC hardware is functioning properly. If it is not, contact Digital's customer support organization. If it is, contact Oracle support.

message: increment or adjust of sequence number failed
cause: A call to the SSN failed to increment the sequence number.
solution: Verify that the MC hardware is functioning properly. If it is not, contact Digital's customer support organization. If it is, contact Oracle support.

message: initial service identifier is non-zero
cause: A valid service identifier existed before the sequence number service was opened.
solution: Verify that the instance is completely shut down.

message: unable to obtain the current sequence number
cause: A call to the SSN failed to return its current value. Either there are many errors occurring on the MC hardware, or the sequence number has become invalid and cannot be validated.
solution: Verify that the MC hardware is functioning properly. If it is, contact Oracle Support.

message: unable to get/convert SCN recovery lock
cause: A process has timed out trying to get or convert the SCN recovery lock. Another process probably has the lock in EX or SHR mode, but is not releasing it.
solution: Contact Oracle Support.

message: unsupported optimization of Oracle binary, check alert log for more info
cause: ORACLE binary has been optimized with unsupported options or a required option has not been used.
solution: Check the documentation for a list of supported and required flags for the optimizing utility that you used to optimize ORACLE. Shutdown the instance, optimize ORACLE again with supported combination of options and restart the instance.

message: required operating system patch needs to be applied
cause: The operating system could not return the start time of a process.
solution: Check that the operating system kernel has been patched to return process start time. Apply the required operating system patch and restart the instance.

message: NETASY: port open failure
cause: Autologin unable to open port
solution: Check log file for OS-specific error code

message: NETASY: port set-up failure
cause: Autologin unable to change port attributes
solution: Check log file for OS-specific error code

message: NETASY: port read failure
cause: Autologin unable to read from port
solution: Check log file for OS-specific error code

message: NETASY: port write failure
cause: Autologin unable to write to port
solution: Check log file for OS-specific error code

message: NETASY: dialogue file open failure
cause: Autologin unable to open dialogue file
solution: Check connect string for accuracy/typos

message: NETASY: dialogue file read failure
cause: Autologin unable to read dialogue file
solution: Check log file for OS-specific error code

message: NETASY: dialogue execute failure
cause: Expected response never received
solution: None

message: NETASY: bad dialogue format
cause: Dialogue file contains syntax error
solution: Correct the dialogue file

message: NETASY: dialogue filename too long
cause: Full file spec for dialogue file exceeds 64 bytes
solution: Amend connect string accordingly

message: NETASY: dialogue file too long
cause: Dialogue file exceeds 768 bytes in length
solution: Simplify dialogue (e.g. remove comments, redundant white space), or split into two and link with "more" command

message: NETASY: dialogue too long
cause: One of two: 1. Dialogue contains more than 24 exchange blocks 2. Dialogue send string exceeds 84 bytes in length
solution: Simplify dialogue or split into two and link with "more" command

message: NETASY: message receive failure
cause: Async driver gets I/O error while doing network read operation
solution: Check log file for OS-specific error code and contact your customer support representative.

message: NETASY: message send failure
cause: Async driver gets I/O error while doing network write operation
solution: Check log file for OS-specific error code and contact your customer support representative.

message: NETASY: invalid login (connect) string
cause: Syntax error in login string.
solution: Resubmit with correct string.

message: NETASY: initialisation failure
cause: Async driver unable to complete initialisation
solution: Check log file for OS-specific error code

message: NETASY: connect failed
cause: Async driver unable to establish connection with partner
solution: Check log file for OS-specific error code

message: NETASY: channel open failure
cause: no free channel [should never happen]
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: NETASY: port open failure
cause: Async driver unable to open port
solution: Check log file for OS-specific error code

message: NETASY: VTM error
cause: Virtual Terminal Manager unable to read/write to port
solution: Check log file for OS-specific error code

message: NETASY: Configuration error
cause: Async driver genned for server-only, but client service requested
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: NETASY: port close failure
cause: Async driver unable to close port
solution: Check log file for OS-specific error code

message: NETASY: channel close failure
cause: Async driver unable to close channel
solution: Check log file for OS-specific error code

message: NETASY: unable to intialise for logging
cause: Async driver unable to initialise for logging I/O
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: NETASY: port assignment failure
cause: Async driver unable to assign port to channel [should never happen]
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: NETDNT: connect failed, unrecognized node name
cause: Node name specified in host string is unknown (probably misspelled)
solution: Retry with correct node name

message: NETDNT: connect failed, unrecognized object name
cause: Host string contains reference to object (which doesn't exist): @d:<node>-<obj> => object is ORDN<obj>; when <node> is VMS, the object is ORDN<obj>.COM when <node> is UNIX, the object is ORDN<obj> @d:<node>::"task=<obj>" => object is <obj>; when <node> is VMS, the object is <obj>.COM when <node> is UNIX, the object is <obj>
solution: Retry with correct object name or create the required object on host node

message: NETDNT: connect failed, access control data rejected
cause: Host string contains invalid username/password
solution: Retry with correct username/password

message: NETDNT: connect failed, partner rejected connection
cause: Connection with partner was made but was rejected.
solution: Contact your network administrator.

message: NETDNT: connect failed, partner exited unexpectedly
cause: Connection with host node was made but partner aborted
solution: Make sure object (see 06031, above) is working (for VMS run the command file and make sure that the ORACLE server process starts up); sometimes happens when the network/node is under stress - in this case a retry often works.

message: NETDNT: connect failed, insufficient resources
cause: Insufficient system resources are available to complete the connection; for example, all DECnet channels are in use.
solution: Contact your network administrator.

message: NETDNT: connect failed, node unreachable
cause: Host node is down.
solution: Contact your network administrator.

message: NETDNT: connect failed
cause: Connect failed for unexpected reason (see OSD error).
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: NETDNT: invalid login (connect) string
cause: Syntax error in login string.
solution: Resubmit with correct string.

message: NETDNT: disconnect failed
cause: Driver gets error while doing network close operation
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: NETDNT: message receive failure
cause: Driver gets I/O error while doing network read operation
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: NETDNT: message send failure
cause: Driver gets I/O error while doing network write operation
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: NETDNT: connect failed, byte count quota exceeded
cause: Connect failed because of insufficient byte count quota.
solution: Increase byte count quota.

message: NETTCP: cannot allocate context area
cause: Insufficient dynamic memory available for connection context area.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: NETTCP: remote host is unknown
cause: Host name specified in the login (connect) string is unknown.
solution: Check spelling; make sure name is in the TCP/IP HOST file.

message: NETTCP: socket creation failure
cause: Process open file quota probably exceeded.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: NETTCP: ORACLE network server not found
cause: No entry in SERVICES file for ORACLE server.
solution: Add ("orasrv") entry to the TCP/IP SERVICES file.

message: NETTCP: connect to host failed
cause: Connection attempt to remote host has failed. Probably means that the SQL*Net TCP/IP server on the remote host is not up, or the host itself is not up (check the latter by targeting it with Telnet).
solution: Start the SQL*Net TCP/IP server process on the remote host.

message: NETTCP: message receive failure
cause: I/O error occurred while attempting network read operation.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: NETTCP: message send failure
cause: I/O error occurred while attempting network write operation.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: NETTCP: disconnect failure
cause: Error occurred while closing a socket.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: NETTCP: invalid buffer size
cause: The buffer size specified in the login string exceeds the allowed maximum (of 4096).
solution: Re-submit with valid buffer size.

message: NETTCP: Too many connections
cause: The maximum no. of concurrently open connections has been reached.
solution: Exit an application with an open connection which is no longer required.

message: NETTCP: SID lookup failure
cause: From the remote host's SQL*Net TCP/IP server: the database SID, specified in the login (connect) string, was not recognized.
solution: Add the appropriate SID entry to the CONFIG.ORA file on the remote host (and restart the SQL*Net TCP/IP server).

message: NETTCP: unable to create ORACLE logicals
cause: The host's SQL*Net TCP/IP server was unable to create the necessary logicals required by the ORACLE server process. See the SQL*Net TCP/IP server log file for more details.
solution: Contact your system administrator.

message: NETTCP: unable to create ORASRV process
cause: The host's SQL*Net TCP/IP server was unable to create the ORACLE server process. See the SQL*Net TCP/IP server log file for more details.
solution: Contact your system administrator.

message: NETTCP: unable to create ORASRV: quota exceeded
cause: The host's SQL*Net TCP/IP server was unable to create the ORACLE server process because of quota depletion.
solution: Increase quota allocations to the SQL*Net TCP/IP server process.

message: NETTCP: unable to complete handshake with ORASRV
cause: The ORACLE server process was started but failed to complete its initialization.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: NETTCP: spurious client request
cause: The host's SQL*Net TCP/IP server was unable to recognize this connection request. See the SQL*Net TCP/IP server log file for more details.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: NETTCP: network driver not loaded
cause: The TCP/IP network driver is not loaded.
solution: Check that the TCP/IP driver is loaded correctly.

message: NETTCP: access failure
cause: The host's SQL*Net TCP/IP server was unable to test the accessibility of the SID mapping file (specified in CONFIG.ORA) associated with this connection request. See the SQL*Net TCP/IP server log file for more details.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: NETTCP: setup failure
cause: The host's SQL*Net TCP/IP server was unable to set up the appropriate environment to service this connection request. See the SQL*Net TCP/IP server log file for more details.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: NETTCP: cannot set KEEPALIVE
cause: The host's SQL*Net TCP/IP server was unable to set the socket KEEPLIVE option. See the SQL*Net TCP/IP server log file for more details.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: NETTCP: timeout waiting for ORASRV
cause: The ORACLE server process was started but failed to respond after N secs.
solution: For heavily loaded systems this is not an uncommon occurrence. Increase the value of N (the default is 30) by placing the following entry in the CONFIG.ORA file: SQLNET ORASRV_WAIT = <no. of secs> which will come into effect the next time the SQL*Net TCP/IP server is started.

message: NETTCP: ORASRV exited unexpectedly
cause: The ORACLE server process was started but exited unexpectedly. Possible causes: 1. Insufficient quotas to run ORASRV 2. ORACLE is not installed See the ORASRV output file for more details; the file will be in the ORA_SQLNET directory and will have a name of the form: ORA_SRVTnn_<SID>.OUT
solution: If appropriate action is not obvious from the ORASRV output file then contact your customer support representative.

message: NETTCP: ORASRV unable to open network connection
cause: The ORACLE server process was started but was unable to open the socket passed to it by TCPSRV.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: NETTCP: unable to change username
cause: The host's SQL*Net TCP/IP server could not establish a PROXY LOGIN connection because the client username is unknown (to the host OS).
solution: Create new user account on host.

message: NETTCP: unable to create mailbox
cause: The host's SQL*Net TCP/IP server was unable to create a mailbox (needed for IPC communication with the ORACLE server process). See the SQL*Net TCP/IP server log file for more details.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: NETTCP: unable to transfer socket ownership to ORASRV
cause: The host's SQL*Net TCP/IP server was unable to transfer the network communication handle to the ORACLE server process. See the SQL*Net TCP/IP server log file for more details.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: NETTCP: host access denied
cause: The host's SQL*Net TCP/IP server rejected this connection request because the client node does not have access privilege - as determined by the contents of the Valid Node Table (VNT), a component of the host's CONFIG.ORA.
solution: To grant access, add appropriate entry to the host's VNT.

message: NETTCP: user access denied
cause: The host's SQL*Net TCP/IP server rejected this connection request because the client user(name) does not have access privilege - as determined by the contents of the Username Mapping Table (UMT), a component of the host's CONFIG.ORA.
solution: To grant access, add appropriate entry to the host's UMT.

message: NETTCP: access denied, wrong password
cause: The host SQL*Net TCP/IP server rejected this connection request because the client password did not match the host password.
solution: To grant access, get passwords in sync.

message: NETTCP: file not found
cause: The host's SQL*Net TCP/IP server could not find the SID mapping file (specified in CONFIG.ORA) associated with this connection request.
solution: Check CONFIG.ORA for spelling; make correct entry.

message: NETTCP: file access privilege violation
cause: The host's SQL*Net TCP/IP server did not have READ/ EXECUTE permission for the SID mapping file (specified in CONFIG.ORA) associated with this connection request.
solution: Change protection on SID mapping file.

message: NETTCP: connection rejected; server is stopping
cause: The host's SQL*Net TCP/IP server rejected this connection request because it is in the process of stopping.
solution: Re-start SQL*Net TCP/IP server.

message: NETTCP: error during connection handshake
cause: Network I/O failure occurred while communicating with the host's SQL*Net TCP/IP server. See the SQL*Net TCP/IP server log file for more details.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: NETTCP: error during connection handshake
cause: Network I/O failure occurred while communicating with the host's SQL*Net TCP/IP server. See the SQL*Net TCP/IP server log file for more details.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: NETTCP: error during connection handshake
cause: Network I/O failure occurred while communicating with the host's SQL*Net TCP/IP server. See the SQL*Net TCP/IP server log file for more details.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: NETTCP: no such user
cause: A proxy login connect attempt failed because the client username has no counterpart on the host.
solution: None

message: NETTCP: no privilege for user
cause: A proxy login connect attempt failed because the SQL*Net TCP/IP server had insufficient privileges to access the proxy account.
solution: Change account protection; change server privilges.

message: NETTCP: error getting user information
cause: A proxy login connect attempt failed because the SQL*Net TCP/IP server was unable to access the proxy account. See the SQL*Net TCP/IP server log file for more details.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: NETTCP: maximum connections exceeded
cause: The connect failed because the maximum conncurrent connections supported by the host's SQL*Net TCP/IP server has already been reached.
solution: Wait for a short period and re-try.

message: NETTCP: SID (database) is unavailable
cause: The database administrator on the host has varied the SID offline.
solution: Wait for it to be varied back on-line.

message: NETTCP: unable to start ORASRV: images not installed
cause: The host's SQL*Net TCP/IP server was unable to start the ORACLE server process because the ORACLE protected images were not installed.
solution: Install the images.

message: NETNTT: cannot allocate send and receive buffers
cause: Two-task driver could not allocate data buffers.
solution: There is insufficient memory to run your program. Kill off other processes to free up memory.

message: NETNTT: cannot translate address file name
cause: ORACLE_HOME environment variable not set.
solution: Make sure that the ORACLE_HOME environment variable has been properly set and exported.

message: NETNTT: cannot open address file
cause: The NTT two-task driver could not open a file containing address information.
solution: Make sure that the ORACLE_HOME environment variable has been properly set and exported. Make sure the instance you are attempting to connect to is actually up and running.

message: NETNTT: cannot read arguments from address file
cause: The NTT two-task driver could not read addressing information from its addressing file.
solution: Make sure that the ORACLE_HOME environment variable has been properly set and exported. Make sure the instance you are attempting to connect to is actually up and running.

message: NETNTT: cannot share connection to cube
cause: The NTT two-task driver could not share a connection to the cube.
solution: Make sure that the ORACLE_HOME environment variable has been properly set and exported. Make sure the instance you are attempting to connect to is actually up and running.

message: NETNTT: cannot read pid of remote process
cause: An error occurred while reading the NTT communications link.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: NETNTT: remote fork failed
cause: The Oracle listener process on the cube could not fork off a shadow process.
solution: The instance you are trying to connect to probably doesn't have enough memory to run another shadow process. Ask someone else to log off, or connect to a different instance.

message: NETNTT: cannot send command line to shadow process
cause: An error occurred while writing the NTT communications link.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: NETNTT: cannot allocate context area
cause: Two-task driver could not allocate data buffers.
solution: There is insufficient memory to run your program. Kill off other processes to free up memory.

message: NETNTT: cannot read from remote process
cause: An error occurred while reading the NTT communications link.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: NETNTT: cannot write to remote process
cause: An error occurred while writing the NTT communications linke.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: NETNTT: nrange() failed
cause: The call to 'nrange()' failed while attempting to establish a connection.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: NETNTT: nfconn() failed
cause: The call to 'nfconn()' failed while attempting to establish a connection.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: NETNTT: out of memory in pi_connect
cause: Two-task driver could not allocate data buffers.
solution: There is insufficient memory to run your program. Kill off other processes to free up memory.

message: NETNTT: data protocol error
cause: The NTT two-task driver received an unexpected message type."
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: NETNTT: break protocol error
cause: The NTT two-task driver received an unexpected message type."
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: NETNTT: bad write length
cause: The NTT two-task driver failed on an internal consistency check.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: NETNTT: bad state
cause: The NTT two-task driver failed on an internal consistency check.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: NETNTT: cannot read /etc/oratab
cause: The NTT two-task driver could not read configuration information from /etc/oratab.
solution: Make sure /etc/oratab exists and is readable. This error may occur if the file is incorrectly formatted. It also may occur if the driver has run out of memory.

message: IPA: Disconnect failure
cause: A fatal error occurred during the disconnect from the server. This was probably caused by inaccessible message queues.
solution: If there is no message queue, restart the SQL*Net IPA servers using ipactl. Otherwise contact your customer support representative.

message: IPA: Cannot allocate driver context
cause: The memory pool is exhausted.
solution: Check the circumstances and try to allocate less memory in your program or adjust the init parameters in your INIT.ORA file and retry.

message: IPA: Cannot connect to remote host
cause: found.
solution: Check sequentially for the above causes and eliminate the actual

message: IPA: Message send error
cause: The SQL*Net IPA driver could not write the message into the message queue.
solution: Make sure that the message queue exists and is accessible. If necessary rerun ipactl.

message: IPA: Message receive error
cause: The SQL*Net IPA driver could not read a message from the message queue.
solution: Make sure that the message queue exists and is accessible. If necessary rerun ipactl.

message: IPA: Illegal message type
cause: The communication between user and ORACLE is out of synchronization. This message should not normally be issued.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: IPA: Message write length error
cause: The IPA driver tried to write a message in the queue that was too big for the queue.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: IPA: Cannot reset connection
cause: A fatal error occurred during the resetting of the connection.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: IPA: No more connections available
cause: You have exhausted all your connections.
solution: Try again when some of the current users have logged off.

message: IPA: No message queue available
cause: The SQL*Net IPA servers have not been started.
solution: Run ipactl.

message: IPA: Environment variable(s) not set
cause: Environment variable(s) not set correctly.
solution: Check and correct.

message: IPA: Maximum number of servers reached
cause: Maximum number of servers reached.
solution: Shutdown and restart with an increased maximum number of servers. Note that database links consume one server per link. Be sure to start up enough servers to support database links.

message: IPA: Incorrect outgoing service name supplied
cause: Incorrect outgoing service name supplied.
solution: Check and correct the service name.

message: IPA: Shared memory failed to initialise
cause: The shared memory has not been set up correctly.
solution: Contact your system manager.

message: IPA: Event set up failure
cause: Fatal interprocess communication error.
solution: Contact your system manager.

message: IPA: Invalid connect string
cause: The connect string is malformed.
solution: Check and correct.

message: IPA: Invalid database SID
cause: The SID is unknown at the remote side.
solution: Either the database does not exist, is not running, or there are no reserved servers for that SID.

message: IPA: Local maximum number of users exceeded
cause: The maximum number of simultaneous users of SQL*Net IPA has been exceeded on the local side.
solution: Wait for free connections to become available. If the problem persists, contact your system manager.

message: IPA: Local maximum number of connections exceeded
cause: The maximum number of simultaneous connections that SQL*Net IPA can handle to different hosts has been exceeded on the local side.
solution: Wait for free connections to become available. If the problem persists, contact your system manager.

message: IPA: Remote maximum number of users exceeded
cause: The maximum number of simultaneous users of SQL*Net IPA has been exceeded on the remote side.
solution: Wait for free connections to become available. If the problem persists, contact your system manager.

message: IPA: Remote maximum number of connections exceeded
cause: The maximum number of simultaneous connections that SQL*Net IPA can handle from different hosts has been exceeded on the remote side.
solution: Wait for free connections to become available. If the problem persists, contact your system manager.

message: IPA: Cannot reach the remote side
cause: There has been a timeout on an attempt to connect to a remote server the reason for which is most likely to be the remote SQL*Net IPA software is not running. An alternative reason could be that the remote initiator service name is incorrect.
solution: Check and start the remote SQL*Net software. Check that it is started with the correct service names supplied.

message: IPA: Fatal shared memory error
cause: An internal error has occurred in the shared memory handling.
solution: Contact customer support.

message: IPA: Cause event error
cause: Fatal interprocess communication error.
solution: Contact your system manager.

message: NETCMN: No default host string specified
cause: There was no default host string specified in the configuration and the user didn't specify any explicit connect string.
solution: Either reconfigure the system specifying a default connect string or use an explicit connect string.

message: NETCMN: invalid driver designator
cause: The login (connect) string contains an invalid driver designator.
solution: Correct the string and re-submit.

message: NETCMN: error receiving break message
cause: Error occurred while attempting to read a break message.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: Unable to allocate memory.
cause: System unable to allocate needed virtual memory.
solution: Configure more memory, reduce load, or simply try again.

message: NETCMN: invalid login (connect) string
cause: Syntax error in login string.
solution: Correct string and re-submit.

message: NETCMN: reset protocol error
cause: Unable to reset out of break state.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: NETCMN: error sending break message
cause: Error occurred while attempting to send a break message.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: NETCMN: unable to set up break handling environment
cause: Error occurred while attempting to set up asynchronous handlers for in-coming, out-of-band break messages.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: NETCMN: incorrect message format
cause: Message from partner contains bad header.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: Connection not open.
cause: Unable to establish connection.
solution: Use diagnostic procedures to ascertain exact problem.

message: NETCMN: error on test
cause: Error occurred while testing I/O status of the network connection.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: NETCMN: server can not start oracle
cause: The remote server was unable to start an ORACLE process on behalf of the client.
solution: Make sure permissions on the remote ORACLE program are correctly set. Contact your system administrator.

message: NETCMN: SID lookup failure
cause: From the remote host's server: the database SID, specified in the login (connect) string, was not recognized.
solution: Add the appropriate SID entry to the CONFIG.ORA or oratab file on the remote host (restarting the remote server may be needed).

message: NETCMN: Error detected in the read-in data
cause: Error found during recomputation of checksum or CRC.
solution: Possible hardware failures of communication nodes. Contact system administrator immediately.

message: NETCMN: Error in sending data
cause: Unable to transmit data to remote host.
solution: Try reconnect to remote host, and contact your system administrator.

message: NETCMN: Error in receiving data
cause: Unable to receive data from remote host.
solution: Try reconnect to remote host, and contact your system administrator.

message: ssaio: Seals do not match
cause: A function was called with an invalid argument.
solution: Contact your Oracle Customer Support Representative.

message: ssaio: Invalid Block number
cause: The file block number is out of range of the file. The additional information returns the block number.
solution: Verify that the block number is correct. Run dbfsize and check if the block number is in that range. Contact your Oracle Customer Support Representative.

message: ssaio: Buffer Not Aligned
cause: The I/O buffer was not aligned on a 2K boundary.
solution: Contact your Oracle Customer Support Representative.

message: ssaio: LSEEK error, unable to seek to requested block.
cause: The additional information returns the block number
solution: Look up the additional information returned in your operating system reference manual. Verify that the block number is correct.

message: ssaio: read error, unable to read requested block from database file.
cause: The read system call returned an error.
solution: The additional information indicates the block number. Look up the additional information returned in your operating system manual.

message: ssaio: write error, unable to write requested block to database file.
cause: The write system call returned an error.
solution: The additional information indicates the block number. Look up the additional information returned in your operating system manual.

message: ssaio: asynchronous I/O failed due to incorrect parameters.
cause: The Asynchronous I/O system call returned an error.
solution: The additional information indicates the block number. Look up the additional information returned in your operating system manual.

message: ssaio: the asynchronous write was unable to write to the database file.
cause: The Asynchronous I/O system call returned an error.
solution: The additional information indicates the block number. Look up the additional information returned in your operating system manual.

message: ssaio: the asynchronous read was unable to read from the database file.
cause: The Asynchronous I/O system call returned an error.
solution: The additional information indicates the block number. Look up the additional information returned in your operating system manual.

message: ssaio: the asynchronous write returned incorrect number of bytes
cause: This write call may have been truncated. The additional information returns the block number and number of bytes.
solution: Verify that the block number and the number of bytes written are correct.

message: ssaio: the asynchronous read returned incorrect number of bytes
cause: This read call may have been truncated. The additional information returns the block number and number of bytes.
solution: Verify that the block number and the number of bytes read are correct.

message: ssvwatev: Incorrect parameter passed to function call
cause: Either the ORACLE process id, or wait time or event ID is invalid.
solution: The additional information indicates the process id, time and event id.

message: ssvwatev: Failed with unexpected error number.
cause: Some system problems may exists on your system, please check error logs.
solution: The additional information indicates the error number. Look up the additional information returned in your operating system manual.

message: ssvpstev: Incorrect parameter passed to function call
cause: An invalid event ID is passed in to this routine.
solution: The additional information indicates the event id.

message: ssvpstev: Failed with unexpected error number.
cause: Some system problems may exist on your system, please check error logs.
solution: The additional information indicates the error number. Look up the additional information returned in your operating system manual.

message: ssvpstevrg: Incorrect parameters passed to function call
cause: An invalid event id, or the low and high event ID do not exist.
solution: The additional information indicates the error number. It also contains the event id, low boundary and high boundary.

message: ssvpstevrg: Failed with unexpected error number.
cause: Some system problems may exist on your system, please check error logs.
solution: The additional information indicates the error number. Look up the additional information returned in your operating system manual.

message: ssvpstp: Incorrect parameter passed to function call
cause: Invalid oracle process ID is passed in to this routine.
solution: The additional information indicates the process id.

message: ssvpstp: Failed with unexpected error number.
cause: Some system problems may exists on your system, please check error logs.
solution: The additional information indicates the error number. Look up the additional information returned in your operating system manual.

message: The list IO or the sysvendor is not installed.
cause: ORACLE tries to use the sysvendor interface (INIT.ORA parameter use_sysvendor=true) but the UNIX kernel does not have the ORACLE sysvendor interface linked in.
solution: Set use_sysvendor=false in INIT.ORA, if you don't want to use this interface or link the UNIX kernel with this interface so that ORACLE can use it.

message: PL/SQL: storage error
cause: PL/SQL was unable to allocate additional storage. This message normally appears with an ORA-4030 or ORA-4031 error which gives additional information. Sometimes this error can be caused by runaway programs.
solution: 1) Ensure there are no issues or bugs in your PL/SQL program which are causing excessive amounts of memory to be used. 2) Programmatically cause unused objects to be freed (e.g. by setting them to NULL). 3) Increase the amount of shared or process memory (as appropriate) available to you.

message: PL/SQL: program error
cause: This is an internal error message. An error has been detected in a PL/SQL program.
solution: Contact Oracle Support Services.

message: PL/SQL: Function returned without value
cause: A call to PL/SQL function completed, but no RETURN statement was executed.
solution: Rewrite PL/SQL function, making sure that it always returns a value of a proper type.

message: PL/SQL: Return types of Result Set variables or query do not match
cause: Number and/or types of columns in a query does not match declared return type of a result set variable, or declared types of two Result Set variables do not match.
solution: Change the program statement or declaration. Verify what query the variable actually refers to during execution.

message: PL/SQL: variable requires more than 32767 bytes of contiguous memory
cause: A PL/SQL variable was declared with a constraint which required more than 32767 bytes of memory. PL/SQL does not currently support allocations of contiguous memory greater than 32767 bytes.
solution: Consider reducing the constraint in the variable declaration. If that is not possible, try changing the database or national character set to such, that requires less memory for the same constraint. Note: changing the character set will impact execution of all PL/SQL code.

message: PL/SQL: unhandled user-defined exception
cause: A user-defined exception was raised by PL/SQL code, but not handled.
solution: Fix the problem causing the exception or write an exception handler for this condition. Or you may need to contact your application administrator or DBA.

message: PL/SQL: cursor already open
cause: An attempt was made to open a cursor that was already open.
solution: Close cursor first before reopening.

message: PL/SQL: index for PL/SQL table out of range for host language array
cause: An attempt is being made to copy a PL/SQL table to a host language array. But an index in the table is either less than one or greater than the maximum size of the host language array. When copying PL/SQL tables to host language arrays, the table entry at index 1 is placed in the first element of the array, the entry at index 2 is placed in the second element of the array, etc. If an table entry has not been assigned then the corresponding element in the host language array is set to null.
solution: Increase size of host language array, or decrease size of PL/SQL table. Also make sure that you don't use index values less than 1.

message: PL/SQL: The remote call cannot be handled by the server
cause: The remote call has parameters that are cursor variables or lob variables. This cannot be handled by stored procedures on your server.
solution: Avoid using cursor variables or lob variables as parameters for stored procedures on this server or upgrade your server to a version that supports this.

message: PL/SQL: unhandled exception string
cause: An exception was raised by PL/SQL code, but not handled. The exception number is outside the legal range of Oracle errors.
solution: Fix the problem causing the exception or write an exception handler for this condition. Or you may need to contact your application administrator or DBA.

message: PL/SQL: the Probe packages do not exist or are invalid
cause: A Probe operation, probably an attempt to initialize the ORACLE server to debug PL/SQL, could not be completed because the Probe packages were not loaded or have become invalid.
solution: DBA should load the Probe packages. This can be done by running the pbload.sql script supplied with the RDBMS.

message: PL/SQL: Probe error - string
cause: An error occurred while passing a Probe operation to the server for execution.
solution: Refer to the entry for the embedded error message.

message: PL/SQL: Probe version string incompatible with version string
cause: The current version of Probe is incompatible with the version on the ORACLE server.
solution: Refer to the documentation to ensure that this degree of compatibility is supported.

message: active autonomous transaction detected and rolled back
cause: Before returning from an autonomous PL/SQL block, all autonomous transactions started within the block must be completed (either committed or rolled back). If not, the active autonomous transaction is implicitly rolled back and this error is raised.
solution: Ensure that before returning from an autonomous PL/SQL block, any active autonomous transactions are explicitly committed or rolled back. ----------------------------------------------------------------------- 06520 through 06529 reserved for Foreign function errors

message: PL/SQL: Error loading external library
cause: An error was detected by PL/SQL trying to load the external library dynamically.
solution: Check the stacked error (if any) for more details.

message: PL/SQL: Error mapping function
cause: An error was detected by PL/SQL trying to map the mentioned function dynamically.
solution: Check the stacked error (if any) for more details.

message: string
cause: ORA-06520 or ORA-065211 could stack this error with a system specific error string.
solution: This error string should give the cause for errors ORA-06520 or ORA-065211

message: Maximum number of arguments exceeded
cause: There is an upper limit on the number of arguments that one can pass to the external function.
solution: Check the port specific documentation on how to calculate the upper limit.

message: Unsupported option : string
cause: The option specified is an unsupported feature for external procedures.
solution: Correct the syntax in the external specification

message: Length Mismatch for CHAR or RAW data
cause: The length specified in the length variable has an illegal value. This can happen if you have requested requested a PL/SQL INOUT, OUT or RETURN raw variable to be passed as a RAW with no corresponding length variable. This error can also happen if there is a mismatch in the length value set in the length variable and the length in the orlvstr or orlraw.
solution: Correct the external procedure code and set the length variable correctly.

message: Unable to load PL/SQL library
cause: PL/SQL was unable to instantiate the library referenced by this referenced in the EXTERNAL syntax. This is a serious error and should normally not happen.
solution: Report this problem to customer support.

message: External procedure SQLLIB error: string
cause: An error occurred in sqllib during execution of a Pro* external procedure.
solution: The message text indicates the actual SQLLIB error that occurred. Consult the Oracle Error Messages and Codes manual for a complete description of the error message and follow the appropriate action.

message: Error executing PL/SQL profiler
cause: An error occurred in during execution of a PL/SQL profiler procedure.
solution: Check the stacked errors for more details.

message: Version mismatch - PL/SQL profiler
cause: The PL/SQL profiler package (dbmspb.sql, prvtpbp.plb) does not match the version of the code in the server implementing the profiler.
solution: Run the package profload.sql in $ORACLE_HOME/rdbms/admin to load the correct version of the PL/SQL profiler packages

message: Reference to uninitialized composite
cause: An object, LOB, or other composite was referenced as a left hand side without having been initialized.
solution: Initialize the composite with an appropriate constructor or whole-object assignment.

message: Reference to uninitialized collection
cause: An element or member function of a nested table or varray was referenced (where an initialized collection is needed) without the collection having been initialized.
solution: Initialize the collection with an appropriate constructor or whole-object assignment.

message: Subscript outside of limit
cause: A subscript was greater than the limit of a varray or non-positive for a varray or nested table.
solution: Check the program logic and increase the varray limit if necessary.

message: Subscript beyond count
cause: An in-limit subscript was greater than the count of a varray or too large for a nested table.
solution: Check the program logic and explicitly extend if necessary.

message: Cannot access Serially Reusable package string
cause: The program attempted to access a Serially Reusable package in PL/SQL called from SQL context (trigger or otherwise). Such an access is currently unsupported.
solution: Check the program logic and remove any references to Serially Reusable packages (procedure, function or variable references) which might happen in PL/SQL called from sql context (trigger or otherwise).

message: statement string in string is NULL or 0 length
cause: The program attempted to use a dynamic statement string that was either NULL or 0 length.
solution: Check the program logic and ensure that the dynamic statement string is properly initialized.

message: IN bind variable bound to an OUT position
cause: The program attempted to bind an IN bind variable to a statement that was expecting an OUT bind variable at that position.
solution: Make sure that an OUT or IN OUT bind mode is specified for the bind argument.

message: OUT bind variable bound to an IN position
cause: The program attempted to bind an OUT bind variable to a statement that was expecting an IN bind variable at that position.
solution: Make sure that an IN or IN OUT bind mode is specified for the bind argument.

message: statement violates string RESTRICT_REFERENCES pragma
cause: The program attempted to execute a dynamic statement which does not meet the purity level specified (in the pragma RESTRICT_REFERENCES directive) for the module executing the statement.
solution: Ensure that the dynamic statement meets the purity level specified for the module executing the statement.

message: target of OPEN must be a query
cause: The program attempted to perform an OPEN cursor operation on a dynamic statement that was not a query.
solution: Ensure that the OPEN cursor operation is done on a dynamic query statement. -------------------------------------------------------- 06540 through 06549 reserved for pl/sql error handling

message: PL/SQL: compilation error
cause: A pl/sql compilation error occurred. However, the user generally will not see this error message. Instead, there will be accompanying PLS-nnnnn error messages.
solution: See accompanying PLS-nnnnn error messages.

message: PL/SQL: compilation error - compilation aborted
cause: A pl/sql compilation error occurred and the compilation was aborted; but the compilation unit was written out to the backing store. However, unlike ora-06545, the user generally will not see this error message. Instead, there will be accompanying PLS-nnnnn error messages.
solution: See accompanying PLS-nnnnn error messages.

message: PL/SQL: internal error, arguments: [ string ], [ string ], [ string ], [ string ], [ string ], [ string ], [ string ], [ string ]
cause: A pl/sql internal error occurred.
solution: Report as a bug; the first argument is the internal error nuber.

message: PL/SQL: compilation error - compilation aborted
cause: A pl/sql compilation error occurred and the compilation was aborted completely without the compilation unit being written out to the backing store. Unlike ora-06541, the user will always see this error along with the accompaning PLS-nnnnn error messages.
solution: See accompanying PLS-nnnnn error messages.

message: DDL statement is executed in an illegal context
cause: DDL statement is executed dynamically in illegal PL/SQL context. - Dynamic OPEN cursor for a DDL in PL/SQL - Bind variable's used in USING clause to EXECUTE IMMEDIATE a DDL - Define variable's used in INTO clause to EXECUTE IMMEDIATE a DDL
solution: Use EXECUTE IMMEDIATE without USING and INTO clauses to execute the DDL statement.

message: RETURNING clause must be used with INSERT, UPDATE, or DELETE statements
cause: EXECUTE IMMEDIATE with a RETURNING clause is used to execute dynamic UPDATE, INSERT, or DELETE statements only.
solution: use RETURNING clause in EXECUTE IMMEDIATE for INSERT, UPDATE, or DELETE statements only. For other statements, use USING clause instead.

message: no more rows needed
cause: The caller of a pipelined function did not need more rows to be produced by the pipelined function.
solution: Do not catch the NO_DATA_NEEDED exception in an exception handling block.

message: PL/SQL: failed to dynamically open shared object (DLL): string : string
cause: One possible cause might be there are too many DLLs open at the same time.

message: line string , column string : string
cause: Usually a PL/SQL compilation error.
solution: None

message: package DBMS_STANDARD must be created before using PL/SQL
cause: The DBMS specific extensions to PL/SQL's package "STANDARD" are in package "DBMS_STANDARD". This package must be created before using PL/SQL.
solution: Create package "DBMS_STANDARD". The source for this PL/SQL stored package is provided with the distribution.

message: this name is currently reserved for use by user SYS
cause: You tried to create a package named "STANDARD", "DBMS_STANDARD" or "DEBUG_IO". These are currently reserved for use by user SYS.
solution: Choose another name for your package.

message: the pipe is empty, cannot fulfill the unpack_message request
cause: There are no more items in the pipe.
solution: Check that the sender and receiver agree on the number and types of items placed on the pipe.

message: null values are not allowed for any parameters to pipe icd's
cause: Internal error from the dbms_pipe package.
solution: None

message: buffer in dbms_pipe package is full. No more items allowed
cause: The pipe buffer size has been exceeded.
solution: None

message: wrong datatype requested, string , actual datatype is string
cause: The sender put different datatype on the pipe than that being requested (package 'dbms_pipe'). The numbers are: 6 - number, 9 - char, 12 - date.
solution: Check that the sender and receiver agree on the number and types of items placed on the pipe.

message: pos, string , is negative or larger than the buffer size, string
cause: Internal error from the dbms_pipe package.
solution: None

message: given statement is not supported by package DBMS_SQL
cause: Attempting to parse an unsupported statement using procedure PARSE provided by package DBMS_SQL.
solution: Only statements which begin with SELECT, DELETE, INSERT, UPDATE, LOCK, BEGIN, DECLARE or << (PL/SQL label delimiter) are supported.

message: type of out argument must match type of column or bind variable
cause: Attempting to get the value of a column or a bind variable by calling procedure COLUMN_VALUE or VARIABLE_VALUE of package DBMS_SQL but the type of the given out argument where to place the value is different from the type of the column or bind variable that was previously defined by calling procedure DEFINE_COLUMN (for defining a column) or BIND_VARIABLE (for binding a bind variable) of package DBMS_SQL.
solution: Pass in an out argument of the correct type when calling procedure COLUMN_VALUE or VARIABLE_VALUE. The right type is the type that was provided when defining the column or binding the bind variable.

message: name has too many parts
cause: The name to be resolved was specified as one of the following: - With three parts (A.B.C) but the A.B parts resolved to an object that did not expose visible nested procedures; the C part could not be resolved. - With two parts (A.B) and the A part resolved to an object that did not expose visible nested procedures; the B part could not be resolved.
solution: Specify the valid name of an object or of a packaged procedure or function without specifying any additional trailing parts.

message: object string does not exist
cause: The named object could not be found. Either it does not exist or you do not have permission to access it.
solution: Create the object or get permission to access it.

message: cannot execute string from within stored procedure
cause: The named procedure cannot be executed from within a stored procedure, function or package. This function can only be used from pl/sql anonymous blocks.
solution: Remove the procedure from the calling stored procedure.

message: invalid number of rows specified
cause: An invalid number of rows was specified in a call to the procedure DEFINE_COLUMN in the package DBMS_SQL. For a given parsed statement in a given cursor, all columns must be defined to have the same number of rows, so all the calls to DEFINE_COLUMN must specify the same number of rows.
solution: Specify a number that matches that for previously defined columns.

message: invalid number of values specified
cause: An invalid number of values to be bound was specified in a call to the procedure BIND_VARIABLE in the package DBMS_SQL. In order to execute a given parsed statement in a given cursor, the same number of values must have been bound for all bind variables, so when EXECUTE is called, the latest calls to BIND_VARIABLE must must have specified the same number of values to be bound for all bind variables.
solution: Make sure that the same number of values have been bound for all of the bind variables.

message: obsolete ICD procedure called
cause: An obsolete ICD procedure was called by a PL/SQL program. The PL/SQL program was probably written for an eralier release of RDBMS.
solution: Make sure that all PL/SQL programs have been upgraded to the latest release of the RDBMS. This can be accomplished by following upgrade instructions in the README file, or by running the catproc.sql script supplied with the RDBMS.

message: Collection bound by bind_array contains no elements
cause: A collection with zero elements was bound to a bind variable in a call to procedure BIND_ARRAY in the package DBMS_SQL. In order to execute a bind of a collection, the collection must contain at least one element. If no elements are present then at execute time there will be no value for this bind and the statement is meaningless.
solution: Fill the collection with the elements you want to bind and try the bind call again.

message: shared pool object does not exist, cannot be pinned/purged
cause: The specified shared pool shared cursor could not be found, therefore it cannot be pinned/purged.
solution: Remove the procedure from the calling stored procedure.

message: Function string does not guarantee not to update database
cause: There are two possible causes for this message: * A SQL statement references a packaged, PL/SQL function that does not contain a pragma that prevents the database from being updated. * A SQL statement references a stand-alone, PL/SQL function that contains an instruction to update the database.
solution: If the referenced function is a packaged, PL/SQL function: Recreate the PL/SQL function with the required pragma; be certain to include the 'Write No Database State' (WNDS) argument in the argument list of the pragma. If the referenced function is a stand-alone, PL/SQL function: Do not use the function.

message: Function string has out arguments
cause: A SQL statement references either a packaged, or a stand-alone, PL/SQL function that contains an OUT parameter in its argument list. PL/SQL functions referenced by SQL statements must not contain the OUT parameter.
solution: Recreate the PL/SQL function without the OUT parameter in the argument list.

message: Function string modifies package state, cannot be used here
cause: There are two possible causes for this message: * A SQL statement references a packaged, PL/SQL function that does not contain a pragma containing the 'Write no Package State' (WNPS). * A SQL statement references a stand-alone, PL/SQL function that modifies a package state. A stand-alone, PL/SQL function referenced by a SQL statement cannot modify a package state.
solution: If the function is a packaged, PL/SQL function: Recreate the function and include a pragma containing the 'Write no Package State' (WNPS). If the function is a stand-alone, PL/SQL function: Delete the function from the SQL statement.

message: Function string references package state, cannot execute remotely
cause: There are two possible causes for this message: * A remote, packaged function or a remote-mapped, local, packaged function that does not contain a pragma with the 'Write no Package State' (WNPS) and 'Read no Package State' (RNPS) arguments references a package state. * A remote, stand-alone function or a remote-mapped, local, stand-alone function contains a reference to a package state (reads or writes a package variable). Only local functions that are referenced in a SELECT list, VALUES clause of an INSERT statement, or SET clause of an UPDATE statement can modify a package state.
solution: If the function is a packaged function: Recreate the function and include a pragma containing the 'Write no Package State' (WNPS) and 'Read no Package State' (RNPS) arguments. If the function is a stand-alone function: Do not call the function.

message: Package or function string is in an invalid state
cause: A SQL statement references a PL/SQL function that is in an invalid state. Oracle attempted to compile the function, but detected errors.
solution: Check the SQL statement and the PL/SQL function for syntax errors or incorrectly assigned, or missing, privileges for a referenced object.

message: not a valid function or procedure name
cause: Could not find a function (if an INTO clause was present) or a procedure (if the statement did not have an INTO clause) to call.
solution: Change the statement to invoke a function or procedure

message: output parameter not a bind variable
cause: The argument corresponding to an IN/OUT or OUT parameter for a function or a procedure or a function return value in a CALL statement must be a bind variable.
solution: Change the argument to a bind variable

message: output parameter cannot be a duplicate bind
cause: The bind variable corresponding to an IN/OUT or OUT parameter for a function or a procedure or a function return value in a CALL statement cannot be a duplicate bind variable.
solution: Change the bind variable to be unique

message: Bind variable not big enough to hold the output value
cause: The bind variable specified by the user is not large enough to hold the output returned by the function or a procedure.
solution: Specify a bind variable of larger size.

message: Hash Join ran out of memory while keeping large rows in memory
cause: Hash Join reserves 3 slots (each slot size = DB_BLOCK_SIZE * HASH_JOIN_MULTIBLOCK_IO_COUNT) for a row. If a row is larger than that, this error will be raised.
solution: Increase HASH_JOIN_MULTIBLOCK_IO_COUNT so that each joined row fits in a slot. HASH_AREA_SIZE may also need to be increaed.

message: CASE not found while executing CASE statement
cause: A CASE statement must either list all possible cases or have an else clause.
solution: Add all missing cases or an else clause.

message: string is not supported with natively compiled PL/SQL modules
cause: Specified feature is not yet supported for natively compiled PL/SQL modules yet.
solution: Recompile the relevant PL/SQL modules in non-native mode by setting the parameter plsql_compiler_flags to INTERPRETED.

message: REF CURSOR parameters are not supported in forwarded RPC calls
cause: An attempt was made to make a forwarded RPC call with a REF CURSOR parameter.
solution: Either call the remote function directly (i.e., not by way of forwarding), or move the remote function to a database where it can be called directly.

message: object cannot be purged, object is permanently kept in shared pool
cause: The specified object was permanently kept, therefore, cannot be purged.
solution: Use DBMS_SHARED_POOL.UNKEEP procedure to unkeep the object and then purge it.

message: Failed to increase the session's call stack memory to string bytes at a depth of string calls. (The current maximum is string bytes.)
cause: PL/SQL program execution used more call stack memory than permitted.
solution: * Ask your DBA to increase the maximum allowed call stack memory. * Decrease the amount of call stack used by the program. This may be accomplished by using fewer, smaller local variables, or by limiting the depth of function call nesting.

message: LU6.2 Driver: SNA software is not loaded
cause: The SNA software is not running.
solution: Start the SNA software and try again.

message: LU6.2 Driver: Invalid database ID string
cause: The database string in the connect was invalid.
solution: Provide a valid database string, as defined in documentation.

message: LU6.2 Driver: Error allocating context area
cause: Context area failure.
solution: Contact your local service representative.

message: LU6.2 Driver: Error allocating memory
cause: Operating system refused request for memory.
solution: Contact you local service representative.

message: LU6.2 Driver: Unable to allocate session with remote LU
cause: Allocate system call failed.
solution: Ensure that the SNA software is running and that sessions are free. If this is the case, then check your SNA configuration data for errors. You may have entered an incorrect parameter.

message: LU6.2 Driver: Unexpected line turnaround
cause: SNA software switched from send to receive unexpectedly.
solution: Check the SNA configuration data, particularly parameters associated with a session.

message: LU6.2 Driver: Unexpected response from SNA
cause: A parameter in an SNA call returned an unexpected value.
solution: Attempt to reproduce problem, debug and record the value of the 'what' data parameter at the time of error. Then contact your service representative.

message: LU6.2 Driver: Reset occurred in send state
cause: A reset was issued whilst in send state.
solution: Check the SNA LOG data, if relevent, for further information.

message: LU6.2 Driver: Reset occurred in receive state
cause: A reset was received from the partner whilst in receive state. This may be because the partner deallocated.
solution: Check the SNA LOG data, if relevent, for further information.

message: LU6.2 Driver: Failed during deallocation
cause: LU6.2 driver was unable to deallocate gracefully.
solution: Check the reason for deallocation. Consult the SNA LOG data.

message: LU6.2 Driver: Attach to LU failed
cause: The SQL*Net LU6.2 driver was unable to attach to the LU specified in the connect string, or was unable to attach to the default LU.
solution: Check that the LU name specified in the connect string, or the default LU name if no LU was specified, is correctly configured and operational.

message: LU6.2 Driver: Unable to attach to SNA
cause: The SQL*Net LU6.2 driver could not attach to the SNA software on your machine. The most likely cause is that the SNA software is not operational.
solution: Check the status of the SNA software, ensure that it is operational and then try again.

message: TLI Driver: incorrect message type from host
cause: TLI received a message with an unrecognizable message type.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: TLI Driver: incorrect number of bytes written
cause: TLI sent a message that was apparently successful, but the number of bytes transmitted did not match the number of bytes supplied to the driver.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: TLI Driver: cannot allocate context area
cause: TLI could not allocate heap space for the context area.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: TLI Driver: send break message failed
cause: TLI failed to send a break message across the connection.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: TLI Driver: receive break message failed
cause: TLI failed to receive an expected break message.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: TLI Driver: remote node is unknown
cause: TLI could not find your remote host information.
solution: Make sure you specified the hostname correctly on the command line. (Also, check your capitalization and spelling.)

message: TLI Driver: service not found
cause: TLI could not find service information for the specified service name.
solution: If you specified the service name on the command line or with the environment variable TLI_SERVER, make sure you specified it correctly. If the service name is not in the SERVICES file for your protocol, ask your system adminstrator to add it.

message: TLI Driver: connection failed
cause: TLI failed to establish the connection to a SQL*Net TCP/IP server due to an error encountered by the remote server, which has supplied a string describing the remote error.
solution: See the SQL*Net TCP/IP User's Guide section "orasrv Messages" for the specific cause and action.

message: TLI Driver: message receive failure
cause: TLI encountered an error receiving a message from the communication channel.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: TLI Driver: message send failure
cause: TLI encountered an error sending a message across the communication channel.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: TLI Driver: send interrupt break message failed
cause: TLI failed to send a break message while handling an interrupt signal from the user.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: TLI Driver: error on bind
cause: TLI failed to assign a network address to the communication channel.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: TLI Driver: error on accept
cause: TLI failed to accept a connection request from the client.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: TLI Driver: error on connect
cause: TLI failed to connect the client to the remote server. The network line to the remote host may be down.
solution: Use other network login programs to make sure that the remote host is accessible.

message: TLI Driver: SID lookup failure
cause: The database SID supplied in the database login string was not recognized by the remote host.
solution: Ask your system administrator to add the appropriate SID entry to oratab on the remote host.

message: TLI Driver: spurious client req
cause: The remote TLI server received an undefined request.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: TLI Driver: connection setup failure
cause: The remote TLI server rejected the connection request, and the client was unable to retrieve an error code or message.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: TLI Driver: unable to open clone device
cause: TLI failed to open the Streams clone device associated with the transport provider.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: TLI Driver: cannot alloc t_call
cause: TLI cannot allocate space for the client's connection information.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: TLI Driver: cannot alloc t_discon
cause: TLI cannot allocate space for the client's disconnection information.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: TLI Driver: failed to receive disconnect
cause: TLI failed to receive an expected disconnection message during connection release.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: TLI Driver: cannot connect
cause: TLI failed to connect the client to the remote server.
solution: Check that the remote TLI server is running.

message: TLI Driver: client failed to close error conn
cause: TLI failed to properly close a connection after an error was received.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: TLI Driver: server not running
cause: TLI timed out while attempting to connect to the remote TLI server.
solution: Check that the remote TLI server is running with the status utility for the transport provider you are using. If it is not, ask your system adminstrator to start it.

message: TLI Driver: connection failed
cause: TLI could not establish a connection to the remote TLI server.
solution: Check that the remote TLI server is running with the status utility for the transport provider you are using.

message: TLI Driver: unable to open protocol device
cause: The TLI server failed to open the Streams device associated with the transport provider.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: TLI Driver: cannot alloc t_bind
cause: The TLI server cannot allocate space for its requested network address.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: TLI Driver: cannot alloc t_bind
cause: The TLI server cannot allocate space for its actual network address.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: TLI Driver: listener cannot bind
cause: The TLI server failed to assign the correct network address on which to listen for connections.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: TLI Driver: listener already running
cause: The network address on which the TLI server awaits connection requests is in use, possibly because the server is already running.
solution: Ensure that the TLI server is not already running. If it is not running and this error message recurs, contact your customer support representative.

message: TLI Driver: cannot alloc t_call
cause: TLI cannot allocate space for the TLI server's connection information.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: TLI Driver: error in listen
cause: The TLI server encountered an error while listening for connection requests.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: TLI Driver: cannot allocate t_discon
cause: TLI cannot allocate space for the TLI server's disconnection information.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: TLI Driver: option not allowed across network
cause: The requested TLI server command must be issued from the same host on which the server is running.
solution: Log in to the remote host and try again.

message: TLI Driver: sync failed
cause: The ORACLE process started by the TLI server was unable to synchronize its inherited connection.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: TLI Driver: bound addresses unequal
cause: The osn check server address failed. The bound server address was not the same as the requested binding address.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: TLI: error in signal setup
cause: A call to sigaction() returned with a system error.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: TLI Driver: name-to-address mapping failed
cause: For SVR4, the netdir_getbyname() call failed for some unknown reason.
solution: Contact your custumer service representative.

message: TLI Driver: unable to get local host address
cause: The name of the remote host to connect to was not specified, and the name of the local host cannot be retrieved from the HOSTS file.
solution: Contact your system administrator.

message: TLI Driver: cannot close transport endpoint
cause: The TLI server was unable to close a connection after passing it to an ORACLE process.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: TLI Driver: cannot open oratab
cause: The TLI server could not open the file used to define the locations of remotely accessible databases.
solution: Ask your system administrator to check that the file exists and has the correct permissions.

message: TLI Driver: server got bad command
cause: The TLI server received an invalid command.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: TLI Driver: timeout reading orderly release
cause: TLI was not able to retreive an expected disconnect message while closing the communication channel.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: TLI Driver: error sending orderly release
cause: TLI encountered an error sending a disconnect message closing the communication channel.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: TLI Driver: error reading orderly release
cause: TLI encountered an error receiving an expected disconnect message while closing the communication channel.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: TLI Driver: error sending disconnect
cause: TLI encountered an error sending a disconnect message closing the communication channel.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: TLI Driver: error reading disconnect
cause: TLI was not able to retreive an expected disconnect message while closing the communication channel.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: TLI Driver: error awaiting orderly release
cause: TLI encountered an error awaiting a disconnect message while closing the communication channel.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: TLI Driver: close failed during release
cause: TLI failed to close the communication channel after receiving a disconnect message.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: TLI Driver: alloc failed during release
cause: TLI cannot allocate space for disconnection information while closing the communication channel.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: TLI Driver: error sending version
cause: TLI encountered an error while sending its version information during connection establishment.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: TLI Driver: error reading version
cause: TLI encountered an error while awaiting the expected version information during connection establishment.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: TLI Driver: error sending command
cause: TLI encountered an error while sending a command message during connection establishment.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: TLI Driver: error reading command
cause: TLI encountered an error while awaiting the expected command message during connection establishment.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: TLI Driver: error sending break mode
cause: TLI encountered an error while sending break-mode message during connection establishment.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: TLI Driver: error reading break mode
cause: TLI encountered an error while awaiting the expected break-mode message during connection establishment.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: TLI Driver: error sending parms
cause: TLI encountered an error while sending the connection parameters during connection establishment.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: TLI Driver: error reading parms
cause: TLI encountered an error while awaiting the expected connection parameter message during connection establishment.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: TLI Driver: error sending ccode
cause: TLI encountered an error while sending the completion status message during connection establishment.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: TLI Driver: error reading ccode
cause: TLI encountered an error while awaiting the expected completion status message during connection establishment.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: TLI Driver: recv error code failed
cause: TLI encountered an error while awaiting an expected error message during connection establishment.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: TLI Driver: error reading negotation string
cause: TLI encountered an error while awaiting the expected negotiation message during connection establishment.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: TLI Driver: poll failed
cause: TLI was unable to poll the communication channel for possible incoming messages.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: TLI Driver: poll returned error event
cause: TLI received an unexpected event while polling the communication channel for possible incoming messages.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: TLI Driver: server cannot exec oracle
cause: The remote TLI server was unable to start an ORACLE process on behalf of the client.
solution: Note the operating system error message or number and contact your system adminstrator. The permissions on the remote ORACLE program may be set incorrectly.

message: TLI Driver: server cannot create new process
cause: The remote TLI server was unable to start an ORACLE process on behalf of the client.
solution: Note the operating system error message or number and contact your system adminstrator. The remote host may be unable to create any new processes due to a full process table.

message: TLI Driver: shadow process could not retrieve protocol info
cause: The ORACLE process either failed to allocate memory to store the protocol information record, or the protocol rejected the request for some unknown reason.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: TLI Driver: SQL*Net SPX client went away during reconnect
cause: The client process was aborted by the system or the user, and was unable to complete the connection establishment with the server listener process.
solution: Determine cause of client exit, and reattempt connection.

message: TLI Driver: listen for SPX server reconnect failed
cause: An unknown event occurred on the client's listening socket.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: TLI Driver: could not open the /etc/netware/yellowpages file
cause: The /etc/netware/yellowpages file does not exist, or is not readable by the TLI listener process.
solution: Insure the file exists and is readable. Make sure that the server machine's node name, network number, ethernet address, and listening socket number are encoded in the file.

message: TLI Driver: the IPX device file could not be opened
cause: The /dev/ipx file does not exist, or the driver has not been installed in the kernel correctly.
solution: Reinvoke the Oracle root installation. If problem continues, contact your customer support representative.

message: TLI Driver: could not bind an IPX address at initialization
cause: The IPX driver has not been correctly installed.
solution: Reinvoke the Oracle root installation. If problem continues, contact your customer support representative.

message: TLI Driver: could not send datagram SAP packet for SPX
cause: The socket endpoint for sending SAP packet was corrupted for some unknown reason.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: TLI Driver: could not complete protocol initialization for SPX
cause: A step in the SPX/IPX protocol initialization failed.
solution: Check the previous error reported, and follow corrective action.

message: TLI Driver: could not open ethernet device driver file
cause: The file /dev/eth does not exist, or the driver it references could not be opened.
solution: The system's real ethernet device file, for example /dev/wd, for the Western Digital ethernet driver, should be linked to the file /dev/eth. If this has been done, insure that the ethernet driver has been installed by completing the TCP/IP installation on your system, and testing a connection. If problem continues, contact your customer support representative for a list of supported ethernet drivers.

message: TLI Driver: could not link IPX and ethernet streams
cause: Either the ethernet driver has not been installed in the system correctly, or the ethernet driver is not supported.
