solution: Redefine the geometric element type in the <layer>_SDOGEOM table for the specified geometric element using one of the supported SDO_ETYPE values. See the Oracle Spatial documentation for an explanation of SDO_ETYPE and its possible values.

message: unable to read dimension definition from string
cause: There was a problem reading the dimension definition from the <layer>_SDODIM table.
solution: Verify that the <layer>_SDODIM table exists and that the appropriate privileges exist on the table. Address any other errors that might appear with the message.

message: Invalid Gtype in the SDO_GEOMETRY object
cause: There is an invalid SDO_GTYPE in the SDO_GEOMETRY object.
solution: Verify that the geometries have valid gtypes.

message: Invalid SRID in the SDO_GEOMETRY object
cause: There is an invalid SDO_SRID in the SDO_GEOMETRY object. The specified SRID may be outside the valid SRID range.
solution: Verify that the geometries have valid SRIDs.

message: Invalid dimension for the SDO_GEOMETRY object
cause: There is a mismatch between the dimension in the SDO_GTYPE and dimension in the SDO_GEOM_METADATA for the SDO_GEOMETRY object.
solution: Verify that the geometries have valid dimensionality.

message: Invalid Gtype in the SDO_GEOMETRY object for point object
cause: There is an invalid SDO_GTYPE in the SDO_GEOMETRY object where the VARRAYs are NULL but the SDO_GTYPE is not of type POINT.
solution: Verify that the geometries have valid gtypes.

message: Invalid NULL SDO_GEOMETRY object
cause: There are invalid SDO_POINT_TYPE or SDO_ELEM_INFO_ARRAY or SDO_ORDINATE_ARRAY fields in the SDO_GEOMETRY object.
solution: Verify that the geometries have valid fields. To specify a NULL geometry, specify the whole SDO_GEOMETRY as NULL instead of setting each field to NULL.

message: Invalid data in the SDO_ELEM_INFO_ARRAY in SDO_GEOMETRY object
cause: There is invalid data in the SDO_ELEM_INFO_ARRAY field of the SDO_GEOMETRY object. The triplets in this field do not make up a valid geometry.
solution: Verify that the geometries have valid data.

message: Invalid data in the SDO_ORDINATE_ARRAY in SDO_GEOMETRY object
cause: There is invalid data in the SDO_ORDINATE_ARRAY field of the SDO_GEOMETRY object. The coordinates in this field do not make up a valid geometry. There may be NULL values for X or Y or both.
solution: Verify that the geometries have valid data.

message: Invalid data (arcs in geodetic data) in the SDO_GEOMETRY object
cause: There is invalid data in the SDO_ELEM_INFO_ARRAY field of the SDO_GEOMETRY object. There are arcs in a geometry that has geodetic coordinates.
solution: Verify that the geometries have valid data.

message: Operation [ string ] not supported for Point Data
cause: The specified geometry function is not supported for point data.
solution: Make sure that the specified geometry function is not called on point data.

message: SRIDs do not match for the two geometries
cause: A Spatial operation is invoked with two geometries where one geometry has an SRID and the other geometry does not have an SRID.
solution: Make sure that the spatial operations are invoked between two geometries with compatible SRIDs.

message: failed to update spatial index for element string . string . string
cause: Another error will accompany this message that will indicate the problem.
solution: Correct any accompanying errors. If no accompanying error message appears, contact Oracle Support Services.

message: failed to subdivide tile
cause: This is an internal error.
solution: Note any accompanying errors and contact Oracle Support Services.

message: failed to compare tile with element string . string . string
cause: The spatial relationship between a generated tile and the specified element could not be determined.
solution: This is an internal error. Verify the geometry using the VALIDATE_GEOMETRY_WITH_CONTEXT procedure. If the procedure does not return any errors, note any errors that accompany ORA-13041 and contact Oracle Support Services.

message: invalid SDO_LEVEL and SDO_NUMTILES combination
cause: An invalid combination of SDO_LEVEL and SDO_NUMTILES values was read from the <layer>_SDOLAYER table. The most likely cause is that the columns are NULL.
solution: Verify the that SDO_LEVEL and SDO_NUMTILES columns contain valid integer values as described in the Oracle Spatial documentation. Then retry the operation.

message: failed to read metadata from the <layer>_SDOLAYER table
cause: An error was encountered reading the layer metadata from the <layer>_SDOLAYER table.
solution: This error is usually the result of an earlier error which should also have been reported. Address this accompanying error and retry the current operation. If no accompanying error was reported, contact Oracle Support Services.

message: the specified tile size is smaller than the tolerance
cause: The tile size specified for fixed size tessellation is smaller than the tolerance as specified in the layer metadata.
solution: See the Oracle Spatial documentation for an explanation of tiling levels, tile size, and tiling resolution. Ensure that the tiling parameters are set such that any generated tile is always larger than or equal to a tile at the maximum level of resolution. This can be achieved by using a fewer number of tiles per geometric object or specifying a smaller tile size value than the current one.

message: invalid compatibility flag
cause: This is an internal error.
solution: Contact Oracle Support Services.

message: invalid number of arguments
cause: An invalid number of arguments were specified for an SDO_GEOM function.
solution: See the Oracle Spatial documentation for a description of the syntax and semantics of the relevant SDO_GEOM function.

message: unable to determine ordinate count from table <layer>_SDOLAYER
cause: An SDO_GEOM function was unable to determine the number of ordinates for the SDO layer <layer>.
solution: Verify that the <layer>_SDOLAYER table has a valid value for the column SDO_ORDCNT. Then retry the operation.

message: recursive SQL fetch error
cause: This is an internal error.
solution: Contact Oracle Support Services.

message: unable to determine tolerance value from table <layer>_SDODIM
cause: An SDO_GEOM function was unable to determine the tolerance value for the SDO layer <layer>.
solution: Verify that the <layer>_SDODIM table has a valid value for the column SDO_TOLERANCE.

message: unable to construct spatial object
cause: This is an internal error.
solution: Contact Oracle Support Services.

message: failed to initialize spatial object
cause: This is an internal error.
solution: Contact Oracle Support Services.

message: unsupported geometric type for geometry string . string
cause: The geometry type for a specific instance in a <layer>_SDOGEOM table is not among the set of geometry types supported by Oracle Spatial.
solution: Check the Oracle Spatial documentation for the list of supported geometry types and workarounds that permit the storage and retrieval of non-supported geometric types with the SDO schema.

message: maximum number of geometric elements in argument list exceeded
cause: The maximum number of geometric elements that can be specified in the argument list for an SDO_GEOM function was exceeded.
solution: Check the Oracle Spatial documentation for the syntax of the SDO_GEOM function and use fewer arguments to describe the geometry, or check the description of the SDO_WINDOW package for a workaround that permits storing the object in a table and then using it in as an argument in a call to the SDO_GEOM function.

message: recursive SQL parse error
cause: This is an internal error.
solution: Contact Oracle Support Services.

message: Oracle object string does not exist in specified table
cause: The requested object is not present in the specified table.
solution: Verify the syntax of the function or procedure that reported this error and verify that the object does indeed exist in the specified table. Then retry the operation.

message: topology with the name string already exists
cause: The specified topology name was not unique in the database.
solution: Verify that the CREATE_TOPOLOGY call specifies the correct topology name and that the procedure is invoked from the correct schema.

message: topology with the name string does not exist
cause: The specified topology did not exist in the database.
solution: Verify that the current procedure/function call specifies the correct schema and topology name.

message: topology IDs do not match in the feature table and the topology
cause: The specified topology ID in the feature table did not match the topology ID stored in the topology metadata.
solution: Verify that the specified topology ID matches the topology ID stored in the topology metadata.

message: relationship information table is missing data for feature table [ string ]
cause: The topology relationship information table (xxx_RELATION$) did not have the matching partition corresponding to the feature table.
solution: Make sure the correct topology IDs and names are specified in the call to register the feature table with the topology.

message: relationship information table has inconsistent data for feature table [ string ]
cause: The topology_id, tg_layer_id values stored in the feature table did not match the values stored in the topology relationship information table (xxx_RELATION$).
solution: Make sure that the correct feature tables are specified in the call to register the feature table with the topology.

message: cannot delete a child layer with a parent layer
cause: A call was made to delete a feature layer which has a dependent layer defined on it.
solution: Make sure that all dependent feature layers are deleted before deleting the current feature layer.

message: wrong feature geometry or element type
cause: The SDO_TOPO_GEOMETRY object had the wrong geometry and/or element type.
solution: Correct the geometry and/or element type in the SDO_TOPO_GEOMETRY object.

message: operator requires both parameters from the same topology
cause: Both SDO_TOPO_GEOMETRY parameters did not come from the same topology.
solution: Make sure both the parameters to the operator are from the same topology. If this is not possible, consider using a signature of the operator that does not use two SDO_TOPO_GEOMETRY parameters.

message: wrong table or column name in SDO_TOPO_GEOMETRY constructor
cause: An SDO_TOPO_GEOMETRY constructor was invoked with incorrect parameters for table name and/or column name.
solution: Fix the parameters in the call and try again.

message: spatial table string not found
cause: The specified spatial table does not exist.
solution: Check the Spatial data dictionary to make sure that the table is registered.

message: spatial table string exists
cause: The specified spatial table is registered in the Spatial data dictionary.
solution: Remove the existing table from the Spatial data dictionary or use a different name.

message: cannot drop topology with associated topo_geometry tables
cause: The drop_topology procedure was invoked for a topology that has assocated topo_geometry layers with it.
solution: Delete the topo_geometry layers from the topology before dropping the topology. Use SDO_TOPO.delete_topo_geometry_layer to delete topo_geometry layers from the topology.

message: cannot add topo_geometry layer [ string ] to topology
cause: It was not possible to add the specified topo_geometry layer to the topology.
solution: Make sure the topo_geometry layer table exists in the database.

message: cannot delete topo_geometry layer [ string ] from topology
cause: It was not possible to delete the specified topo_geometry layer from the topology.
solution: Check USER_SDO_TOPO_METADATA to see if the specified topo_geometry layer is part of the topology. Only those topo_geometry layers which are part of the topology can be deleted from it.

message: invalid tg_layer_id in sdo_topo_geometry constructor
cause: An invalid layer_id was passed to the SDO_TOPO_GEOMETRY constructor.
solution: Valid layer_ids are obtained by adding a topo_geometry layer to the topology. Check USER_SDO_TOPO_METADATA to find out the layer_id for an existing topo_geometry layer.

message: [ string ]_NODE$ table does not exist
cause: The NODE$ table for the topology did not exist in the database.
solution: There is a severe corruption of the topology. Call Oracle Support Services with the error number.

message: [ string ]_EDGE$ table does not exist
cause: The EDGE$ table for the topology did not exist in the database.
solution: There is a severe corruption of the topology. Call Oracle Support Services with the error number.

message: [ string ]_FACE$ table does not exist
cause: The FACE$ table for the topology did not exist in the database.
solution: There is a severe corruption of the topology. Call Oracle Support Services with the error number.

message: [ string ]_RELATION$ table does not exist
cause: The RELATION$ table for the topology did not exist in the database.
solution: There is a severe corruption of the topology. Call Oracle Support Services with the error number.

message: invalid node_id [ string ]
cause: A topology node operation was invoked with an invalid node_id.
solution: Check the topology node$ table to see if the specified node_id exists in the topology.

message: invalid edge_id [ string ]
cause: A topology edge operation was invoked with an invalid edge_id.
solution: Check the topology edge$ table to see if the specified edge_id exists in the topology.

message: invalid face_id [ string ]
cause: A topology face operation was invoked with an invalid face_id.
solution: Check the topology face$ table to see if the specified face_id exists in the topology.

message: layer type type mismatch with topo_geometry layer type
cause: The tg_type in SDO_TOPO_GEOMETRY constructor did not match the type specified for the layer.
solution: Check the USER_SDO_TOPO_METADATA view to see the layer type for the layer and use it in the constructor.

message: invalid topo_geometry specified
cause: The SDO_TOPO_GEOMETRY object passed into the function/operator was not valid.
solution: Check the SDO_TOPO_GEOMETRY object and verify that it is a valid topo_geometry object.

message: invalid <TOPOLOGY> name specified
cause: The create_topo operation requires a unique TOPOLOGY name, that already does not exist in the database.
solution: Check to see if there is already an entry in the USER_SDO_TOPO_METADATA (or the MDSYS.SDO_TOPO_METADATA_TABLE) with this topology name.

message: unable to determine column id for column string
cause: This is an internal error.
solution: Contact Oracle Support Services.

message: partition key is already set
cause: A partition key is already set for the spatial table.
solution: Only one partition key can be specified per spatial table.

message: unable to determine class for spatial table string
cause: This is an internal error.
solution: Contact Oracle Support Services.

message: failed to generate target partition
cause: This is an internal error.
solution: Contact Oracle Support Services.

message: current tiling level exceeds user specified tiling level
cause: This is an internal error.
solution: Contact Oracle Support Services.

message: HHCODE column string not found
cause: The specified spatial column does not exist.
solution: Verify that the specified column is a spatial column by checking the Spatial data dictionary.

message: failed to alter spatial table
cause: This is an internal error.
solution: Contact Oracle Support Services.

message: null common code generated
cause: This is an internal error.
solution: Contact Oracle Support Services.

message: failed to generate tablespace sequence number
cause: This is an internal error.
solution: Contact Oracle Support Services.

message: could not determine name of object string
cause: This is an internal error.
solution: Contact Oracle Support Services.

message: could not obtain column definition for string
cause: This is an internal error.
solution: Contact Oracle Support Services.

message: invalid target type
cause: The specified target type is not valid.
solution: Substitute a valid target type. Valid target types are TABLE and VIEW.

message: invalid RANGE window definition
cause: The RANGE window specified is not correctly defined.
solution: A RANGE window is defined by specifying the lower and upper boundary of each dimension as a pair of values (e.g.: lower_bound1,upper_bound1,lower_bound2,upper_bound2,...). There should be an even number of values.

message: invalid PROXIMITY window definition
cause: The PROXIMITY window specified is not correctly defined.
solution: A PROXIMITY window is defined by specifying a center point and a radius. The center point is defined by ND values. There should be ND+1 values.

message: invalid POLYGON window definition
cause: The POLYGON window specified is not correctly defined.
solution: A POLYGON window is defined by specifying N pairs of values that represent the vertices of the polygon. There should be an even number of values.

message: target table string not found
cause: This is an internal error.
solution: Contact Oracle Support Services.

message: failed to generate range list
cause: This is an internal error.
solution: Contact Oracle Support Services.

message: could not find table substitution variable string
cause: The partition name substitution variable %s was not found in the SQL filter.
solution: The substitution variable %s must be in the SQL filter to indicate where that partition name should be placed.

message: failed to generate MBR
cause: This is an internal error.
solution: Contact Oracle Support Services.

message: failed to generate SQL filter
cause: This is an internal error.
solution: Contact Oracle Support Services.

message: failed to generate next sequence number for spatial table string
cause: This is an internal error.
solution: Contact Oracle Support Services.

message: failed to insert exception record
cause: Operation failed to insert a record into the exception table.
solution: Fix any other errors reported.

message: failed to remove exception record
cause: Operation failed to remove a record from the exception table.
solution: Fix any other errors reported.

message: invalid HHCODE type
cause: Specified HHCODE type is not valid.
solution: Substitute a valid HHCODE type. Valid HHCODE types are POINT and LINE.

message: invalid high water mark specified
cause: The high water mark must be greater than or equal to zero.
solution: Make sure that the high water mark is an integer greater than or equal to zero.

message: invalid precision specified
cause: The precision specified is out of range.
solution: The precision must be an integer greater than or equal to zero.

message: invalid number of dimensions specified
cause: The number of dimensions specified is out of range.
solution: The number of dimension must be between 1 and 32.

message: table to be registered string . string is not empty
cause: The specified table has rows in it.
solution: Make sure that the table to be registered is empty.

message: Oracle error ORA string encountered while string
cause: The specified Oracle error was encountered.
solution: Correct the Oracle error.

message: Oracle object string does not exist
cause: The specified object does not exist.
solution: Verify that the specified object exists.

message: Oracle table string already exists
cause: The specified table already exists.
solution: Drop the specified table.

message: unable to determine length of column string _SDOINDEX.SDO_CODE
cause: The length of the SDO_CODE column in the <layer>_SDOINDEX table could not be determined.
solution: Make sure that the <layer>_SDOINDEX table exists with the SDO_CODE column. Verify that the appropriate privileges exist on the table. Then retry the operation.

message: failed to read element string . string . string
cause: The specified element could not be read from the <layer>_SDOGEOM table.
solution: Verify that the specified element exists in the table. Then retry the operation.

message: unsupported geometric type for geometry string . string
cause: The geometry type in the <layer>_SDOGEOM table is unsupported.
solution: Modify the geometry type to be one of the supported types.

message: failed to initialize tessellation package
cause: Initialization of the tessellation package failed.
solution: Record the error messages that are returned and contact Oracle Support Services.

message: failed to generate initial HHCODE
cause: This is an internal error.
solution: Record the error messages that are returned and contact Oracle Support Services.

message: fixed tile size tessellation failed
cause: This is an internal error.
solution: Record the error messages that are returned and contact Oracle Support Services.

message: subdivision failed
cause: This is an internal error.
solution: Record the error messages that are returned and contact Oracle Support Services.

message: cell decode failed
cause: This is an internal error.
solution: Record the error messages that are returned and contact Oracle Support Services.

message: recursive SQL parse failed
cause: This is an internal error.
solution: Record the error messages that are returned and contact Oracle Support Services.

message: recursive SQL fetch failed
cause: This is an internal error.
solution: Record the error messages that are returned and contact Oracle Support Services.

message: failed to read SDO_ORDCNT value
cause: This is an internal error.
solution: Record the error messages that are returned and contact Oracle Support Services.

message: failed to read number of element rows
cause: This is an internal error.
solution: Record the error messages that are returned and contact Oracle Support Services.

message: failed to allocate space for geometry
cause: There was insufficient memory to read the geometry from the database.
solution: Validate the geometry. Record the error messages that are returned and contact Oracle Support Services.

message: failed to decode supercell
cause: This is an internal error.
solution: Contact Oracle Support Services.

message: failed to generate maximum tile value
cause: This is an internal error.
solution: Record the error messages that are returned and contact Oracle Support Services.

message: failed to compute supercell for element string . string . string
cause: The system was unable to compute the minimum bounding HHCODE or supercell for the geometry.
solution: Another error might accompany this error. Correct the accompanying error. Also, validate the geometry for correctness.

message: element string . string . string is out of range
cause: Tessellation did not generate any tiles for this element. This error could be caused if the geometry definition puts the geometry outside the domain defined in the <layer>_SDODIM table.
solution: Verify that the geometry is valid and within the defined domain.

message: Spatial error: string
cause: Internal error in some Oracle Spatial stored procedure.
solution: Record the sequence of procedure calls or events that preceded this error, and contact Oracle Support Services if the error message text does not clearly specify the cause of the error.

message: string
cause: This is an internal error.
solution: Contact Oracle Support Services.

message: internal error [ string ] in spatial indexing.
cause: This is an internal error.
solution: Contact Oracle Support Services with the exact error text.

message: invalid parameters supplied in CREATE INDEX statement
cause: An error was encountered while trying to parse the parameters clause for the spatial CREATE INDEX statement.
solution: Check the Oracle Spatial documentation for the number, syntax, and semantics of expected parameters for spatial index creation.

message: failed to create or insert into the SDO_INDEX_METADATA table
cause: An error was encountered while trying to create the SDO_INDEX_METADATA table or insert data into it.
solution: Verify that the current user has CREATE TABLE privilege and that the user has sufficient quota in the default or specified tablespace.

message: failed to read USER_SDO_GEOM_METADATA view
cause: An error encountered while trying to read the USER_SDO_GEOM_METADATA view.
solution: Check that USER_SDO_GEOM_METADATA has an entry for the current geometry table.

message: failed to create spatial index table
cause: An error was encountered while trying to create the index table.
solution: Check that user has CREATE TABLE privilege in the current schema and that the user has sufficient quota in the default or specified tablespace.

message: internal error while parsing spatial parameters
cause: An internal error was encountered while parsing the spatial parameters.
solution: Check that the parameters passed in the parameter string are all valid.

message: internal error [ string ] while creating the spatial index
cause: An internal error was encountered while creating the spatial index.
solution: Contact Oracle Support Services with the exact error text.

message: incorrect use of the [ string ] operator
cause: An error was encountered while evaluating the specified operator.
solution: Check the parameters and the return type of the specified operator.

message: internal error while evaluating [ string ] operator
cause: An internal error was encountered.
solution: Contact Oracle Support Services with the exact error text.

message: internal error while reading SDO_INDEX_METADATA table
cause: An internal error was encountered while trying to read the SDO_INDEX_METADATA table.
solution: Contact Oracle Support Services. Note this and accompanying error numbers.

message: error inserting data into the index table
cause: An error was encountered while trying to insert data into the index table. Likely causes are: - Insufficient quota in the current tablespace - User does not appropriate privileges
solution: Check the accompanying error messages.

message: failed to tessellate the window object
cause: An internal error was encountered while trying to tessellate the window object.
solution: Verify the geometric integrity of the window object using the VALIDATE_GEOMETRY_WITH_CONTEXT procedure.

message: failed to compare tile with the window object
cause: The spatial relationship between a generated tile and the specified window object could not be determined.
solution: This is an internal error. Verify the geometry using the VALIDATE_GEOMETRY_WITH_CONTEXT procedure. If the procedure does not return any errors, note any accompanying errors and contact Oracle Support Services.

message: failed to generate spatial index for window object
cause: Another error, indicating the real cause of the problem, should accompany this error.
solution: Correct any accompanying errors. If no accompanying error message appears, contact Oracle Support Services.

message: failed to compute supercell for window object
cause: The system was unable to compute the minimum bounding tile or supercell for the geometry.
solution: Another error might accompany this error. Correct the accompanying error. Also, validate the geometry for correctness.

message: window object is out of range
cause: Tessellation did not generate any tiles for this geometry. This error could be caused if the geometry definition puts the geometry outside the domain defined in the USER_SDO_GEOM_METADATA view.
solution: Verify that the geometry is valid and within the defined domain.

message: failed to update spatial index
cause: Another error will accompany this message that will indicate the problem.
solution: Correct any accompanying errors. If no accompanying error message appears, contact Oracle Support Services.

message: invalid parameters supplied in ALTER INDEX statement
cause: An error was encountered while trying to parse the parameters clause for the spatial ALTER INDEX statement.
solution: Check the Oracle Spatial documentation for the number, syntax, and semantics of expected parameters for the spatial ALTER INDEX statement.

message: max number of supported index tables reached for [ string ] index
cause: An add_index parameter was passed to ALTER INDEX when the number of existing index tables is already at maximum.
solution: Delete one of the index tables before adding another index table.

message: failed to create spatial index table [ string ]
cause: An error was encountered while trying to create the index table.
solution: There is a table in the index's schema with the specified name. The CREATE INDEX statement will try to create an index table with this name. Either rename this table or change the name of the index.

message: failed to compare tile with the geometry
cause: The spatial relationship between a generated tile and the specified geometry could not be determined.
solution: This is an internal error. Validate the geometry using the VALIDATE_GEOMETRY_WITH_CONTEXT procedure. If the procedure does not return any errors, note any errors that accompany ORA-13220 and contact Oracle Support Services.

message: unknown geometry type in the geometry object
cause: The SDO_GTYPE attribute in the geometry object contains an invalid value
solution: Redefine the geometric type in the geometry table using one of the supported SDO_GTYPE values. See the Oracle Spatial documentation for an explanation of SDO_GTYPE and its possible values.

message: failed to compute supercell for geometry in string
cause: The system was unable to compute the minimum bounding tile or supercell for a geometry in the specified table.
solution: Another error might accompany this error. Correct the accompanying error. Also, validate the geometry for correctness.

message: duplicate entry for string in SDO_GEOM_METADATA
cause: There are duplicate entries for the given table and column value pair in the USER_SDO_GEOM_METADATA view.
solution: Check that the specified table and geometry column names are correct. There should be only one entry per table, geometry column pair in the USER_SDO_GEOM_METADATA view.

message: zero tolerance specified for layer in USER_SDO_GEOM_METADATA
cause: A tolerance of zero or NULL is supplied for a layer in USER_SDO_GEOM_METADATA view.
solution: Check the tolerance specified to make sure it is a positive value.

message: specified index table name is too long for a spatial index
cause: An index table name is specified which is longer than the supported length of the spatial index table name.
solution: Check the supported size of the index table name and reduce the size of the index name.

message: interface not supported without a spatial index
cause: The geometry table does not have a spatial index.
solution: Verify that the geometry table referenced in the spatial operator has a spatial index on it.

message: SDO_LEVEL values for the two index tables do not match
cause: The SDO_LEVEL values for the two index tables used in the spatial join operator do not match.
solution: Verify that two compatible indexes are used for the spatial join operator. Quadtree indexes are compatible if they have the same SDO_LEVEL and SDO_NUMTILES values

message: spatial index create failed due to invalid type
cause: An Attempt was made to create a spatial index on a column of type other than SDO_GEOMETRY.
solution: Make sure that the index is created on a column of type SDO_GEOMETRY.

message: failed to create temporary table [ string ] during R-tree creation
cause: The specified temporary table either already exists or there is not enough tablespace.
solution: Delete the table if it already exists and verify if the current user has CREATE TABLE privileges and has sufficient space in the default or specified tablespace.

message: failed to create index table [ string ] during R-tree creation
cause: The specified index table either already exists or there is not enough tablespace.
solution: Delete the table if it already exists and verify if the current user has CREATE TABLE privileges and has sufficient space in the default or specified tablespace. If that fails to correct the problem, contact Oracle Support Services.

message: failed to allocate memory during R-tree creation
cause: This feature assumes a minimum of 64K memory for bulk creation.
solution: Create the index for a small subset of the data. Then, use transactional insert operations for the rest of the data.

message: failed to create sequence number [ string ] for R-tree
cause: The specified sequence number exists.
solution: Delete the sequence object, or contact Oracle Support Services.

message: failed to access R-tree-index table [ string ]
cause: The index table is either deleted or corrupted.
solution: Rebuild the index or contact Oracle Support Services with accompanying error messages.

message: internal error in R-tree processing: [ string ]
cause: An internal error occurred in R-tree processing.
solution: Contact Oracle Support Services with the message text.

message: internal error during R-tree concurrent updates: [ string ]
cause: An inconsistency is encountered during concurrent updates, possibly due to the use of serializable isolation level.
solution: Change the isolation level to "read committed" using the ALTER SESSION statement, or contact Oracle Support Services with the message text.

message: sdo_dimensionality not specified during n-d R-tree creation
cause: An error occurred in reading the dimensionality parameter
solution: Check the documentation for a valid range, and specify the dimensionality as a parameter.

message: specified dimensionality greater than that of the query mbr
cause: An error occurred because of too few values in the query minimum bounding rectangle (MBR).
solution: Omit the dimensionality, or use the dimensionality of the query.

message: specified dimensionality does not match that of the data
cause: An error occurred because the dimensionality specified in the CREATE INDEX statement does not match that of the data.
solution: Change the statement to reflect the data dimensionality.

message: specified operator is not supported for 3- or higher-dimensional R-tree
cause: Currently, an R-tree index with three or more index dimensions can be used only with the SDO_FILTER operator.
solution: Use the SDO_FILTER operator, and check the documentation for the querytype parameter for SDO_FILTER; or contact Oracle Support Services.

message: string
cause: An internal error was encountered in the extensible spatial index component. The text of the message is obtained from some other server component.
solution: Contact Oracle Support Services with the exact error text.

message: insufficient privileges to modify metadata table entries
cause: The user requesting the operation does not have the appropriate privileges on the referenced tables.
solution: Check that the specified feature and geometry table names are correct, and then verify that the current user has at least SELECT privilege on those tables.

message: duplicate entry string in metadata table
cause: The specified entry already exists in the metadata table.
solution: Check that the specified feature and geometry table names are correct. A feature-geometry table association should be registered only once.

message: layer table string does not exist
cause: Data migration source table <layer>_SDOGEOM does not exist.
solution: Ensure that the specified layer name is correct and that the corresponding spatial layer tables exist in the current schema.

message: geometry table string does not exist
cause: The specified geometry table does not exist in the current schema.
solution: Create a table containing a column of type SDO_GEOMETRY and a column of type NUMBER for the GID values.

message: geometry column string does not exist in table string
cause: The specified table does not have a column of type SDO_GEOMETRY.
solution: Alter or re-create the table such that it includes a column of type SDO_GEOMETRY and a column of type NUMBER.

message: column string in table string is not of type SDO_GEOMETRY
cause: The column intended for storing the geometry is not of type SDO_GEOMETRY.
solution: Alter the column definition to be of type SDO_GEOMETRY.

message: geometry identifier column string does not exist in table string
cause: The specified table does not contain a GID column.
solution: Confirm that the GID column name was correctly specified and that it exists in the specified table.

message: geometry identifier column string in table string is not of type NUMBER
cause: GID column is not of type NUMBER.
solution: Alter the table definition such that the column containing the geometry identifier (GID) is of type NUMBER.

message: error inserting data into table string
cause: An OCI error occurred, or the user has insufficient quota in the active tablespace, or the rollback segments are too small.
solution: There should be an accompanying error message that indicates the cause of the problem. Take appropriate action to correct the indicated problem.

message: error reading data from layer table string
cause: There was an error reading the geometry data from the <layer>_SDOGEOM table.
solution: Verify that <layer>_SDOGEOM and <layer>_SDODIM exist. If they do exist, run VALIDATE_LAYER_WITH_CONTEXT on the specified layer.

message: error obtaining dimension from USER_SDO_GEOM_METADATA
cause: There is no entry in the USER_SDO_GEOM_METADATA view for the specified geometry table.
solution: Insert an entry for the destination geometry table with the correct dimension information.

message: internal error [ string ] encountered when processing geometry table
cause: An internal error occurred.
solution: Contact Oracle Support Services with the exact error message text.

message: OCI error string
cause: An OCI error occurred while processing the layer or geometry tables.
solution: Take the appropriate steps to correct the OCI-specific error.

message: error allocating memory for geometry object
cause: Insufficient memory.
solution: Make more memory available to the current session/process.

message: geometric object string in table string is invalid
cause: The specified object failed the geometric integrity checks performed by the validation function.
solution: Check the Oracle Spatial documentation for information about the geometric integrity checks performed by VALIDATE_GEOMETRY_WITH_CONTEXT and correct the geometry definition if required.

message: dimension metadata table string does not exist
cause: The <layer>_SDODIM table does not exist.
solution: Verify that the specified layer name is correct and that the <layer>_SDODIM table exists in the current schema.

message: operator invoked with non-compatible SRIDs
cause: A Spatial operator was invoked with a window geometry with an SRID but the layer has no SRID; or the window has no SRID but the layer has an SRID.
solution: Make sure that the layer and window both have an SRID or that they both do not have an SRID.

message: spatial index creation failure on unsupported type
cause: An attempt was made to create a spatial index create on a column that is not of type SDO_GEOMETRY.
solution: A spatial index can only be created on a column of type SDO_GEOMETRY. Make sure the indexed column is of type SDO_GEOMETRY.

message: internal error [ string ] in coordinate transformation
cause: OCI internal error.
solution: Contact Oracle Support Services with the exact error message text.

message: failure to convert SRID to native format
cause: OCI internal error.
solution: Contact Oracle Support Services with the exact error message text.

message: failure in execution of SQL statement to retrieve WKT
cause: OCI internal error, or SRID does not match a table entry.
solution: Check that a valid SRID is being used.

message: failure on initialization of coordinate transformation
cause: Parsing error on source or destination coordinate system WKT, or incompatible coordinate systems.
solution: Check the validity of the WKT for table entries, and check if the requested transformation is valid.

message: failure to get new geometry object for conversion in place
cause: OCI internal error.
solution: Contact Oracle Support Services with the exact error message text.

message: failure to copy geometry object for conversion in place
cause: OCI internal error.
solution: Contact Oracle Support Services with the exact error message text.

message: Geometry coordinate transformation error
cause: A coordinate pair was out of valid range for a conversion/projection.
solution: Check that data to be transformed is consistent with the desired conversion/projection.

message: can't transform unknown gtype
cause: A geometry with a gtype of <= 0 was specified for transformation. Only a gtype >= 1 is allowed.
solution: Check the Oracle Spatial documentation for SDO_GTYPE values, and specify a value whose last digit is 1 or higher.

message: point coordinate transformation error
cause: An internal error occurred while transforming points.
solution: Check the accompanying error messages.

message: the specified unit is not supported
cause: An Oracle Spatial function was called with an unknown UNIT value.
solution: Check Spatial documentation for the supported units, and call the function with the correct UNIT parameter.

message: conversion error between the specified unit and standard unit
cause: Cannot convert the specified unit from/to standard unit for linear distance, angle, or area.
solution: Check the unit specification and respecify it.

message: incorrect ARC_TOLERANCE specification
cause: When a SDO_BUFFER or SDO_AGGR_BUFFER function is called on a geodetic geometry, or SDO_ARC_DENSIFY is called, ARC_TOLERANCE must be specified, and it should not be less than the tolerance specified for the geometry.
solution: Check ARC_TOLERANCE specification and make sure it is correct.

message: cannot specify unit for geometry without a georeferenced SRID
cause: An Oracle Spatial function with a UNIT parameter was called on a geometry without a georeferenced SRID.
solution: Make sure that spatial functions with UNIT parameters are only called on geometries with georeferenced SRIDs.

message: cannot transform geometry containing circular arcs
cause: It is impossible to transform a 3-point representation of a circular arc without distortion.
solution: Make sure a geometry does not contain circular arcs.

message: geometry objects are in different coordinate systems
cause: An Oracle Spatial function was called with two geometries that have different SRIDs.
solution: Transform geometry objects to be in the same coordinate system and call the spatial function.

message: incorrect coordinate system specification
cause: Wrong numbers in WKT for Earth radius or flattening for the current SRID.
solution: Check WKT in the MDSYS.CS_SRS table for Earth radius and inverse flattening.

message: single point transform error
cause: Low-level coordinate transformation error trap.
solution: Check the accompanying error messages.

message: failure to retrieve a geometry object from a table
cause: OCI internal error.
solution: Contact Oracle Support Services with the exact error message text.

message: failure to insert a transformed geometry object in a table
cause: OCI internal error.
solution: Contact Oracle Support Services with the exact error message text.

message: invalid MASK
cause: The MASK passed to the RELATE function is not valid.
solution: Verify that the mask is not NULL. See the Oracle Spatial documentation for a list of supported masks.

message: invalid LRS segment
cause: The given LRS segment was not a valid line string.
solution: A valid LRS geometric segment is a line string geometry in Oracle Spatial. It could be a simple or compound line string (made of lines or arcs, or both). The dimension information must include the measure dimension as the last element in the Oracle Spatial metadata. Currently, the number of dimensions for an LRS segment must be greater than 2 (x/y or longitude/latitude, plus measure)

message: invalid LRS point
cause: The specified LRS point was not a point geometry with measure information.
solution: Check the given point geometry. A valid LRS point is a point geometry in Oracle Spatial with an additional dimension for measure.

message: invalid LRS measure
cause: The given measure for linear referencing was out of range.
solution: Redefine the measure.

message: LRS segments not connected
cause: The specified geometric segments are not connected.
solution: Check the start/end points of the given geometric segments.

message: LRS measure information not defined
cause: The measure information of a geometric segment was not assigned (IS NULL).
solution: Assign/define the measure information. An LRS geometric segment is defined if its start and end measure are assigned (non-null).

message: failure in converting standard diminfo/geometry to LRS dim/geom
cause: There is no room for the measure dimension in the given diminfo, or the specified standard geometry is not a point a line string.
solution: Check if the diminfo dimensions are less than 3 or if the geometry type is point or line string.

message: failure in concatenating LRS polygons
cause: LRS concatenation involving LRS polygons is not supported.
solution: Check the geometry and element types to make sure the concatenate operation is not called with a polygon type.

message: failure in reversing LRS polygon/collection geometry
cause: Reversing an LRS polygon/collection geometry produces an invalid geometry.
solution: Check the geometry type to make sure this operation is called on non-polygon geometries.

message: LRS polygon clipping across multiple rings
cause: Clipping (dynseg) a polygon across multiple rings is not allowed.
solution: Polygon clipping is allowed only for a single ring.

message: a point geometry has more than one coordinate
cause: A geometry, specified as being a point, has more than one coordinate in its definition.
solution: A point has only one coordinate. If this geometry is intended to represent a point cluster, line, or polygon, set the appropriate SDO_GTYPE or SDO_ETYPE value. If this is a single point object, remove the extraneous coordinates from its definition.

message: a line geometry has fewer than two coordinates
cause: A geometry, specified as being a line, has fewer than two coordinates in its definition.
solution: A line must consist of at least two distinct coordinates. Correct the geometric definition, or set the appropriate SDO_GTYPE or SDO_ETYPE attribute for this geometry.

message: an arc geometry has fewer than three coordinates
cause: A geometry, specified as being an arc, has fewer than three coordinates in its definition.
solution: An arc must consist of at least three distinct coordinates. Correct the geometric definition, or set the appropriate SDO_GTYPE or SDO_ETYPE attribute for this geometry.

message: a polygon geometry has fewer than four coordinates
cause: A geometry, specified as being a polygon, has fewer than four coordinates in its definition.
solution: A polygon must consist of at least four distinct coordinates. Correct the geometric definition, or set the appropriate SDO_GTYPE or SDO_ETYPE attribute for this geometry.

message: an arcpolygon geometry has fewer than five coordinates
cause: A geometry, specified as being an arcpolygon, has fewer than five coordinates in its definition.
solution: An arcpolygon must consist of at least five coordinates. An arcpolygon consists of an ordered sequence of arcs, each of which must be described using three coordinates. Since arcs are connected the end-point of the first is the start of the second and does not have to be repeated. Correct the geometric definition, or set the appropriate SDO_GTYPE or SDO_ETYPE attribute for this geometry.

message: a compound polygon geometry has fewer than five coordinates
cause: A geometry, specified as being a compound polygon, has fewer than five coordinates in its definition.
solution: A compound polygon must contain at least five coordinates. A compound polygon consists of at least one arc and one line, each of which must be described using three and at least two distinct coordinates respectively. Correct the geometric definition, or set the appropriate SDO_GTYPE or SDO_ETYPE attribute for this geometry.

message: the coordinates defining an arc are collinear
cause: Invalid definition of an arc. An arc is defined using three non-collinear coordinates.
solution: Alter the definition of the arc, or set the SDO_ETYPE or SDO_GTYPE to the line type.

message: the coordinates defining an arc are not distinct
cause: Two or more of the three points defining an arc are the same.
solution: Alter the definition of the arc to ensure that three distinct coordinate values are used.

message: polygon boundary is not closed
cause: The boundary of a polygon does not close.
solution: Alter the coordinate values or the definition of the SDO_GTYPE or SDO_ETYPE attribute of the geometry.

message: polygon boundary crosses itself
cause: The boundary of a polygon intersects itself.
solution: Correct the geometric definition of the object.

message: two or more rings of a complex polygon touch
cause: The inner or outer rings of a complex polygon touch.
solution: All rings of a complex polygon must be disjoint. Correct the geometric definition of the object.

message: two or more rings of a complex polygon overlap
cause: The inner or outer rings of a complex polygon overlap.
solution: All rings of a complex polygon must be disjoint. Correct the geometric definition of the object.

message: the coordinates do not describe a circle
cause: The set of coordinates used to describe a circle are incorrect.
solution: Confirm that the set of coordinates actually represent points on the circumference of a circle.

message: ELEM_INFO_ARRAY not grouped in threes
cause: The ELEM_INFO_ARRAY in an SDO_GEOMETRY definition has more or fewer elements than expected.
solution: Confirm that the number of elements in ELEM_INFO_ARRAY is divisible by 3.

message: incorrect offset in ELEM_INFO_ARRAY
cause: The offset field in ELEM_INFO_ARRAY of an SDO_GEOMETRY definition references an invalid array subscript in SDO_ORDINATE_ARRAY.
solution: Confirm that the offset is a valid array subscript in SDO_ORDINATE_ARRAY.

message: SDO_ORDINATE_ARRAY not grouped by number of dimensions specified
cause: The number of elements in SDO_ORDINATE_ARRAY is not a multiple of the number of dimensions supplied by the user.
solution: Confirm that the number of dimensions is consistent with data representation in SDO_ORDINATE_ARRAY.

message: adjacent points in a geometry are redundant
cause: There are repeated points in the sequence of coordinates.
solution: Remove the redundant point.

message: extent type does not contain 2 points
cause: Extent type should be represented by two points: lower left and upper right.
solution: Confirm that there are only two points for an extent type.

message: circle type does not contain 3 points
cause: Circle type should be represented by three distinct points on the circumference.
solution: Confirm that there are only three points for a circle type.

message: extent does not have an area
cause: The two points representing the extent are identical.
solution: Confirm that the two points describing the extent type are distinct.

message: invalid subtype in a compound type
cause: This subtype is not allowed within the ETYPE specified.
solution: Check the Oracle Spatial documentation for type definitions.

message: not enough sub-elements within a compound ETYPE
cause: The compound type declare more sub-elements than actually defined.
solution: Confirm that the number of sub-elements is consistent with the compound type declaration.

message: disjoint sub-element in a compound polygon
cause: Compound polygon must describe an enclosed area.
solution: Confirm that all sub-elements are connected.

message: no valid ETYPE in the geometry
cause: None of the ETYPEs within the geometry is supported.
solution: Confirm that there is at least one valid ETYPE.

message: layer dimensionality does not match geometry dimensions
cause: The spatial layer has a geometry with a different dimensions than the dimensions specified for the layer.
solution: Make sure that all geometries in a layer have the same dimensions and that they match the dimensions in the SDO_DIM_ARRAY object for the layer in the USER_SDO_GEOM_METADATA view.

message: layer SRID does not match geometry SRID
cause: The spatial layer has a geometry with a different SRID than the SRID specified for the layer.
solution: Make sure that all geometries in a layer have the same SRID and that the SRIDs match the SRID for the layer in the USER_SDO_GEOM_METADATA view.

message: invalid combination of interior exterior rings
cause: In an Oracle Spatial geometry, interior and exterior rings are not used consistently.
solution: Make sure that the interior rings corresponding to an exterior ring follow the exterior ring in the ordinate array.

message: wrong orientation for interior/exterior rings
cause: In an Oracle Spatial geometry, the exterior and/or interior rings are not oriented correctly.
solution: Be sure that the exterior rings are oriented counterclockwise and the interior rings are oriented clockwise.

message: simple polygon type has more than one exterior ring
cause: In a polygon geometry there is more than one exterior ring.
solution: Set the type to be multipolygon if more than one exterior ring is present in the geometry.

message: invalid value for etype in the 4-digit format
cause: A 4-digit etype for a non-polygon type element is used, or the orientation is not a valid orientation for interior/exterior rings of the polygon.
solution: Correct the geometry definition.

message: failure in applying 3D LRS functions
cause: Only non-geodetic 3D line string geometries (made of line segments) are supported for 3D LRS functions.
solution: Check the geometry and element types and the SRID values.

message: invalid position of measure dimension
cause: LRS measure dimension has to be after spatial dimensions. The position has to be either 3rd or 4th in the dim_info_array.
solution: Check the geometry's gtype and its position in the dim_info_array.

message: failure in modifying metadata for a table with spatial index
cause: Modifying the metadata after the index is created will cause an inconsistency between the geometry's gtype and diminfo.
solution: Modify (or Prepare) metadata before creating an index on the SDO_GEOMETRY column.

message: invalid line segment in geodetic data
cause: A geodetic line segment was not less than half of a great circle.
solution: Densify the line by adding points.

message: SDO_MBR not supported for geodetic data
cause: The SDO_MBR functionality is not supported for geodetic data.
solution: Find an alternative function that can be used in this context.

message: the layer is of type [ string ] while geometry inserted has type [ string ]
cause: The layer has a type that is different or inconsistent with the type of the current geometry.
solution: Change the geometry type to agree with the layer type, or change the layer type to agree with the geometry type.

message: invalid type name specified for layer_gtype parameter
cause: An invalid type name is specified for the layer_gtype constraint.
solution: See the Spatial documentation for of valid keywords that can be used in defining a layer_gtype constraint.

message: invalid combination of elements with orientation
cause: An element of the geometry has orientation specified while some other element has no orientation specified (4-digit etype).
solution: Make sure all the polygon elements have orientation specified using the 4-digit etype notation.

message: invalid index for element to be extracted
cause: An invalid (or out of bounds) index was specified for extracting an element from a geometry.
solution: Make sure the parameters to the extract function are in the valid range for the geometry.

message: invalid index for sub-element to be extracted
cause: An invalid (or out of bounds) index was specified for extracting a sub-element from a geometry.
solution: Make sure the parameters to the extract function are in the valid range for the geometry.

message: network not found
cause: The specified network was not found in the network metadata.
solution: Insert the network information in the USER_SDO_NETWORK_METADATA view.

message: table: string not found in network: string
cause: The specified table was not found in the network metadata.
solution: Insert the table information in the USER_SDO_NETWORK_METADATA view.

message: geometry metadata (table: string column: string ) not found in spatial network: string
cause: The specified geometry metadata was not found in the spatial network metadata.
solution: Insert the spatial metadata information in the USER_SDO_NETWORK_METADATA view.

message: inconsistent network metadata: string
cause: There was an inconsistency between the network metadata and the node/link information.
solution: Check the network metadata and the node/link information.

message: error in network schema: string
cause: The network table(s) did not have required column(s)
solution: Check the network schema.

message: error in network manager: [ string ]
cause: There was an internal error in network manager.
solution: Contact Oracle Customer Support for more help.

message: commit/rollback operation error: [ string ]
cause: The index-level changes were not fully incorporated as part of the commit or rollback operation.
solution: Correct the specified error and use the following statement: ALTER INDEX <index-name> PARAMETERS ('index_status=synchronize');

message: sdo_batch_size for array inserts should be in the range [ number , number ]
cause: The specified value for sdo_batch_size was too high or too low.
solution: Change the value to be in the specified range.

message: invalid value for dst_spec parameter
cause: The dst_spec parameter was specified in the wrong format.
solution: Check the documentation for this parameter.

message: unable to compute buffers or intersections in analysis function
cause: There was an internal error in computing the buffers or intersections in the specified spatial analysis function.
solution: Modify the tolerance value in the USER_SDO_GEOM_METADATA view before invoking the spatial analysis function.

message: error in spatial analysis and mining function: [ string ]
cause: There was an internal error in the specified analysis function.
solution: Contact Oracle Customer Support for more help.

message: string
cause: An attempt was made to violate GeoRaster management restrictions.
solution: Check the documentation for more detailed information.

message: null or invalid string parameter
cause: The operation failed because the input parameter was null or invalid.
solution: Correct the parameter and try again.

message: duplicate entry for string in USER_SDO_GEOR_SYSDATA view
cause: The current operation caused a duplicate RASTER_DATA_TABLE and RASTER_ID combination to be inserted into the USER_SDO_GEOR_SYSDATA view.
solution: Ensure that the RASTER_DATA_TABLE and RASTER_ID combination to be inserted into the USER_SDO_GEOR_SYSDATA view is unique.

message: duplicate entry for string in USER_SDO_GEOR_SYSDATA view
cause: The RASTER_DATA_TABLE and RASTER_ID columns contained the same information in two or more rows in the USER_SDO_GEOR_SYSDATA view.
solution: Ensure that the RASTER_DATA_TABLE and RASTER_ID columns in the USER_SDO_GEOR_SYSDATA view contain the correct information, and that the value pair is unique for each row.

message: the rasterType is null or not supported
cause: The specified rasterType was null or not supported.
solution: Check the documentation for the rasterType number and/or formats supported by GeoRaster.

message: invalid rasterDataTable specification: string
cause: Each GeoRaster object must have an associated raster data table whose name is unique among raster data table names in the database. If the GeoRaster object is not empty and not blank, the raster data table must exist, be visible in the current schema, be defined in the same schema as the GeoRaster data table, and be an object table of SDO_RASTER type. However, one or more of these requirements were not met.
solution: Check the rasterDataTable specification and ensure that all relevant raster data table requirements are met.

message: invalid ultCoordinate parameter
cause: The ultCoordinate array parameter had the wrong length or contained an invalid value.
solution: Check the documentation, and make sure the ultCoordinate parameter is correct.

message: null or invalid dimensionSize parameter
cause: The dimensionSize array parameter was null, had the wrong length, or contained an invalid value.
solution: Check the documentation, and make sure the dimensionSize parameter is correct.

message: null or invalid GeoRaster object for output
cause: The GeoRaster object for output was null or invalid.
solution: Make sure the GeoRaster object for output has been initialized properly.

message: invalid storage parameter string
cause: The storage parameter contained an invalid specification.
solution: Check the documentation, and make sure the storage parameter is correct.

message: invalid blockSize storage parameter
cause: The blockSize storage parameter had the wrong length or contained invalid value.
solution: Check the documentation, and make sure the blockSize storage parameter is correct.

message: null or invalid pyramidLevel parameter
cause: The specified pyramidLevel parameter was null or invalid.
solution: Make sure the pyramidLevel parameter specifies a valid pyramid level value for the GeoRaster object.

message: invalid layerNumbers or bandNumbers parameter
cause: The layerNumbers or bandNumbers parameter was invalid.
solution: Check the documentation and make sure the layerNumbers or bandNumbers parameter is valid.

message: subset results in null data set
cause: The intersection of cropArea and source GeoRaster object was null.
solution: Check the documentation, and make sure the cropArea parameter is correct.

message: invalid scale parameter string
cause: The scale parameter contained an invalid specification.
solution: Check the documentation, and make sure the scale parameter is correct.

message: null or invalid resampling parameter
cause: The resampling parameter was null or invalid.
solution: Check the documentation, and make sure the resampling parameter is correct.

message: invalid pyramid parameter
cause: The pyramid parameter was invalid.
solution: Check the documentation, and make sure the pyramid parameter is correct.

message: invalid or out of scope point specification
cause: The point position specified by the <ptGeom, layerNumber> or <rowNumber, colNumber, bandNumber> parameter combination was invalid or out of scope.
solution: Make sure the parameter(s) specify a valid point that is or can be translated into a cell position inside the cell space of the GeoRaster object.

message: invalid geometry parameter
cause: The geometry parameter did not specify a valid single-point geometry.
solution: Specify a valid single-point geometry.

message: null or invalid layerNumber parameter
cause: The layerNumber parameter was null or out of scope.
solution: Specify a valid layerNumber parameter.

message: null or invalid parameter(s) for set functions
cause: A parameter for set metadata operations was null or invalid.
solution: Check the documentation for information about the parameters.

message: cannot perform mosaick operation on the specified table column
cause: An attempt to perform a mosaick operation failed because the GeoRaster objects in the specified table column did not meet necessary conditions.
solution: Check the documentation for SDO_GEOR.Mosaick for details.

message: the SRID of the geometry parameter was not null
cause: The input geometry must be in the GeoRaster cell space, which has a null SRID value.
solution: Make sure the geometry parameter has a null SRID.

message: NULL or invalid cell value
cause: The cell value was NULL or out-of-scope.
solution: Make sure the cell value is not NULL and is in the range as designated by the cellDepth definition of the specified GeoRaster object.

message: invalid model coordinate parameter
cause: The model coordinate array parameter had the wrong length or had null ordinate element(s).
solution: Make sure the model coordinate parameter is valid.

message: invalid cell coordinate parameter
cause: The cell coordinate array parameter had the wrong length or had null ordinate element(s).
solution: Make sure the cell coordinate parameter is valid.

message: the GeoRaster object is not spatially referenced
cause: The GeoRaster object was not spatially referenced.
solution: Make sure the GeoRaster object is spatially referenced.

message: invalid background filling value parameter
cause: The background filling value parameter was invalid either because the array had the wrong size or because some of the element values were invalid.
solution: Make sure the parameter that specifies the background filling value is valid. The size of the array must equal to either 1 (the value is for all bands) or the exact band dimension size. The element values must be valid cell values as determined by the cell depth.

message: invalid window parameter
cause: The specified window parameter was invalid.
solution: Specify a valid window parameter. Check the documentation for details.

message: invalid bitmap mask
cause: The bitmap mask was not a valid 1BIT GeoRaster object, or it had the wrong dimension sizes.
solution: Make sure the bitmap mask is a valid 1BIT GeoRaster object with only one band, and the row and column dimension sizes of the bitmap mask are the same as those of the target GeoRaster object.

message: invalid modelCoordinateLocation
cause: The program [or user] specified a modelCoordinateLocation that is not supported, or the modelCoordinateLocation of the GeoRaster object was wrong.
solution: Set or specify the modelCoordinateLocation to be CENTER (0) or UPPERLEFT (1).

message: invalid xCoefficients or yCoefficients parameter(s)
cause: An attempt to perform a georeference operation failed. Possible reasons include xCoefficients or yCoefficients having the wrong number of coefficients or invalid coefficients.
solution: Check the documentation for supported coefficient specifications.

message: the GeoRaster object has null attribute(s)
cause: The metadata or rasterType of the GeoRaster object was null.
solution: This object may only be used as an output parameter of procedures or functions. It is not valid for other purposes.

message: GeoRaster metadata rasterType error
cause: The rasterType in the metadata of the GeoRaster object was inconsistent with the GeoRaster rasterType attribute.
solution: Make sure the rasterType in the metadata of the GeoRaster object and the GeoRaster rasterType attribute have the same value.

message: NULL or invalid blankCellValue
cause: The blankCellValue element could not be found in the metadata of a blank GeoRaster object, or the specified blankCellValue element value was NULL or invalid.
solution: Call SDO_GEOR.setBlankCellValue to add blankCellValue to the metadata whenever the isBlank element value is TRUE, and make sure that the specified blankCellValue element value is not NULL and is in the range as designated by the cellDepth definition of the GeoRaster object.

message: GeoRaster metadata default RGB error
cause: At least one of the defaultRed, defaultGreen, and defaultBlue values (logical layer numbers) was zero, negative, or out of range.
solution: Check the documentation for details.

message: GeoRaster metadata cellRepresentation error
cause: The cellRepresentation type was not supported.
solution: Check the documentation for supported cellRepresentation types.

message: GeoRaster metadata dimension inconsistent
cause: The specification of dimensions or totalDimensions was inconsistent with rasterType, or vice versa.
solution: Make sure dimension specifications are consistent.

message: GeoRaster metadata dimensionSize error
cause: Either the dimensionSize for each dimension was not specified, or an extraneous dimensionSize was specified.
solution: Add a dimsenionSize for each dimension of the GeoRaster object and delete extra dimensionSize elements.

message: GeoRaster metadata blocking error
cause: Either the wrong block number(s) or block size(s) along dimensions were specified, or the block numbers and sizes when taken together were not consistent.
solution: Check the documentation for details.

message: GeoRaster metadata pyramid type error
cause: The specified pyramid type was not supported.
solution: Check the documentation for supported pyramid types.

message: GeoRaster metadata pyramid maxLevel error
cause: The specified maxLevel exceeded the maximum level allowed by the specified pyramid type.
solution: Check the documentation for supported pyramid types and their total level limitations.

message: GeoRaster metadata compression type error
cause: The specified compression type was not supported.
solution: Check the documentation for supported compression types.

message: GeoRaster metadata SRS error: string
cause: The specified error relates to the polynomialModel element in the Spatial Reference System (SRS) metadata.
solution: Check the documentation and make sure that a valid polynomial model is specified.

message: GeoRaster object not registered: string
cause: There was no sysdata entry for the specified GeoRaster object.
solution: Make sure that a sysdata entry has been inserted for the specified GeoRaster object.

message: null or invalid values in string
cause: There were null or invalid component values in the specified metadata.
solution: Check the documentation and make sure that all the component values are valid.

message: cannot perform mergeLayers operation
cause: The two GeoRaster objects whose layers are to be combined together either had different row or column dimension sizes, or their georeferencing information did not match.
solution: Make sure the objects have the same row and column dimension sizes. If neither is georeferenced, their ULTCoordinate values must be the same. Otherwise, they must be both georeferenced and cover the same area in the model space.

message: NULL or invalid NODATA value or value range
cause: There was invalid NODATA value or value range in the metadata, or the specified NODATA value or value range was invalid.
solution: Make sure the NODATA value or value range is not NULL and is completely contained in the range as designated by the cellDepth definition of the specified GeoRaster object.

message: GeoRaster metadata TRS error
cause: The GeoRaster Temporal Reference System was not supported.
solution: Set isReferenced to FALSE.

message: GeoRaster metadata BRS error
cause: The GeoRaster Band Reference System was not supported.
solution: Set isReferenced to FALSE.

message: GeoRaster metadata BRS error
cause: The GeoRaster spectral extent specification was incorrect.
solution: The MIN value must be less than the MAX value in the spectralExtent element.

message: GeoRaster metadata ULTCoordinate error
cause: The GeoRaster rasterInfo ULTCoordinate was not correct.
solution: Check the documentation for restrictions.

message: GeoRaster metadata layerInfo error
cause: The GeoRaster had more than one layerInfo element, or the layerDimension value was not supported.
solution: The current release only supports one layerInfo element; layer can only be defined along one dimension, and this dimension must be BAND.

message: GeoRaster metadata scaling function error
cause: The scaling function had a zero denominator.
solution: Make sure the scaling function denominator is not zero.

message: GeoRaster metadata BIN function error
cause: The bin function data did not match its type.
solution: For EXPLICIT type, provide a binTableName element; otherwise, provide a binFunctionData element.

message: GeoRaster metadata layer error
cause: Too many subLayers were defined for the GeoRaster object, or layerNumber or layerDimensionOrdinate was not assigned correctly.
solution: The total number of logical layers cannot exceed the total number of physical layers, and each logical layer must be assigned a valid physical layer number following the same order. Check the documentation for more details.

message: GeoRaster metadata is invalid
cause: The GeoRaster metadata was invalid against its XML Schema.
solution: Run the schemaValidate routine to find the errors.

message: GeoRaster metadata TRS error
cause: The beginDateTime value was later than the endDateTime value.
solution: Make sure that the beginDateTime value is not later than the endDateTime value.

message: GeoRaster cell data error: string
cause: There was an error in the original GeoRaster cell data or in the cell data of the pyramids.
solution: If the error is related to the original GeoRaster cell data, the GeoRaster object is invalid and has to be deleted or manually repaired. If the error is related to pyramids, delete the pyramids and regenerate them.

message: bitmap mask cell data error: string
cause: There was an error in the cell data of an original bitmap mask or in the cell data of the pyramids of a bitmap mask.
solution: If the error is related to an original bitmap mask, remove the bitmap mask. If the error is related to the pyramids of a bitmap mask, delete the pyramids and regenerate them.

message: GeoRaster metadata SRS error
cause: The polynomial model did not match the requirements of a rectified GeoRaster object.
solution: Check the documentation for the requirements of the polynomial model for a rectified GeoRaster object, or set isRectified to be false.

message: GeoRaster metadata SRS error
cause: The polynomial model was not an six-parameter transformation, or the six-parameter transformation was not valid.
solution: Check the documentation and make sure the polynomial model is a valid six-parameter affine transformation.

message: GeoRaster metadata SRS error
cause: The referenced GeoRaster object had a zero model space SRID or the specified model space SRID was zero.
solution: Set or specify the model space SRID to be a nonzero number.

message: the interleaving type is not supported
cause: The interleaving type of the GeoRaster object was not supported.
solution: Check the documentation for the interleaving types supported by GeoRaster. Use SDO_GEOR.changeFormatCopy to transform the image to a supported interleaving type.

message: invalid blocking specification
cause: The specified blocking configuration was invalid.
solution: Check the documentation for the blocking specification supported by GeoRaster.

message: error retrieving GeoRaster data: string
cause: An internal error occurred while retrieving GeoRaster data from the database.
solution: Check the error message for details.

message: error loading GeoRaster data: string
cause: An internal error occurred while loading GeoRaster data into the database.
solution: Check the error message for details.

message: null or invalid table or column specification
cause: The specified table or column did not exist, or the column was not a GeoRaster column.
solution: Make sure the specified table exists and the specified column is a GeoRaster column.

message: format not appropriate for specified compression method: string
cause: The operation failed because the GeoRaster object had an inappropriate type or format for the specified compression method. The GeoRaster type or format is not supported for the specified compression.
solution: Check the error message for details. Check the documentation for the appropriate GeoRaster types and formats for each compression method. Use SDO_GEOR.changeFormatCopy to transform the GeoRaster object to an appropriate format, or apply another compression method.

message: unsupported GeoRaster metadata specification: string
cause: The GeoRaster metadata specification is not supported.
solution: Check the documentation for the supported GeoRaster metadata specifications.

message: invalid blockMBR
cause: Invalid blockMBR geometries were stored in the raster data table.
solution: Make sure the blockMBR geometries stored in the raster data table are valid, or call SDO_GEOR.generateBlockMBR() to regenerate the blockMBR geometries.

message: cannot perform updateRaster operation
cause: The data of the source GeoRaster object could not be used to update that of the target GeoRaster object.
solution: Make sure the source and the target GeoRaster objects have the same cell depth, and that both objects are either georeferenced or not georeferenced at all. If both are georeferenced, they should be in the same coordinate system and have the same spatial resolutions.

message: target and source layers or bands mismatched
cause: The number of specified target layers or bands and source layers or bands did not match.
solution: When updating layers or bands of a target GeoRaster object to reflect the associated layers or bands of the source GeoRaster object, specify the same number of layers or bands for both the source and the target objects. Check the documentation for details.

message: unable to determine the owner of string
cause: The owner of the specified raster data table could not be determined.
solution: Make sure the GeoRaster object that refers to the raster data table has been registered by inserting the object into a GeoRaster table.

message: invalid geometry parameter
cause: The geometry parameter did not specify a valid geometry.
solution: Specify a valid 2D or 3D geometry. If the model SRID is null or indicates a 2D coordinate system, the geometry must be 2D. If the model SRID indicates a 3D coordinate system, the geometry must either be a 3D geometry or a 2D geometry that can be converted to 3D with the specified vertical axis (or vertical SRID) and ellipsoidal parameters.

message: invalid rasterSpec parameter
cause: The rasterSpec parameter contained an invalid specification.
solution: Check the documentation and make sure the rasterSpec parameter contains only valid keywords and values.

message: invalid rasterDataTable name: string
cause: The rasterDataTable name was not a valid nonquoted identifier, it contained a period separator, or not all of the alphanumeric characters were uppercase.
solution: Ensure that the table name is a valid nonquoted identifier without any period separators, and that all the alphanumeric characters are uppercase.

message: invalid GeoRaster object for output
cause: The output GeoRaster object had the same RASTER_DATA_TABLE and RASTER_ID combination as that of an input GeoRaster object.
solution: Ensure that the output GeoRaster object is different from any of the input GeoRaster objects.

message: invalid or out of scope point specification
cause: The point position specified by the point geometry parameter or the rowNumber/colNumber parameter combination was null or out of scope.
solution: Ensure that the parameters specify a valid point that translates or can be translated into a cell position inside the cell space of the GeoRaster object.

message: invalid GCP georeferencing specification: string
cause: The specified functional fitting method was not supported, the number of GCPs was insufficient, some GCPs were invalid, or the distribution of the GCPs led to no solution or an unstable solution.
solution: Check the GeoRaster documentation for the supported functional fitting methods and the requirements of GCPs.

message: the target SRID is the same as the source GeoRaster object's SRID
cause: The target SRID was not different from the source GeoRaster object's SRID.
solution: Specify a different valid SRID for the target GeoRaster object.
