message: Smart I/O failed because of an internal error when determining the time zone file version. Error code " string "
cause: An internal error caused a smart I/O operation to fail.
solution: Report the problem to Oracle Support Services along with the process trace file and alert log.

message: The value of string is not valid for parameter string
cause: Incorrect value is specified for an internal parameter.
solution: This parameter should only be set by Oracle Support Services. Check the additional diagnostic information in the trace file and contact Oracle Support Services for recommendations on setting this parameter.

message: Cell automation SQL action failed
cause: Cell automation manager or worker process failed to execute SQL action through OCI recursive call.
solution: Check the alert log and process trace file for additional information. Contact Oracle Support Services if the errors specified in the trace file cannot be corrected.

message: Smart I/O failed because the number of reconnects to the cell " string " exceeded the maximum allowed " string ".
cause: The number of reconnects to a cell exceeded the maximum allowed. This problem indicates a possible network problem or a software problem on the cell.
solution: If the cellsrv is being restarted repeatedly, in a short interval, check the system load. The problem may be corrected by rebooting the cell. If the system is not overloaded, the repeated restarts are likely due to software problem. Report the problem to Oracle Support Services along with alert log and trace files. If the cellsrv is not restarting, the problem may be in the IB network. Check the network between the host and all the cells.

message: Exadata configuration failed.
cause: One or both of the files, cellinit.ora and cellip.ora, were either invalid or missing.
solution: Check if the files, cellinit.ora and cellip.ora, are both present. They can be found in the $OSSCONF directory. If both are present, check if their contents are valid and correct. If the files are invalid or missing, produce files with valid information in the $OSSCONF directory. For information on how to set up these files, see the Exadata Users Guide.

message: Exadata error: string ( string )
cause: The cause of this error is dependent on the context in which this error is reported.
solution: See the primary error reported with this error.

message: An invalid value was specified for the parameter string .
cause: An invalid value was specified for a parameter.
solution: Check the additional diagnostic information in the trace file and contact Oracle Support Services if further help is required.

message: the password will expire within string days
cause: The user's account is about to about to expire and the password needs to be changed
solution: change the password or contact the DBA

message: password verification for the specified password failed
cause: The new password did not meet the necessary complexity specifications and the password_verify_function failed
solution: Enter a different password. Contact the DBA to know the rules for choosing the new password

message: invalid argument for function specified in PASSWORD_VERIFY_FUNCTION string
cause: The password verification function does not have the required number and type of input/output arguments and/or the return argument
solution: Check the manual to find out the format of the password verification function

message: invalid logon flags
cause: The flags are not properly set or conflicting flags are set in making calls
solution: Call the function with appropriate flags set.

message: conflicting values for parameters string and string
cause: The parameters PASSWORD_REUSE_TIME and PASSWORD_REUSE_MAX cannot both be set. One parameter should be unlimited while other is set
solution: Set one value to UNLIMITED explicitly

message: the password cannot be reused
cause: The password cannot be reused for the specified number of days or for the specified nunmber of password changes
solution: Try the password that you have not used for the specified number of days or the specified number of password changes Refer to the password parameters in the CREATE PROFILE statement

message: invalid old password
cause: old password supplied is wrong; Hence user cannot be authenticated using old password
solution: Supply the correct old password for authentication

message: connection as SYS should be as SYSDBA or SYSOPER
cause: connect SYS/<password> is no longer a valid syntax
solution: Try connect SYS/<password> as SYSDBA or connect SYS/<password> as SYSOPER

message: cannot expire external or global accounts
cause: If a user account is created as IDENTIFIED EXTERNALLY, or IDENTIFIED GLOBALLY, this account cannot be expired
solution: Try to expire the password of the user that has database password

message: the account will expire soon; change your password now
cause: The user's account is marked for expiry; the expiry period is unlimited.
solution: Change the password or contact the DBA.

message: the password has expired
cause: The password of the proxy user expired.
solution: Connect directly as proxy user to change the password or contact the DBA.

message: Account unlock attempted on read-only database but a conflicting account lockout on the primary exists
cause: An attempt to unlock an account on a read-only database was prevented, because the account was previously marked as locked on the primary database. All attempts to unlock the account on the read-only database will be prevented as long as the overriding "account locked" condition exists at the primary database.
solution: If this database is part of a Data Guard configuration, perform the account unlock action on the primary database. If this database is read-only, then set the database to read/write and perform the account unlock action.

message: IDENTIFIED GLOBALLY already specified
cause: The IDENTIFIED GLOBALLY clause was specified twice.
solution: Use only one IDENTIFIED GLOBALLY clause.

message: cannot grant global roles
cause: The role granted was IDENTIFIED GLOBALLY. Global roles can only be granted via a central authority for the domain.
solution: Use ALTER ROLE to change the type of role (from IDENTIFIED GLOBALLY to other, such as IDENTIFIED BY password), or allocate it to a global user via the central authority.

message: cannot grant external roles to global user or role
cause: The role granted was IDENTIFIED EXTERNALLY. External roles cannot be granted to global users, to global roles or to any other roles.
solution: Use ALTER ROLE to change the type of the role being granted (from IDENTIFIED EXTERNALLY to other, such as NOT IDENTIFIED) or use ALTER USER to change the type of the user that is the grantee.

message: must revoke grants of this role to other user(s) first
cause: The role altered to IDENTIFIED GLOBALLY was granted to one or more other users and/or roles. Global roles cannot be granted to any user or role.
solution: Use REVOKE to revoke the role from other users or roles first.

message: must revoke grants of external roles to this role/user
cause: The user or role altered to IDENTIFIED GLOBALLY has external roles directly granted - these must be revoked, since external roles cannot be granted to global users or roles.
solution: Use REVOKE to revoke the external roles from the user or role to be ALTERed.

message: missing or null external name
cause: The IDENTIFIED EXTERNALLY AS or IDENTIFIED GLOBALLY AS clause was specified with a valid external name.
solution: Provide a valid external name.

message: user with same external name already exists
cause: The external name specified for the user being created or altered already exists for another user.
solution: External names must be unique among users. Specify another.

message: privileged database links may be used by global users
cause: Only users IDENTIFIED GLOBALLY may use a privileged database link.
solution: Either change the user to a global user or try to use a different database link.

message: could not authenticate remote server
cause: During the course of opening a privileged database link, the remote server was not securely identified using the network security service. Additional errors should follow.
solution: Consult the network security service documentation on how to properly configure the remote server.

message: could not authorize remote server for user string
cause: During the course of opening a privileged database link, the remote server was found to lack the necessary authorizations to connect as the current global user. This may be because the server was not authorized by the network security service. Or it may be because the local server is restricting access by the remote server using the DBMS_SECURITY_DOMAINS_ADMIN package.
solution: Grant the remote server the proper authorization to connect as the given global user, and check that the local server is not restricting access.

message: Server encountered problems accessing LDAP directory service
cause: Unable to access LDAP directory service
solution: Please contact your system administrator

message: maximum of string enabled roles exceeded
cause: The user attempted to enable too many roles.
solution: Enable fewer roles.

message: Your password has expired and the database is set to read-only
cause: Your password expired and needs to be changed before your login request can be processed. Because the database is currently open in read-only mode, the password change operation cannot be performed on this database.
solution: Log in to the primary database to change your password, then retry your login request at the standby database.

message: Cannot Get Session Key for Authentication
cause: Client and server cannot negotiate shared secret during logon
solution: User should not see this error. Please contact your system administrator

message: Cannot Get Session Key for RACF Authentication
cause: Client and server cannot negotiate shared secret during logon
solution: User should not see this error. Please contact your system administrator

message: disallow O2LOGON

solution: None

message: cannot validate Kerberos service ticket
cause: The Kerberos service ticket provided was invalid or expired
solution: Provide a valid, unexpired service ticket.

message: No matching authentication protocol
cause: No acceptible authentication protocol for both client and server
solution: Administrator should set SQLNET_ALLOWED_LOGON_VERSION parameter on both client and servers to values that matches the minimum version supported in the system.

message: Authentication protocol internal error
cause: Authentication protocol failed with an internal error
solution: None

message: Server authentication failed
cause: Server failed to authenticate itself to the client
solution: Confirm that the server is a valid database server.

message: invalid bind credentials for DB-OID connection
cause: The Database password stored in the wallet did not match the one in OID .
solution: Use DBCA to reset the database password so that it is the same in database wallet and in OID.

message: unsupported directory type
cause: The database tried to work with a directory which is not OID.
solution: Enterprise User Security works only with Oracle Internet Directory. Update the ldap.ora file to reflect an appropriate OID.

message: SSL authentication between database and OID failed
cause: Server failed to authenticate itself to the Directory.
solution: Make sure the sqlnet.ora used is pointing to the wallet with the right certificate.

message: Password change for SYS disallowed
cause: REMOTE_LOGIN_PASSWORDFILE is set to SHARED, prohibiting SYS password changes.
solution: Change setting of REMOTE_LOGIN_PASSWORDFILE to EXCLUSIVE or NONE.

message: database is not a member of any enterprise domain in OID
cause: An enterprise user login was attempted on a database that is not a member of any enterprise domain in OID.
solution: An administrator should put the database into an enterprise domain in OID, and then the user should reconnect.

message: database is a member of multiple enterprise domains in OID
cause: An enterprise user login was attempted on a database that is a member of multiple enterprise domains in OID.
solution: An administrator should put the database into only one enterprise domain in OID, and then the user should reconnect.

message: the password has expired
cause: The enterprise user's password has expired and the password needs to be changed.
solution: change the password in the directory or contact the directory administrator.

message: specified user or role cannot be dropped
cause: The specified user or role was reserved and cannot be dropped.
solution: None

message: the account is locked
cause: The enterprise user has consecutively entered the wrong password for maximum number of times specified in the realm's password policy profile.
solution: Contact the directory administrator.

message: the account is disabled
cause: The enterprise user's account in the directory has been disabled.
solution: Contact the directory administrator.

message: the account is inactive
cause: The enterprise user's account in the directory is currently not active.
solution: Contact the directory administrator.

message: the password has expired. string Grace logins are left
cause: The enterprise user's password has expired. The user is able to login because he has gracelogins left.
solution: change the password in the directory or contact the directory administrator.

message: the password will expire within string days
cause: The enterprise user's password is about to expire.
solution: Change the password in the directory or contact the directory administrator.

message: Writing audit records to Windows Event Log failed
cause: Unable to write an audit entry to the Windows event log used as the audit trail.
solution: Check the error number for a possible operating system error. If there is no error, contact Oracle Support Services.

message: name of the password file could not be constructed
cause: Possibly environment variable ORACLE_SID was not set.
solution: Set value for the ORACLE_SID environment variable.

message: Cross-instance call failed
cause: An attempt to inform other Oracle RAC instances of a security event failed.

message: A data redaction policy already exists on this column.
cause: A data redaction policy was already in existence on this column.
solution: Specify a colunm which does not already have a redaction policy defined on it, or use DBMS_REDACT.ALTER_POLICY to alter the existing redaction policy for this column.

message: This object cannot have a data redaction policy defined on it.
cause: An attempt was made to define a data redaction policy on an object other than a table or view. Note that a data redaction policy cannot be defined on an editioned view, or on specialized tables created internally by the server in conjunction with various features such as materialized view.
solution: Specify the name of a table or view.

message: The policy expression is too long.
cause: The policy expression was longer than 4000 characters.
solution: Specify a policy expression of at most 4000 characters.

message: The policy expression is empty.
cause: The EXPRESSION parameter to DBMS_REDACT.ADD_POLICY was empty.
solution: A nonempty policy expression must be specified in the EXPRESSION parameter to DBMS_REDACT.ADD_POLICY.

message: The redaction function is not valid.
cause: The FUNCTION_TYPE parameter to DBMS_REDACT.ADD_POLICY was invalid.
solution: Specify the FUNCTION_TYPE parameter to DBMS_REDACT.ADD_POLICY as one of the following: DBMS_REDACT.NONE, DBMS_REDACT.FULL, DBMS_REDACT.RANDOM, DBMS_REDACT.PARTIAL, DBMS_REDACT.REGEXP, or NULL. Note that only full redaction may be applied to columns of type BLOB, CLOB, or NCLOB.

message: invalid column " string "
cause: An invalid column was specified in the COLUMN_NAME parameter.
solution: Check the columns in the object and specify the right column name.

message: missing or invalid column name
cause: A valid column name was not specified in the COLUMN_NAME parameter when a column name was required. Note that when using DBMS_REDACT.ALTER_POLICY, the default action is DBMS_REDACT.ADD_COLUMN
solution: Specify the name of a column.

message: The object " string " does not have a data redaction policy.
cause: The specified object did not have a data redaction policy defined on it.
solution: Specify the name of an object which has a data redaction policy, or use DBMS_REDACT.ADD_POLICY to add a data redaction policy.

message: A data redaction policy already exists on this object.
cause: A data redaction policy was already in existence on this object.
solution: Specify a table or view which does not already have a redaction policy defined on it, or use DBMS_REDACT.ALTER_POLICY to alter the existing redaction policy for this object.

message: The column " string " does not have a data redaction policy.
cause: The specified column did not have a data redaction policy defined on it.
solution: Specify the name of a column which has a data redaction policy.

message: The action is not valid.
cause: The ACTION parameter to DBMS_REDACT.ALTER_POLICY was invalid.
solution: Specify the ACTION parameter to DBMS_REDACT.ALTER_POLICY as one of the following values: DBMS_REDACT.MODIFY_EXPRESSION, DBMS_REDACT.MODIFY_COLUMN, DBMS_REDACT.ADD_COLUMN, or DBMS_REDACT.DROP_COLUMN.

message: The specified policy name is incorrect.
cause: The POLICY_NAME parameter was incorrect.
solution: Specify the POLICY_NAME parameter with the name of the redaction policy currently defined on the object.

message: The column " string " has an unsupported data type.
cause: The column had a data type which is not supported by data redaction. The supported data types are CHAR, NCHAR, VARCHAR2, NVARCHAR2, NUMBER types, BINARY_FLOAT, BINARY_DOUBLE, DATE, and TIMESTAMP. For regular expression-based redaction, with FUNCTION_TYPE of DBMS_REDACT.REGEXP, only the string data types (VARCHAR2, NVARCHAR2, CHAR, and NCHAR) are supported by data redaction. Virtual columns are not supported by data redaction.
solution: Specify the name of a column which has a supported data type.

message: The " string " field of the redaction parameters is not valid.
cause: The redaction parameters specified had one or more fields that were invalid.
solution: Specify the redaction parameters according to Oracle documentation.

message: The policy expression has unsupported functions.
cause: The EXPRESSION parameter had unsupported functions.
solution: Specify only valid functions for the EXPRESSION parameter.

message: An attribute was not specified for SYS_SESSION_ROLES.
cause: An attribute was not specified for the SYS_SESSION_ROLES namespace in the policy expression.
solution: Specify an attribute for SYS_SESSION_ROLES in the policy expression.

message: The attribute specified ( string ) exceeds the maximum length.
cause: The attribute specified in the policy expression for the SYS_SESSION_ROLES namespace exceeded the maximum length.
solution: Change the policy expression to use a valid attribute for SYS_SESSION_ROLES namespace.

message: A regular expression parameter is missing or invalid.
cause: The FUNCTION_TYPE was DBMS_REDACT.REGEXP, but one or more of the regular expression parameters were missing or invalid, the REGEXP_PATTERN failed to compile properly, or the regular expression replacement operation failed.
solution: Specify the regular expression parameters according to Oracle documentation. At a minimum, the REGEXP_PATTERN and the REGEXP_REPLACE_STRING must be specified. Ensure that the REGEXP_PATTERN can compile properly as a regular expression, for example by testing it with REGEXP_REPLACE in a SQL query against a column containing some of the data to be redacted.

message: The policy was already enabled.
cause: The redaction policy specified has already been enabled.
solution: Only disabled redaction policies can be enabled.

message: The policy was already disabled.
cause: The redaction policy specified has already been disabled.
solution: Only enabled redaction policies can be disabled.

message: Insufficient privileges - the command references a redacted object.
cause: The command referenced a redacted column in an object protected by a data redaction policy.
solution: If possible, modify the command to avoid referencing any redacted columns. Otherwise, drop the data redaction policies that protect the referenced tables and views, or ensure that the user issuing the command has the EXEMPT REDACTION POLICY system privilege, then retry the operation. The EXEMPT REDACTION POLICY system privilege is required for creating or refreshing a materialized view when the materialized view is based on an object protected by a data redaction policy. The EXEMPT REDACTION POLICY system privilege is required for performing a data pump schema-level export including any object protected by a data redaction policy. All data redaction policies are listed in the REDACTION_COLUMNS catalog view.

message: The parameter string is invalid.
cause: The specified parameter was either empty or too long.
solution: Specify a parameter of correct length. See the documentation for length requirements.

message: A redacted column was referenced in a virtual column expression.
cause: This redacted column was referenced in a virtual column expression.
solution: Ensure the column expression definition for any virtual column does not refer to any redacted columns. To check for columns with redaction policies, use the REDACTION_COLUMNS catalog view which lists all data redaction policies.

message: The input and output lengths of the redaction do not match.
cause: As specified, the redaction parameters produced an output with a length different to that of the input.
solution: Use regular expression redaction instead of partial redaction.

message: The evaluation of the policy expression failed. string
cause: The evaluation of the policy expression failed.
solution: Specify a valid policy expression.

message: policy function schema string is invalid
cause: The schema was dropped after the policy associated with the function had been added to the object.
solution: Drop the policy and re-create it with a policy function owned by a valid user. Or re-create the user and the policy function under the new user.

message: policy already exists
cause: A policy with the same name for the same object already exists.
solution: Check if the policy has already been added or use a different policy name.

message: policy does not exist
cause: Try to drop/enable/refresh a non-existent policy.
solution: Correct the policy name argument.

message: adding a policy to an object owned by SYS is not allowed
cause: Try to add a policy to a table or a view owned by SYS.
solution: You can not perform this operation.

message: input value for string is not valid
cause: Input value for the argument is not valid
solution: specify a valid argument value.

message: cannot create security relevant column policy in an object view
cause: Security relevant column argument is not null in policy creation for an object view
solution: None

message: input value for argument # string is not valid
cause: Input values for the argument is missing or invalid.
solution: Correct the input values.

message: policy was disabled
cause: Try to flush a disabled policy.
solution: If the policy is supposed to be enforced, it must be enabled.

message: circular security policies detected
cause: Policies for the same object reference each other.
solution: Drop the policies

message: the number of related policies has exceeded the limit of 16
cause: Too many policies are involved in the same objects.
solution: Drop one or more policies. Or combine a few of them into one.

message: policy function or package string . string has error
cause: The policy function may have been dropped, or is no longer valid.
solution: Check the status of the function and correct the problem. Or re-create the policy with a valid function.

message: insufficient privilege to evaluate policy predicate
cause: Predicate has a subquery which contains objects that the owner of policy function does not have privilege to access.
solution: Grant appropriate privileges to the policy function owner.

message: failed to execute policy function
cause: The policy function has one or more error during execution.
solution: Check the trace file and correct the errors.

message: policy predicate has error
cause: Policy function generates invalid predicate.
solution: Review the trace file for detailed error information.

message: policy with check option violation
cause: Policy predicate was evaluated to FALSE with the updated values.
solution: None

message: insufficient privileges to do direct path access
cause: Users with insufficient privileges attempting to do direct path access of tables with fine grain access control policies.
solution: Ask the database administrator to do the operation. Note that users can work with security administrator to temporarily drop/disable the policies at time of export, import, or load, but this has security implication, and thus access of the database must be controlled carefully.

message: integrity constraint violated - parent record not found
cause: try to update/insert a child record with new foreign key values, but the corresponding parent row is not visible because of fine-grained security in the parent.
solution: make sure that the updated foreign key values must also visible in the parent

message: policy group already exists
cause: try to create a policy group that already exists
solution: None

message: policy group does not exist
cause: try to drop a policy group that does not exist
solution: None

message: driving context already exists
cause: try to create a driving context that already exists
solution: None

message: driving context does not exist
cause: try to drop a driving context that does not exist
solution: None

message: can not update SYS_DEFAULT policy group
cause: An attempt was made to execute either DBMS_RLS.CREATE_POLICY_GROUP or DBMS_RLS.DELETE_POLICY_GROUP using SYS_DEFAULT as the policy group name.
solution: Do not attempt to CREATE or DELETE the SYS_DEFAULT policy group. This action is not permitted.

message: Driving context ' string , string ' contains invalid group ' string '
cause: A previous call to DBMS_SESSION.SET_CONTEXT specified an invalid policy group.
solution: Ensure that a valid policy group is passed to DBMS_SESSION.SET_CONTEXT when initializing a policy driving context.

message: Column string in sec_relevant_cols cannot be of an object data type
cause: A column specified in sec_relevant_cols was of an object data type.
solution: Ensure that none of the columns specified in sec_relevant_cols is of an object data type or XMLType.

message: The MERGE INTO syntax does not support the security policy.
cause: The MERGE INTO syntax did not support a security policy on the destination table, because the policy's statement_types did not include each of INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE.
solution: If you do not have the privilege to modify the security policy, then instead of MERGE INTO, use the INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE DML statements on the table that has a security policy defined on it. If you have the privilege to modify the security policy, then redefine it in such a way that statement_types includes all of the DML statement types (INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE).

message: object cannot have fine-grained access control policy
cause: Only tables, views, or synonyms of tables or views may have VPD policies
solution: None

message: Invalid FGA audit Handler
cause: An invalid audit handler was specified.
solution: Specify a valid audit handler.

message: Error in Policy Predicate
cause: An invalid policy predicate was specified.
solution: Please specify a valide policy Predicate for the FGA policy

message: Maximum allowed Fine Grain Audit Policies Exceeded
cause: A maximum of 256 policies can be enabled on an object
solution: Drop or disable an existing policy before creating more

message: Invalid column specified
cause: Column name specified during policy creation is invalid
solution: Please specify a valid column name. Object columns are not supported

message: error in creating audit index file
cause: ORACLE was not able to create the file being used to hold audit file names.
solution: Examine the directory pointed to by the initialization parameter "audit_file_dest." Make sure that all of the following is true: 1. The directory exists. 2. The name indeed points to a directory and not a file. 3. The directory is accessible and writable to the ORACLE user.

message: error in accessing audit index file
cause: ORACLE was not able to access the file being used to hold audit file names.
solution: Make sure the file exists in the directory pointed to by the initialization parameter "audit_file_dest" and is readable by the ORACLE user.

message: Invalid argument passed to FGA ADD_POLICY procedure
cause: Invalid input argument was specified for FGA ADD_POLICY procedure.
solution: Specify correct type and number of arguments to FGA ADD_POLICY procedure.

message: Failed to execute fine-grained audit handler
cause: An error was encountered while executing fine-grained audit handler.
solution: Refer to the trace file for details.

message: proxy not authorized to connect as client
cause: A proxy user attempted to connect as a client, but the proxy was not authorized to act on behalf of the client.
solution: Grant the proxy user permission to perform actions on behalf of the client by using the ALTER USER ... GRANT CONNECT command.

message: more than one user name specified for command
cause: More than one user name was specified for an ALTER USER command.
solution: Try the command again with only one user name.

message: proxy user ' string ' may not specify initial role ' string ' on behalf of client ' string '
cause: A proxy user attempted to specify an initial role for a client, but the client does not possess the role.
solution: Change the proxy user so that it does not specify the role or grant the role to the client.

message: Invalid client initial role specified: ' string '
cause: A role specified by a proxy user as an initial role to be activated upon connecting on behalf of a client is invalid.
solution: Connect again as the client specifying a valid role.

message: Proxy user may not act as client ' string '
cause: A proxy user may not assume the identity of a privileged user in order to limit the privileges that a proxy may possess.
solution: Execute the statement again specify a client other than a privileged user.

message: user ' string ' specified as a proxy is actually a role
cause: A user specified in an AUDIT <operation> BY <proxy> ON BEHALF OF <client> is actually a role.
solution: Execute the statement again with a valid proxy user.

message: Proxy user ' string ' not authorized to set role ' string ' for client ' string '
cause: A proxy user has not been granted the right to use a role on behalf of a client.
solution: Execute the command ALTER USER <client> GRANT CONNECT THROUGH PROXY <proxy> to grant the needed role.

message: Proxy user ' string ' forbidden to set role ' string ' for client ' string '
cause: A proxy user was forbidden to use a role on behalf of a client through the command ALTER USER <client> GRANT CONNECT THROUGH <proxy> WITH ALL ROLES EXCEPT <role>
solution: Execute the command ALTER USER <client> GRANT CONNECT THROUGH PROXY <proxy> to grant the needed role.

message: GRANT already specified
cause: The GRANT clause was specified twice.
solution: Use only one GRANT clause.

message: REVOKE already specified
cause: The REVOKE clause was specified twice.
solution: Use only one REVOKE clause.

message: proxy ' string ' may not specify password-protected role ' string ' for client ' string '
cause: A proxy user attempted to activate a role on behalf of a client which has a password associated with it. Since the proxy does not have a password, this activation cannot be allowed.
solution: Attempt to activate a different role or change the role administratively so that there is no password.

message: duplicate rolename in list
cause: The name of a role was specified more than once in a list.
solution: Repeat the command specifying the role once.

message: attempted to grant password-protected role
cause: An ALTER USER ... GRANT CONNECT command was attempted specifying a role that is protected by a password as a role which the proxy may execute on behalf of a client.
solution: Either specify a role that does not have a password or alter the role so that a password is not required.

message: unsupported certificate type
cause: The type of certificate from which the server is to extract the credentials of the client is not supported.
solution: Specify a supported type.

message: unsupported certificate version
cause: The version of the certificate from which the server is to extract the credentials of the client is not supported.
solution: Specify a supported version.

message: unsupported Kerberos version
cause: the version the Kerberos ticket which the server is to use to validate the identity of the client is not supported.
solution: Specify a supported version.

message: distinguished name not provided by proxy
cause: A client user is to be identified using a distinguished name, but none was provided by the proxy user.
solution: Provide a distinguished name.

message: certificate not provided by proxy
cause: A client user is to be identified using a certificate but none was provided by the proxy user.
solution: Provide a certificate.

message: Kerberos ticket not provided by proxy
cause: A client user is to be authenticated using a Kerberos ticket but none was provided by the proxy user.
solution: Provide a Kerberos ticket.

message: incorrect certificate type
cause: the type of certificate provided by the proxy user to identify a client user does not match the type that is required.
solution: Provide a certificate of the correct type.

message: incorrect certificate version
cause: the version of certificate provided by the proxy user to identify a client user does not match the version that is required.
solution: Provide a certificate of the correct version.

message: incorrect Kerberos ticket version
cause: the version of Kerberos ticket provided by the proxy user to authenticate a client user does not match the version that is required.
solution: Provide a Kerberos ticket of the correct version.

message: password not provided by proxy
cause: A client user is to be authenticated using a database password but none was provided by the proxy user.
solution: Provide a password.

message: client user name not provided by proxy
cause: No user name was provided by the proxy user for the client user.
solution: Either specify a client database user name, a distinguished name or an X.509 certificate.

message: multiple authentication methods provided by proxy
cause: More than one authentication method was specified by the proxy user for the client user.
solution: Specify only one of the following: a client database user name, a distinguished name or an X.509 certificate.

message: proxy ' string ' failed to enable one or more of the specified initial roles for client ' string '
cause: Attempt to enable specified initial roles after logon resulted in failure.
solution: Check that the initial roles are valid, granted to client, and not password protected.

message: cannot acquire Kerberos service ticket for client
cause: An attempt to use a Kerberos forwardable ticket granting ticket to obtain a Kerberos service ticket failed.
solution: Check that the Kerberos forwardable ticket granting ticket belongs to the client, is valid, and that the key distribution center is available.

message: proper authentication not provided by proxy
cause: A client user must be authenticated but no authentication credentials were provided by the proxy user.
solution: Provide some form of authentication credentials.

message: global user cannot have proxy permissions managed in the directory
cause: The client name specified was a global user.
solution: Use ALTER USER to change the type of user (from IDENTIFIED GLOBALLY to something else, such as IDENTIFIED BY password or IDENTIFIED EXTERNALLY).

message: IDENTIFIED USING already specified
cause: The IDENTIFIED USING clause was specified twice.
solution: Use only one IDENTIFIED USING clause.

message: REPLACE not specified
cause: User is changing password but password verification function is turned on and the original password is not specified and the user does not have the alter user system privilege.
solution: Supply the original password.

message: first login requires password change
cause: This user was globally authenticated. Password policy settings in Oracle Internet Directory (OID) requires the password to be changed for the first connection. Further connections to the database will be denied if the password in OID is not changed.
solution: Connect to the OID to change the password.

message: no data passed to obfuscation toolkit
cause: A NULL value was passed to a function or procedure.
solution: Make sure that the data passed is not empty.

message: invalid input length for obfuscation toolkit
cause: Length of data submitted for encryption or decryption is not a multiple of 8 bytes.
solution: Make sure that the length of the data to be encrypted or decrypted is a multiple of 8 bytes.

message: double encryption not supported
cause: The obfuscation toolkit does not support the encryption of already-encrypted data.
solution: Do not attempt to encrypt already-encrypted data.

message: key length too short
cause: The key specified is too short for the algorithm. DES requires a key of at least 8 bytes. Triple DES requires a key of least 16 bytes in two-key mode and 24 bytes in three-key mode.
solution: Specify a longer key.

message: algorithm not available
cause: The encryption algorithm desired is not available.
solution: Run the installer to install the needed algorithm in Oracle Advanced Security.

message: invalid Triple DES mode
cause: An unknown value was specified for the mode in which triple DES encryption is to run.
solution: Specify a valid value. See the package declaration for a list of valid values.

message: seed length too short
cause: The seed specified for the key generation routine must be at least 80 characters.
solution: Specify a longer seed.

message: no seed provided
cause: A NULL value was passed in as the seed to be used in generating a key.
solution: Provide a non-NULL value for the seed.

message: no key provided
cause: A NULL value was passed in as an encryption or decryption key.
solution: Provide a non-NULL value for the key.

message: CURRENT_USER can not be used in PLSQL Definer's Right procedure.
cause: An attempt to retrieve CURRENT_USER using SYS_CONTEXT PLSQL interface.
solution: Use a SQL statement to query CURRENT_USER inside a DR procedure.

message: global_context_pool_size has invalid value.
cause: Parameter global_context_pool_size has a value less than the minimum required value (10K).
solution: Please specify a value for the init.ora parameter global_context_pool_size which is atleast 10k.

message: Insufficient memory in global context pool
cause: Allocations for the global context heap exceeded the value set in init.ora.
solution: Increase the value of global_context_pool_size parameter in init.ora or clear usused global context.

message: Client identifier is too long
cause: The length of the client identifier is longer than 64
solution: Set a client identifier whose length is less than 64.

message: NameSpace beginning with 'sys_' is not allowed
cause: Namespace beginning with 'sys_' is not allowed.
solution: Use a namespace that does not begin with 'sys_'.

message: Invalid NameSpace Value
cause: Context NameSpace conflicts with reserved key words or a secure Namespace is not allowed for this type of Application Context.
solution: Use a valid namespace.

message: Exceeded the maximum allowed size for Context information in a session
cause: The maximum size specified by the _session_context_size init.ora parameter was exceeded.
solution: Please change the value for _session_context_size in the init.ora file.

message: Malformed user nickname for password authenticated global user.
cause: An attempt to login as password-auuthenticated global user with a malformed user nickname.
solution: Make sure the nickname is valid and re-login.

message: No permission to read user entry in LDAP directory service.
cause: ORACLE server does not have read permission on user nickname's X.500 user entry.
solution: Make sure ORACLE server is using right SSL credentials to connect to LDAP directory services. Make sure permissions for LDAP user entries are right.

message: Domain policy restricts password based GLOBAL user authentication.
cause: Domain policy does not allow password-authenticated GLOBAL users.
solution: Make sure ORACLE server is using right SSL credentials to connect to LDAP directory services. Make sure orclDBAuthTypes attributes within Oracle enterprise domain object is either set to PWD or ALL.

message: No mapping for user nickname to LDAP distinguished name exists.
cause: ORACLE server cannot map the given user nickname to LDAP distinguished name.
solution: Make sure user entries in LDAP are correctly provisioned with correct user nickname attribute values.

message: No ORACLE password attribute corresponding to user nickname exists.
cause: LDAP user entry corresponding to user nickname does not have a ORACLE password attribute or the attribute is not initialized.
solution: Make sure user entries in LDAP are correctly provisioned with correct ORACLE password attribute values.

message: Multiple mappings for user nickname to LDAP distinguished name exist.
cause: The given user nickname maps to more than one LDAP distinguished name.
solution: Make sure user nickname is unique within the enterprise.

message: Invalid ORACLE password attribute.
cause: The ORACLE password attribute of a user entry has an invalid format.
solution: Make sure ORACLE password attribute value is RFC-2307 compliant.

message: LDAP search, while authenticating global user with passwords, failed.
cause: The LDAP search for finding the appropriate user entry and ORACLE password failed.
solution: Make sure LDAP directory service is up and running.

message: No domain policy registered for password based GLOBAL users.
cause: No policy about password authenticated GLOBAL users has been registered.
solution: Add attribute orclDBAuthTypes to the database server's Enterprise domain.

message: Error reading ldap_directory_access init parameter.
cause: ldap_directory_access parameter is not specified corrrectly.
solution: Make sure spfile.ora has ldap_directory_access set correctly. Possible correct values are PASSWORD, SSL and NONE.

message: Multiple entries for ORACLE database password exist.
cause: The ORACLE password attribute of a user entry has multiple entries of ORACLE database password.
solution: Make sure ORACLE password attribute has one entry for ORACLE Database password.

message: Global application context is not updated on one or more Oracle RAC instances
cause: While updating global application context across Oracle RAC instances, the background process errored out or the timeout expired due to some failure.
solution: Ensure every instance in Oracle RAC is operational and retry the operation.

message: Multiple entries found for the same Kerberos Principal Name
cause: Multiple user entries has been configured with the same krbPrincipalName
solution: Modify enterprise user's entry to assign its Kerberos principal name Make sure the user entries in LDAP are provisioned correctly.

message: No Kerberos Principal Value found.
cause: Oracle server fails to get value of krbPrincipalName attribute
solution: Make sure user entries are correctly provisioned with correct Kerberos principal value

message: No Domain Policy registered for Kerberos based authentication
cause: The enterprise domain entry is not configured for Kerberos based global authentication.
solution: Modify orclDBAuthType of the database server's enterprise domain entry and assign it "ALL" or "KRB5"

message: No matched Kerberos Principal found in any user entry
cause: Oracle server fails to find the principal in the user search base
solution: Make sure the user search base is correct. Use ESM to configure the enterprise user its Kerberos principal name

message: No permission to read user entry in LDAP directory service.
cause: ORACLE server does not have read permission on user entries.
solution: Make sure ORACLE server is using right credentials to connect to LDAP directory services. Make sure permissions for LDAP user entries are configured correctly.

message: Domain Policy hasn't been registered for SSL authentication.
cause: An attempt was made to authenticate with SSL, but the database enterprise domain was not configured for SSL authentication.
solution: Modify orclDBAuthType of the server's enterprise domain entry and assign it "ALL" or "SSL".

message: User does not exist in the LDAP directory service.
cause: An attempt was made to authenticate with SSL using the user's certificate, but there was no user entry in the LDAP server that matched the user's Distinguished Name.
solution: Add an user entry whose DN matches the user's PKI DN in the LDAP directory.

message: Distinguished name for user exceeds maximum supported length
cause: The user's distinguished name (DN) exceeded the maximum supported length.
solution: Shorten the user's distinguished name (DN) and retry.

message: encryption is not allowed for this data type
cause: Data type was not supported for column encryption.
solution: None

message: encrypted column size too long for its data type
cause: column was encrypted and for VARCHAR2, the length specified was > 3932; for CHAR, the length specified was > 1932; for NVARCHAR2, the length specified was > 1966; for NCHAR, the length specified was > 966;
solution: Reduce the column size.

message: cannot have more than one password for the encryption key
cause: More than one password was specified in the user command.
solution: None

message: column is not encrypted
cause: An attempt was made to rekey or decrypt an unencrypted column.
solution: None

message: column is already encrypted
cause: An attempt was made to encrypt an encrypted column.
solution: None

message: referenced or referencing FK constraint column cannot be encrypted
cause: encrypted columns were involved in the referential constraint
solution: None

message: cannot encrypt SYS owned objects
cause: An attempt was made to encrypt columns in a table owned by SYS.
solution: None

message: the specified index may not be defined on an encrypted column
cause: Index column was either a functional, domain, or join index.
solution: None

message: Column(s) cannot be both indexed and encrypted with salt
cause: An attempt was made to encrypt index column with salt or an attempt was made to create an index on encrypted column with salt.
solution: Alter the table and specify column encrypting without salt.

message: missing or invalid encryption algorithm
cause: Encryption algorithm was missing or invalid in the user command.
solution: Must specify a valid algorithm.

message: a different encryption algorithm has been chosen for the table
cause: Existing encrypted columns were associated with a different algorithm.
solution: No need to specify an algorithm, or specify the same one for the existing encrypted columns.

message: cannot encrypt constraint column(s) with salt
cause: An attempt was made to encrypt constraint columns with salt.
solution: Encrypt the constraint columns without salt.

message: integrity check fails on column key
cause: Encryption metadata may have been improperly altered.
solution: None

message: fails to encrypt data
cause: data or encryption metadata may have been improperly altered or the security module may not have been properly setup
solution: None

message: fails to decrypt data
cause: data or encryption metadata may have been improperly altered or the security module may not have been properly setup
solution: None

message: cannot downgrade because there exists encrypted column
cause: An attempt was made to downgrade when there was an encrypted column in the system.
solution: Decrypt these columns before attempting to downgrade.

message: an encrypted column cannot serve as a partitioning column
cause: An attempt was made to encrypt a partitioning key column or create partitioning index with encrypted columns.
solution: The column must be decrypted.

message: encryption properties mismatch
cause: An attempt was made to issue an ALTER TABLE EXCHANGE PARTITION | SUBPARTITION command, but encryption properties were mismatched.
solution: Make sure encrytion algorithms and columns keys are identical. The corresponding columns must be encrypted on both tables with the same salt and non-salt flavor.

message: index defined on the specified column cannot be encrypted
cause: An attempt was made to encrypt a column which is in a functional index, domain index, or join index.
solution: drop the index

message: cannot encrypt the specified column recorded in the materialized view log
cause: An attempt was made to encrypt a column which is already recorded in the materialized view log.
solution: drop the materialized view log

message: cannot encrypt the specified column recorded in CDC synchronized change table
cause: An attempt was made to encrypt a column which is already recorded in CDC synchronized change table.
solution: drop the synchronized change table

message: cannot encrypt the column of a cluster key
cause: An attempt was made to encrypt a column of the cluster key. A column of the cluster key in a clustered table cannot be encrypted.
solution: None

message: failed to open wallet
cause: The database was unable to open the security module wallet due to an incorrect wallet path or password It is also possible that a wallet has not been created. Type mkwallet from command line for instructions.
solution: Execute the command again using the correct wallet password or verfying a wallet exists in the specified directory. If necessary, create a new wallet and initialize it.

message: Encryption wallet, auto login wallet, or HSM is already open
cause: Encryption wallet, auto login wallet, or HSM was already opened.
solution: None

message: invalid open wallet syntax
cause: The command to open the wallet contained improper spelling or syntax.
solution: If attempting to open the wallet, verify the spelling and syntax and execute the command again.

message: password required to open the wallet
cause: A password was not provided when executing the open wallet command.
solution: Retry the command with a valid password.

message: improper set key syntax
cause: The command to set the master key contained improper spelling or syntax.
solution: If attempting to set the master key for Transparent Database Encryption, verify the spelling and syntax and execute the command again.

message: invalid certificate identifier
cause: The certificate specified did not exist in the wallet.
solution: Query the V$WALLET fixed view to find the proper certificate identifier for certificate to be used.

message: master key not yet set
cause: The master key for the instance was not set.
solution: Execute the ALTER SYSTEM SET KEY command to set a master key for the database instance.

message: master key not found
cause: The required master key required could not be located. This may be casued by the use of an invalid or incorrect wallet.
solution: Check wallet location parameters to see if they specify the correct wallet. Also, verify that an SSO wallet is not being used when an encrypted wallet is intended.

message: buffer provided not large enough for output
cause: A provided output buffer is too small to contain the output.
solution: Check the size of the output buffer to make sure it is initialized to the proper size.

message: invalid wallet operation
cause: The command to operate the wallet contained improper spelling or syntax.
solution: Verify the spelling and syntax and execute the command again.

message: wallet is not open
cause: The security module wallet has not been opened.
solution: Open the wallet.

message: invalid database encryption operation
cause: The command for database encryption contained improper spelling or syntax.
solution: Verify the spelling and syntax and execute the command again.

message: wallet does not exist
cause: The Oracle wallet has not been created or the wallet location parameters in sqlnet.ora specifies an invalid wallet path.
solution: Verify that the WALLET_LOCATION or the ENCRYPTION_WALLET_LOCATION parameter is correct and that a valid wallet exists in the path specified.

message: cannot auto-create wallet
cause: The database failed to auto create an Oracle wallet. The Oracle process may not have proper file permissions or a wallet may already exist.
solution: Confirm that proper directory permissions are granted to the Oracle user and that neither an encrypted or obfuscated wallet exists in the specified wallet location and try again.

message: cannot add files to encryption-ready tablespace when offline
cause: You attempted to add files to an encryption-ready tablespace when all the files in the tablespace were offline.
solution: Bring the tablespace online and try again

message: ENCRYPT storage option not allowed
cause: You attempted to specify the ENCRYPT storage option. This option may only be specified during CREATE TABLESPACE.
solution: Remove this option and retry the statement.

message: ENCRYPTION clause and/or ENCRYPT storage option not allowed
cause: You attempted to specify the ENCRYPTION clause or ENCRYPT storage option for creating TEMP or UNDO tablespaces.
solution: Remove these options and retry the statement.

message: missing ENCRYPT storage option for encrypted tablespace
cause: You attempted to specify ENCRYPTION property for CREATE TABLESPACE without specifying ENCRYPT storage option to encrypt the tablepsace.
solution: Add ENCRYPT storage option and retry the statement.

message: missing ENCRYPTION clause for encrypted tablespace
cause: You attempted to specify storage option ENCRYPT in CREATE TABLESPACE without specifying ENCRYPTION property to encrypt the tablepsace.
solution: Add ENCRYPTION clause and retry the statement.

message: typed master key not found in wallet
cause: You attempted to access encrypted tablespace or redo logs with a typed master key not existing in the wallet.
solution: Copy the correct Oracle Wallet from the instance where the tablespace was created.

message: cannot perform cross-endianism conversion on encrypted tablespace
cause: You attempted to perform cross-endianism conversion on encrypted tablespace.
solution: Cross-endianism conversion on encrypted tablespace is not supported.

message: cannot find PKCS11 library
cause: The HSM vendor's library cannot be found.
solution: Place the HSM vendor's library in the following directory structure: For Unix like system: /opt/oracle/extapi/[32,64]/hsm/{VENDOR}/{VERSION}/lib<apiname>.<ext> For Windows systems: %SYSTEM_DRIVE%\oracle\extapi\[32,64]\hsm\{VENDOR}\{VERSION}\lib<apin// ame>.<ext> [32, 64] - refers to 32bit or 64bit binary. {VENDOR} - The name of the vendor supplying the library. {VERSION} - Version of the library, perferably in num#.num#.num# for// mat.

message: No need to migrate from wallet to HSM
cause: There are either no encrypted columns or all column keys are already encrypted with the HSM master key.
solution: No action required.

message: Wallet not open after setting the Master Key
cause: The Master Key has been set or reset. However, wallet could not be reopened successfully.
solution: Reopen the wallet.

message: a different integrity algorithm has been chosen for the table
cause: Encrypted columns were associated with a different algorithm.
solution: You do not need to specify an algorithm, or specify the same one for the existing encrypted columns.

message: Global wallet operation in RAC failed
cause: Wallet operation in RAC failed.
solution: Check V$WALLET_ENCRYPTION table to verify if the wallet operation succeeded on any instance. Retry the operation.

message: cannot do a PKI certificate-based Master Key migration
cause: A PKI certificate-based Master Key migration was not allowed.
solution: Execute a symmetric Master Key migration.

message: cannot perform Tablespace Encryption
cause: Tablespace Encryption was attempted when PKI certificate-based Master Key was in use.
solution: Perform a symmetric Master Key Rekey.

message: cannot perform a PKI certificate-based migration
cause: A PKI certificate-based migration to HSM was attempted.
solution: Perform a symmetric Master Key migration.

message: cannot perform a PKI certificate-based Master Key Rekey
cause: A PKI certificate-based Master Key Rekey was attempted when Tablespace Encryption or HSM was in use.
solution: Perform a symmetric Master Key Rekey or disable Tablespace Encryption for all tablespaces.

message: Could not acquire an enqueue for wallet operation in Oracle RAC
cause: Enqueue to block TDE operations in Oracle RAC database could not be obtained.
solution: Retry the wallet operation.

message: database is not open in read/write mode
cause: Database was not open in read/write mode and could not perform these wallet operations.
solution: Open the database in read/write mode and retry this command.

message: cannot close auto login wallet
cause: Auto login wallet could not be closed because it was opened with another wallet or HSM requiring a password.
solution: Close the wallet or HSM with a password.

message: auto login wallet not open but encryption wallet may be open
cause: Auto login wallet was not open. But, the encryption wallet may still be open and subsequent TDE operations might succeed.
solution: If auto login wallet is closed but TDE operations succeed, check the status of the encryption wallet and close that if required.

message: cannot close wallet or HSM, password mismatch
cause: Password provided did not match the password of the open wallet or HSM.
solution: Provide the correct password for wallet or HSM to close the wallet or HSM.

message: invalid close wallet syntax
cause: The command to close the wallet contained improper spelling or syntax.
solution: If attempting to close the wallet, verify the spelling and syntax and execute the command again.

message: password required to close the wallet
cause: A password was not provided when executing the close wallet command.
solution: Retry the command with a valid password.

message: decryption of data of length string failed
cause: Decryption of data failed. Error may be due to plain text data in an external file being submitted for decryption, data encrypted with a different key or a utility being submitted for decryption, or TDE encrypted data in data files being corrupted.
solution: Verify that the correct external file is being specified or contact Oracle Support Services.

message: could not write the new master key to the wallet
cause: An attempt was made to write the new master key to the wallet. The wallet or the parent directory may not have the proper file permissions to write the master key in the wallet.
solution: Check the password-based wallet, auto login wallet, the parent directory permissions and disk space availability on the file system. Make sure that the Oracle processes have read/write permissions on the password-based and auto login wallets. Retry the command.

message: rekey of enc$ dictionary table failed
cause: One or more master keys required for the rekey operation could not be found in the wallet. Either incorrect master key identifiers were inserted into the enc$ dictionary table or the wallet containing the referenced master keys were improperly modified or deleted.
solution: Restore the most recent copy of the wallet and try again.

message: cannot online file string since it has a passphrase-wrapped key
cause: The encrypted tablespace file was rewrapped using passphrase through the DBMS_TTS.PASSPHRASE_REWRAP_KEY procedure. Therefore it cannot be part of the database until it is converted by RMAN.
solution: Do not attempt to online files with passphrase-wrapped keys.

message: cannot rewrap encryption key for this file
cause: Cannot rewrap encryption key for this file because it was not from an encrypted tablespace, or it had already been rewrapped.
solution: Verify that the file is a copy of a file from an encrypted tablespace.

message: file string cannot be modified because it is an online data file
cause: An attempt was made to modify an online data file when the file was not expected to be part of the database.
solution: Check the status of the file and its tablespace and make sure it is offline or is a copy of a data file

message: role cannot be altered
cause: An attempt was made to alter the role to become a global, external, password protected, or secure application role. The role could not be altered because it was already granted to one or more other roles.
solution: Use REVOKE to revoke the role from other roles first.

message: cannot grant secure role to a role
cause: Role granted was a password protected or secure application role. This role can only be granted directly to a user.
solution: Grant the role directly to a user.

message: Hardware Security Module error detected
cause: Hardware Security Module (HSM) connection may have been lost or another internal HSM error was reached.
solution: Check the trace files for error details and try the following: 1) Retry the command. If the error repeats, go to step 2. 2) Verify that the HSM is configured correctly and connected. Retry the command. If the error repeats, go to step 3. 3) Ask your Security Officer to close and open the security module. Retry the command. If the error repeats, go to step 4. 4) Bounce the database if possible. Retry the command. If the error repeats, contact Oracle Support Services or your HSM vendor's support.

message: encryption using passphrase failed
cause: Encryption with the passphrase failed which was likely due to an invalid or missing passphrase or due to an internal error.
solution: Verify that the passphrase is provided and try the operation again. If the problem persists contact Oracle Support Services.

message: decryption using passphrase failed
cause: Decryption with the passphrase failed which was likely due to an invalid or missing passphrase or due to an internal error.
solution: Verify that the passphrase is provided and try the operation again. If the problem persists contact Oracle Support Services.

message: connection from ORACLE to a non-Oracle system returned this message:
cause: The cause is explained in the forwarded message.
solution: See the non-Oracle system's documentation of the forwarded message.

message: communication error on heterogeneous database link
cause: An unexpected communication failure occurred on a heterogeneous database link to a non-Oracle system. The message above will be followed by a second message generated by the connected non-Oracle system.
solution: See the documentation for the non-Oracle system for an explanation of the second error message.

message: internal communication error on heterogeneous database link
cause: A communication error internal to ORACLE's heterogeneous services has occurred.
solution: Contact Oracle customer support.

message: bind value cannot be translated into SQL text for non-Oracle system
cause: A SQL statement used bind variables on a Heterogenous Services database link to a non-Oracle system, but the non-Oracle system does not support bind variables.
solution: Change your SQL statement so that it does not use bind variables.

message: ROWID not found in ROWID cache for heterogeneous database link
cause: The ROWID cache for Heterogeneous Services held no entry that corresponds to the specified ROWID. The ROWID entry may have been overwritten in the ROWID cache.
solution: Enlarge the Heterogeneous Services ROWID cache size by increasing the value of the Heterogenous Services initialization parameter HS_ROWID_CACHE_SIZE.

message: cannot get non-Oracle system capabilities from string
cause: ORACLE was unable to retrieve capability information for the non-Oracle system connected through a heterogeneous database link. This capability information should be stored in data dictionary tables viewable with the HS_CLASS_CAPS or HS_INST_CAPS data dictionary views.
solution: Contact the DBA to check the server data dictionary table named in the error message. If table contents are incorrect, the DBA should restore all data dictionary content for this FDS_CLASS_NAME and/or FDS_INST_NAME. It usually is sufficient to delete all current data dictionary content for this class and/or instance and initiate a new connection to let the connected agent upload new data dictionary content to the server.

message: parse error in data dictionary translation for string stored in string
cause: A reference to an ORACLE data dictionary table or view name on a heterogeneous database link to a non-Oracle system could not be translated. The ORACLE data dictionary tables shown with view HS_CLASS_DD contain invalid SQL for the data dictionary translation.
solution: Contact customer support of the agent vendor.

message: error in data dictionary view string
cause: The initialization parameter table for the Heterogeneous Services was not available, or its structure (number of columns or column types) was incorrect.
solution: Verify correct installation of the following Heterogeneous Services' initialization parameter views: HS_CLASS_INIT and HS_INST_INIT. If these views are not available, make sure you ran the script CATHS.SQL in the $ORACLE_HOME/rdbms/admin directory.

message: invalid value string for Heterogeneous Services initialization parameter string
cause: The specified Heterogeneous Services initialization parameter had an invalid value when attempting to connect to a non-Oracle system.
solution: Check the Heterogeneous Services and agent documentation to determine acceptable values

message: unable to establish a connection to non-Oracle system
cause: Initialization of a database link to a non-Oracle system failed to connect to the Heterogeneous Services agent process for this non-Oracle system.
solution: Check the Net8 service name definition in the following places: -- the USING clause of the CREATE DATABASE LINK statement -- the TNSNAMES.ORA file -- the Oracle Names Server The following are possible reasons for name mismatches: -- The USING clause in the CREATE DATABASE LINK statement has to match the service name defined in the TNSNAMES.ORA file or in the Oracle Names Server. -- The protocol-specific information in the service name definition must match the protocol-specific definition of the responding listener. -- The SID=<name> in the service name definition (in the TNSNAMES.ORA file or in Oracle Names Server) must match the value in the LISTENER.ORA file for the responding listener.

message: heterogeneous database link initialization failed
cause: Initialization of a heterogeneous database link to a non-Oracle system failed due to an error identified by the agent for this non-Oracle system.
solution: Make sure the non-Oracle system is up and running and that all of the environment and initialization values for the agent are set correctly.

message: lost RPC connection to heterogeneous remote agent using SID= string
cause: A fatal error occurred in one of the following places: -- the connection between the ORACLE server and the agent -- the heterogeneous services remote agent itself -- the connection to the non-Oracle system This error occurred after communication had been established successfully.
solution: Check for network problems and remote host crashes. The problem is probably in the agent software. If so, contact a customer support representative of the agent vendor.

message: cannot get data dictionary translations from string
cause: ORACLE was unable to retrieve data dictionary translation information for the non-Oracle system connected through a heterogeneous database link. This data dictionary translation information should be stored in data dictionary tables viewable with the HS_CLASS_DD or HS_INST_DD data dictionary views.
solution: Ask your DBA to check the server data dictionary table named in the error message. If table contents are incorrect, the DBA should restore all data dictionary content for this FDS_CLASS_NAME and/or FDS_INST_NAME. It usually is sufficient to delete all current data dictionary content for this class and/or instance and initiate a new connection to let the connected agent upload new data dictionary content to the server.

message: internal error in heterogeneous remote agent
cause: An internal error has occurred in the Oracle remote agent supporting a heterogeneous database link.
solution: Make a note of how the error was produced and contact the customer support representative of the agent vendor.

message: heterogeneous database link initialization could not convert system date
cause: The system date was not retrievable.
solution: Verify that the ORACLE server's host machine and operating system are operational. This error should not occur unless low level system functions are failing.

message: cannot get external object definitions from string
cause: ORACLE was unable to retrieve definitions of distributed external procedures or remote libraries registered for the non-Oracle system instance, probably because the underlying data dictionary table does not exist or is malformed.
solution: Verify that the ORACLE server's Heterogeneous Services data dictionary was installed correctly. If the Heterogeneous Services data dictionary is not installed, execute the CATHS.SQL script in the $ORACLE_HOME/rdbms/admin directory.

message: data dictionary translation has illegal translation type
cause: A data dictionary translation definition, either in the ORACLE server data dictionary or in data dictionary content uploaded from a Heterogeneous Services agent, specified an illegal translation type code. Legal values are 'T' or 't' for 'translate', 'M' or 'm' for 'mimic'. Information on the exact data dictionary translation causing the error is written to a trace (*.TRC) file for the ORACLE instance and to the ORACLE instance's alert log. This error occurs when a Heterogeneous Services agent uploads data dictionary content to an ORACLE server on the first connection from the server to the agent.
solution: Contact the customer support of the agent vendor.

message: no heterogeneous data dictionary translations available
cause: The ORACLE server's data dictionary did not define data dictionary translations for the connected non-Oracle system, and automatic self-registration (data dictionary upload) was disabled.
solution: Ask a DBA to resolve this problem. The easiest solution is to enable automatic self-registration by setting the ORACLE server's HS_AUTO_REGISTER initialization parameter to TRUE. An alternative is to load the Heterogeneous Services data dictionary with information specific for the non-Oracle system by executing a SQL script supplied by the agent vendor. If the script is run and the error persists, contact the customer support representative of the agent vendor.

message: error initializing heterogeneous data dictionary translations
cause: ORACLE was unable to retrieve data dictionary translations for the non-Oracle system instance, probably because the underlying data dictionary table does not exist or is formed incorrectly.
solution: Verify that the ORACLE server's Heterogeneous Services data dictionary was installed correctly. If the Heterogeneous Services data dictionary is not installed, execute the CATHS.SQL script in the $ORACLE_HOME/rdbms/admin directory. If the connected agent, identified by FDS_CLASS_NAME, requires a custom installation script for the ORACLE server, verify that the script has been run. If both scripts were executed and the error persists, contact the customer support representative of the agent vendor.

message: no heterogeneous capability information available
cause: The ORACLE server's data dictionary did not contain capability definitions for the connected non-Oracle system, and automatic self-registration (data dictionary upload) was disabled.
solution: Ask a DBA to resolve this problem. The easiest resolution is to enable automatic self-registration by setting the ORACLE server's HS_AUTO_REGISTER initialization parameter to TRUE. An alternative is to load the Heterogeneous Services data dictionary with information specific for the non-Oracle system by executing a SQL script supplied by the agent vendor. If the script is run and the error persists, contact the customer support representative of the agent vendor.

message: error initializing heterogeneous capabilities
cause: ORACLE was unable to retrieve capability definitions for the non-Oracle system instance, probably because the underlying data dictionary table does not exist or is formed incorrectly.
solution: Verify that the ORACLE server's Heterogeneous Services data dictionary was installed correctly. If the Heterogeneous Services data dictionary is not installed, execute the CATHS.SQL script in the $ORACLE_HOME/rdbms/admin directory. If the connected agent, identified by FDS_CLASS_NAME, requires a custom installation script for the ORACLE server, verify that the script has been run. If both scripts were executed and the error persists, contact the customer support representative of the agent vendor.

message: ORACLE and heterogeneous agent are incompatible versions
cause: An operation on a database link attempted to connect to a non-Oracle system, but the ORACLE instance and the agent process for the non-Oracle system are incompatible.
solution: Ask your DBA to confirm configuration of both the ORACLE instance and the agent. Additional information on the version incompatibility is logged in trace (*.TRC) files, the ORACLE instance and the agent, and in the ORACLE instance's alert log. Check the documentation for your agent to find out which releases of the Oracle Server are supported.

message: unable to create Heterogeneous Services error message text
cause: Incorrect arguments were passed into the error message creation routine.
solution: Contact Oracle customer support.

message: invalid describe information returned to Heterogeneous Services
cause: The Heterogeneous Services received invalid describe information for a select list, bind list, or stored procedure from the Heterogeneous Services agent. This indicates a problem with the Heterogeneous Services' non-Oracle system agent.
solution: Contact customer support of the agent vendor.

message: Heterogeneous Services datatype mapping error
cause: Either an Oracle datatype could not be mapped to a non-Oracle datatype, or a non-Oracle datatype could not be mapped to an Oracle datatype. These mappings are defined as capability definitions in the ORACLE server's data dictionary.
solution: Verify that the ORACLE server's data dictionary has been initialized with correct capability definitions for the connected FDS_CLASS_NAME and FDS_INST_NAME. If table contents are incorrect, a DBA should restore all data dictionary content for this FDS_CLASS_NAME and/or FDS_INST_NAME. It usually is sufficient to delete all current data dictionary content for this class and/or instance and initiate a new connection to let the connected agent upload new data dictionary content to the server. If the error persists contact the customer support representative of the agent vendor.

message: Heterogeneous Services datatype conversion error
cause: Either an Oracle datatype could not be converted to a non-Oracle datatype, or a non-Oracle datatype could not be converted to an Oracle datatype. The following are possible reasons for for the conversion failure: -- overflow problems (in the case of numbers) -- length limitations (in the case of character strings) -- invalid values passed into the conversion routines
solution: Contact customer support of the agent vendor. If the problem is due to size discrepancies between Oracle and the non-Oracle system, it may not be possible to convert the value.

message: invalid or missing parameter in Net8 service name definition
cause: There was an invalid or missing Heterogeneous Services parameter in the Net8 service name definition stored in either the TNSNAMES.ORA file or in the Oracle Names Server.
solution: Ask your DBA to make sure the information in the Net8 service definition is correct and complete. The correct information that should be included in the Net8 service definition can be found in the agent's documentation.

message: Heterogeneous Services initialization error in NLS language ID
cause: Heterogeneous Services was unable to initialize an NLS language ID. Both the ORACLE server and the Heterogeneous Services agent for the connected non-Oracle system must have language IDs.
solution: Contact Oracle customer support.

message: Heterogeneous Services coercion handling error
cause: The Heterogeneous Services encountered an error in coercion handling. The HS can, if the agent vendor so chooses, perform extra processing on SQL statements that contain implicit coercions or that contain coercion functions such as TO_CHAR, TO_NUMBER or TO_DATE. This functionality is controlled by coercion-related capabilities. HS logic reports this error when it encounters an error in one of these capability definitions.
solution: The capability table settings are controlled by the agent vendor and can be modified by the DBA. Contact your DBA and agent vendor and get the correct set of capabilities installed.

message: Heterogeneous Services preprocessing error
cause: One of the things that the Heterogeneous Services can do is to preprocess parts of SQL statements that contain implicit coercions or calls to explicit coercion functions like TO_CHAR TO_NUMBER or TO_DATE. For example, it could convert a call to TO_DATE to a bind variable, pre-evaluate the TO_DATE function call and pass the resulting value to the non-Oracle system as the bind value. This behavior is controlled by some coercion related capabilities. If the capabilities are set incorrectly, the HS could encounter errors when it attempts to do the preprocessing. If it does then this error will be signaled.
solution: The capability table settings are controlled by the agent vendor and can be modified by the DBA. Contact your DBA and agent vendor and get the correct set of capabilities installed.

message: invalid Heterogeneous Services context
cause: A Heterogeneous Services agent's driver module called an HS service routine with an invalid HS context value. This probably is a logic error in the driver.
solution: Contact Oracle customer support or your agent vendor.

message: error in processing Heterogeneous Services initialization parameters
cause: An error described by a subsequent error message prevented successful processing of Heterogeneous Services initialization parameters from the ORACLE server data dictionary.
solution: Check server data dictionary views HS_CLASS_INIT, HS_INST_INIT, and HS_ALL_INITS. Look for conditions which could produce the error identified in the error message immediately following this one.

message: no more result sets
cause: This error code was used internally within Oracle Database Gateway and Heterogeneous Services code and should not be reported to a client program.
