solution: Contact Oracle customer support.

message: result set not found
cause: The client program tried fetching from a result set that is not open anymore. Many gateways will, on execution of a stored procedure, automatically close all result sets that were returned by any previously executed stored procedure.
solution: Check the documentation for the gateway that you are using and see if it will automatically close currently open result sets each time a stored procedure is executed. Then check if your client program is doing anything that violates this rule. If it is, fix your program. If it is not then contact Oracle customer support.

message: gateway does not support result sets
cause: The client program tried executing a stored procedure that returns one or more result sets through a gateway that does not have result set support.
solution: Check the documentation for the gateway that you are using and see if it supports result sets returned from stored procedures. If it does not, then the only way of accessing such stored procedures is to upgrade to a version of the gateway that does support result sets (if such a version exists). If the gateway does have result set support and you are still seeing this error then contact Oracle customer support.

message: internal result set error
cause: A protocol error internal to Heterogeneous Services or Oracle Database Gateway code has occurred.
solution: Contact Oracle customer support.

message: Error in HS init file on line number .
cause: A syntax error occurred in the gateway initialization file.
solution: Check gateway init file to correct the syntax error. For further information, check the error message in the gateway trace file.

message: Error in reading HS init file
cause: Reading the gateway init file generated an error.
solution: Check the gateway initialization file name to see that the gateway initialization file acctually exists. Check the ifile parameter to see that it points to the correct location.

message: Error initializing apply connection to non-Oracle system
cause: Attempt to initialize connection to non-Oracle for heterogeneous replication failed.
solution: Check if the listener used to connect to the gateway is up and is correctly configured. Make sure that the database link used has been configured correctly and, if a tnsnames alias has been used in the database link definition, make sure that the configuration of the entry in tnsnames.ora has been done correctly.

message: connect to agent failed, probable Net8 administration error
cause: Net8 reported a failure to make a RSLV connection or a protocol mode error when the Oracle server attempted to establish communication with a Heterogeneous Services agent or an external procedure agent. This usually is due to an administration error in setting up Net8 service definitions in TNSNAMES.ORA or LISTENER.ORA: A basic network connection is opened, but it connects to a program which does not use the appropriate protocol. This often is a sign that the connection goes to the wrong program.
solution: Check Net8 administration in the following ways: -- When using TNSNAMES.ORA or an Oracle Names server, make sure that the connection from the ORACLE server uses the correct service name or SID. -- Check LISTENER.ORA on the agent's host machine to assure that the service name or SID refers to the correct agent executable in its (PROGRAM=...) clause. -- Confirm in TNSNAMES.ORA or the equivalent service definition that sevice 'extproc_connection_data' does NOT contain (HS=), or that the service definition used by a Heterogeneous Services database link DOES contain (HS=).

message: error diagnosed by Net8 when connecting to an agent
cause: An attempt to call an external procedure or to issue SQL to a non-Oracle system on a Heterogeneous Services database link failed at connection initialization. The error diagnosed by Net8 NCR software is reported separately.
solution: Refer to the Net8 NCRO error message. If this isn't clear, check connection administrative setup in tnsnames.ora and listener.ora for the service associated with the Heterogeneous Services database link being used, or with 'extproc_connection_data' for an external procedure call.

message: connection initialization failed, probable Net8 admin error
cause: A failure occurred during initialization of a network connection from the Oracle server to a second process: The connection was completed but a disconnect occurred while trying to perform protocol-specific initialization, usually due to use of different network protocols by opposite sides of the connection. This usually is caused by incorrect Net8 administrative setup for database links or external procedure calls. The most frequent specific causes are: -- Database link setup for an Oracle-to-Oracle connection instead connects to a Heterogeneous Services agent or an external procedure agent. -- Database link setup for a Heterogeneous Services connection instead connects directly to an Oracle server. -- The extproc_connection_data definition in tnsnames.ora connects to an Oracle instance instead of an external procedure agent. -- Connect data for a Heterogeneous Services database link, usually defined in tnsnames.ora, does not specify (HS=). -- Connect data for an Oracle-to-Oracle database link, usually defined in tnsnames.ora, specifies (HS=).
solution: Check Net8 administration in the following ways: -- When using TNSNAMES.ORA or an Oracle Names server, make sure that the connection from the ORACLE server uses the correct service name or SID. -- Check LISTENER.ORA on the connection end point's host machine to assure that this service name or SID connects to the correct program. -- Confirm in TNSNAMES.ORA or the equivalent service definition that service 'extproc_connection_data' does NOT contain (HS=), or that the service definition used by a Heterogeneous Services database link DOES contain (HS=).

message: connection to server failed, probable Oracle Net admin error
cause: A failure occurred during initialization of a network connection from a client process to the Oracle server. The connection was completed but a disconnect occurred while trying to perform protocol-specific initialization, usually due to use of different network protocols by opposite sides of the connection. This usually is caused by incorrect Oracle Net administrative setup for database links or external procedure calls. The most frequent specific causes are: -- The connection uses a connect string which refers to a Heterogeneous Services agent instead of an Oracle server. -- The connection uses a connect string which includes an (HS=) specification. -- Hitting Ctrl+C before connection initialization is complete. -- Using DRCP on Windows with SQLNET.AUTHENTICATION_SERVICES set to NTS. -- Connection timeout due to SQLNET.INBOUND_CONNECT_TIMEOUT parameter when all shared servers are busy in shared server configuration.
solution: Check Oracle Net administration in the following ways: -- When using TNSNAMES.ORA or an Oracle Names server, make sure that the client connection to the Oracle server uses the correct service name or SID. -- Check LISTENER.ORA on the connection end point's host machine to assure that this service name or SID refers to the correct server. -- Confirm in TNSNAMES.ORA or the equivalent service definition that the connect string does not contain (HS=). -- Set SQLNET.AUTHENTICATION_SERVICES to NONE when using DRCP on Windows.

message: pass-through SQL: cursor not found
cause: A value passed to a pass-through SQL function or procedure call as a cursor does not identify a currently open cursor.
solution: Use a cursor number returned by the pass-through SQL OPEN_CURSOR call.

message: pass-through SQL: SQL parse error
cause: A non-Oracle system rejected text supplied as a pass-through SQL statement.
solution: Ensure that the SQL supplied to the pass-through SQL PARSE call is legal for the non-Oracle system.

message: pass-through SQL: call flow error
cause: A pass-through SQL function was called in an invalid order.
solution: Correct program flow by changing the order of API calls to match the flow described in the manual.

message: pass-through SQL: invalid bind-variable position
cause: A pass-through SQL function referring to the position of a bind variable in the currently-parsed SQL statement supplied an invalid bind-variable position. Valid values are 1 through n, where n is the number of bind-variable place-holders in the SQL text.
solution: Verify that the bind-variable position parameter is in the correct range to represent a place-holder in the SQL text. Confirm that the SQL text uses the correct syntax for a bind-variable place-holder, as required by the non-Oracle system.

message: pass-through SQL: out of cursors
cause: The maximum number of open cursors has been exceeded.
solution: Close open cursors by using the pass-through SQL CLOSE_CURSOR function.

message: pass-through SQL: required parameter missing or NULL
cause: An attempt was made to pass a NULL value to a non-NULL parameter.
solution: Use a non-NULL value for the parameter.

message: authorization insufficient to access table
cause: A query attempted to access a table in the non-Oracle system that is either privileged or has privileged columns.
solution: Contact the DBA for the non-Oracle system. The DBA can grant permission to access the privileged table or columns.

message: unknown string for database link to non-Oracle system
cause: When attempting to connect to a non-Oracle system through a Heterogeneous Services database link, the agent supporting this non-Oracle system failed to return FDS_CLASS_NAME and/or FDS_INST_NAME. ORACLE requires these names to configure the heterogeneous database link.
solution: Contact the DBA to check setup of the connection and the Heterogeneous Services agent.

message: HS_FDS_CONNECT_STRING undefined for non-Oracle system
cause: A database link to a non-Oracle system had no HS_FDS_CONNECT_STRING initialization parameter in the ORACLE server's data dictionary for Heterogeneous Services. Without this parameter, the connection could not be completed.
solution: Contact your DBA to verify correct setup of an HS_FDS_CONNECT_STRING entry in the ORACLE Heterogeneous Services data dictionary.

message: FDS_CLASS_NAME is string , FDS_INST_NAME is string
cause: An associated error was reported in another message, and this message supplies supplementary information to assist diagnosis of that error. FDS_CLASS_NAME and FDS_INST_NAME are used to access information in tables and views of the ORACLE data dictionary that direct operation of Heterogeneous Services on a database link to a non-Oracle data store.
solution: Use the FDS_CLASS_NAME and FDS_INST_NAME values to check ORACLE data dictionary contents when necessary to diagnose the cause of the associated error.

message: error in configuration of agent process
cause: An ORACLE server invoked a function not supported by the connected agent (Heterogeneous Services or external procedures). The most probable cause is incorrect Net8 setup, resulting in use of the wrong agent executable.
solution: Check Net8 administration in the following ways: -- When using TNSNAMES.ORA or an Oracle Names server, make sure that the connection from the ORACLE server uses the correct SID. -- Check LISTENER.ORA on the agent's host machine to assure that this SID refers to the correct agent executable in its (PROGRAM=...) clause.

message: unable to set date format on non-Oracle system
cause: Initialization of a Heterogeneous Services connection to set the date format to be used on the connected non-Oracle system.
solution: If the Oracle data dictionary supplies a value for the HS_NLS_DATE_FORMAT parameter, confirm that this value is formatted correctly by the rules of the non-Oracle system. Also check for additional information in log and trace files generated by the Heterogeneous Services agent.

message: Heterogeneous Services data truncation error
cause: A select operation was attempted with an insufficient data buffer to satisfy the request.
solution: Contact your DBA to verify whether your gateway initialization parameter HS_KEEP_REMOTE_COLUMN_SIZE is set appropriately based on your requirement. If it is, make sure the sizes of bind parameters are sufficient. If the problem persists, contact Oracle Support Services.

message: unable to open RPC connection to external procedure agent
cause: Initialization of a network connection to the extproc agent did not succeed. This problem can be caused by network problems, incorrect listener configuration, or incorrect transfer code.
solution: Check listener configuration in LISTENER.ORA and TNSNAMES.ORA, or check Oracle Names Server.

message: lost RPC connection to external procedure agent
cause: of this error is abnormal termination of the invoked "C" routine. If this is not the case, check for network problems. Correct the problem if you find it. If all components appear to be normal but the problem persists, the problem could be an internal logic error in the RPC transfer code. Contact your customer support representative.
solution: First check the 3GL code you are invoking; the most likely

message: argument string of external procedure string has unsupported datatype string
cause: While transferring external procedure arguments to the agent, an unsupported datatype was detected.
solution: Check your documentation for the supported datatypes of external procedure arguments.

message: protocol error during callback from an external procedure
cause: An internal protocol error occurred while trying to execute a callback to the Oracle server from the user's 3GL routine.
solution: Contact Oracle customer support.

message: network error during callback from external procedure agent
cause: An internal network error occurred while trying to execute a callback to the Oracle server from the user's 3GL routine.
solution: Contact Oracle customer support.

message: recursive external procedures are not supported
cause: A callback from within a user's 3GL routine resulted in the invocation of another external procedure.
solution: Make sure that the SQL code executed in a callback does not directly call another external procedure, or indirectly results in another external procedure, such as triggers calling external procedures, PL/SQL procedures calling external procedures, etc.

message: protocol error while executing recursive external procedure
cause: An internal protocol error occurred while trying to execute an external procedure resulting from a callback in another external procedure.
solution: Contact Oracle customer support.

message: a direct connection to this agent is not allowed
cause: A user or a tool tried to establish a direct connection to either an external procedure agent or a Heterogeneous Services agent, for example: "SVRMGR> CONNECT SCOTT/TIGER@NETWORK_ALIAS". This type of connection is not allowed.
solution: When executing the CONNECT statement, make sure your database link or network alias is not pointing to a Heterogeneous Option agent or an external procedure agent.

message: remote references are not permitted during agent callbacks
cause: A Heterogeous Services agent issued a callback to the Oracle server which attemted to to access a remote system. This is not supported.
solution: Make sure that SQL code issued by Heterogeneous Services agents does not reference a database link.

message: heterogeneous apply internal error
cause: The apply slave process encountered an error while trying to apply changes through a gateway to a non-Oracle system.
solution: Make sure that the apply database link is correctly configured and that the gateway listener and the non-Oracle system are correctly set up and are up and running. If everything is configured correctly and the problem still occurs, contact Oracle customer support. errors 28590 - 28599 are reserved for the HS agent control utility

message: agent control utility: illegal or badly formed command
cause: The user has issued an unrecognized or syntactically incorrect command.
solution: Refer to documentation and correct the syntax of the command.

message: agent control utility: unable to access parameter file
cause: The agent control utility was unable to access its parameter file. This could be because it could not find its admin directory or because permissions on directory were not correctly set.
solution: The agent control utility puts its parameter file in either the directory pointed to by the environment variable AGTCTL_ADMIN or in the directory pointed to by the environment variable TNS_ADMIN. Make sure that at least one of these environment variables is set and that it points to a directory that the agent has access to.

message: agent control utility: agent SID not set
cause: The agent needs to know the value of the AGENT_SID parameter before it can process any commands. If it does not have a value for AGENT_SID then all commands will fail.
solution: Issue the command SET AGENT_SID <value> and then retry the command that failed.

message: agent control utility: command terminated with error
cause: An error occurred during the processing of the command. There could be several causes. A SET or an UNSET command could have been issued after the agent was started. This is illegal. The user may have attempted to start two agents with the same SID value or the user could have attempted to shutdown an agent that is no longer running.
solution: If the user wishes to issue a SET or an UNSET command, he should make sure the agent is shutdown first by issuing the SHUTDOWN command.

message: agent control utility: invalid parameter name
cause: The user tried to set or unset an invalid agent parameter.
solution: Refer to documentation and correct the parameter name.

message: Extproc agent : Invalid DLL Path
cause: The path of DLL supplied for the extproc execution is invalid.
solution: Check if the DLL path is set properly using the EXTPROC_DLLS environment variable. errors 28600 - 28620 are reserved for bitmap indexes

message: invalid [no]MINIMIZE option
cause: user didn't type this alter table <table_name> MINIMIZE RECORDS_PER_BLOCK or alter table <table_name> NOMINIMIZE RECORDS_PER_BLOCK
solution: reenter correct sql command

message: statement not permitted on tables containing bitmap indexes
cause: table has bitmap indexes and user is minimizing or nominimizing records_per_block
solution: drop all bitmap indexes before changing records_per_block

message: statement not permitted on empty tables
cause: table is empty and statement does not work on empty tables
solution: try statement after loading your data

message: table too fragmented to build bitmap index ( string , string , string )
cause: The table has one or more blocks that exceed the maximum number of rows expected when creating a bitmap index. This is probably due to deleted rows. The values in the message are: (data block address, slot number found, maximum slot allowed)
solution: Defragment the table or block(s). Use the values in the message to determine the FIRST block affected. (There may be others).

message: bitmap indexes cannot be reversed
cause: user tried to create reverse bitmap index
solution: don't do this; it is not supported

message: block too fragmented to build bitmap index ( string , string )
cause: The block(s) exceed the maximum number of rows expected when creating a bitmap index. This is probably due to maximum slot allowed set too low. The values in the message are: (slot number found, maximum slot allowed)
solution: alter system flush shared_pool; update tab$ set spare1 = 8192 where obj# = (select obj# from obj$ where NAME=<table_name> AND owner# = <table_owner>; commit;

message: bitmap index is corrupted - see trace file for diagnostics
cause: Validate Index detected bitmap corruption in its argument index
solution: Drop this bitmap index and create a new one.

message: Primary index on an IOT cannot be rebuilt
cause: An attempt is made to issue alter index rebuild on IOT-TOP
solution: Use Alter table MOVE to reorganize the table(IOT)

message: Primary index on IOTs can not be marked unusable
cause: An attempt is made to mark IOT-TOP unusable thru ALTER INDEX
solution: Remove the option UNUSABLE

message: overflow segment attributes cannot be specified
cause: During ALTER MOVE ONLINE of a index-organized table, the user attempted to enter one or more of the following options: OVERFLOW, PCTTHRESHOLD,INCLUDING.
solution: Remove the illegal option(s).

message: tables must both be index-organized
cause: Attempt to exchange a non IOT table/partition with a partition/table respectively
solution: Ensure that non-partitioned and partitioned tables are both index-organized.

message: table and partition not overflow compatible
cause: If one of the tables (partitioned/non-partitioned) has overflow data segment and the other one doesn't.
solution: Ensure that non-partitioned and partitioned tables both have overflow data segment or neither one does.

message: Alter table add overflow syntax error
cause: Syntax error
solution: Check the syntax.

message: incomplete attribute specification
cause: The attribute specification is not done for all partitions"
solution: Specify the storage attributes either for ALL partitions or NONE

message: This operation is supported only for Index-Organized tables
cause: Attempt to perform some IOT specific operation on a non-IOT
solution: don't do this. This is not supported

message: COMPRESS must be specified at object level first
cause: Attempt to specify COMPRESS at partition level without first specifying at the table level
solution: Specify COMPRESS at table level. Use ALTER TABLE xxx MODIFY DEFAULT ATTRIBUTES COMPRESS ...

message: Partitioned Index-Organized table may not be MOVEd as a whole
cause: Attempt to MOVE partitioned IOT as a whole
solution: don't do this. This is not supported

message: Object already has COMPRESS clause specified
cause: Attempt to specify compress for iot/index which already has a compression clause.
solution: This is a 'create time only' attribute

message: IOT index and overflow segments must share the same LOGGING attribute
cause: Attempt to specify LOGGING for one segment and NOLOGGING for the other segment.
solution: don't do that

message: Logging/Nologging attribute can not be specified in the statement ALTER TABLE ADD OVERFLOW
cause: Attempt to specify LOGGING for a Alter Table Add Overflow.
solution: don't do that

message: a partitioned table may not be coalesced as a whole
cause: User attempted to coalesce a partitioned IOT using ALTER TABLE COALESCE statement, which is illegal
solution: Coalesce the table a partition at a time (using ALTER TABLE MODIFY PARTITION COALESCE)

message: table and partition must have same compression attribute
cause: User attempted to EXCHANGE a compression enabled partition with a compression disabled table or vice versa OR the # of columns compressed is different for table and partition
solution: Make sure the compression attributes match If they don't, fix it using ALTER TABLE MOVE [PARTITION] COMPRESS

message: option not allowed for an index on UROWID column(s)
cause: User attempted to build a REVERSE or COMPRESSED or GLOBAL partitioned index on UROWID column(s)
solution: Build the index without these options

message: USING INDEX option not allowed for the primary key of an IOT
cause: User attempted to define storage attributes for the primary key index of an Index-Organized table with USING INDEX clause. All the storage attribute defined for the (IOT)table applies to the primary key index and a separate USING INDEX clause is not required.
solution: Remove the USING INDEX clause and specify all attributes directly for the table

message: cannot reference mapping table of an index-organized table
cause: An attempt to directly access the mapping table of an index-organized table
solution: Issue the statement against the parent index-organized table containing the specified mapping table.

message: bitmap index can not be created on an IOT with no mapping table
cause: User attempted to create a bitmap index on an index-organized table without a mapping table.
solution: Enable bitmap indexes on the Index-organized table by creating a mapping table using 'ALTER TABLE .. MOVE MAPPING TABLE'.

message: mapping table cannot be dropped due to an existing bitmap index
cause: User attempted to drop the mapping table with NOMAPPING option when the IOT has one or more bitmap indexed.
solution: Drop the bitmap index(es) before dropping the mapping table.

message: UPDATE BLOCK REFERENCES may not be used on a partitioned index as a whole
cause: User attempted to UPDATE BLOCK REFERENCES on a partitioned index using ALTER INDEX UPDATE BLOCK REFERENCES statement, which is illegal.
solution: Issue a partition level operation with ALTER INDEX .. PARTITION .. UPDATE BLOCK REFERENCES

message: UPDATE BLOCK REFERENCES may not be used on a global index
cause: User attempted to UPDATE BLOCK REFERENCES on a global partitioned or non-partitioned index. This feature is not supported for non-partitioned or global partitioned index on a partitioned IOT and a global partitioned index on a non-partitioned IOT.
solution: Use online index [partition] rebuild to fix the block references

message: Merge operation not allowed on an index-organized table
cause: User attempted merge operation on an index-organized table. Merge is not supported on a IOT .
solution: Use updates and inserts on index-organized table .

message: cannot reference transient index-organized table

solution: Issue the statement against the associated permanent index-organized table.

message: Seed generation for Random Number Generator failed.
cause: Generation of seed for random number generator failed.
solution: Enable tracing and attempt the connection again. Contact Oracle customer support with the trace output.

message: The allocated buffer is too small.
cause: The output buffer is too small.
solution: Enable tracing and attempt the connection again. Contact Oracle customer support with the trace output.

message: The global context is incorrect.
cause: The global context is incorrectly configured or invalid.
solution: Enable tracing and attempt the connection again. Contact Oracle customer support with the trace output.

message: Cannot create certificate object.
cause: Creation of the certificate object failed. The application could have run out of memory.
solution: Enable tracing and attempt the connection again. Contact Oracle customer support with the trace output.

message: Cannot import in the der format.
cause: Cannot import the certificate into the certificate object. The reason could be a malformed certificate.
solution: Enable tracing and attempt the connection again. Contact Oracle customer support with the trace output.

message: DES self-test failure
cause: DES power up self-test has failed.
solution: Enable tracing and attempt the connection again. Contact Oracle customer support with the trace output.

message: 3DES self-test failure
cause: 3DES power up self-test has failed.
solution: Enable tracing and attempt the connection again. Contact Oracle customer support with the trace output.

message: SHA-1 self-test failure
cause: The SHA-1 power up self-test has failed.
solution: Enable tracing and attempt the connection again. Contact Oracle customer support with the trace output.

message: RSA self-test failure
cause: The RSA power up self-test has failed.
solution: Enable tracing and attempt the connection again. Contact Oracle customer support with the trace output.

message: deterministic RNG self-test failure
cause: The deterministic Random Number Generator power up self-test has failed.
solution: Enable tracing and attempt the connection again. Contact Oracle customer support with the trace output.

message: continuous key pair consistency check self-test failure
cause: The public-private key pair check test failed.
solution: Enable tracing and attempt the connection again. Contact Oracle customer support with the trace output.

message: conditional RNG self-test failure
cause: Continuous Random Number Generator test, which is needed in FIPS mode, has failed.
solution: Enable tracing and attempt the connection again. Contact Oracle customer support with the trace output.

message: Unable to build an absolute path to the library.
cause: Not able to construct an absolute path to the location of the library.
solution: Enable tracing and attempt the connection again. Contact Oracle customer support with the trace output.

message: Unable to open library.
cause: Opening of the library failed.
solution: Check to ensure that the library is present in the location specified, and that it has the appropriate file permissions.

message: Unable to read library.
cause: Not able to read the library on which the DAC check has to be performed. Read call failed.
solution: Check if the library has the appropriate file permissions.

message: NZ library being used is different.
cause: The NZ library being used at runtime is not the same one on which the digest was computed for the software integrity check.
solution: Check to ensure that the library being used is the same as the one on which the digest was pre-computed.

message: software integrity self-test failure
cause: The software integrity check test on the NZ shared library has failed.
solution: Check to ensure that the library being used is the same as the one on which the digest was pre-computed.

message: Non-FIPS cipher suites being used in FIPS mode.
cause: The cipher suite being used does not contain FIPS-approved algorithms.
solution: Use cipher suites that contain FIPS-approved algorithms.

message: Third party PKI vendor is not supported in FIPS mode.
cause: Third party PKI vendors like Entrust and MCS are not supported in FIPS mode.
solution: Use only Oracle PKI when running in FIPS mode.

message: External PKCS #12 wallet is not supported in FIPS mode.
cause: PKCS #12 wallets created using third party software cannot be used in FIPS mode.
solution: Use only PKCS #12 wallets created by Oracle Wallet Manager when running in FIPS mode.

message: CRL signature verification failed
cause: A CRL is verified before being used. CRL signature cannot be verified.
solution: Get a new CRL from CA

message: certificate serial number is not in CRL
cause: Cert is not revoked
solution: None

message: certificate serial number is in CRL
cause: Cert has been revoked
solution: Reject the certificate

message: certificate validation check failed
cause: Could not complete checking certificate status with a CRL.
solution: Enable tracing to find more information on this error. Contact Oracle customer support if needed.

message: Unsupported validation protocol
cause: The certificate validation protocol is not supported
solution: Make sure a supported certificate validation protocol is specified

message: ldap_open failed
cause: Could not connect to the LDAP server
solution: Ensure that correct LDAP information was provided. Enable tracing to find more information. Contact Oracle customer support if needed.

message: ldap_bind failed
cause: Could not log in to the LDAP server
solution: Ensure that correct LDAP credentials were provided. Enable tracing to find more information. Contact Oracle customer support if needed.

message: ldap_search failed
cause: Failed to complete search operation in LDAP server
solution: Enable tracing to find more information on this error. Contact Oracle customer support if needed.

message: ldap_result failed
cause: Failed to retrieve results from LDAP operation
solution: Enable tracing to find more information on this error. Contact Oracle customer support if needed.

message: ldap_first_attribute failed
cause: Could not get the first attribute from LDAP entry.
solution: Enable tracing to find more information on this error. Contact Oracle customer support if needed.

message: ldap_get_values_len failed
cause: Failed to retrieve attribute values from LDAP entry
solution: Enable tracing to find more information on this error. Contact Oracle customer support if needed.

message: unsupported validation mechanism
cause: The validation mechanism specified in OID is not supported
solution: Make sure a supported validation mechanism is set in OID

message: ldap_count_entries failed
cause: Failed to get count of entries from a search result chain.
solution: Enable tracing to find more information on this error. Contact Oracle customer support if needed.

message: No entry found in OID
cause: CRL not found in OID
solution: Upload the CRL to OID

message: Multiple entries in OID
cause: For a given issuer name there should be only one CRL in OID
solution: Make sure there is only one CRL for a given issuer name in OID

message: OID connection information not set
cause: To connect to OID the connection information must be available
solution: Set the OID connection information.

message: Validation mechanism not set in OID
cause: The validation mechanism to be used is not set in OID
solution: Set validation mechanism to be used in OID at cn=ValidationMechanism, cn=Validation, cn=PKI, cn=Products, cn=OracleContext

message: no CRL found using CRLDP mechanism
cause: A CRL could not fetched using CRL Distribution point (CRLDP)
solution: Contact the CA

message: no CRL found in cache
cause: CRL not in cache
solution: None

message: CRL is expired
cause: CRL nextUpdate time is in the past
solution: Get a new CRL from the CA

message: Distinguished name does not match.
cause: Distinguished name (DN) on certificate doesn't match user.
solution: Create the global user in the database with the DN that matches with the one in the user certificate on the client side.

message: Cannot create certificate chain.
cause: Unable to create a certificate chain with the existing trust points for the certificate that is to be installed.
solution: Install the trust point that signed the certificate.

message: Cannot locate matching certificate request.
cause: No matching certificate request for the certificate was found.
solution: Install the correct certificate.

message: Certificate already installed.
cause: Attempting to install a certificate into a persona which already has it.
solution: Do not install the certificate.

message: No matching private key found.
cause: Could not locate a matching private key in the persona for the given certificate (public key).
solution: None

message: Certificate is expired.
cause: Certificate is no longer valid..
solution: Obtain another certificate or renew this certificate.

message: Cannot calculate the number of bytes for output.
cause: The cryptographic engine is confused about the algorithm.
solution: Check the parameters being used with the cryptographic functions.

message: the magic number found in the header does not match expected
cause: The input TDU has either been corrupted or is not being used correctly.
solution: Check that the TDU is being used from the beginning. If possible, compare the size of the TDU upon generation to the size being used.

message: the header length is not sufficient for message header
cause: The input TDU has either been corrupted or it is not being used correctly.
solution: Check that the TDU is being used from the beginning. If possible, compare the size of the TDU upon generation to the size being used.

message: the cryptographic engine failed to initialize
cause: During initialization of the cryptographic engine, some failure occurred. Possible causes include running out of memory and trying to seed the random number generator.
solution: Make sure the executable has been linked with compatible library versions, and that you are not running out of swap space.

message: the cryptographic engine key initialization failed
cause: During initialization of a key for cryptography, some failure occurred. This includes running out of memory and passing illegal arguments.
solution: Make sure the executable has been linked with compatible library versions, and that the correct parameters are being used for the cryptographic functions.

message: the key object could not be encoded
cause: The key object may be corrupted or may be an unsupported type.
solution: Check the key object being passed to the encoding routine.

message: a key object was not extracted from encoding
cause: The encoding may be corrupted or may not be a key object at all.
solution: Check the encoding and parameters passed to decoding routine.

message: the key information could not be retrieved
cause: The key may be corrupted or may be an unsupported type.
solution: Check the parameters being used with the cryptographic functions.

message: the random number generator will not accept seed
cause: The cryptographic engine may have run out of memory.
solution: Make sure the executable has been linked with compatible library versions.

message: the cryptographic engine could not finish the algorithm
cause: The cryptographic engine does not have enough information to correctly finish applying the algorithm.
solution: Check the parameters being used with the cryptographic functions.

message: the cryptographic engine could not apply the algorithm
cause: The cryptographic engine does not have enough information to correctly apply the algorithm.
solution: Check the parameters being used with the cryptographic functions.

message: the cryptographic engine could not initialize the algorithm
cause: The cryptographic engine does not have enough information to correctly initialize the algorithm.
solution: Check the parameters being used with the cryptographic functions.

message: the cryptographic engine does not recognize the algorithm
cause: The application may be passing wrong parameters.
solution: Check the parameters being used with the cryptographic functions.

message: a buffer block needs more space but its length is fixed
cause: The application has preallocated an output buffer that is too short for the operation and has specified that the buffer should not grow as needed.
solution: Either preallocate a larger buffer or allow the toolkit to grow the output buffer as needed.

message: the asymmetric key is too short to be used with the data.
cause: An asymmetric key must be at least 11 bytes longer than the data it is being used to encrypt.
solution: Use an asymmetric key with more bits or break the data into smaller pieces.

message: the toolkit does not recognize the type of key being used
cause: The application may be passing wrong parameters.
solution: Check the parameters being used with the toolkit functions.

message: the toolkit does not recognize the function being used
cause: The application is probably passing the wrong parameters.
solution: Check the parameters being used with the toolkit functions.

message: the toolkit could not parse the tdu
cause: The TDU could be corrupted.
solution: Check the parameters being used with the toolkit functions.

message: an unopen toolkit object was used before it was opened
cause: Some toolkit objects must be opened before they can be used.
solution: Check the parameters being used with the toolkit functions.

message: an unrecognized WRL was used to open a wallet
cause: WRL's have a specific set of types and must be formatted correctly.
solution: Check the parameters being used with the toolkit functions.

message: an unrecognized state was passed to a cryptographic function
cause: The application is probably passing the wrong parameters.
solution: Check the parameters being used with the toolkit functions.

message: Invalid index specifed in call to dbms_sql.bind_array
cause: An invalid index was specified in a call to bind_array of dbms_sql. The index may have been null or of an improper value.
solution: Correct the index value by modifying your PL/SQL program and try the bind_array call again.

message: Index1 is greater than Index2 in call to dbms_sql.bind_array
cause: The value of index1 was greater than the value for index2 in the call to bind_array. This is illegal since the elements of the table that will be bound are those with indexes greater than or equal to index1 and less than or equal to index2.
solution: Correct the value of the two indexes and try the call to again bind_array.

message: collection does not contain elements at index locations in call to dbms_sql.bind_array
cause: The bound table does not contain elements at both index locations in call to bind_array of dbms_sql. This is illegal. Both index locations must contain elements. In other words tab.exists(index1) and tab.exists(index2) must both return true.
solution: Either modify the two indexes or the contents of the table and try the call again.

message: Invalid count argument passed to procedure dbms_sql.define_array
cause: The count argument specified in the call to procedure define_array of package dbms_sql had an invalid value. Invalid values are negative numbers and nulls. The argument must be a positive integer.
solution: Correct your PL/SQL program so that only valid arguments are passed to define_array and try again.

message: Invalid lower_bound argument passed to procedure dbms_sql.define_array
cause: The lower_bound argument specified in the call to procedure define_array had an invalid value. Legal values are all integers (both positive and negative) including zero. The null value is illegal.
solution: Correct your PL/SQL program so that only valid arguments are passed to define_array and try again.

message: Cursor contains both bind and define arrays which is not permissible
cause: Both define_array and bind_array have been called on this cursor. This is illegal. It is not possible for a cursor to both contain array binds and array defines. The semantics of this setting are nonsensical. Array defines are used to move data from select queries into PL/SQL tables and array binds to bind PL/SQL tables to non-select queries.
solution: Modify your PL/SQL program to only perform calls to one of the two functions depending on the kind of cursor at hand.

message: Cursor contains both regular and array defines which is illegal
cause: Both define_array and define_column have been called on this cursor. This is illegal. It is not possible for a cursor to both contain regular and array defines. The semantics of this setting are nonsensical. Array defines are used to move data from select queries into PL/SQL tables and regular defines to move data from select queries into PL/SQL variables.
solution: Modify your PL/SQL program to only perform calls to one of the two functions depending on the situation at hand.

message: host string unknown
cause: The specified host was unknown.
solution: Check the spelling of the host name or the IP address. Make sure that the host name or the IP address is valid.

message: buffer too small
cause: The input or output buffer was too small for the operation.
solution: Increase the size of the buffer and retry the operation.

message: end-of-input reached
cause: The end of the input was reached.
solution: If the end of the input is reached prematurely, check if the input source terminates prematurely. Otherwise, close the connection to the input.

message: network error: string
cause: A network error occurred.
solution: Fix the network error and retry the operation.

message: bad argument
cause: A bad argument was passed to the PL/SQL API.
solution: Check the arguments passed to the PL/SQL API and retry the call.

message: bad URL
cause: An improperly formed URL was passed to the PL/SQL API.
solution: Check the URL and retry the call.

message: HTTP protocol error
cause: A HTTP protocol error occured during the HTTP operation.
solution: Check the HTTP server that the HTTP operation was performed to make sure that it follows the HTTP protocol standard.

message: unknown or unsupported URL scheme
cause: The URL scheme was unknown or unsupported.
solution: Check the URL to make sure that the scheme is valid and supported.

message: HTTP header not found
cause: The requested HTTP header was not found.
solution: Check to make sure that the requested HTTP header is present.

message: end-of-body reached
cause: The end of the HTTP response body was reached.
solution: If the end of the HTTP response is reached prematurely, check if the HTTP response terminates prematurely. Otherwise, end the HTTP response.

message: illegal call
cause: The call to the PL/SQL API was illegal at the current stage of the operation.
solution: Retry the call at a different stage of the operation.

message: HTTP client error string
cause: The HTTP response indicated that the HTTP client error occurred.
solution: Fix the HTTP client error and retry the HTTP request.

message: HTTP server error string
cause: The HTTP response indicated that the HTTP server error occurred.
solution: Fix the HTTP server error and retry the HTTP request. Contact the admistrator of the HTTP server when necessary.

message: too many open HTTP requests
cause: Too many HTTP requests were opened.
solution: End some HTTP requests and retry the HTTP request.

message: not connected
cause: The network connection was not made while the network operation was attempted.
solution: Retry the network operation after the network connection is made successfully.

message: initialization failed
cause: The UTL_HTTP package failed to initialize.
solution: Free up some memory or other system resources and retry the operation.

message: HTTP request failed
cause: The UTL_HTTP package failed to execute the HTTP request.
solution: Use get_detailed_sqlerrm to check the detailed error message. Fix the error and retry the HTTP request.

message: fixed-width multibyte character set not allowed for a URL
cause: The character set used as an encoding of the URL is a fixed-width multibyte character set and is not allowed for a URL.
solution: Use the corresponding variable-width multibyte character set for the URL instead.

message: partial multibyte character
cause: The requested read operation could not complete because a partial multibyte character was found at the end of the input.
solution: Ensure that the complete multibyte character is sent from the remote server and retry the operation. Or read the partial multibyte character as RAW.

message: transfer timeout
cause: Timeout occurred while reading from or writing to a network connection.
solution: Check the remote server or the network to ensure that it responds within the timeout limit. Or increase the timeout value.

message: invalid SMTP operation
cause: The SMTP operation was invalid at the current stage of the SMTP transaction.
solution: Retry the SMTP operation at the appropriate stage of the SMTP transaction.

message: SMTP transient error: string
cause: A SMTP transient error occurred.
solution: Correct the error and retry the SMTP operation.

message: SMTP permanent error: string
cause: A SMTP permanent error occurred.
solution: Correct the error and retry the SMTP operation.

message: invalid directory path
cause: A corresponding directory object does not exist.
solution: Correct the directory object parameter, or create a corresponding directory object with the CREATE DIRECTORY command.

message: invalid mode
cause: An invalid value was specified for file open mode.
solution: Correct the mode to be one of the values: 'r','a', or 'w'.

message: invalid file ID
cause: A file ID handle was specified for which no corresponding open file exists.
solution: Verify that the file ID handle is a value returned from a call to UTL_FILE.FOPEN.

message: file read error
cause: An attempt to read from a file failed.
solution: Verify that the file exists, and that it is accessible, and that it is open in read mode.

message: file write error
cause: Failed to write to, flush, or close a file.
solution: Verify that the file exists, that it is accessible, and that it is open in write or append mode.

message: internal error
cause: A fatal error occurred while allocating PL/SQL session memory.
solution: Verify that the PL/SQL session is connected and that adequate memory resources are available.

message: invalid maximum line size
cause: An invalid maximum line size value was specified.
solution: Correct the maximum line size to be in the range [1, 32767].

message: invalid file name
cause: A NULL or zero length file name was specified.
solution: Correct the file name to be a nonzero length string.

message: directory access denied
cause: A directory object was specified for which no access is granted.
solution: Grant access to the directory object using the command GRANT READ ON DIRECTORY [object] TO [username];.

message: invalid offset specified for seek
cause: An attempt was made to seek past the end of the file, or both the absolute and relative offsets were NULL, or absolute offset was less than zero.
solution: If specifying an absolute offset, ensure it is in the range [0, <total number of bytes in the file>], or if specifying a relative offset, ensure it is no greater than the current byte position plus the number of bytes remaining in the file.

message: file remove operation failed
cause: A file deletion attempt was refused by the operating system.
solution: Verify that the file exists and delete privileges granted on the directory and the file.

message: file rename operation failed
cause: A file rename attempt was refused by the operating system either because the source or destination directory does not exist or is inaccessible, or the source file isn't accessible, or the destination file exists.
solution: Verify that the source file, source directory, and destination directory exist and are accessible, and that the destination file does not already exist.

message: A stream error occurred during compression or uncompression.
cause: The stream state was discovered to be invalid during compression or uncompression, or an invalid compression quality was requested or a NULL or invalid compression parameter was detected.
solution: Verify that quality is within the range [0,9] and that valid input source data exists.

message: A data error occurred during compression or uncompression.
cause: An error occurred while compressing or uncompressing input source.
solution: Verify that source data is a valid compressed or uncompressed data set.

message: invalid mime header tag
cause: An error occurred while scanning string for mime header tag
solution: Verify that source data is a valid mime header string, in the format: =?<charset>?<encoding>?<encoded string>?=

message: invalid encoded string
cause: An error occurred while decoding the input string
solution: Verify that source data is a valid encoded string.

message: The compressed representation is too big
cause: The compressed output is too big to return.
solution: Do not attempt to compress source data.

message: Character set mismatch
cause: The character set mode in which the file was opened did not match the character set of the read or write operation.
solution: Use the correct UTL_FILE read and write procedures which coorespond to the character set mode in which the file was opened.

message: Invalid handle for piecewise compress or uncompress
cause: The process program opened too many handles, and the specified handle was either uninitialized or outside a valid range.
solution: Close some handles and verify that the specified handle is opened or within a valid range.

message: ORACLE error, tablespace point-in-time recovery
cause: Another ORACLE error occured in the DBMS_PITR package.
solution: See the text of the error message for a description of the error.

message: wrong DBMS_PITR package function/procedure order
cause: The DBMS_PITR package function/procedure was called in an incorrect order.
solution: Restart tablespace point-in-time recovery with a correct procedure.

message: database is not open clone
cause: The database was not opened as a clone database.
solution: Mount the database clone and open the database.

message: user does not login as SYS
cause: The user did not log in as SYS to perform tablespace point-in-time recovery in a clone database.
solution: Log in as SYS and restart tablespace point-in-time recovery.

message: tablespace ' string ' does not exist
cause: The selected tablespace does not exist in the database.
solution: Check the list of tablespaces in V$TABLESPACE and select a valid tablespace.

message: cannot point-in-time recover tablespace ' string '
cause: An attempt was made to ALTER the tablespace to be read only.
solution: Check if the tablespace is SYSTEM or with online rollback segment.

message: datafile string is not online
cause: The selected datafile was not online.
solution: Bring the the datafile online and rename it if necessary.

message: datafile string error, string
cause: The datafile is not ready for tablespace point-in-time recovery.
solution: Check the correct tablespace point-in-time recovery procedure.

message: view TS_PITR_CHECK failure
cause: Some objects which crossed the boundary of the recovery set were not allowed in the tabelspace point-in-time recovery.
solution: Query TS_PITR_CHECK and resolve the boundary crossing objects.

message: export dump file was generated by different version of DBMS_PITR package
cause: The version of DBMS_PITR is different from the version of the cloned database.
solution: Load the version of DBMS_PITR which matches the version of the cloned database.

message: database is not open, or opened as a clone
cause: Either the database was not open, or an attempt was made to open it as a cloned database.
solution: Open the production database instead.

message: export dump file was not generated by this database, string does not match
cause: The export dump files were imported to an incorrect database.
solution: Open the correct production database and try the import again.

message: tablespace ' string ' cannot be imported twice
cause: This is an internal error.
solution: Contact your database administrator.

message: tablespace ' string ' is not OFFLINE FOR RECOVER nor READ ONLY
cause: Tablespace clean SCN is either 0 or invalid.
solution: ALTER the tablespace OFFLINE FOR RECOVER.

message: tablespace ' string ' has been recreated
cause: An attempt was made to recover a tablespace to a point-in-time before it was recreated.
solution: Choose a different point in time for recovery.

message: datafile string been imported twice
cause: This is an internal error.
solution: Contact your database administrator.

message: datafile string does not exist
cause: The specified datafile could not be found in the production database.
solution: Copy the datafile from the clone database.

message: datafile string is online
cause: The datafile is online.
solution: Take the datafile offline.

message: datafile string is not correct
cause: An incorrect datafile was copied to the production database. The datafile information in the export dump file differs with the information in the datafile in the production database.
solution: Copy the datafile from the clone database to the production database.

message: datafile header error
cause: An error occured during reading datafile header.
solution: Copy the correct datafile from the clone database to the production database, then retry the operation.

message: too many datafiles added since the point-in-time
cause: Too many datafiles were added to the recovery set since the point-in-time recovery.
solution: Divide the recovery set into smaller subsets and retry.

message: SCN string size too long -- maximum size 58 bytes/characters
cause: Too many characters in specifying the SCN string
solution: Remove all unnecessary characters. Only 15 characters are required for both the hex and decimal representation of the 48 bit SCN.

message: ALTER DATABASE SET COMPATIBILITY command not supported by string
cause: The ALTER DATABASE SET COMPATIBILITY command failed because one or more instances do not support dynamic compatible setting change.
solution: No action required.

message: SET COMPATIBILITY release string format is wrong
cause: It should be of the form x.x.x
solution: Use the correct format.

message: SET COMPATIBILITY release number lower than string
cause: The SET COMPATIBILITY release compatibility release number was lower than the current compatible setting.
solution: Specify a higher release number.

message: SET COMPATIBILITY release number higher than string
cause: The ALTER DATABASE SET COMPATIBILITY command failed because one or more instances had a lower release number.
solution: Specify a lower release number.

message: unsupported client compatibility mode used when talking to the server
cause: The client compatibility mode is higher than the version of the server.
solution: Using SET COMPATIBILITY command, specify the same release number as the server.

message: too many datafiles in this tablespace ' string '
cause: Too many datafiles in this bitmap tablespace. ORACLE does not support at this moment.
solution: Call Oracle Support.

message: Table not of type XMLType
cause: Table is not XMLType table
solution: Ensure table is a XMLType table

message: Source script length too big
cause: Source script length exceeded the maximum size of 4 Gigabytes.
solution: Make sure source script length is not greater than 4 Gigabytes.

message: tablespace ' string ' is not read only
cause: The tablespace is not read only.
solution: Make the tablespace read only and retry the operation.

message: Internal error [ string ] [ string ] from DBMS_PLUGTS
cause: Internal error from package DBMS_PLUGTS.
solution: Call Oracle Support.

message: tablespace ' string ' has a non-standard block size ( string )
cause: The tablespace has a non-standard block size and making such a tablespace read-write is not permitted.
solution: Use some other mechanism to import the data

message: datafile string is in an undesired state ( string , string )
cause: The referred datafile is not in a state ready for tablespace copy operation. For example, the datafile may be offline. The datafile needs to be ONLINE, and either READ ONLY or READ WRITE.
solution: Put the datafile into the desired state.

message: tablespace block size string does not match configured block sizes
cause: The block size of the tablespace to be plugged in or created does not match the block sizes configured in the database.
solution: Configure the appropriate cache for the block size of this tablespace using one of the various (db_2k_cache_size, db_4k_cache_size, db_8k_cache_size, db_16k_cache_size, db_32K_cache_size) parameters.

message: export file appears to be corrupted: [ string ] [ string ] [ string ]
cause: This is caused either by a corrupted export file or by an Oracle internal error.
solution: Make sure the export file used for transportable tablespace is not corrupted. If the error still occurs, call Oracle support.

message: The transportable set is not self-contained
cause: The set of objects in the set of tablespaces selected are not self-contained.
solution: Consider using different export options, or removing some of the pointers that caused the violation, or selecting a different set of tablespaces.

message: user string does not exist in the database
cause: The referred user is one of the owners of data in the pluggable set. This user does not exist in the database.
solution: Consider either creating the user in the database or map the user to a different user via FROM_USER and TO_USER import options.

message: user string (mapped from user string ) does not exist in the database
cause: The referred user is one of the owners of data in the pluggable set. This user does not exist in the database.
solution: Consider either creating the user or map the original user to a different user.

message: Owner validation failed - failed to match owner ' string '
cause: The system failed to match the referred owner. There are two cases that this may occur. (1) This user owns data in the transportable set, but this user is not specified in the TTS_OWNERS list of the import command line option, assuming that TTS_OWNERS is specified. (2) This user is specified in the TTS_OWNER list, but this user does not own any data in the transportable set.
solution: Retry import with a different OWNER list.

message: cannot plug a tablespace into a database using an incompatible character set
cause: Oracle does not support plugging a tablespace into a database using an incompatible character set.
solution: Use import/export or unload/load to move data instead.

message: invalid tablespace list
cause: the tablespace list supplied to dbms_tts.transport_set_check PL/SQL routine is in an incorrect format.
solution: Check the manual and use the correct format.

message: Tablespace name validation failed - failed to match tablespace ' string '
cause: The system failed to match the referred tablespace. There are 2 cases that this may happen. (1) This tablespace is in the transportable set, but it is not specified in the TABLESPACES list of the import command line option, assuming that TABLESPACES is specified. (2) This tablespace is in the TABLESPACES list, but it is not in the transportable set.
solution: Retry the operation with the correct TABLESPACES list.

message: You must specify the datafiles to be plugged in
cause: The datafiles to be plugged in are not specified.
solution: Specify the datafiles via the import DATAFILES command line option.

message: tablespace ' string ' already exists
cause: Tried to plug-in a tablespace which already exists.
solution: Drop the offending tablespace if possible. Otherwise use a different method (e.g., import/export) to move data.

message: can not transport system, sysaux, or temporary tablespace ' string '
cause: The referred tablespace is either the system tablespace, the sysaux tablespace, or a temporary tablespace.
solution: Do not include this tablespace in the transportable set.

message: event ' string ' is not an internal event
cause: The DBMS_SYSTEM.WAIT_FOR_EVENT procedure was called with an event name that is not an internal event.
solution: Check the list of events from X$KSLED and verify the event name parameter passed to the WAIT_FOR_EVENT procedure.

message: The transportable list is too long.
cause: The transportable list exceeds the buffer size of 32767.
solution: Reduce the list of tablespaces to transport.

message: NULL or invalid string argument specified
cause: The named argument was either invalid or specified as a NULL
solution: Specify non-null, valid arguments.

message: These parameters can be specified only for directives that refer to consumer groups
cause: The below parameters were specified as an argument to procedure CREATE_PLAN_DIRECTIVE or UPDATE_PLAN_DIRECTIVE of package DBMS_RESOURCE_MANAGER.where the GROUP_OR_SUBPLAN argument is a resource plan. "ACTIVE_SESS_POOL_P1", "QUEUEING_P1", "PARALLEL_DEGREE_LIMIT_P1", "SWITCH_P1", "SWITCH_P2", "SWITCH_P3", "MAX_EST_EXEC_TIME", "UNDO_POOL"
solution: Specify these parameters only for consumer group directives.

message: object string already exists
cause: The name specified as argument to procedure CREATE_PLAN, CREATE_CONSUMER_GROUP, or CREATE_CATEGORY of package DBMS_RESOURCE_MANAGER is already in use.
solution: Specify an unused name.

message: resource plan string does not exist
cause: An invalid plan name was specified as an argument to procedure UPDATE_PLAN of package DBMS_RESOURCE_MANAGER.
solution: Specify an existing plan name.

message: invalid method name string specified for resource plan string
cause: An invalid method was specified as an argument to procedure CREATE_PLAN or UPDATE_PLAN of package DBMS_RESOURCE_MANAGER.
solution: Specify a valid method name.

message: resource plan string contains multiple directives for subplan string
cause: A resource plan and its subplans had more than one directive for a particular subplan.
solution: Modify the resource plan or its subplans so that there is at most one directive for this subplan.

message: value string is outside valid range of 0 to 100
cause: An invalid value was specified for a plan directive parameter.
solution: Specify a value between 0 and 100 inclusive.

message: plan directive string , string does not exist
cause: A non-existent plan directive was specified for procedure UPDATE_PLAN_DIRECTIVE of package DBMS_RESOURCE_MANAGER.
solution: Specify an existing plan directive for update.

message: plan directive string , string is mandatory and cannot be modified or deleted
cause: An attempt was made to modify a mandatory plan directive.
solution: Do not attempt to modify mandatory plan directives because they are required by the Resource Manager and cannot be modified.

message: plan directive string , string already exists
cause: An attempt was made to create a plan directive that already exists.
solution: Retry the create operation using different values.

message: parameters string and string cannot both be set
cause: An attempt was made to set both parameters.
solution: Only set one of parameters or neither of them.

message: invalid CONSUMER_GROUP argument specified
cause: An invalid consumer group name was specified.
solution: Specify a non-NULL, valid consumer group name.

message: object string does not exist
cause: A non-existent object name was specified as an argument to procedure CREATE_PLAN_DIRECTIVE of package DBMS_RESOURCE_MANAGER.
solution: Specify a valid plan or consumer group name.

message: consumer group string does not exist
cause: An non-existent consumer group was specified.
solution: Specify an existing consumer group.

message: invalid method name string specified for consumer group string
cause: An invalid method name was specified as an argument to procedure CREATE_CONSUMER_GROUP or UPDATE_CONSUMER_GROUP of package DBMS_RESOURCE_MANAGER.
solution: Specify a valid method name.

message: pending area is already active
cause: An attempt was made to activate a pending area that is already active.
solution: Wait until the pending area is no longer active; then, retry the operation.

message: pending area is not active
cause: An attempt was made to make changes without creating a pending area.
solution: Invoke procedure CREATE_PENDING_AREA before making any changes.

message: identifier string is too long; it must be less than string characters
cause: An attempt was made to specify an identifier that is more than 30 characters long.
solution: Use an identifier that is 30 characters or less in length.

message: resource manager is not on
cause: An attempt was made to execute an operation that cannot be executed with the resource manager being off
solution: Turn on the resource manager and try again.

message: resource plan string in top-plan string has no plan directives
cause: A plan was created in the pending area that is an orphan or stand-alone.
solution: Create plan directives if needed. Otherwise, delete the plan.

message: sum of values string for level string , plan string exceeds string
cause: The sum of plan directive parameter values for the specified plan level exceeded 100.
solution: Alter the values for the level so that they sum to 100.

message: number of consumer groups string in plan string exceeds string
cause: The number of consumer groups in the specified plan was more than 28.
solution: Change the plan to have no more than 28 consumer groups.

message: consumer group string is not part of top-plan string
cause: OTHER_GROUPS was not included as part of the specified top-plan. Each top plan must include the built-in consumer group OTHER_GROUPS.
solution: Create a plan directive with the argument GROUP_OR_SUBPLAN being OTHER_GROUPS somewhere in the top-plan.

message: invalid consumer group mapping priorities
cause: The mapping priorities were not unique integers within the valid range.
solution: Set the mapping priorities to unique integers within the documented range.

message: resource plan string is involved in a loop in top-plan string
cause: A loop was discovered while validating a top-plan.
solution: Check the plans that have the specified plan as a GROUP_OR_SUBPLAN, and remove the plan directive that causes the loop.

message: resource plan string is currently active and cannot be deleted
cause: An attempt was made to delete an active plan in the pending area. No changes can be made to active plans.
solution: Delete the plan when it is not in use.

message: plan/consumer_group string referred to by another plan and cannot be deleted
cause: An attempt was made to delete a plan or consumer group that is referred to by another plan.
solution: Remove all plan directives that have the plan or consumer group as GROUP_OR_SUBPLAN; then delete the plan or consumer group.

message: validation of pending area failed
cause: Invalid changes were attempted in the pending area.
solution: See documentation and the error messages that follow this one.

message: all leaves of top-plan string must be consumer groups
cause: An attempt was made to create or modify the specified top-plan but it has some plans as leaves.
solution: To identify which plans and/or plan directives need to be modified, look at all plans that have no plan directives. Then, alter the top-plan so that all its leaves are consumer groups.

message: number of consumer groups and subplans for plan string exceeds string
cause: An attempt was made to create or modify the specified plan, but the plan has more than 28 consumer groups or subplans.
solution: Make sure the specified plan points to no more than 28 distinct consumer groups or subplans.

message: cannot create plan directive from string to string
cause: An attempt was made to create a plan directive from a plan to itself.
solution: Make sure the arguments PLAN and GROUP_OR_SUBPLAN to procedure CREATE_PLAN_DIRECTIVE of package DBMS_RESOURCE_MANAGER are different.

message: plan or consumer group string is mandatory and cannot be deleted or modified
cause: An attempt was made to delete or modify the specified mandatory plan or consumer group.
solution: Do not attempt to delete or modify mandatory plans and consumer groups.

message: no top-plans found in the pending area
cause: The VALIDATE_PENDING_AREA procedure found that either the intended top-plan(s) are involved in a loop or there are no top-plans.
solution: Check all edges going from a subplan to the intended top-plan. Make sure the top plan does not have any plan referring to it.

message: plan/consumer_group string is part of more than one top-plan
cause: An attempt was made to delete a subtree that includes a plan or consumer group that is part of more than one top-plan as part of procedure DELETE_PLAN_CASCADE or package DBMS_RESOURCE_MANAGER. Such a plan or consumer group cannot be deleted.
solution: Check the ancestors of the plan or consumer group and make sure it is only part of the top-plan that includes the subtree being deleted.

message: too many errors during validation
cause: The number of errors detected during validation is too high.
solution: Perform the necessary actions to remove some errors, and retry validation.

message: some resource plans are not part of any top-plan
cause: An attempt was made to create or modify some plans in the pending area that are not part of any top-plan
solution: Remove these plans are try validation again.

message: string and string must be mandatory to create a mandatory plan directive
cause: An attempt was made to create a mandatory plan directive where either PLAN or GROUP_OR_SUBPLAN or both were not mandatory
solution: Recreate these objects as mandatory and then create the plan directive.

message: cpu parameters for level string for plan string must be zero
cause: The cpu parameters for the specified level had a non-zero value, which is not a valid value for the plan's current cpu policy.
solution: Change the cpu level parameters for the specified level to zero or change the plan cpu policy.

message: user string does not exist or is not logged on
cause: An invalid user name was specified as argument to procedure SET_INITIAL_CONSUMER_GROUP of package DBMS_RESOURCE_MANAGER or SWITCH_CONSUMER_GROUP_FOR_USER of package DBMS_SYSTEM or the specified user was not logged on.
solution: Specify a valid user name.

message: session id string and serial# string do not exist
cause: Invalid session id and serial# were specified as arguments to procedure SWITCH_CONSUMER_GROUP_FOR_SESS of package DBMS_SYSTEM.
solution: Specify valid values from the view V$SESSION.

message: cannot set the initial consumer group to string
cause: An attempt was made to set the initial consumer group of a user to OTHER_GROUPS or an INTERNAL_USE group.
solution: Certain groups are only for the resource manager's internal use. Specify another consumer group.

message: cannot switch group to string
cause: An attempt was made to switch the consumer group of a user or a session to OTHER_GROUPS or an INTERNAL_USE group.
solution: Certain groups are only for the resource manager's internal use. Specify another consumer group.

message: cannot grant/revoke switch privilege for string
cause: An attempt was made to grant or revoke the privilege to switch to OTHER_GROUPS or an INTERNAL_USE group.
solution: Certain groups are only for the resource manager's internal use. Specify another consumer group.

message: invalid privilege name specified
cause: An invalid privilege name was specified as an argument to procedure GRANT_SYSTEM_PRIVILEGE or REVOKE_SYSTEM_PRIVILEGE of package DBMS_RESOURCE_MANAGER_PRIVS.
solution: Specify a valid privilege name.

message: user string does not have privilege to switch to consumer group string
cause: An attempt was made to set the initial consumer group of the specified user but the user does not have the privilege to switch to that group.
solution: Grant the privilege to switch to the consumer group to the user and then set the initial group.

message: data cartridge error string
cause: An error has occurred in a data cartridge external procedure. This message will be followed by a second message giving more details about the data cartridge error.
solution: See the data cartridge documentation for an explanation of the second error message.

message: Effective userid or roles are not the same as when cursor was parsed
cause: The effective userid or roles on this call to DBMS_SQL are not the same as those at the time the cursor was parsed.
solution: Make sure the effective userid and roles are the same as when cursor was pared.

message: DBMS_SQL access denied
cause: DBMS_SQL access was denied due to security concerns.
solution: Check the alert log and trace file for more information.

message: DBMS_SQL.OPEN_CURSOR failed. security_level is outside the valid range of 0 to 2
cause: An invalid security_level value was specified.
solution: Specify a valid range of 0 to 2.

message: privilege checking level specified for ' string ' must be between 0 and 2
cause: Invalid privilege checking level specified.
solution: Correct the privilege checking level specified.

message: DBMS_SQL.OPEN_CURSOR failed. security_level of 0 is not allowed
cause: Security level of 0 is specified with DBMS_SQL.OPEN_CURSOR.
solution: Specify a valid security level.

message: useLogonRoles=>TRUE not permitted with userid=>NULL
cause: An unsupported combination of argument values was present in a call to DBMS_SYS_SQL.PARSE_AS_USER.
solution: Specify a valid combination of argument values.

message: DBMS_SQL.CLOSE_CURSOR failed
cause: An attempt was made to close a DBMS_SQL cursor while it was executing under its own context.
solution: Rewrite the program so that it does not attempt to close a DBMS_SQL cursor while it is executing under its own context.

message: SQL statement size in bytes is too big
cause: The size of the SQL statement exceeded 4 gigabytes -1.
solution: Reduce the size of the SQL statement.

message: insufficient privilege
cause: The ADM_PARALLEL_EXECUTE role needed to execute the subprogram was not granted.
solution: Obtain ADM_PARALLEL_EXECUTE role and try again.

message: invalid table for chunking
cause: An attempt was made to chunk a table by ROWID, but the table was not a physical table or the table was an IOT. physical table or the table is an IOT.
solution: Use a table which has physical ROWID.

message: invalid state for create chunk
cause: An attempt was made to create chunks on a task which was not in the CREATED state.
solution: Make sure that the task is in the CREATED state.

message: invalid status
cause: An attempt was made to set an invalid value to the chunk status.
solution: Make sure that the status value is valid.

message: invalid state for run task
cause: An attempt was made to execute the task which was not in the CHUNKED state.
solution: Make sure that the task is in the CHUNKED state.

message: invalid state for resume task
cause: An attempt was made to resume execution but the task was not the FINISHED_WITH_ERROR or CRASHED state.
solution: Make sure that the task is in the FINISHED_WITH_ERROR or CRASHED state.

message: Parameter [ string ] is null or its value length exceeds the maximum limit [ string ]
cause: The input argument was null, or it exceeded the maximum length limit.
solution: Make sure that the argument is not null, and its length is within the limit.

message: duplicate task name
cause: A task with the same name was already in existence.
solution: Use another name.

message: task not found
cause: The task did not exist.
solution: Use an existing task.

message: chunk not found
cause: The specified chunk did not exist.
solution: Specify an existing chunk.

message: NAMED keyword is invalid in CREATE JAVA CLASS
cause: A NAMED keyword was specified in the CREATE JAVA CLASS statement. NAMED keywords are valid only in CREATE JAVA SOURCE or RESOURCE statements.
solution: Remove the NAMED keyword from the CREATE JAVA CLASS statement.

message: invalid or missing Java source, class, or resource name
cause: The required name for a Java source, class, or resource was invalid or missing.
solution: Specify a valid name.

message: NAMED keyword required in CREATE JAVA RESOURCE
cause: The name for a Java resource was not specified. The name must be specified with the NAMED keyword.
solution: Specify a valid name with the NAMED keyword.

message: SCHEMA keyword not valid with NAMED keyword
cause: SCHEMA and NAMED keywords were used together in the same CREATE JAVA command, but only one may be used in a CREATE JAVA command.
solution: Remove either the NAMED or the SCHEMA keyword.

message: invalid or missing schema name
cause: The required schema name was invalid or missing.
solution: Specify a valid schema name.

message: AS keyword is invalid in CREATE JAVA CLASS or RESOURCE
cause: The AS keyword was used in CREATE JAVA CLASS or RESOURCE. The AS keyword is valid only in CREATE JAVA SOURCE.
solution: Use the USING keyword in CREATE JAVA CLASS or RESOURCE.

message: invalid query derived from USING clause
cause: The USING clause did not form a valid query.
solution: Correct the USING clause.

message: query derived from USING clause found zero or many rows
cause: The USING clause defined a query that either did not return any values, or returned more than one value.
solution: Correct the USING clause.

message: query derived from USING clause did not select a value of type string
cause: The USING clause did not form a query that selects a value of the type specified by the term following the USING keyword.
solution: Correct the USING clause.

message: incorrectly formed Java binary class definition
cause: An attempt was made to create a Java class using data expected to be in binary (Java .class) format. The data was found not to be in this format, or to be incorrectly formed.
solution: Correct the definition data.

message: name, string . string , already used by an existing object
