cause: A CREATE JAVA command attempted to create a source, class, or resource object with a name that is already in use.
solution: Drop the existing object that is using the desired name, or use a different name for the new object.

message: could not resolve Java class
cause: A CREATE AND RESOLVE NOFORCE JAVA CLASS command specified definition data that could not be resolved, or resolution failed for some referenced class.
solution: Remove the NOFORCE option or remove impediments to resolution.

message: incorrectly formed name resolver specification
cause: A name resolver was not specified in the required form: (( <name pattern> , <schema name>) ...)
solution: Correct the specification.

message: referenced class name too long
cause: An attempt was made to import a .class file containing a class name of length greater than %d. The .class file could not be imported because the referenced class name was too long.
solution: Shorten the referenced class name in the .class file.

message: class name contains illegal character
cause: An attempt was made to import a .class file containing a character that cannot be converted to the server character set. The .class file could not be imported because of the illegal character.
solution: Correct the illegal character in the .class file.

message: exit called from Java code with status string
cause: Java code included a call to java.lang.Runtime.exitInternal.
solution: Do not include this call unless non-local exit is desired.

message: Aurora assertion failure: string
cause: An internal error occurred in the Aurora module.
solution: Contact Oracle Worldwide Support.

message: recursive resolution failed for a referenced class
cause: An attempt to resolve a referenced class failed.
solution: Review the errors for referenced classes and complete the necessary actions to correct them.

message: name string resolved to an object in schema string that is not a Java class
cause: A referenced name was resolved to an object that is not a Java class.
solution: Adjust name resolver or add missing Java class.

message: name string resolved via a synonym in schema string to a class with a different name
cause: A referenced name was resolved to a synonym, which translated to a class whose name does not match the referenced name.
solution: Adjust name resolver or add missing Java class.

message: name string resolved to a class in schema string that could not be accessed
cause: An attempt to access a referenced class failed.
solution: Adjust authorizations or name resolution.

message: referenced name string could not be found
cause: Name resolution failed to find an object with the indicated name.
solution: Adjust name resolver or add missing Java class.

message: authorization error for referenced name string . string
cause: An attempt was made to resolve a class that is not authorized to use the indicated referenced class.
solution: Adjust authorizations or name resolution.

message: authorization error for unknown referenced name
cause: An attempt was made to resolve a class that is not authorized to use a referenced class. The name of the referenced class could not be determined.
solution: Adjust authorizations or name resolution.

message: wrong types of arguments in call to ' string '
cause: A method was called with argument(s) of incompatible type(s).
solution: Adjust caller.

message: referenced name is too long: ' string '
cause: An attempt was made to create a class that references a name longer than 4000 characters. The class could not be created because the name is too long.
solution: Adjust the definition.

message: created Java class string " string "
cause: An informational message, not an error.
solution: None

message: created Java source string " string "
cause: An informational message, not an error.
solution: None

message: invalid Java call in trigger string
cause: The Java method specified in trigger does not exist or cannot be called as used.
solution: Adjust trigger definition.

message: invalid function or method call string in trigger string
cause: The function or method specified in Java trigger call expression could not be resolved.
solution: Adjust trigger definition.

message: could not create shortened name for string
cause: Insert into shortened name translation table failed.
solution: Retry the insert.

message: no method string in class string
cause: An attempt was made to execute a non-existent method in a Java class.
solution: Adjust the call or create the specified method.

message: Java call terminated by uncaught Java exception: string
cause: A Java exception or error was signaled and could not be resolved by the Java code.
solution: Modify Java code, if this behavior is not intended.

message: attempt to overwrite class or resource string while defining or compiling string . string
cause: A class or resource defined by a SQLJ source conflicted with an existing object.
solution: Remove existing object, or modify SQLJ source.

message: referenced object string . string could not be resolved
cause: Name resolution determined that the indicated object is referenced but could not be resolved.
solution: Correct name resolver or address resolution problems in the referenced class, or correct compilation problems in its source.

message: source requires recompilation
cause: The reason the current class object was invalid is recorded with the source object from which it was compiled.
solution: Inspect errors in the source object and take the necessary corrective actions.

message: badly formed source: string
cause: An attempt was made to create a Java source object with text that could not be parsed adequately to determine the class(es) defined by it.
solution: Correct errors in source.

message: class or resource cannot be created or dropped directly
cause: An attempt was made to create or drop a Java class or resource that is known to result from compilation of an existing Java source object.
solution: Act on the class or resource by acting on the source, or change the source so that it no longer defines the class or resource.

message: Java not installed
cause: An attempt was made to use a Java command when Java is not installed.
solution: Install Java, or do not use the command.

message: Java system classes already installed
cause: An attempt was made to use the CREATE JAVA SYSTEM command in a database where the Java system classes already are installed.
solution: Use CREATE OR REPLACE JAVA SYSTEM.

message: class string does not exist
cause: Java method execution failed to find a class with the indicated name.
solution: Correct the name or add the missing Java class.

message: class string . string could not be resolved
cause: An attempt was made to execute a method in a Java class that had not been previously and cannot now be compiled or resolved successfully.
solution: Adjust the call or make the class resolvable.

message: class string already defined by source string
cause: An attempt was made to create a Java source object that would define a class that is already defined by a different Java source object.
solution: Either drop the old source or modify the new source.

message: Java command string not yet implemented
cause: An attempt was made to use a Java command that is not yet implemented.
solution: Do not use the command.

message: invalid type
cause: The type argument in a call to a Java export or import command did not have a recognized value.
solution: Correct the value.

message: badly formed class: string
cause: An attempt was made to create a Java class object with bytecodes that were rejected by the Java verifier.
solution: It is possible that an attempt was made to create the Java class from a damaged class file, in which case the CREATE should be reattempted with a correct class file. It is also possible that the message is the result of using "-" in the resolver so that the verifier could not check the correctness of some code. In that case, the class needs to be created with a resolver.

message: badly formed resource: string
cause: An attempt was made to create a Java resource object with data that was rejected by the Java verifier.
solution: Correct the data.

message: Java system class not available: string
cause: An attempt was made to use a command that requires a Java system class that was not yet present or was invalid.
solution: Load the system classes, or do not use the command.

message: Java system class reported: string
cause: A command that uses a Java system class was aborted due to an error reported by the Java system class.
solution: Correct the error that was reported.

message: class string . string has changed, Java session state cleared
cause: A class in use by the current session was redefined or dropped, invalidating the current Java session state and requiring that it be cleared.
solution: No action required.

message: Java session state cleared
cause: The Java state in the current session became inconsistent and was cleared.
solution: No action required.

message: could not convert string to Unicode
cause: A string in the database character set could not be converted to Unicode, as required for use by Java.
solution: Correct the string.

message: verification warning: string
cause: An attempt was made to create a Java class object with bytecodes that caused the Java verifier to issue a warning.
solution: It is possible that the Java class was created from a damaged class file, in which case the CREATE should be reattempted with a correct class file. It is also possible that the message is the result of using "-" in the resolver so that the verifier could not check the correctness of some code. In that case, the class needs to be created with a resolver.

message: class in use: string . string
cause: An attempt was made to modify a Java class that is in use in the current call.
solution: Correct the code in use in this call.

message: unhandled Java out of memory condition
cause: The session encountered an out of memory condition in Java from which it could not recover. Java session state was cleared.
solution: No action required.

message: Java source, class or resource is not allowed here
cause: A Java source, class, or resource was specified in an inappropriate place in a statement.
solution: Make sure the name is correct or remove it.

message: object type has changed
cause: A database object name that named a Java source, class, or resource now names an object of a different type.
solution: No action required.

message: Java system class string cannot be modified
cause: A command was attempted that would have modified a Java system class.
solution: No action required.

message: JAccelerator (NCOMP) not installed. Refer to Install Guide for instructions.
cause: JAccelerator (NCOMP) is not installed.
solution: Please refer to the Post-installation Tasks section in the Database Install Guide for instructions on how to install JAccelerator (NCOMP).

message: Java VM JIT not supported on this platform.
cause: Java VM JIT is not supported on this platform.
solution: No action required.

message: USING clause is incompatible with its supertype
cause: The USING clause of a type has to be the same as its supertype or compatible with it.
solution: Make sure the USING clause is compatible with its supertype.

message: Invalid option for USING
cause: The class has to implement the required interface for the value of the option for USING.
solution: Make sure the USING clause is supported.

message: class defined in EXTERNAL NAME clause is used in another subtype
cause: The supertype has an existing type that has the same value for the EXTERNAL NAME.
solution: Make sure the EXTERNAL NAME clause is unique among subtypes.

message: EXTERNAL NAME clause is not compatible with its supertype
cause: The EXTERNAL NAME clause of the type is not a subclass of the supertype EXTERNAL NAME.
solution: Make sure the EXTERNAL NAME clause of the type is a subclass of the EXTERNAL NAME of its supertype.

message: SQLJ Object Type validation failed to get default connection
cause: Unable to connect using the JDBC default connection.
solution: No action required.

message: Unable to find the class defined in the EXTERNAL NAME clause
cause: The class is not loaded in the database.
solution: Make sure the EXTERNAL NAME corresponds to a loaded class in the the database.

message: Unable to find the superclass of the defined in the EXTERNAL NAME
cause: The class is not loaded in the database.
solution: Make sure the superclass of the EXTERNAL NAME is loaded in the the database.

message: Unable to find a field that matches one or more of the attributes
cause: The EXTERNAL NAME option of one or more attributes do not match any fields in the defined class.
solution: Make sure the EXTERNAL NAME option of each attribute matches a field in the defined in the defined class.

message: Unable to find a method that matches one or more of the functions
cause: The EXTERNAL NAME option of one or more functions do not match any method in the defined class.
solution: Make sure the EXTERNAL NAME option of each function matches a method in the defined in the defined class.

message: Unable to generate the helper class for the defined type
cause: The helper class used for supporting SQLJ Object Type is not generated.
solution: No Action is required.

message: Java thread deadlock detected
cause: The Java VM has detected a thread deadlock.
solution: Modify the Java program to avoid the deadlock condition.

message: unable to connect to Cluster Synchronization Service
cause: Connect to CSS failed or timed out.
solution: Verify the state of the CSS. If the CSS was not started, start it and then retry the database startup. If the CSS died or is not responding, check the Oracle and CSS trace files for errors and contact Oracle Support Services.

message: error occurred in Cluster Group Service operation
cause: An unexpected error occurred while performing a CGS operation.
solution: Verify that the LMON process is still active. Check the Oracle LMON trace files for errors. Also, check the related CSS trace file for errors.

message: error occurred in global enqueue service operation
cause: An unexpected error occurred while performing a global enqueue service operation.
solution: Check oracle trace files for errors.

message: cannot specify ACTIVE_INSTANCE_COUNT in 8.1.5 or earlier release
cause: The ACTIVE_INSTANCE_COUNT parameter was specified when one of the instances in the cluster was running Oracle 8.1.5 or an earlier release.
solution: Restart the instance without specifying the ACTIVE_INSTANCE_COUNT parameter. Or, upgrade all instances to Oracle 8.1.6 or later release and then specify the parameter.

message: ACTIVE_INSTANCE_COUNT is string which is incompatible with the value in other instances
cause: The value of the ACTIVE_INSTANCE_COUNT parameter must be the same in all Oracle cluster database instances.
solution: Check your initialization parameter files in all instances and ensure that the ACTIVE_INSTANCE_COUNT parameter has the same value. Then restart the instance.

message: incorrect value string for parameter ACTIVE_INSTANCE_COUNT
cause: The ACTIVE_INSTANCE_COUNT parameter must be set to 1 in a two node cluster database configuration or unspecified if a secondary instance is not needed.
solution: Check your initialization parameter files and correct the value of the ACTIVE_INSTANCE_COUNT parameter. If you are configuring a two node primary/secondary cluster database, set this value to 1. Otherwise, do not specify any value for the parameter.

message: inconsistent value string for initialization parameter string with other instances
cause: The value of the initialization parameter in error must be identical on all Oracle cluster database instances and was not.
solution: Check your INIT.ORA files on all instances and ensure that the initialization parameters in error have the same value.

message: error occurred in Cluster Synchronization Services
cause: An unexpected error occurred while performing a CSS operation.
solution: Verify the state of the CSS. If the CSS died or is not responding, check the ORACLE and CSS trace files for errors and contact Oracle Support Services.

message: Communication failure with Cluster Synchronization Services
cause: Could not communicate with CSS to complete the operation.
solution: Verify the state of the CSS. If the CSS died or is not responding, check the ORACLE and CSS trace files for errors and contact Oracle Support Services.

message: Current operation aborted by Cluster Synchronization Services
cause: The operation could not be performed or CSS was shutting down.
solution: Check the log file of Cluster Synchronization Services daemon to verify the state of the service. Start the service if needed; otherwise, contact Oracle Support Services.

message: error occurred during registration of Oracle process with CSS
cause: this error and it is an expected result. Otherwise, contact Oracle Support Services.
solution: Confirm that the database, and any ASM instances on which it depends, is operating normally. An outage in one of these can

message: instance specified no longer exists
cause: A client of the global enqueue service specified an instance that no longer existed.
solution: Process aborts current operation due to termination of an instance

message: evicted by instance number string , group incarnation string
cause: This instance was evicted from the group by another instance of the cluster database group for one of several reasons, which may include a communications error in the cluster and failure to issue a heartbeat to the control file.
solution: Check the trace files of other active instances in the cluster group for indications of errors that caused a reconfiguration.

message: IMR active for some, but not all members of cluster
cause: The IMR feature is not active for this instance, but is active for another instance in the cluster database.
solution: Ensure that all instances have the same value for the _imr_active init.ora parameter

message: incompatible Instance Membership Recovery protocol among instances
cause: The selected Instance Membership Recovery protocol was not compatible with other running instances in the cluster database.
solution: Check the Instance Membership Recovery initialization parameters of all instances to ensure their consistency.

message: Cluster Synchronization Service is being shut down.
cause: The administrator has shut down the Cluster Synchronization Service daemon. This error message is intended to be informative to users on the status of the service.
solution: Check the log file of the Cluster Synchronization Service daemon to verify the state of the service.

message: instance_number parameter not specified
cause: The init.ora file did not contain a value for the instance_number which is required to identify this instance to other instances of the database running on the same cluster
solution: Assign a value to the instance_number parameter in the init.ora parameter file

message: global enqueue process string (OSID string ) is hung for more than string seconds
cause: The specified process mades no progress within the maximum allowed time.
solution: Check the alert file and relevent trace files and contact Oracle Support Services with the incident information.

message: process string (OSID string ) blocks string (OSID string ) for more than string seconds
cause: The specified process blocked a global enqueue process for the maximum allowed time.
solution: Check the alert file and relevent trace files and contact Oracle Support Services with the incident information.

message: unable to connect to GPnP daemon [ string ]
cause: Attempt to connect to the GPnP deamon failed with the error reported.
solution: Take the corrective action to resolve the error reported. Refer to GPnP logs and documentation to figure out why the call failed.

message: GPnP attribute SET failed with error [ string ]
cause: Attempt to set the GPnP attribute failed. See the brackets for the reason.
solution: Resolve the problem in the included message and retry the request.

message: Attribute update operation not permitted
cause: The update operation for attributes was not permitted because Cluster Synchronization Services (CSS) was not running on the host.
solution: Start Cluster Synchronization Services (CSS) and retry the operation.

message: GPnP attribute GET failed with error [ string ]
cause: Attempt to get the GPnP attribute failed. See the brackets for the reason.
solution: Resolve the problem in the included message and retry the request.

message: SIHA attribute GET failed with error [ string ]
cause: Attempt to get the SIHA attribute failed. See the brackets for the reason.
solution: Resolve the problem in the included message and retry the request.

message: SIHA attribute SET failed with error [ string ]
cause: Attempt to set the SIHA attribute failed. See the brackets for the reason.
solution: Resolve the problem in the included message and retry the request.

message: Network interface query failed with error [ string ]
cause: Attempt to get the network information failed. See the brackets for the reason.
solution: Resolve the problem in the included message and retry the request.

message: Cannot change user session parameters for a non-user session
cause: An attempt was made to change user session parameters for a non-user session.
solution: Execute the operation when connected with a user session

message: Transactions cannot be replayed
cause: The user attempted to replay a transaction.
solution: Reconnect and re-execute the transaction.

message: invalid name for operator
cause: The name specified for the operator is incorrect.
solution: Specify a correct name for the operator.

message: missing RETURN keyword
cause: The RETURN keyword has not been specified.
solution: Specify the RETURN keyword or check the SQL statement.

message: missing CONTEXT keyword
cause: The CONTEXT keyword has not been specified.
solution: Specify the CONTEXT keyword or check the SQL statement.

message: missing ANCILLARY keyword
cause: The ANCILLARY keyword has not been specified.
solution: Specify the ANCILLARY keyword or check the SQL statement.

message: missing DATA keyword
cause: The DATA keyword has not been specified.
solution: Specify the DATA keyword or check the SQL statement.

message: missing COLUMN keyword
cause: Keyword COLUMN is expected .
solution: Either specify the COLUMN keyword or specify another option.

message: specified binding does not exist
cause: The operator binding which has been specified does not exist.
solution: Ensure that the operator binding that has been specified does exist.

message: specified operator does not exist
cause: The operator which has been specified does not exist.
solution: Ensure that the operator that has been specified does exist.

message: specified primary operator binding does not exist
cause: The specified binding for the primary operator does not exist.
solution: Ensure that the specified binding for the primary operator exists.

message: cannot drop an operator with dependent objects
cause: The operator which is being dropped has some dependent objects.
solution: Either drop the dependent objects first and then issue the DROP OPERATOR command or specify the FORCE option with DROP OPERATOR.

message: inadequate operator privileges
cause: The user does not have the appropriate privileges to perform the specified operation on the operator.
solution: Grant the appropriate privileges to the user and then reissue the statement.

message: missing STATISTICS keyword
cause: This is not a valid option with the ASSOCIATE command.
solution: Specify STATISTICS keyword after the ASSOCIATE command.

message: incorrect object name specified
cause: The specified name is not a valid name.
solution: Specify the correct name of the object with for which an association needs to be defined.

message: non-supported object type with associate statement
cause: The type of object specified is not supported with the associate statistics statement.
solution: Use a valid object type with the associate command.

message: expecting USING or DEFAULT keyword
cause: Expecting the USING or DEFAULT keyword after the names of object(s).
solution: Provide the USING or DEFAULT keyword.

message: object being associated is not present
cause: The object for which the association is being defined is not present.
solution: Ensure that all the objects for which the association is being defined are present.

message: object being disassociated is not present
cause: Object which is being disassociated is not present.
solution: Ensure that the object which needs to be disassociated is present.

message: non-supported option with disassociate statement
cause: The type of object specified is not supported with the disassociate statistics statement.
solution: Use a object type which is supported with the disassociate command.

message: column name not properly specified
cause: Name of the column should contain the table and the column name.
solution: Specify a valid column name.

message: cannot associate default values with columns
cause: User tried to associate DEFAULT values with columns which is not a valid option .
solution: Specify a valid option.

message: the statistics type is not present
cause: The statistics type which is being associated with object(s) is not present.
solution: Ensure that the type which contains the statistics functions is present.

message: specified primary operator does not exist
cause: The specified primary operator does not exist.
solution: Check the primary operator and the signature specified.

message: selectivity cannot be specified for the type of object
cause: User tried to associate selectivity with index or indextypes which is not allowed .
solution: Specify a valid option.

message: object being analyzed is not a table
cause: The object being analyzed is not a table and is not supported
solution: Specify only a supported option.

message: operator is invalid
cause: The operator is invalid.
solution: Drop and recreate the operator.

message: invalid name for indextype
cause: Indextype name or Indextype schema name has invalid characters.
solution: Verify that the name has valid characters and it is not a reserved word.

message: keyword FOR is missing
cause: FOR keyword must be provided with Create Indextype statement.
solution: Use FOR keyword and provide relevant operator information.

message: keyword USING is missing
cause: USING keyword and corresponding implementation details must be provided.
solution: Provide USING keyword and relevant implementation details with Create Indextype statement.

message: invalid name for implementation type
cause: Implementation type or Implementation schema name is invalid.
solution: Verify that the name has valid characters and it is not a reserved word.

message: implementation type does not exist
cause: The implementation type specified with USING clause could not be found.
solution: Check to see if the type exists and the user has EXECUTE privilege on this type.

message: operator does not exist
cause: The operator could not be found.
solution: Verify that the operator exists and the user has EXECUTE privilege for this operator.

message: operator binding not found
cause: The specified binding for the operator is not available from the operator schema object.
solution: Verify that the operator with the specified binding exists.

message: cannot drop or replace an indextype with dependent indexes
cause: One or more indexes are dependent upon the indextype.
solution: Drop all the indexes which are dependent upon the indextype before dropping the indextype itself.

message: indextype does not exist
cause: There is no indextype by the specified name.
solution: Use public views for the indextypes to see if an indextype by the specified name has been created.

message: REF datatype not supported with operators
cause: The user specified a REF datatype which is not supported in CREATE OPERATOR.
solution: Reissue the CREATE OPERATOR statement without the REF datatype.

message: ODCIGETINTERFACES routine does not return required interface(s)
cause: The ODCIObjectList returned by the ODCIGetInterfaces routine does not contain the interface(s) required by the current usage.
solution: Ensure that the ODCIGetInterfaces routine returns the name(s) of the required interface(s).

message: failed to validate referenced operators
cause: One of the operators referenced cannot be compiled.
solution: Try to recompile the operators which are referenced by this indextype. Use USER_INDEXTYPE_OPERATORS view to find out the referenced operators.

message: insufficient privileges to execute implementation type
cause: User does not have privileges to execute the implementation type.
solution: The owner of the implementation type must grant appropriate privileges to the user.

message: insufficient privileges to execute the operator(s)
cause: User does not have privileges to execute one of the operators.
solution: The owner of the operators must grant appropriate privileges to the user .

message: failed to validate implementation type
cause: Implementation type cannot be compiled.
solution: Try to compile the implementation type.

message: indextype and implementation type are not in same schema
cause: Indextype and implementation type are in different schema.
solution: Put the indextype and implementation type in the same schema.

message: invalid option for ALTER INDEXTYPE
cause: The user specified an invalid option with the ALTER INDEXTYPE command
solution: Choose a valid option with the ALTER INDEXTYPE command

message: option not supported with the version string of the indextype interface
cause: User specified an option which is not supported with the version of the indextype interface provided
solution: User should either not request for this option or should provide an implementation type that implements the correct version of the indextype interface.

message: indextype should support atleast one operator
cause: User attempted to drop all the operators from the indextype
solution: Do not drop all the operators from the indextype

message: duplicate operator name specified
cause: User attempted to add an operator name to an indextype which is already supported by the indextype
solution: Remove the duplicate operator and retry the command

message: indextype does not support local domain index on string partitioned table
cause: User specified a create local domain index statement using an indextype that does not support local domain indexes on tables partitioned with the given method
solution: Use a different indextype or build a global domain index

message: cannot create a local domain index on a string partitioned table
cause: User specified a create local domain index statement on a table partitioned using a method not supported by domain indexes
solution: Build a global domain index on the partitioned table

message: cannot create a local domain index on a partitioned index-organized table
cause: User specified a create local domain index statement on a partitioned index-organized table
solution: Build a global domain index on the partitioned index-organized table

message: error occurred in the execution of ODCIINDEXMERGEPARTITION routine
cause: Failed to successfully execute the ODCIIndexMergePartition routine.
solution: Check to see if the routine has been coded correctly.

message: error occurred in the execution of ODCIINDEXSPLITPARTITION routine
cause: Failed to successfully execute the ODCIIndexSplitPartition routine.
solution: Check to see if the routine has been coded correctly.

message: invalid option for creation of domain indexes
cause: The user specified an invalid option like ASC, DESC, SORT or a parallel clause, partitioning clause or physical attributes clause.
solution: Choose one of the valid clauses for creation of domain indexes.

message: cannot build a domain index on more than one column
cause: User attempted to build a domain index on more than one column.
solution: Build the domain index only on a single column.

message: keyword IS is missing
cause: IS keyword must be specified with Create Index statement for domain indexes.
solution: Use IS keyword and then specify the indextype name.

message: keyword UNIQUE may not be used in creating domain indexes
cause: An attempt was made to create a domain index with the UNIQUE attribute.
solution: Remove UNIQUE from the CREATE INDEX statement.

message: keyword BITMAP may not be used in creating domain indexes
cause: An attempt was made to create a domain index with the BITMAP attribute.
solution: Remove BITMAP from the CREATE INDEX statement.

message: error occurred in the execution of ODCIINDEXCREATE routine
cause: Failed to successfully execute the ODCIIndexCreate routine.
solution: Check to see if the routine has been coded correctly.

message: error occurred in the execution of ODCIINDEXDROP routine
cause: Failed to successfully execute the ODCIIndexDrop routine.
solution: Check to see if the routine has been coded correctly.

message: domain indexes and/or secondary objects exist in the tablespace
cause: An attempt was made to drop a tablespace which contains secondary objects and/or domain indexes.
solution: Drop the domain indexes in his tablespace. Also, find the domain indexes which created secondary objects in this tablespace and drop them. Then try dropping the tablespace.

message: error occurred in the execution of ODCIINDEXALTER routine
cause: Failed to successfully execute the ODCIIndexAlter routine.
solution: Check to see if the routine has been coded correctly.

message: error occurred in the execution of ODCIINDEXTRUNCATE routine
cause: Failed to successfully execute the ODCIIndexTruncate routine.
solution: Check to see if the routine has been coded correctly.

message: cannot truncate a table with domain indexes marked LOADING
cause: The table has domain indexes defined on it that are marked LOADING.
solution: Wait to see if the ongoing index DDL ends and the index state changes from LOADING state. Else ,drop the domain indexes marked as LOADING with the FORCE option.

message: domain index is marked LOADING/FAILED/UNUSABLE
cause: An attempt has been made to access a domain index that is being built or is marked failed by an unsuccessful DDL or is marked unusable by a DDL operation.
solution: Wait if the specified index is marked LOADING Drop the specified index if it is marked FAILED Drop or rebuild the specified index if it is marked UNUSABLE.

message: cannot specify FORCE option for dropping non-domain index
cause: A DROP INDEX FORCE was issued for a non-domain index.
solution: Reissue the command without the FORCE option.

message: warning in the execution of ODCIINDEXCREATE routine
cause: A warning was returned from the ODCIIndexCreate routine.
solution: Check to see if the routine has been coded correctly Check user specified log tables for greater detail.

message: analyzing domain indexes marked LOADING/FAILED not supported
cause: Tried to analyze a domain index which was marked as LOADING or FAILED.
solution: If the index was marked LOADING, wait till it is marked valid before retrying the analyze. If index was marked FAILED, drop it OR rebuild it and retry the analyze.

message: indextype is invalid
cause: The indextype is invalid.
solution: Drop and recreate the indextype.

message: cannot create domain index on a column of index-organized table
cause: Tried to create a domain index on a column of an index-organized table.
solution: Do not attempt to create a domain index on columns of an index-organized table.

message: cannot create a domain index on a LONG column
cause: The user attempted to create a domain index on a column of LONG datatype.
solution: Do not create a domain index on a LONG column.

message: cannot issue DDL on a domain index marked as LOADING
cause: Tried to issue a DROP/ALTER/TRUNCATE on a domain index in a LOADING state.
solution: Wait till the index operation completes OR issue a DROP INDEX FORCE to drop the index.

message: cannot issue ALTER without REBUILD on a domain index marked FAILED
cause: Tried to issue a DROP/ALTER on a domain index in a FAILED state.
solution: Truncate the table to mark the index as valid OR do ALTER INDEX REBUILD to rebuild the index.

message: specified options are only valid for altering a domain index
cause: Specified the ONLINE or PARAMETERS clause with a non-domain index.
solution: Reissue the statement with the correct syntax for alter.

message: invalid alter option for a domain index
cause: The user specified an invalid option for altering a domain index.
solution: Reissue the alter statement with a valid option.

message: parameters clause cannot be combined with the specified options
cause: The user combined PARAMETERS clause with other alter index options.
solution: Reissue the statement with the correct syntax for alter.

message: warning in the execution of ODCIINDEXDROP routine
cause: A waring was returned from the ODCIIndexDrop routine.
solution: Check to see if the routine has been coded correctly Check the user defined warning log tables for greater details.

message: warning in the execution of ODCIINDEXALTER routine
cause: A waring was returned from the ODCIIndexAlter routine.
solution: Check to see if the routine has been coded correctly Check the user defined warning log tables for greater details.

message: failed in the execution of the ODCIINDEXINSERT routine
cause: Failed to successfully execute the ODCIIndexInsert routine.
solution: Check to see if the routine has been coded correctly.

message: failed in the execution of the ODCIINDEXDELETE routine
cause: Failed to successfully execute the ODCIIndexDelete routine.
solution: Check to see if the routine has been coded correctly.

message: failed in the execution of the ODCIINDEXUPDATE routine
cause: Failed to successfully execute the ODCIIndexUpdate routine.
solution: Check to see if the routine has been coded correctly.

message: warning in the execution of ODCIINDEXTRUNCATE routine
cause: A warning was returned from the ODCIIndexTruncate routine.
solution: Check to see if the routine has been coded correctly Check the user defined warning log tables for greater details.

message: cannot create multiple domain indexes on a column list using same indextype
cause: An attempt was made to define multiple domain indexes on the same column list using identical indextypes.
solution: Check to see if a different indextype can be used or if the index can be defined on another column list.

message: such column list already indexed using another domain index and indextype
cause: An attempt was made to create multiple domain indexes on a column list using indextypes which do not have disjoint operators.
solution: Check to see if the operator sets for the indextypes can be made disjoint.

message: failed to validate indextype
cause: Indextype cannot be compiled.
solution: Try to compile the indextype which is referenced by the domain index.

message: insufficient privileges to execute indextype
cause: User does not have privileges to execute the indextype.
solution: The owner of the indextype must grant appropriate privileges to the user.

message: cannot create a domain index on column expressions
cause: User specified an expression in the column list.
solution: Specify only simple columns in the column list for domain index.

message: domain index is defined on the column to be dropped
cause: An ALTER TABLE DROP COLUMN was issued on a column on which a domain index exists.
solution: Drop the domain index before attempting to drop the column.

message: domain index is defined on the column to be modified
cause: An ALTER TABLE MODIFY COLUMN was issued on a column on which a domain index exists.
solution: Drop the domain index before attempting to modify the column.

message: feature not supported for domain indexes
cause: Feature is not supported for domain indexes.
solution: No action required.

message: cannot support row movement if domain index defined on table
cause: An ALTER TABLE ENABLE ROW MOVEMENT was issued on a table which has a domain index defined on it.
solution: Drop the domain index if you want to enable row movement and then reissue the command.

message: cannot create domain index on a table with row movement enabled
cause: A create domain index statement was issued on a table that has row movement enabled.
solution: Disable the row movement in the table and then reissue the create domain index statement.

message: specified primary operator does not have an index context
cause: The primary operator does not have an index and scan contexts.
solution: Create the primary operator with a context clause.

message: indextypes with array DML do not support the given data type
cause: The user specified a REF or a LONG datatype which is not supported in CREATE/ALTER INDEXTYPE WITH ARRAY DML (DATA_TYPE, VARRAY_TYPE).
solution: Reissue the CREATE/ALTER INDEXTYPE statement without the REF or LONG datatype.

message: indextypes without column data do not need the given data type
cause: WITH ARRAY DML (DATA_TYPE, VARRAY_TYPE) option and WITHOUT COLUMN DATA option conflicted in an alter indextype statement
solution: Reissue the ALTER INDEXTYPE statement without the conflict.

message: base or varray datatype does not exist
cause: One of the base and varray datatypes specified in WITH ARRAY DML (DATA_TYPE, VARRAY_TYPE) clause could not be found.
solution: Check to see if the datatype exists and the user has EXECUTE privilege on this datatype.

message: duplicate base datatype specified
cause: User attempted to add a base datatype to an indextype with ARRAY DML which is already supported by the indextype
solution: Remove the duplicate base datatype and retry the command

message: Length of PARAMETER string longer than string characters
cause: An attempt was made to specify a parameter value that is longer than the allowed maximum.
solution: Reduce the parameter value length.

message: operator binding does not exist
cause: There is no binding for the current usage of the operator.
solution: Change the operator arguments to match any of the existing bindings or add a new binding to the operator.

message: function underlying operator binding does not exist
cause: The function underlying the operator binding does not exist.
solution: Ensure that the function corresponding to the operator invocation exists.

message: error in executing ODCIIndexStart() routine
cause: The execution of ODCIIndexStart routine caused an error.
solution: Examine the error messages produced by the indextype code and take appropriate action.

message: error in executing ODCIIndexFetch() routine
cause: The execution of ODCIIndexFetch routine caused an error.
solution: Examine the error messages produced by the indextype code and take appropriate action.

message: error in executing ODCIIndexClose() routine
cause: The execution of ODCIIndexClose routine caused an error.
solution: Examine the error messages produced by the indextype code and take appropriate action.

message: method string does not exist in type string . string
cause: A required method with the required signature does not exist in the specified type.
solution: Add the required method to the type.

message: indextype string . string does not exist
cause: The indextype does not exist.
solution: Create the indextype.

message: found duplicate labels in primary invocations
cause: There are multiple primary invocations of operators with the same number as the label.
solution: Use distinct labels in primary invocations.

message: missing primary invocation for ancillary operator
cause: The primary invocation corresponding to an ancillary operator is missing.
solution: Add the primary invocation with the same label as the ancillary operator.

message: label for the ancillary operator is not a literal number
cause: The label used for invoking the ancillary operator is not a literal number.
solution: Use a literal number as the label.

message: invalid callback operation
cause: Encountered an invalid callback operation.
solution: Ensure that all the callbacks executed from callouts are valid in the statement context.

message: null scan context returned by ODCIIndexStart() routine
cause: The ODCIIndexStart() routine returned a null scan context
solution: Ensure that the ODCIIndexStart() routine returns a non-null scan context.

message: ODCIGETINTERFACES routine does not return required stream version
cause: The ODCIObjectList returned by the ODCIGetInterfaces routine does not contain the required stream version for external tables.
solution: Ensure that the ODCIGetInterfaces routine returns the required stream version.

message: cannot select FOR UPDATE from collection operand
cause: Collection operands cannot be updated
solution: Remove FOR UPDATE clause

message: cannot lock a table which gets its rows from a collection operand
cause: Tables which gets its rows from a collection operand cannot be locked
solution: Don't lock the table

message: cannot create domain indexes on temporary tables
cause: An attempt was made to create a domain index on a temporary table
solution: Either create another type of index on the temporary table or change the table from temporary to a permanent table

message: failed in the execution of the ODCIINDEXUPDPARTMETADATA routine
cause: Failed to successfully execute the ODCIINDEXUPDPARTMETADATA routine.
solution: Check to see if the routine has been coded correctly.

message: failed in the partition maintenance operation of secondary table
cause: Failed to successfully execute the partition maintenance operation of a secondary table in system managed domain index.
solution: Check to see if the partition of a secondary table exists.

message: Ancillary operator not supported with set view query block
cause: Outer view query block contains ancillary operator and view query block contains union all.
solution: Define the union-all view query to contain the primary and ancillary query terms. i.e. have the operators within the view definition rather than in the query outside the view.

message: Invalid rowid returned by the user-defined query methods
cause: An invalid row identifier was returned by the user-defined query methods.
solution: Check the implementation of the indextype methods to make sure that the index creation and query methods are correct.

message: cannot execute string
cause: The specified function does not exist or does not have an appropriate signature.
solution: Implement the function with the appropriate signature.

message: association already defined for the object
cause: The object for which the association is being defined, already has a statistics type associated with it.
solution: Disassociate the object and then associate the object.

message: error in executing the ODCIStatsCollect / ODCIStatsDelete routine
cause: The ODCIStatsCollect / ODCIStatsDelete function is causing an error.
solution: Check the ODCIStatsCollect / ODCIStatsDelete function.

message: duplicate default selectivity specified
cause: The keyword DEFAULT SELECTIVITY can only be specified once.
solution: Remove the duplicate keyword.

message: missing SCAN Keyword
cause: The scan context is not specified.
solution: Supply the SCAN keyword.

message: COMPUTE ANCILLARY DATA specified without the INDEX CONTEXT clause
cause: The COMPUTE ANCILLARY DATA option was specified without the WITH INDEX CONTEXT clause.
solution: Specify the WITH INDEX CONTEXT option.

message: specified association does not exist
cause: One or more of the object(s) that have been specified to be disassociated, do not have an association defined for them.
solution: Verify the objects which have an association defined and issue the disassociate command again.

message: the type being dropped is a statistics type
cause: Some objects have defined their statistics methods in the type being dropped.
solution: First drop the relevant associations using the DISASSOCIATE command and then retry the DROP command, or use the FORCE option with DROP TYPE command.

message: object being disassociated has some user defined statistics stored
cause: There are some user defined statistics collected for the object being disassociated.
solution: First delete the user defined statistics and then reissue the DISASSOCIATE command or specify the FORCE option with DISASSOCIATE.

message: index specified for association is not a domain index
cause: The user issued an ASSOCIATE STATISTICS command with an index which is not a domain index.
solution: Issue an ASSOCIATE STATISTICS WITH INDEXES command on a domain index only

message: missing FROM keyword
cause: The keyword FROM is missing.
solution: Specify the FROM keyword or check the SQL statement.

message: NULL association is allowed only with a column or an index
cause: User tried to use the ASSOCIATE command with a schema object other than a column or an index
solution: Specify the NULL clause only with a column or an index

message: domain index cannot be system-managed
cause: An ASSOCIATE STATISTICS command was issued with a domain index which is system-managed.
solution: Check to see if the domain index has been implemented with system-managed storage tables. To associate statitics with a system-managed domain index, issue ASSOCIATE STATISTICS command with the indextype of this domain index.

message: both indextype and statistics type should be system-managed
cause: Either an ASSOCIATE STATISTICS WITH SYSTEM MANAGED STORAGE TABLES command was issued with an indextype which is not system-managed, or an ASSOCIATE STATISTICS command was issued with an indextype which is system-managed.
solution: Check to see if both indextype and statistics type are implemented with system-managed storage tables.

message: could not implicitly transform user-managed domain index to system-managed domain index
cause: Implicit validation of a user-managed domain index with a system-managed indextype failed.
solution: Issue an ALTER INDEX COMPILE command on the domain index.

message: warning in the execution of ODCIINDEXMERGEPARTITION routine
cause: A warning was returned from the ODCIIndexMergePartition routine.
solution: Check to see if the routine has been coded correctly Check user specified log tables for greater detail.

message: warning in the execution of ODCIINDEXSPLITPARTITION routine
cause: A warning was returned from the ODCIIndexSplitPartition routine.
solution: Check to see if the routine has been coded correctly Check user specified log tables for greater detail.

message: cannot issue DDL on a domain index partition marked as LOADING
cause: Tried to issue a DROP/ALTER/TRUNCATE on a domain index partition in a LOADING state.
solution: Wait till the index partition operation completes OR issue a DROP INDEX FORCE to drop the index OR issue a ALTER TABLE DROP PARTITION to drop the partition.

message: cannot issue DDL on a domain index partition marked as FAILED
cause: Tried to issue a DROP/ALTER on a domain index partition in a FAILED state.
solution: do ALTER INDEX REBUILD PARTITION to rebuild the index partition OR ALTER TABLE TRUNCATE PARTITION to mark the index partition as valid.

message: domain index partition is marked LOADING/FAILED/UNUSABLE
cause: An attempt has been made to access a domain index that is being built or is marked failed by an unsuccessful DDL or is marked unusable by a DDL operation.
solution: Wait if the specified index partition is marked LOADING Rebuild the specified index partition if it is marked FAILED or UNUSABLE.

message: error occurred in the execution of ODCIINDEXEXCHANGEPARTITION routine
cause: Failed to successfully execute the ODCIIndexExchangePartition routine.
solution: Check to see if the routine has been coded correctly.

message: warning in the execution of ODCIINDEXEXCHANGEPARTITION routine
cause: A warning was returned from the ODCIIndexExchangePartition routine.
solution: Check to see if the routine has been coded correctly Check user specified log tables for greater detail.

message: cannot create a function-based domain index on a string table
cause: User specified an unsupported create function-based domain index statement.
solution: Issue the create function-based domain index statement only on supported types of tables.

message: fatal error occurred in the execution of ODCIINDEXCREATE routine
cause: Failed to successfully execute the ODCIIndexCreate routine.
solution: Check to see if the routine has been coded correctly.

message: error in the execution of the string routine for one or more of the index partitions
cause: An error occurred during execution of the routine for one or more of the index partitions
solution: Check the *_IND_PARTITIONS view to see which partitions are marked FAILED. Rebuild or Truncate the FAILED index partitions

message: line string , string
cause: The ODCIIndex DDL routine has put a warning message into table SYS.ODCI_WARNINGS$
solution: Check the warning message

message: too many warnings occurred in the execution of ODCIIndex DDL routine
cause: The number of warnings during the ODCIIndex DDL routine is too high.
solution: Query table SYS.ODCI_WARNINGS$ to get more warning messages

message: fatal error occurred in the execution of ODCIINDEXALTER routine
cause: Failed to successfully execute the ODCIIndexAlter routine.
solution: Check to see if the routine has been coded correctly.

message: missing BINDING keyword
cause: Keyword BINDING is expected .
solution: Specify the BINDING keyword or check the SQL statement.

message: missing ADD or DROP keyword
cause: One of the keywords ADD or DROP is expected.
solution: Specify the ADD or DROP keyword or check the SQL statement.

message: The specified binding does not exist
cause: The binding specified in the DROP BINDING clause is not a valid binding for this operator.
solution: Specify an existing binding for this op in DROP BINDING clause.

message: The only binding of an operator cannot be dropped
cause: This operator only has one binding. It cannot be dropped using Alter Operator Drop Binding.
solution: If you wish to drop the entire operator, call Drop Operator.

message: Cannot drop an operator binding with dependent objects
cause: The operator binding that is being dropped has dependent objects.
solution: Either drop the dependent objects first and then issue the ALTER OPERATOR DROP BINDING command or specify the FORCE option with ALTER OPERATOR DROP BINDING.

message: No primary operator bindings found for ancillary binding # string
cause: At least one ancillary binding of the specified operator could not be validated because all of its associated primary operator bindings have been dropped.
solution: Either drop the ancillary binding whose primary operators are missing, or drop the entire operator, if this is the only binding. This binding cannot be re-validated.

message: Specified registration id does not exist
cause: An incorrect regid value was passed to dbms_chnf procedure.
solution: pass the correct regid value.

message: Specified table name not found or does not have any registrations
cause: The database could not locate the passed in table name
solution: CHeck the table name passed in.

message: user does not have privilege to change/ create registration
cause: User passed in an incorrect or someone else's regid/ handle.
solution: Check the passed in regid/ reg handle

message: Unsupported query or operation during change notification registration
cause: The user attempted to register an unsupported query type or an unsupported operation like a DML/DDL for change notification.
solution: Please check the statement being executed and refer to the documentation.

message: Cannot register a query in the middle of an active transaction
cause: User tried to register a query within an uncommitted transction.
solution: Commit the transaction and retry.

message: Unsupported query for registration in guaranteed mode
cause: An operator or expression in the query was incompatible with query registration in the guaranteed granularity mode.
solution: Check all expressions, clauses and operators in the query and refer to the documentation for supported query types. The application can reattempt the query registration in best effort mode.

message: Unsupported column type for query registration in guaranteed mode
cause: An attempt was made to register a query with an unsupported column type or too many columns.
solution: Examine all column datatypes in the expression and refer to the documentation for supported query types. The application can reattempt the query registration in best effort mode.

message: Query registration not supported at current compatible setting
cause: An attempt was made to register a query with the database compatible setting lower than 11.
solution: Increase the database compatible setting to 11.0.0.0.0

message: Cannot register query: conflicting DDL in progress
cause: A query registration was attempted while there was a a concurrent DDL in progress.
solution: Retry the query registration.

message: Table type not supported for query registration in guaranteed mode
cause: The user attempted to register a query involving an unsupported table type.
solution: Examine all tables in the query registration and refer to the documentation for supported table types. The application can reattempt registration in best effort mode.

message: Unsupported query for Continuous Query Notification
cause: The query cannot be registered for Continuous Query Notification.
solution: The query has some constructs that make it incompatible with Continous Query Notification like synonyms or views. Please check the documentation for complete list.

message: Query Registration is only supported for automatic undo management
cause: User is using manual undo management
solution: Switch to using automatic undo management

message: Cannot complete operation because of cross-instance issue
cause: The operation attempted by the user could not be completed because of a cross-instance issue (for example, an instance died).
solution: Retry the operation.

message: missing either trim specification or char expression in TRIM
cause: Since FROM is specified in TRIM function, either trim specification (TRAILING, HEADING, BOTH) or trim character or both must be specified.
solution: Add either trim specification (TRAILING, HEADING, BOTH) or trim character or both.

message: trim set should have only one character
cause: Trim set contains more or less than 1 character. This is not allowed in TRIM function.
solution: Change trim set to have only 1 character.

message: SYS_CONNECT_BY_PATH function is not allowed here
cause: SYS_CONNECT_BY_PATH function was called at places other than the SELECT list and ORDER BY clause.
solution: Remove calls to SYS_CONNECT_BY_PATH function at places other than the SELECT list and ORDER BY clause.

message: when using SYS_CONNECT_BY_PATH function, cannot have separator as part of column value
cause: A column value contained the string that the SYS_CONNECT_BY_PATH function was to use to separate column values.
solution: Specify another separator for the SYS_CONNECT_BY_PATH function to use which does not occur in any column value, then retry.

message: missing or invalid WAIT interval
cause: A non-zero integer must be specified for wait interval (in seconds) after the WAIT keyword.
solution: Correct the syntax and retry.

message: resource busy; acquire with WAIT timeout expired
cause: The requested resource is busy.
solution: Retry the operation later.

message: CONNECT BY ROOT operator is not supported in the START WITH or in the CONNECT BY condition
cause: An attempt was made to use CONNECT BY ROOT operator in the START WITH or in the CONNECT BY condition.
solution: Remove CONNECT BY ROOT operator from the START WITH or from the CONNECT BY condition.

message: CONNECT BY clause must reference a PRIOR
cause: A CONNECT BY clause did not include a predicate referencing a PRIOR so there was no condition connecting a parent row to its child row.
solution: Add a reference to a PRIOR in the CONNECT BY clause.

message: Not enough memory for string operation
cause: The memory size was not sufficient to process all the levels of the hierarchy specified by the query.
solution: In WORKAREA_SIZE_POLICY=AUTO mode, set PGA_AGGREGATE_TARGET to a reasonably larger value. Or, in WORKAREA_SIZE_POLICY=MANUAL mode, set SORT_AREA_SIZE to a reasonably larger value.

message: Not enough I/O buffers for the sort operation
cause: The sort was unable to allocate enough I/O buffers.
solution: Increase the amount of memory allowed for the sort or increase the maximum number of I/O buffers allowed in the system and retry the query.

message: Error simulated: psite= string , ptype= string
cause: error generated for testing purposes.
solution: None

message: undo tablespace ' string ' does not exist or of wrong type
cause: the specified undo tablespace does not exist or of the wrong type.
solution: Correct the tablespace name and reissue the statement.

message: undo tablespace ' string ' is currently in use
cause: the specified undo tablespace is currently used by another instance.
solution: Wait for the undo tablespace to become available or change to another name and reissue the statement.

message: operation only supported in Automatic Undo Management mode
cause: the operation is only supported in automatic undo mode.
solution: restart instance in Automatic Undo Management mode before retrying operation.

message: previously offlined undo tablespace ' string ' is still pending
cause: the current operation is not allowed because an undo tablespace containing active transactions is pending from a previous SWITCH UNDO operation. The operation will be allowed again after all transactions in the previous undo tablespace are committed.
solution: Wait for all previous transactions to commit before reissuing the current statement.

message: undo tablespace ' string ' is already in use by this instance
cause: the specified undo tablespace is currently used by this instance. The operation failed.
solution: If the specified undo tablespace name is wrong, reissue the statement with the correct name.

message: segment ' string ' is not supported in string Undo Management mode
cause: the type of the specified undo segment is incompatible with the current undo management mode of the instance.
solution: Check the undo segment name and the undo management mode and reissue statement if necessary.

message: Create Rollback Segment failed, USN string is out of range
cause: the system runs out of undo segment number. Too many undo segments exist.
solution: drop some of the unused undo segments and retry operation.

message: Illegal rollback Segment operation in Automatic Undo mode
cause: This operation only allowed in Manual Undo mode.
solution: restart instance in Manual Undo_Management mode and retry operation.

message: Operation not allowed on undo tablespace
cause: This operation is not allowed on undo tablespaces
solution: Check the tablespace name and reissue command if necessary

message: Cannot create segments in undo tablespace
cause: Cannot create segments in undo tablespace
solution: Check the tablespace name and reissue command

message: Duplicate undo tablespace specification
cause: Cannot create more than one undo tablespace during database creation
solution: Modify the command to contain only one undo tablespace

message: Invalid specification for CREATE UNDO TABLESPACE
cause: You have specified an clause that should not used with CREATE UNDO TABLESPACE
solution: Drop the clause from the command and reissue it.

message: DROP segment ' string ' (in undo tablespace) not allowed
cause: Explicit DROP operation is not allowed on undo tablespace segments
solution: Check the undo segment name and reissue statement if necessary.

message: Undo tablespace ' string ' has unexpired undo with string (sec) left, Undo_Retention= string (sec)
cause: Tried to drop a tablespace that contains unexpired undo information
solution: lower setting of UNDO_RETENTION or wait a while before reissue command to drop undo tablespace

message: Undo quota violation - failed to get string (bytes)
cause: the amount of undo assigned to the consumer group of this session has been exceeded.
solution: ask DBA to increase undo quota, or wait until other transactions to commit before proceeding.

message: no active undo tablespace assigned to instance
cause: the current instance does not have an active undo tablespace assigned to execute transactions.
solution: ask DBA to create an undo tablespace, online the undo tablespace and then retry operation.

message: the suspended (resumable) statement has been aborted
cause: DBA or the user aborted the execution of the suspended statement in the resumable session
solution: None

message: the suspended (resumable) statement has timed out
cause: A correctible error was signaled in the resumable session and the error was not cleared within the timeout interval.
solution: Fix the correctible error within the timeout. Default is 2 hours. Or increase the (resumable) timeout.

message: Undo tablespace cannot be specified as default user tablespace
cause: It is incorrect to specify undo tablespace as default user tablespace
solution: Check the tablespace name and reissue the command

message: Undo tablespace cannot be specified as temporary tablespace
cause: Undo tablespace cannot be specified as default temporary tablespace for the user
solution: Check the tablespace name and reissue the command

message: Undo tablespace cannot be specified as default temporary tablespace
cause: Undo tablespace cannot be specified as default temporary tablespace for the database
solution: Check the tablespace name and reissue the command

message: Cannot perform parallel DML after a prior DML on the object
cause: Attempt to perform parallel DML after another DML on the same object in the same transaction.
solution: Use bitmap segments to perform multiple (parallel) DML operations on the same object. Or commit before issueing the DML

message: Cannot perform parallel insert on non-partitioned object
cause: Attempt to perform parallel insert on a non-partitioned object after a previous DML on the object in the same transaction.
solution: Commit before issueing the insert.

message: Cannot drop the undo tablespace
cause: Cannot drop an undo tablespace that is in use
solution: Switch to a different undo tablespace and then try to drop

message: Undo tablespace is offline
cause: Cannot operate on an offlined undo tablespace
solution: Online the undo tablespace and redo the operation

message: Cannot grant quota on the tablespace
cause: User tried to grant quota on an undo or temporary tablespace
solution: Check the tablespace name and reissue the command

message: Cannot offline the undo tablespace
cause: Cannot offline an undo tablespace that is in use
solution: Switch to a different undo tablespace and then try to offline

message: Invalid value ' string ' specified for parameter 'Undo_Management'
cause: the specified undo management mode is invalid
solution: Correct the parameter value in the initialization file and retry the operation.

message: 'Retention' can only specified for undo tablespace
cause: An attempt was made to specify retention for a non-undo tablespace.
solution: Modify the CREATE TABLESPACE statement.

message: No undo tablespace name specified
cause: If Create Database has the datafile clause, then undo tablespace name has to be specified, unless using OMF.
solution: Specify the undo tablespace name.

message: Undo tablespace string not found in control file.
cause: The specified undo tablespace is not present in the control file.
solution: Modify the CREATE CONTROLFILE statement that created the current control file to include undo tablespace(s) and reissue the statement.

message: VERSIONS clause not allowed here
cause: A VERSIONS clause was specified when it was not allowed.
solution: Do not use the VERSIONS clause

message: invalid lower limit snapshot expression
cause: The lower limit snapshot expression was below the UNDO_RETENTION limit.
solution: Specify a valid lower limit snapshot expression.

message: invalid upper limit snapshot expression
cause: The upper limit snapshot expression is greater than the SQL statement read snapshot.
solution: Specify a valid upper limit snapshot expression.

message: invalid upper limit snapshot expression
cause: The upper limit snapshot expression is less than the lower limit snapshot expression.
solution: Specify a valid upper limit snapshot expression.

message: NULL snapshot expression not allowed here
cause: The snapshot expression is NULL.
solution: Specify a non-NULL snapshot expression.

message: conversion between datetime/interval and string fail
cause: An error occurs during a conversion between datetime/interval and string data type due to one of the following reasons: - The buffer is too short to hold the result. - The format string is bad.
solution: None

message: invalid time zone value
cause: The value specified for the time zone string, which appears in ALTER SESSION statement, environment variable ORA_SDTZ, or a datetime factor, is not valid.
solution: None

message: invalid adjustment value
cause: The value is none of the followings: 'ADJUST', 'NO_ADJUST', 'ANSI_DATE', 'ADJUST_WITH_ANSI_DATE'. 'NO_ADJUST' is the default value.
solution: set it to one of the three values

message: GLOBAL partitioned index on TIME/TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE not allowed
cause: try to GLOBAL partitioned index on TIME/TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE.
solution: Do not GLOBAL partitioned index on TIME/TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE.

message: TIME/TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE literal must be specified in CHECK constraint
cause: User is trying to create a constraint on a time or timestamp with or without time zone column without explicitly specifying the time zone.
solution: Use time or timestamp with time zone literals only.

message: invalid extract field for extract source
cause: The extract source does not contain the specified extract field.
solution: None

message: illegal casting between specified datetime types
cause: Cannot cast between the specified datetime types.
solution: None

message: partition bound must be TIME/TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE literals
cause: An attempt was made to use a time/timestamp expression whose format does not explicitly have time zone on a TIME/TIMESTAMP or TIME/TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE column.
solution: Explicitly use TIME/TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE literal.

message: cannot alter database timezone when database has TIMESTAMP WITH LOCAL TIME ZONE columns
cause: An attempt was made to alter database timezone with TIMESTAMP WITH LOCAL TIME ZONE column in the database.
solution: Either do not alter database timezone or first drop all the TIMESTAMP WITH LOCAL TIME ZONE columns.

message: invalid data type for datetime/interval arithmetic
cause: The data types of the operands are not valid for datetime/interval arithmetic.
solution: None

message: datetime/interval column to be modified must be empty to decrease fractional second or leading field precision
cause: datetime/interval column with existing data is being modified to decrease fractional second or leading field precisions.
solution: Such columns are only allowed to increase the precisions.

message: syntax error was found in interval value expression
cause: A syntax error was found during parsing an interval value value expression.
solution: Correct the syntax.

message: invalid data type for datetime primary with time zone modifier
cause: When a time zone modifier is specified, the data type of datetime primary must be one of the following: TIME, TIME WITH TIME ZONE, TIMESTAMP, TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE.
solution: None

message: syntax error was found in overlaps predicate
cause: A syntax error was found during parsing an overlaps predicate.
solution: Correct the syntax.

message: interval year-month result not allowed for datetime subtraction
cause: An attempt was made to specify interval year to month as the result of datetime subtraction.
solution: This is not allowed currently due to unclear specification in SQL Standards for this interval type. Change the interval type to interval day to second and resubmit statement.

message: Adding two datetime values is not allowed
cause: An attempt was made to add two datetime values.
solution: This addition is not allowed.

message: datetime/interval precision is out of range
cause: The specified datetime/interval precision was not between 0 and 9.
solution: Use a value between 0 and 9 for datetime/interval precision.

message: missing or invalid <datetime field>
cause: A <datetime field> (YEAR, MONTH, DAY, HOUR, MINUTE, SECOND) is expected but not found, or a <datetime field> specified the <end field> in an <interval qualifier> is more significant than its <start field>.
solution: None

message: secondary translation table not loaded
cause: The secondary translation table for DST patching on TSTZ data was not loaded.
solution: Load the secondary translation table.

message: function not allowed at this stage of DST upgrade process
cause: Query included a function that is not allowed in the current state of DST upgrade process.
solution: This function is not allowed at the currect stage of DST upgrade.

message: function not allowed until the database is restarted
cause: Query included a function that is not allowed until the database is restarted.
solution: Shut down and restart the database.

message: failed to find the time zone data file for version string in $ORACLE_HOME/oracore/zoneinfo
cause: There was no corresponding time zone data file in $ORACLE_HOME/oracore/zoneinfo for the input time zone version.
solution: None

message: internal error [ number ]
cause: An internal error has occurred.
solution: Contact Oracle Worldwide Support and report the error.

message: unknown parameter name ' string '
cause: You have misspelled the parameter name.
solution: Spell the parameter name correctly.

message: ' string ' is not in the legal range for ' string '
cause: The value of the parameter is not within the legal range.
solution: Refer to the manual for the allowable values for this parameter.

message: ' string ' contains an illegal integer radix for ' string '
cause: An illegal integer radix specification was found.
solution: Only 'd', 'h', 'D', and 'H' may be used as radix specifications.

message: ' string ' is not a legal integer for ' string '
cause: The value is not a valid integer.
solution: Specify only valid integers for this parameter.

message: ' string ' is not a legal boolean for ' string '
cause: The value is not a valid boolean.
solution: Refer to the manual for allowable boolean values.

message: parameter name abbreviation ' string ' is not unique
cause: The abbreviation given was not unique.
solution: Use a longer abbreviation to make the parameter name unique.

message: invalid positional parameter value ' string '
cause: An invalid positional parameter value has been entered.
solution: Remove the invalid positional parameter.

message: could not open parameter file ' string '
cause: The parameter file does not exist.
solution: Create an appropriate parameter file.

message: syntax error at ' string '
cause: A syntax error was detected.
solution: Change the input so that the correct syntax is used.

message: no closing quote for value ' string '
cause: A quoted string was begun but not finished.
solution: Put a closing quote in the proper location.

message: multiple values not allowed for parameter ' string '
cause: You attempted to specify multiple values for a parameter which can take only one value.
solution: Do not specify more than one value for this parameter.

message: error when processing file ' string '
cause: A problem occurred when processing this file.
solution: Examine the additional error messages and correct the problem.

message: error when processing from command line
cause: A problem occurred when processing the command line.
solution: Examine the additional error messages and correct the problem.

message: error when processing an environment variable
cause: A problem occurred when processing an environment variable.
solution: Examine the additional error messages and correct the problem.

message: syntax error at ' string ' following ' string '
cause: A syntax error was detected.
solution: Change the input so that the correct syntax is used.

message: syntax error at ' string ' at the start of input
cause: A syntax error was detected.
solution: Change the input so that the correct syntax is used.

message: syntax error at ' string ' at the end of input
cause: A syntax error was detected.
solution: Change the input so that the correct syntax is used.

message: unable to obtain a valid value for ' string '
cause: No valid value was obtained for this parameter.
solution: Rerun the application and enter a valid value.

message: ' string ' is not a legal oracle number for ' string '
cause: The value is not a valid oracle number.
solution: Refer to the manual for allowable oracle number values.

message: ' string ' is not an allowable value for ' string '
cause: The value is not a legal value for this parameter.
solution: Refer to the manual for allowable values.

message: value ' string ' for ' string ' must be between ' number ' and ' number '
cause: The value of the parameter is not within the legal range.
solution: Specify a value that is within the legal range.

message: invalid function argument received
cause: A function received an invalid argument
solution: Check function calls, make sure correct arguments are being passed.

message: invalid parameter key type received
cause: A function received an invalid parameter key type
solution: Check parameter key types in function calls

message: number of keys being set exceeds allocation
cause: Number of parameter keys being set exceeds allocation
solution: Reduce the number of keys being set or increase allocation

message: invalid key index supplied
cause: The key index specified was not within bounds
solution: Change key index to ensure it lies within bounds

message: OCI Thread operation fails
cause: An OCI Thread function call has failed.
solution: Check the function call to make sure that the correct parameters are being passed and take the apropriate action.

message: Drop-in compatibility is not supported for this application
cause: The current application is statically linked with defopt.o from an older release, which is incompatible with the current client shared library.
solution: 1) Relink the application against the new release of the client library; or 2) Relink the application against the older release of the client library without statically linking defopt.o.

message: Invalid argument passed to OCIFile function
cause: An invalid argument is passed to the OCIFile function. The most common cause is that a NULL pointer is passed where a non-NULL pointer is expected.
solution: Make sure that the values passed as arguments are valid. Esp check for NULL pointers.

message: File already exists
cause: Tried to open a file with OCI_FILE_EXCL flag and the file already exists.
solution: OCIFile is supposed throw this exception in this case.

message: File does not exist
cause: The OCIFile function requires the file to exist, but it does not.
solution: Make sure that the file exists.

message: An invalid File Object is passed to the OCIFile function
cause: An invalid File Object is passed to the OCIFile function.
