cause: An attempt was made to perform disassociation operation on a Flashback Data Archive enabled table that is in compliance mode. Or, DDL are not supported on tables in noncompliance mode.
solution: Disable compliance mode before retrying the disassociation operation.

message: DDL operations on Flashback Data Archive-enabled table are not allowed at this point
cause: Flashback Data Archive could not acquire resources to complete the operation on Oracle RAC.
solution: Retry the DDL at a later time.

message: Flashback Data Archive internal SQL error
cause: Flashback Data Archive encountered internal SQL error.
solution: No action required.

message: Insufficient privilege to perform the Flashback Data Archive operation
cause: An attempt was made to disassociate tables enabled for Flashback Data Archive without the required privilege.
solution: No action required.

message: Cannot drop tablespace used by Flashback Data Archive
cause: An attempt was made to drop a Flashback Data Archive tablespace.
solution: Remove the tablespace from Flashback Data Archive before retrying the operation.

message: Table has column names that are reserved by Flashback Data Archive
cause: The table on which Flashback Data Archive is being enabled contains column(s) with names that are reserved by Flashback Data Archive.
solution: Rename column name before retry.

message: Unable to alter system parameter GLOBAL_TXN_PROCESSES at this time
cause: The system was in the process of adjusting the number of global transaction background processes.
solution: Retry the operation at a later time.

message: Unable to bind clusterwide global transactions to compatible undo
cause: Undo tablespace was not onlined for automatic undo management.
solution: Create undo tablespace if it has not been created.

message: XA transactions on RAC are not supported with GLOBAL_TXN_PROCESSES set to 0
cause: The initialization parameter GLOBAL_TXN_PROCESSES was set to 0.
solution: Set the initialization parameter GLOBAL_TXN_PROCESSES to a value greater than 0.

message: GLOBAL_TXN_PROCESSES cannot be set to 0 at runtime
cause: An attempt was made to set initialization parameter GLOBAL_TXN_PROCESSES to 0 at runtime.
solution: Set the initialization parameter GLOBAL_TXN_PROCESSES to 0 before starting RAC instance to disable GTX background processes. Note that XA transactions are not supported on RAC database when GTX background processes are disabled.

message: savepoint ' string ' disabled with interleaved changes across Oracle RAC instances
cause: After the savepoints were established, interleaved changes were made across Oracle RAC instances within the clusterwide global transaction.
solution: Do not make interleaved changes across Oracle RAC instances after savepoints are established.

message: NLS errors while processing Oracle number
cause: Error occurred when trying to convert Oracle number to an integer.
solution: Check the input parameters.

message: Event to control CR activity
cause: The bit values that we consider. 0x1: Remove fix for bug 3514835 which could potentially throw more 8177 errors We have conservatively blocked some serializability errors, where there could potentially be a dependency between a service transaction in an index and forward going transaction.
solution: Set event 55801 to 1 to disable the bug fix, thereby reducing 8177 error, although it might cause some internal errors instead.

message: DRCP: Pool not found
cause: The pool name passed was either null or an invalid pool name.
solution: Input a valid pool name.

message: DRCP: Pool startup failed
cause: The connection pool failed to start up.
solution: Check logs for details.

message: DRCP: Pool is inactive
cause: The operation is only supported on an active pool.
solution: Start the pool.

message: DRCP: Pool is active
cause: The operation is only supported on an inactive pool.
solution: Shutdown the pool.

message: DRCP: Invalid pool configuration parameter name
cause: The configuration paramter name is null or invalid input.
solution: Input a valid configuration parameter name.

message: DRCP: Invalid pool configuration parameter value
cause: The configuration paramter value is null or invalid input.
solution: Input a valid configuration parameter value.

message: DRCP: Pool shutdown failed
cause: Connection pool failed to shutdown.
solution: Check logs for details.

message: DRCP: Pool alter configuration failed
cause: Connection pool failed to configure pool.
solution: Check logs for details.

message: DRCP: Pool startup failed
cause: Connection Broker failed to startup the pool.
solution: Check logs for details.

message: DRCP: Pool shutdown failed
cause: Connection Broker failed to shutdown the pool.
solution: Check logs for details.

message: DRCP: Pool alter configuration failed
cause: Connection Broker failed to configure the pool.
solution: Check logs for details.

message: DRCP: Cross instance synchronization failed
cause: Publish message to all RAC instances failed.
solution: Check logs for details.

message: DRCP: Failed to synchronize RAC instances [ string ]
cause: Some of the RAC instances were not synchronized.
solution: Perform the same operations on all the failed instances.

message: DRCP: Cannot perform requested operation using pooled connection
cause: This operation was not supported using connections from a pool.
solution: Use a regular connection to perform this operation.

message: DRCP: invalid value for maximum number of connections to Connection broker
cause: The value passed exceeded the maximum allowed.
solution: No action required. The maximum number of connections was automatically set to the maximum allowed value.

message: DRCP: Illegal call [ string ]
cause: An illegal OCI function call was issued.
solution: Check the documentation for Database Resident Connection Pool (DRCP) usage.

message: DRCP: Illegal connection class
cause: Wrong value for connection class was given.
solution: Check the documentation for Database Resident connection pool usage.

message: DRCP: Illegal purity
cause: Wrong value for purity was provided.
solution: Check the documentation for Database Resident connection pool usage.

message: DRCP: Internal error
cause: Malformed input values.
solution: Input well-formed values.

message: DRCP: Length[ string ] for string exceeded the MAX allowed
cause: Length exceeded MAX for the value.
solution: Use a value within the MAX allowed.

message: DRCP: Session switching and migration not allowed
cause: Application tried to switch or migrate session across connections.
solution: This usage is irrelevant in the Database Resident connection pooling context and is not supported. Release existing session.

message: DRCP: Client version does not support the feature
cause: The client version is lower than 11g.
solution: Upgrade to a higher client version or turn off (SERVER=POOLED) in the connect string.

message: DRCP: Connection is already authenticated
cause: Attempt to reauthenticate the connection which is authenticated.
solution: Logoff the connection before reauthenticating.

message: DRCP: Server Group feature is not supported
cause: Server Group attribute was set on the server handle, connected to a Database Resident connection pool.
solution: Do not set Server Group attribute on server handles while using Database Resident connection pool.

message: Usage not supported with DRCP
cause: This usage was not supported on a DRCP connection.
solution: Use a dedicated connection to perform this task.

message: plan string is a subplan and SUB_PLAN attribute cannot be modified
cause: An attempt was made to modify the SUB_PLAN attribute of the specified plan.
solution: Do not attempt to modify the SUB_PLAN attribute.

message: INTERNAL_USE attribute of consumer group string cannot be modified
cause: An attempt was made to modify the INTERNAL_USE attribute of the specified consumer group.
solution: Do not attempt to modify the INTERNAL_USE attribute.

message: consumer group string is for internal use only and cannot be a switch target
cause: An attempt was made to specify an INTERNAL_USE consumer group as a switch target.
solution: Do not attempt to switch to INTERNAL_USE consumer groups.

message: VKTM process died unexpectedly
cause: An explicit kill or internal error caused the death of VKTM background process.
solution: Restart the instance.

message: EXPLICIT consumer group mapping priority must be set to 1
cause: An attempt was made to set the EXPLICIT mapping priority to a value other than 1.
solution: Set the mapping priorities to unique integers within the documented range with the EXPLICT priority set to 1.

message: I/O calibration already in progress
cause: An attempt was made to run a second instance of I/O Calibration
solution: Wait until the first I/O calibration run is complete; then, retry the operation.

message: The specified Resource Manager plan is a subplan and cannot be set as a top-level plan
cause: An attempt was made to set a subplan as a top-level plan.
solution: Do not attempt to set subplans as top-level plans.

message: INTERNAL_QUIESCE plan cannot be specified as a top-level Resource Manager plan
cause: An attempt was made to specify INTERNAL_QUIESCE as a top-level Resource Manager plan.
solution: Do not attempt to set INTERNAL_QUIESCE as a Resource Manager plan.

message: Could not find any datafiles with asynchronous i/o capability
cause: There are no datafiles which are asynchronous I/O capable.
solution: Make sure asynchronous i/o is permitted to datafiles.

message: timed_statistics set to FALSE
cause: timed_statistics parameter in database is set to FALSE. Needs to be enabled for calibration.
solution: set timed_statistics=TRUE in init.ora or "alter system set timed_statistics=TRUE"

message: DBRM process died unexpectedly
cause: An explicit kill or internal error caused the death of the DBRM background process.
solution: Restart the instance.

message: string is an invalid string argument
cause: The named argument is invalid.
solution: Specify a valid argument for this procedure.

message: Insufficient Resource Manager privileges
cause: An attempt was made to switch the consumer group of a user without the appropriate privilege.
solution: Ask the database administrator to perform the switch operation or grant switch or system privilege to the user.

message: Plan name string exceeds the maximum length allowed
cause: Plan name is greater than 30 characters long.
solution: Do not exceed 30 characters when naming a resource plan.

message: string resource plan contains a reserved word
cause: The specified plan name is prefixed with a reserved prefix such as FORCE or SCHED.
solution: Do not prefix resource plan name with FORCE or SCHED.

message: Category string does not exist
cause: A non-existent category was specified as an argument to a procedure in the package, DBMS_RESOURCE_MANAGER.
solution: Specify an existing category name or create a new category with this name.

message: SWITCH_TIME is set without specifying SWITCH_GROUP
cause: The plan directive specifies a SWITCH_TIME without a SWITCH_GROUP.
solution: Specify a SWITCH_GROUP parameter in the plan directive.

message: Timeout occurred while setting resource plan
cause: A timeout occurred while waiting for one or more RAC instances to set the resource plan.
solution: Since the resource plan may have actually been set successfully, first check the current resource plan for each instance by querying gv$rsrc_plan. If the resource plan was not successfully set on all instances, then retry the operation.

message: Error spawning or communicating with calibration slave
cause: An error occurred in calibration slave process - Calibration process aborted.
solution: Review trace files for errors.

message: I/O data limit exceeded - call aborted
cause: The Resource Manager SWITCH_IO_MEGABYTES limit was exceeded.
solution: Reduce the complexity of the update or query, or contact your database administrator for more information.

message: I/O data limit exceeded - session terminated
cause: The Resource Manager SWITCH_IO_MEGABYTES limit was exceeded.
solution: Reduce the complexity of the update or query, or contact your database administrator for more information.

message: I/O request limit exceeded - call aborted
cause: The Resource Manager SWITCH_IO_REQS limit was exceeded.
solution: Reduce the complexity of the update or query, or contact your database administrator for more information.

message: I/O request limit exceeded - session terminated
cause: The Resource Manager SWITCH_IO_REQS limit was exceeded.
solution: Reduce the complexity of the update or query, or contact your database administrator for more information.

message: Could not spawn additional calibration slaves
cause: An error occurred when spawning calibration slave process - Calibration process aborted.
solution: Check OS resources required for spawning processes

message: Category string is referred to by a consumer group and cannot be deleted
cause: An attempt was made to delete a category that is referred to by a consumer group.
solution: Modify or remove all consumer groups that use this category and then retry.

message: Orion ( string ) must be invoked using its full, absolute path
cause: Orion is spawning a child process and cannot determine the location of the executable.
solution: Use the full, absolute path for Orion.

message: SQL blocks cannot be nested
cause: An attempt was made to start an SQL block using DBMS_RESOURCE_MANAGER.BEGIN_SQL_BLOCK() while already inside an SQL block.
solution: Close the existing SQL block using DBMS_RESOURCE_MANAGER.BEGIN_SQL_BLOCK() or remove this call.

message: Failed to bind the database instance to processor group string
cause: Binding the database instance to the processor group specified by the PROCESSOR_GROUP_NAME parameter failed.
solution: Set the PROCESSOR_GROUP_NAME to a valid, configured processor group and restart the database instance.

message: DSKM process died unexpectedly
cause: An explicit kill or internal error caused the death of the DSKM background process.
solution: Restart the instance.

message: LIBCELL API error in Master Diskmon
cause: A LIBCELL operation in Master Diskmon failed.
solution: Look in the $ORA_CRS_HOME/log/<hostname>/diskmon/diskmon.log file for additional error information.

message: Master Diskmon cannot connect to a CELL
cause: A LIBCELL operation from Master Diskmon failed to create a network connection to the target CELL.
solution: Look in the $ORA_CRS_HOME/log/<hostname>/diskmon/diskmon.log file for additional error information.

message: LIBCELL operation network error in Master Diskmon
cause: A LIBCELL operation in Master Diskmon failed because of a network error.
solution: Look in the $ORA_CRS_HOME/log/<hostname>/diskmon/diskmon.log file for additional error information.

message: LIBCELL SKGXP error in Master Diskmon
cause: A LIBCELL operation from Master Diskmon failed because of an SKGXP network layer error.
solution: Look in the $ORA_CRS_HOME/log/<hostname>/diskmon/diskmon.log file for additional error information.

message: Master Diskmon " string string " operation cannot complete because of a LIBCELL network error
cause: A LIBCELL operation between Master Diskmon and a CELL failed because of a network error.
solution: Look in the $ORA_CRS_HOME/log/<hostname>/diskmon/diskmon.log file for additional error information.

message: Invalid IP address in CELLINIT.ORA
cause: One or more of the specified IP addresses in CELLINIT.ORA is not valid.
solution: Check that all IP addresses in CELLINIT.ORA are valid.

message: No IP parameter
cause: No IP address is set in CELLINIT.ORA.
solution: Check that one or more valid IP addresses are set in CELLINIT.ORA.

message: Cannot connect to Master Diskmon on pipe " string "
cause: Master Diskmon was not running or the listening pipe was deleted.
solution: Look at the $ORA_CRS_HOME/log/<hostname>/diskmon/diskmon.log, $ORA_CRS_HOME/log/<hostname>/hasmsgs.log and $ORA_CRS_HOME/log/<hostname>/alert<hostname>.log for additional error information.

message: Duplicate IP address in CELLINIT.ORA
cause: One or more of the specified IP addresses in CELLINIT.ORA was repeated.
solution: Check that all IP addresses in CELLINIT.ORA are unique.

message: Attempt to register dead cell with Master Diskmon
cause: An attempt was made by a process to register a cell that is known to be down.
solution: None

message: bind variable is not supported inside pivot|unpivot operation
cause: Attempted to use bind variables inside pivot|unpivot operation.
solution: This is not supported.

message: non-constant expression is not allowed for pivot|unpivot values
cause: Attempted to use non-constant expression for pivot|unpivot values.
solution: Use constants for pivot|unpivot values.

message: expect aggregate function inside pivot operation
cause: Attempted to use non-aggregate expression inside pivot operation.
solution: Use aggregate function.

message: sys_op_pivot function is not allowed here
cause: invalid use of sys_op_pivot function.
solution: Remove sys_op_pivot function.

message: pivot value must have datatype that is convertible to pivot column
cause: Datatype of pivot value is not convertible to the datatype of pivot column.
solution: Check and correct pivot value.

message: a prepare or upgrade window or an on-demand or datapump-job loading of a secondary time zone data file is in an active state
cause: A prepare or upgrade window was started or an on-demand or datapump-job loading of a secondary time zone data file was done.
solution: Make sure there is no active prepare or upgrade window and no active on-demand or datapump-job loading of a secondary time zone data file.

message: invalid time zone version
cause: Invalid time zone version passed.
solution: Check and correct the time zone version.

message: Starting a prepare window failed
cause: Error(s) occurred when starting a prepare window.
solution: Check alert or trace file for error(s).

message: database properties related to time zone version are not set up properly
cause: There were no database properties related to time zone version in dictionary table sys.props$.
solution: Contact Oracle Support Services.

message: prepare window does not exist
cause: There was no active prepare window.
solution: None

message: Ending a prepare window failed
cause: Error(s) occurred when ending a prepare window.
solution: Check alert or trace file for error(s).

message: database must be in UPGRADE mode in order to start an upgrade window
cause: Database was not in UPGRADE mode.
solution: Restart database in UPGRADE mode.

message: Starting an upgrade window failed
cause: Error(s) occurred when starting an upgrade window.
solution: Check alert or trace file for error(s).

message: upgrade window does not exist
cause: There was no active upgrade window.
solution: None

message: Ending an upgrade window failed
cause: Ending an upgrade window failed or there were tables containing TSTZ data which have not been upgraded.
solution: Check alert or trace file for error(s) or complete upgrading of tables containing TSTZ data.

message: database must be restarted before performing upgrade of user tables
cause: Database was not restarted after starting an upgrade window.
solution: Restart database.

message: inconsistent DST patching state found
cause: DST patching was in an inconsistent state.
solution: Contact Oracle Support Services.

message: " string "." string " does not exist
cause: Specified table name was invalid.
solution: Check the existence of the specified table name.

message: Table creation failed
cause: Error(s) occurred when creating the table.
solution: Check the error.

message: database property DST_UPGRADE_STATE for datapump job is in an inconsistent state
cause: Database property DST_UPRGRADE_STATE was not recorded correctly.
solution: Check the alert file.

message: existing datapump jobs are using a different version of time zone data file
cause: An attempt was made from a datapump job to request a different version of time zone data file from the one used by existing datapump jobs.
solution: Wait until existing datapump jobs unload the secondary time zone data file.

message: datapump jobs are utilizing secondary time zone data file
cause: An on-demand loading of secondary time zone data file was requested when there was a secondary time zone data file already loaded in the database utilized by existing datapump jobs.
solution: Wait until existing datapump jobs unload the secondary time zone data file.

message: failed to load the secondary time zone data file
cause: Attempt to load the secondary timezone data file failed.
solution: Check alert or trace files for error(s).

message: no secondary time zone data file being loaded by on-demand or a datapump job
cause: There was no secondary timezone data file being loaded by on-demand or a datapump job.
solution: None

message: failed to unload the secondary time zone data file
cause: Attempt to unload the secondary timezone data file failed.
solution: Check alert or trace files for error(s).

message: Invalid value for incident identifier
cause: Invalid incident identifier argument passed.
solution: Check and correct the identifier

message: Invalid set of export options
cause: The options specified are inconsistent
solution: Check and a consistent set of option parameters

message: referenced file not found
cause: One of the file specified in the test case package is mising
solution: rebuild the SQL test case or make sure that all the referenced files are readable and located in the same directory as the SQL test case manifest.

message: import options do not match export options
cause: The import options specified do not match the export options
solution: Check that import is being invoked with the same values for options like export environment, export data and export metadata

message: Invalid set of import options
cause: The import options specified are inconsistent
solution: Check that import options are consistent and have valid values

message: TimesTen IMDB error: string
cause: An error occurred during a TimesTen operation.
solution: Look up the error code in the TimesTen error documentation to diagnose.

message: adding ( string ) blocks to save undo segment in tablespace string with MAXSIZE ( string )
cause: Save undo for the offline tablespace at segment MAXSIZE.
solution: Check the storage parameters for the system tablespace. The tablespace needs to be brought back online so the undo can be applied.

message: adding ( string ) blocks to temporary segment in tablespace string with MAXSIZE ( string )
cause: Extending a temporary segment violated MAXSIZE limit.
solution: Increase the MAXSIZE limit and retry command.

message: adding ( string ) blocks to table string . string partition string with MAXSIZE ( string )
cause: Extending a table partition violated MAXSIZE limit.
solution: Increase the MAXSIZE limit and retry command.

message: adding ( string ) blocks to table string . string with MAXSIZE ( string )
cause: Extending a table violated MAXSIZE limit.
solution: Increase the MAXSIZE limit and retry command.

message: adding ( string ) blocks to cluster string . string with MAXSIZE ( string )
cause: Extending a cluster violated MAXSIZE limit.
solution: Increase the MAXSIZE limit and retry command.

message: adding ( string ) blocks to index string . string partition string with MAXSIZE ( string )
cause: Extending an index partition violated MAXSIZE limit.
solution: Increase the MAXSIZE limit and retry command.

message: adding ( string ) blocks to index string . string subpartition string with MAXSIZE ( string )
cause: Extending an index subpartition violated MAXSIZE limit.
solution: Increase the MAXSIZE limit and retry command.

message: adding ( string ) blocks to index string . string with MAXSIZE ( string )
cause: Extending an index violated MAXSIZE limit.
solution: Increase the MAXSIZE limit and retry command.

message: adding ( string ) blocks to LOB segment string . string partition string with MAXSIZE ( string )
cause: Extending a LOB segment violated MAXSIZE limit.
solution: Increase the MAXSIZE limit and retry command.

message: adding ( string ) blocks to LOB segment string . string with MAXSIZE ( string )
cause: Extending a LOB segment violated MAXSIZE limit.
solution: Increase the MAXSIZE limit and retry command.

message: adding ( string ) blocks to lob segment string . string subpartition string with MAXSIZE ( string )
cause: Extending a LOB segment violated MAXSIZE limit.
solution: Increase the MAXSIZE limit and retry command.

message: adding ( string ) blocks to table string . string subpartition string with MAXSIZE ( string )
cause: Extending a table subpartition violated MAXSIZE limit.
solution: Increase the MAXSIZE limit and retry command.

message: invalid MAXSIZE storage option value
cause: Invalid value was specified for MAXSIZE storage clause.
solution: Correct the value and retry command.

message: invalid MAXSIZE storage option value
cause: Minimum of 1M should have been specified against the MAXSIZE storage clause.
solution: Correct the value and retry command.

message: invalid RETENTION storage option value
cause: Value of MIN retention should have been nonzero.
solution: Correct the value and retry command.

message: Operation not supported on SECUREFILE segment
cause: The operation to ALTER FREELIST/RETENTION was not supported on SECUREFILE segment.
solution: Check the LOB type and reissue the statement.

message: adding string blocks to rollback segment string with MAXSIZE ( string )
cause: Extending a rollback segment violated MAXSIZE limit.
solution: Increase the MAXSIZE limit and retry command.

message: Creating initial extent of size string in tablespace of extent size string
cause: Creation of SECUREFILE segment failed due to small tablespace extent size.
solution: Create tablespace with larger extent size and reissue command.

message: Event for temp segment cleanup used for temp lobs
cause: Temp LOB segments used for temporary LOBs are deleted only on session exit which may lead to large amounts of memory being held across multiple sessions.
solution: Setting this event will cause temporary LOB segments to be freed when there are no active temporary LOBs in the session. Setting this event will have a significant performance impact as it can cause temporary lob segments to be allocated and deleted many times during a session rather than once per session. Use this event only when temporary LOB segment memory use is an issue.

message: value for parameter cannot contain a comma
cause: Parameter value contained a comma.
solution: Remove the comma from the parameter value.

message: encountered a value of unsupported type or size for XPath ( string )
cause: A value of an unsupported type was encountered in a SQL/XML operator. SQL/XML operators, such as updateXML, expect value operands of type VARCHAR2 and XMLTYPE. XML DML replication is not supported for SQL/XML DML operators with values of unsupported types or very large values of supported types.
solution: Use event 19027 level 1 to dump XML document instead of XMLDiff in redo log.

message: Cannot rewrite a newer version of XML redo diff (encountered: string , supported: string )
cause: Encountered a newer version of XML redo diff that is not supported.
solution: Use RDBMS version that supports rewrite of given version of XML redo diff.

message: operation disallowed: data file string is being moved
cause: The specified data file was being moved.
solution: Wait for the move operation to complete and retry the command.

message: file error during move operation
cause: The move operation encountered an error for the moved data file. The error might be caused by file going offline or by an I/O error. See alert or trace files in all instances for further information.
solution: Retry the move command.

message: a data file copy that is not current
cause: An obsolete copy of a data file left from a data file move operation was used for the CREATE CONTROLFILE command or file header read.
solution: Pass a valid file or perform a media recovery on the file.

message: a half-done data file copy
cause: A half-done copy of a data file created from a previous data file move operation was used for the CREATE CONTROLFILE command or file header read.
solution: Check file headers and pass only valid files.

message: file size refresh failed
cause: An operating system error or device error occurred when retrieving the file's size.
solution: Remedy the operating system or device errors mentioned in the error stack and then perform crash recovery.

message: undo tablespace file suffered media failure
cause: An undo tablespace file was detected as inaccessible due to media failure.
solution: Restore accessibility to the file mentioned in the error stack and restart the instance.

message: data file suffered media failure
cause: A data file was detected as inaccessible due to media failure.
solution: Restore accessibility to the file mentioned in the error stack and restart the instance.

message: specified path already exists
cause: The pathname of a new item specified in a DBFS API operation already exists.
solution: Specify a valid, new pathname for the operation.

message: invalid parent directory in specified path
cause: The pathname of an item specified in a DBFS API operation has one or more invalid parent components.
solution: Specify a valid pathname with valid parent components for the operation.

message: specified path is invalid
cause: The pathname of an item specified in a DBFS API operation is invalid.
solution: Specify a valid pathname for the operation.

message: an unsupported operation was invoked
cause: The current DBFS API operation is unsupported by a provider.
solution: Use the provider feature set to invoke only supported operations.

message: an invalid combination of arguments was specified
cause: The current DBFS API operation specifies an invalid combination of arguments for the specified pathname(s) and operation.
solution: Specify a valid combination of pathname(s) and arguments.

message: access control checks failed
cause: The current DBFS API operation failed access control checks for the pathname(s) being accessed.
solution: Specify valid pathname(s) and principal for the operation, or take store-specific actions to enable access.

message: lock conflict in current operation
cause: A DBFS API locking operation could not be completed due to conflicts in the locking protocol.
solution: Follow the proper lock/unlock protocol according to the provider feature set.

message: invalid store specified
cause: The current operation specifies an invalid store name.
solution: Specify a valid store name for the operation.

message: invalid mount-point specified
cause: The current operation specifies an invalid mount-point.
solution: Specify a valid mount-point for the operation.

message: invalid provider specified
cause: The current operation refers to an invalid or incomplete or non-conformant store provider package.
solution: Specify a valid, complete, and conformant (per "dbms_dbfs_content_spi") store provider package.

message: cannot modify store via read-only mount
cause: The current operation attempts to modify a store via a read-only mount (or specifies a read-only store).
solution: Specify a valid modifiable store/mount for the operation.

message: cross store operation
cause: The current operation attempts to span 2 or more different stores and cannot be implemented entirely by the DBFS API.
solution: Split the operation, at the application-level, into multiple sub-operations to implement the same overall functionality.

message: specified path is a directory
cause: The current operation specifies a path that is a directory element, when a non-directory element is expected.
solution: Specify a path of the proper type for the operation.

message: specified path is not a directory
cause: The current operation specifies a path that is not a directory element, when a directory element is expected.
solution: Specify a path of the proper type for the operation.

message: directory not empty
cause: The current operation specifies a directory element that is not empty as required.
solution: Specify an empty directory element.

message: Cannot alter both a structured and an unstructured component of an XMLIndex in the same ALTER INDEX statement.
cause: An attempt was made to alter the unstructured component and structured component of an XMLIndex at the same time.
solution: Use separate ALTER INDEX statements to change an unstructured component and a structured component of an XMLIndex.

message: Cannot create an XMLIndex with a structured component on a CLOB column within the object-relational storage model.
cause: An attempt was made to create an XMLIndex with a structured component on a CLOB column within the object-relational storage model.
solution: Only unstructured XML indexes can be created on a CLOB column within the object-relational storage model.

message: Cannot create an XMLIndex on an object-relational XML type table or column.
cause: An attempt was made to create an XMLIndex on an XML type table or column that uses the object-relational storage model.
solution: The object-relational storage model does not support an XMLIndex.

message: Column name already used by internal column of the structured component of the XMLIndex.
cause: An attempt was made to use a column name already in use by an internal column of the structured component of the XMLIndex.
solution: Chose another column name.

message: Cannot create domain index on XMLIndex internal tables.
cause: An attempt was made to create a domain index on an internal table of an XMLIndex.
solution: Create the domain index on the base table.

message: Incorrect use of comma(,) punctuation in COLUMN definitions.
cause: An attempt was made to define COLUMNS with incorrect use of comma punctuation.
solution: Properly separate COLUMN definitions with comma punctuation.

message: The XMLIndex has been successfully altered but the metadata could not be updated.
cause: An internal error occured when updating the index metadata. The dbms_metadata.get_ddl function may return improper metadata.
solution: contact Oracle Support Services.

message: Cannot truncate a table that has an XMLIndex whose internal table has been indexed using Oracle Text.
cause: An attempt was made to truncate a table that has an XMLIndex whose internal table has been indexed using Oracle Text.
solution: Drop the Oracle Text index on the XMLIndex internal table.

message: XMLIndex: problems encountered during the dropping of statistics
cause: See associated error message.
solution: Correct the error and retry command.

message: XMLIndex: problems encountered during the gathering of statistics
cause: See associated error message.
solution: Correct the error and retry command.

message: XMLIndex: problems encountered during EXPORT
cause: See associated error message.
solution: Correct the error and retry command.

message: XMLIndex: problems encountered during IMPORT
cause: See associated error message.
solution: Correct the error and retry command.

message: XMLIndex: XDB.XDB$XIDX_IMP_T still has bad data for " string "." string "
cause: See associated error message.
solution: Ask the DBA to delete all the rows that belong to the given schema_name.index_name from the system table XDB.XDB$XIDX_IMP_T."

message: XMLIndex Exchange Partition: the table has no XMLIndex
cause: The non-partitioned table had no XMLIndex.
solution: None

message: XMLIndex Exchange Partition: incompatible XPath subsets
cause: The XMLIndexes on the two tables had different path subsets.
solution: Correct the error and retry the command.

message: XMLIndex Exchange Partition: incompatible modes for asynchronous DML
cause: The XMLIndexes on the two tables had different deferred DML modes.
solution: Correct the error and retry the command.

message: XMLIndex Exchange Partition: incompatible unstructured components
cause: One of the XMLIndexes had no unstructured component.
solution: Correct the error and retry the command.

message: XMLIndex Exchange Partition: incompatible structured components
cause: One of the XMLIndexes had no structured component.
solution: Correct the error and retry the command.

message: XMLIndex Exchange Partition: incompatible structured components
cause: The XMLIndexes had different structured components.
solution: Correct the error and retry the command.

message: XMLIndex DDL: failure of the internal " string "
cause: See associated error message.
solution: Correct the error and retry command.

message: XMLIndex DDL: failure of the recursive " string "
cause: See associated error message.
solution: Correct the error and retry command.

message: XMLIndex DDL: failure of a recursive DDL
cause: See associated error message.
solution: Correct the error and retry command.

message: XMLIndex: failure during the setting of an event
cause: See associated error message.
solution: Correct the error and retry command.

message: XMLIndex: failure during the resetting of an event
cause: See associated error message.
solution: Correct the error and retry command.

message: XMLIndex Table Function: failure at the start of the function
cause: See associated error message.
solution: Examine the error messages and take appropriate action.

message: XMLIndex Table Function: failure at the beginning of the function
cause: See associated error message.
solution: Examine the error messages and take appropriate action.

message: XMLIndex Table Function: failure during the function evaluation
cause: See associated error message.
solution: Examine the error messages and take appropriate action.

message: XMLIndex Table Function: failure at the end of the function
cause: See associated error message.
solution: Examine the error messages and take appropriate action.

message: XMLIndex: invalid namespace mapping " string "
cause: Namespace mapping was invalid. The syntax is XMLNS="string".
solution: Check the namespace string, correct the error and retry command.

message: XMLIndex Metadata: failure during the looking up of the dictionary
cause: See associated error message.
solution: Correct the error and retry command.

message: XMLIndex Metadata: failure during the updating of the dictionary
cause: See associated error message.
solution: Correct the error and retry command.

message: XMLIndex DML: failure of the internal " string "
cause: See associated error message.
solution: Correct the error and retry command.

message: XMLIndex DML: failure of the recursive " string "
cause: See associated error message.
solution: Correct the error and retry command.

message: XMLIndex DML: failure of a recursive DML
cause: See associated error message.
solution: Correct the error and retry command.

message: XMLIndex Asynchronous DML: synchronization failure
cause: See associated error message.
solution: Correct the error and retry command.

message: Cannot drop an XMLIndex whose internal table has been indexed using Oracle Text.
cause: An attempt was made to drop an XMLIndex whose internal table has been indexed using Oracle Text.
solution: Drop the Oracle Text index on the XMLIndex internal table.

message: Cannot drop groups from an XMLIndex whose internal table has been indexed using Oracle Text.
cause: An attempt was made to drop groups from an XMLIndex whose internal table has been indexed using Oracle Text.
solution: Drop the Oracle Text index on the XMLIndex internal table.

message: The type of VIRTUAL column is not XMLTYPE
cause: An attempt was made to create an XML index with VIRTUAL column not of XMLTYPE.
solution: Specify the type of VIRTUAL column to be XMLTYPE.

message: missing chaining XMLTABLE for VIRTUAL column in the index
cause: An attempt was made to create an XML index with VIRTUAL column but without required chaining XMLTABLE.
solution: Specify a chaining XMLTABLE after VIRTUAL column.

message: Can only have a single XMLType column when a table is shared.
cause: An attempt was made to create a shared table with more than one columns.
solution: Specify a correct shared table definition with only one XMLType column.

message: Shared tables must have same semantics for truncation.
cause: An attempt was made to create shared tables with inconsistent semantics for truncation. Either all shared tables should have or should not have (TRUNCATE) keyword.
solution: Be consistent with (TRUNCATE) keyword while defining shared tables.

message: Can only share an existing XMLIndex table with an XMLTYPE column.
cause: An attempt was made to share a table without an XMLTYPE column.
solution: Drop the group containing the XMLIndex table without an XMLTYPE column and re-create the group with new definition.

message: Shared tables must have equivalent paths.
cause: An attempt was made to share a table with different paths.
solution: Specify a correct shared table definition with appropriate paths.

message: Nonblocking alter XMLIndex error
cause: Internal error.
solution: None

message: Invalid use of NONBLOCKING COMPLETE or ABORT.
cause: NONBLOCKING COMPLETE or ABORT is only allowed for XMLIndex that is being modified using NONBLOCKING ADD_GROUP or ADD_COLUMN.
solution: None

message: Cannot complete nonblocking alter index operation.
cause: NONBLOCKING COMPLETE is only allowed for XMLIndex that is being modified using NONBLOCKING ADD_GROUP or ADD_COLUMN and there are no pending rows left.
solution: Call DBMS_XMLINDEX.PROCESS_PENDING to finish pending work.

message: Invalid alter XMLIndex operation.
cause: An attemp was made to alter an XMLIndex that is already being modified using NONBLOCKING ADD_GROUP or ADD_COLUMN. Only NONBLOCKING COMPLETE or ABORT alter index operations are allowed. Also, NONBLOCKING operation is not allowed with alter index rebuild.
solution: Call DBMS_XMLINDEX.PROCESS_PENDING to finish pending work and then execute NONBLOCKING COMPLETE to successfully finish existing NONBLOCKING operation. Execute NONBLOCKING ABORT to cancle existing NONBLOCKING operation.

message: Invalid use of DBMS_XMLINDEX.PROCESS_PENDING.
cause: DBMS_XMLINDEX.PROCESS_PENDING was called on an index that was not modified using NONBLOCKING ADD_GROUP or ADD_COLUMN.
solution: None

message: There are no pending rows to process.
cause: DBMS_XMLINDEX.PROCESS_PENDING was called on an index that does not have any pending rows to process.
solution: Execute NONBLOCKING COMPLETE operation to complete the nonblocking alter index.

message: unregistered LOB value encountered
cause: The LOB value associated with the input locator did not exist in client-side reference tables.
solution: This is an internal error. Contact Oracle Support Services.

message: remote temporary or abstract LOB locator is encountered
cause: Local database encountered a temporary or abstract LOB created on a remote database. Remote access to temporary or abstract LOB is not supported.
solution: Avoid remote queries that return a temporary or abstract LOB.

message: Destination buffer too small to hold CLOB data after character set conversion.
cause: An attempt was made to convert CLOB to CHAR, where the LOB size was bigger than the buffer limit for CHAR types or the CHAR buffer was not big enough to hold all data after character set conversion.
solution: Do one of the following: * Make the LOB smaller before performing the conversion. for example, by using SUBSTR on CLOB * Use DBMS_LOB.SUBSTR to convert CLOB to CHAR.

message: encountered partial multibyte character
cause: The requested operation could not complete because a partial multibyte character was found at the end of the input.
solution: Ensure that the input buffer ends with a complete multibyte character and retry the operation.

message: Invalid compression level specified
cause: The specified archive compression level value was invalid. Valid values are LOW or HIGH.
solution: Choose a valid level and retry the operation.

message: Exadata Hybrid Columnar Compression is not supported for tablespaces on this storage type
cause: An attempt was made to use Exadata Hybrid Columnar Compression on an unsupported storage type.
solution: Create this table in a tablespace residing on Oracle Exadata, Oracle's Sun ZFS or Pillar Axiom storage type or use a different compression type.

message: hybrid columnar compressed table cannot have column with LONG data type
cause: One of the following was attempted: - Create a hybrid columnar compressed table with a LONG data type. - Alter an existing table with a LONG data type to be hybrid columnar compressed. - Add a LONG data type column to a hybrid columnar compressed table.
solution: LONG data types are not supported with hybrid columnar compressed tables. Create table without LONG column or change table to not be hybrid columnar compressed. If adding a column, do not use LONG data type. If modifying attributes of a column to change data type to LONG, the table cannot be hybrid columnar compressed.

message: Multiple token tables are not supported.
cause: An attempt was made to create a new token table. If encountered during an import, a critical patch was possibly missing on the export database.
solution: Use the default token table. If encountered during an import, apply the appropriate patch on the export database and try the export and import again.

message: SQL statement length ( string ) exceeds maximum allowed length ( string )
cause: An attempt was made to issue a SQL statement that exceeded the maximum allowed length of a statement.
solution: Modify the SQL statement or the views to which it refers to fit within the maximum length or split the SQL statement.

message: Export terminated unsuccessfully
cause: Export encountered an Oracle error.
solution: Look up the accompanying Oracle message in the ORA message chapters of this manual, and take appropriate action.

message: data field truncation - column length= number , buffer size= number actual size= number
cause: Export could not fit a column in the data buffer.
solution: Record the given size parameters and the accompanying messages and report this as an Export internal error to customer support. (Part of the table has been exported. Export will continue with the next table.)

message: error in writing to export file
cause: Export could not write to the export file, probably because of a device error. This message is usually followed by a device message from the operating system.
solution: Take appropriate action to restore the device.

message: no storage definition found for segment( number , number )
cause: Export could not find the storage definitions for a cluster, index, or table.
solution: Record the accompanying messages and report this as an Export internal error to customer support.

message: invalid username or password
cause: An invalid username or password was specified.
solution: Retry with a valid username and password.

message: all allowable logon attempts failed
cause: Attempts were repeatedly made to log on with an invalid username or password.
solution: Shut down the utility, then restart and retry with a valid username and password.

message: internal inconsistency error
cause: Export's data structure was corrupted.
solution: Record the accompanying messages and report this as an Export internal error to customer support.

message: dictionary shows no columns for string . string
cause: Export failed to gather column information from the data dictionary. The table may have been dropped.
solution: Retry the export and, if this error recurs, report it as an Export internal error to customer support.

message: ORACLE error number encountered
cause: Export encountered the referenced Oracle error.
solution: Look up the Oracle message in the ORA message chapters of this manual and take appropriate action.

message: no privilege to export string 's table string
cause: An attempt was made to export another user's table. Only a database administrator can export another user's tables.
solution: Ask your database administrator to do the export.

message: string is not a valid username
cause: An invalid username was specified.
solution: Shut down the utility, then restart and retry with a valid username.

message: string . string does not exist
cause: Export could not find the specified table.
solution: Retry with the correct table name.

message: string is not a valid export mode
cause: An invalid export mode was specified.
solution: Retry with a valid export mode.

message: respond with either 'Y', 'N', RETURN or '.' to quit
cause: An invalid response was entered.
solution: Enter any of the responses shown in the message.

message: error on row number of table string
cause: Export encountered an Oracle error while fetching rows.
solution: Look up the accompanying Oracle message in the ORA message chapters of this manual and take appropriate action.

message: error on row number of table string , column string , datatype number
cause: Export encountered an error while fetching or writing the column. An accompanying message gives more information.
solution: Correct the error and try again.

message: ORACLE error encountered while reading default auditing options
cause: Export encountered an Oracle error while reading the default auditing options (those for updates, deletes, and so on).
solution: Look up the accompanying Oracle message in the ORA message chapters of this manual and take appropriate action.

message: feature " string " is needed, but not present in database
cause: The command entered requires the specified feature. Either that feature is not installed, or the row describing the feature is missing from table V$OPTION
solution: Reinstall Oracle with the feature specified in the message.

message: datatype ( number ) for column string , table string . string is not supported
cause: Export does not support the referenced datatype.
solution: Retry with an acceptable datatype (CHAR, NUMBER, DATE, LONG, or RAW).

message: failed to process parameters, type 'EXP HELP=Y' for help
cause: Invalid command-line parameters were specified.
solution: Check the online help screen for the set of valid parameters, then retry.

message: failed to allocate memory of size number
cause: Export failed to allocate the necessary memory.
solution: Decrease the export buffer size so that less memory is required, or increase the runtime memory size for Export.

message: can only perform incremental export in Full Database mode
cause: USER or TABLE mode was specified when doing an incremental export.
solution: Specify FULL database mode (FULL=Y) and retry.

message: must be SYS or SYSTEM to do incremental export
cause: The privileges needed to do an incremental export do not exist. Only a data base administrator can do incremental exports.
solution: Ask the database administrator to do the incremental export.

message: must be a DBA to do Full Database or Tablespace export
cause: The privileges needed to do a FULL database export do not exist. Only a database administrator can do a FULL database export.
solution: Ask the database administrator to do the FULL database export.

message: Export views not installed, please notify your DBA
cause: The necessary Export views were not installed.
solution: Ask the database administrator to install the required Export views.

message: dictionary shows no column for constraint string . number
cause: Export failed to gather column information about the referenced constraint from the data dictionary. The constraint may have been altered.
solution: Retry the export and, if this error recurs, report it as an Export internal error to customer support.

message: conflicting modes specified
cause: Conflicting export modes were specified.
solution: Specify only one parameter and retry.

message: failed to calculate ORACLE block size
cause: Export failed to calculate the Oracle block size.
solution: Report this as an Export internal error to customer support.

message: failed to open string for write
cause: Export failed to open the export file for writing. This message is usually followed by device messages from the operating system.
solution: Take appropriate action to restore the device.

message: Incremental export mode and consistent mode are not compatible
cause: Both consistent and incremental exports were specified.
solution: None. Consistent mode is turned off.

message: Unexpected End-Of-File encountered while reading input
cause: Encountered an End-Of-File while reading the user input.
solution: If input to export is being redirected, check the file for errors.

message: Arraysize not in valid range. Using arraysize= number
cause: The arraysize value specified is not in the valid range.
solution: None

message: Non-DBAs may not export other users
cause: Only database administrators can export to other users. A non- database administrator attempted to specify owner=user where exporter is not the user.
solution: Request that this operation be performed by the database administrator.

message: Could not find environment character set
cause: The environment character set is missing or incorrectly specified.
solution: Ensure that the environment character set is correctly specified and is present.

message: error on rowid: file# number block# number slot# number
cause: Identifies the rowid on which an error occurred.
solution: This is an information message. No action is required.

message: QUERY parameter valid only for table mode exports
cause: You specified the QUERY parameter in an export command, but you are not performing a table mode export. The QUERY parameter cannot be used for a user mode export, a full export, nor a point in time recovery export.
solution: If you want to select a subset of rows for a table, you must export the table independently with a table mode export. Issue a table mode export command that specifies the table name and the query you want to execute during export.

message: Object number non-existent in dictionary
cause: The specified object could not be found in the dictionary. The object might have been dropped during the export
solution: The object no longer exists; no action is needed.

message: Export views not compatible with database version
cause: The Export utility is at a higher version than the database version and is thereby incompatible.
solution: Use the same version of Export utility as the database.

message: Bad Hash cluster id in clu$
cause: The function id in clu$ is not a legal number. Clu$ has become corrupted.
solution: Contact Worldwide Support

message: export file string must be on a disk
cause: On some platforms, export can read files from tape. This message is displayed if the first file in an export file set was on disk and you specified a tape device for a second or subsequent file.
solution: Verify that you have specified the correct file name for the export file. Remember that all export files can be either on disk or all files can be on tape, but not mixed both tape and disk.

message: Dump file and log file must be different
cause: The dump file and log file cannot be the same file.
solution: Specify different file names for the dump file and the log file, then retry the operation.

message: INCTYPE parameter is obsolete
cause: Export encountered the INCTYPE parameter when parsing Export options. Incremental Exports are no longer supported.
solution: Consult the Oracle Backup and Recovery guide. Export will attempt to continue.

message: Missing NLS_CHARACTERSET/NLS_NCHAR_CHARACTERSET in props$
cause: A value for NLS_CHARACTERSET/NLS_NCHAR_CHARACTERSET was not entered in the props$ table"
solution: internal error.

message: Invalid data dictionary information in the row where column " string " is " string " in table string
cause: The export utility retrieved invalid data from the data dictionary.
solution: Contact Oracle Worldwide Suport.

message: must be connected 'AS SYSDBA' to do Point-in-time Recovery or Transportable Tablespace import
cause: The user must log in 'as SYSDBA' to perform transportable tablespace imports or Point-In-Time Recovery imports.
solution: Ask your database adminstrator to perform the Transportable Tablespace import or the Tablespace Point-in-time Recovery import.

message: Cannot export SYSTEM Tablespace for Point-in-time Recovery or Transportable Tablespace
cause: SYSTEM tablespace cannot be part of recovery set or transportable tablespace set.
solution: Contact Oracle Wordwide Support.

message: Tablespace named string does not exist
cause: The specified tablespace does not exist in dictionary.
solution: Contact Oracle Wordwide Support.

message: Missing tablespace name(s)
cause: Tablespace name(s) were not supplied
solution: Provide tablespace name(s)

message: Cannot export SYSAUX Tablespace for Point-in-time Recovery or Transportable Tablespace
cause: SYSAUX tablespace cannot be part of recovery set or transportable tablespace set.
solution: Contact Oracle Wordwide Support.

message: string option is not compatible with Point-in-time Recovery or Transportable Tablespace Export
cause: An option was specified incompatible with Point-in-time Recovery or Transportable Tablespace Export.
solution: Retry the Export without the displayed option.

message: Cannot perform Partition Export " string " on non-partitioned table " string "
cause: The table specified in this Partition Export is not a partitioned table.
solution: Use Table mode, or specify a non-partitioned table.

message: " string " - given partition or subpartition name is not part of " string " table
cause: The specified partition or subpartition name is not in the specified table.
solution: Check if the correct table, partition or subpartition name was specified.

message: error on row number of partition string
cause: Export encountered the referenced Oracle error while fetching rows.
solution: Look up the Oracle message in the ORA message chapters of this manual and take appropriate action.

message: unable to execute QUERY on table string because the table has inner nested tables
cause: You specified the QUERY parameter on a table that has one or more inner nested tables. The QUERY parameter cannot be specified on tables that have inner nested tables.
solution: Export the entire table by omitting the QUERY parameter.

message: error on row number of subpartition string
cause: Export encountered the referenced Oracle error while fetching rows.
solution: Look up the Oracle message in the ORA message chapters of this manual and take appropriate action.

message: string . string is marked not exportable
cause: An object was marked as non-exportable in the NOEXP$ table.
solution: Consult your database administrator.

message: Failure to initialize parameter manager
cause: The parameter manager failed in intialization.
solution: Record the messages that follow and report this to Oracle Wordwide Support as an Export internal bug.

message: Password Verify Function for string profile does not exist
cause: Cannot find the function for the profile.
solution: Check if the profile was created properly.

message: error converting an object type's identifier to characters
cause: An invalid length of an object type identifier prevented its conversion.
solution: Contact Oracle Worldwide Support

message: an object type had multiple TYPE BODYs
cause: More than one TYPE BODY was found for an object type.
solution: Try dropping the TYPE BODY, if that is not successful, contact Oracle Worldwide Support

message: unable to find the outer table name of a nested table
cause: While exporting a bitmap index or posttable action on an inner nested table, the name of the outer table could not be located, using the NTAB$ table.
solution: Verify the table is properly defined.

message: invalid source statements for an object type
cause: TYPE was not found in the statements in SOURCE$ for an Object Type
solution: Contact Oracle Worldwide Support.

message: error in changing language handle
cause: Unable to change language handle.
solution: Contact Oracle Worldwide Support.

message: string is an inner nested table and cannot be exported.
cause: An attempt was made to export an inner nested table without its parent table.
solution: Export the parent of the inner nested table.

message: Error writing lob to the dump file.
cause: The current LOB could not be written to the dump file.
solution: Identify the cause of the write failure and fix it.

message: Object table string is missing its object identifier index
cause: All object tables must have an object identifier index, but the specified table was missing an index on its object identifier column.
solution: Recreate the type table and retry the operation.

message: tablespace string is offline
cause: Export failed to export tablespace (tablespace being offline).
solution: Make tablespace online and re export.

message: attempt to free unallocated memory
cause: An attempt was made to free memory that was not allocated.
solution: Contact Oracle Worldwide Support

message: QUERY parameter not compatible with Direct Path export
cause: You specified a value for the QUERY parameter for a direct path export. The QUERY parameter cannot be used with a direct path export.
solution: Re-issue the export command with DIRECT=N or omit the DIRECT parameter from the command line.

message: error closing export file string
cause: An error occurred while trying to close the export file.
solution: Contact Oracle Worldwide Support.

message: dump file size too small
cause: You specified either the FILESIZE parameter or the VOLSIZE parameter (if your platform supports it), and the value of the parameter is too small to hold the header information for the export file, plus any data.
solution: Increase the value of the FILESIZE or VOLSIZE parameter.

message: rounding VOLSIZE down, new value is string
cause: The VOLSIZE parameter must be a multiple of the RECORDLENGTH, but the value you specified for VOLSIZE does not meet this requirement. The value of VOLSIZE has been rounded down to be a multiple of the RECORDLENGTH used for the dump file.
solution: No action is required. You can adjust the VOLSIZE or RECORDLENGTH parameter to avoid this message. When importing this file, you must specify the VOLSIZE value reported by this message.

message: rounding FILESIZE down, new value is string
cause: The FILESIZE parameter must be a multiple of the RECORDLENGTH, but the value you specified for FILESIZE does not meet this requirement. The value of FILESIZE has been rounded down to be a multiple of the RECORDLENGTH used for the dump file.
solution: No action is required. You can adjust the FILESIZE or RECORDLENGTH parameter to avoid this message. When importing this file, you must specify the FILESIZE value reported by this message.

message: multiple devices specified for tape output
cause: You specified multiple file names when doing an export to a tape device. EXPORT uses the same device for writing all files, of the number of tape volumes required. For this reason, export will accept only one value for the FILE parameter when writing to tape.
solution: Reenter the EXPORT command, but specify only one tape device in the FILE parameter.

message: multiple output files specified for unbounded export file
cause: You specified multiple file names when doing an export and you also specified a value of 0 for the FILESIZE parameter. Note that 0 is the value used if FILESIZE is not specified on the command line. Since a value of 0 for FILESIZE means that only one file will be written and there is no size limit for that file, the other files you specified in the FILE parameter can never be used.
solution: If you intended to write multiple files, respecify the command but use the FILESIZE to specify the maximum number of bytes that EXPORT should write to each file. If you intended to write only one file with no limits on it's size, reissue the EXPORT command but specify only one file name for the FILE parameter.

message: Error exporting metadata for index string . Index creation will be skipped
cause: Domain indexes export private metadata via anonymous PL/SQL blocks prior to the CREATE INDEX statement. Export does this by calling the ODCIIndexGetMetadata method on the implementation type associated with the index. A problem occurred inside this routine. Because the metadata is considered an integral part of the index, the CREATE INDEX statement was not written to the dump file.
solution: Contact the developer of the index's implementation type. If this is an Oracle-supplied index (perhaps via a data cartridge), contact Oracle Worldwide Support.

message: Data in table " string " is protected. Conventional path may only be exporting partial table.
cause: User without the execute privilege on DBMS_RLS, the access control package, tries to export a table that has access control. Since table owner is also subjected to access control, the owner may not be able to export all rows in the table, but only the ones he can see. Also, to preserve integrity of the table, user exporting the table should have enough privilege to recreate the table with the security policies at import time. Therefore, it is strongly recommended the database administrator should be handling exporting of this table. Granting the table owner execute privilege would also satisfy this security check, though it might have other security implications. If the table does not have objects, can use direct mode.
solution: Ask the database administrator to export/import this table/view.

message: Data in table " string " is protected. Using conventional mode.
cause: User without the execute privilege on DBMS_RLS, the access control package, tries to direct export a table that has access control enabled. Using conventional export mode instead. Note that because of access control, only a partial table may be exported.
solution: Ask the database administrator to export/import this table/view.

message: Exporting access control for table/view " string " as non-DBA.
cause: A non-DBA user tries to export table/view and the associated fine grain access control policies. The user may not have enough privilege to recreate the access control policies when importing the table/view. And such an event may cause inconsistency in the security model of the table/view.
solution: Ask the database administrator to export/import this table/view.

message: Invalid function name passed to procedural object support: string
cause: Internal inconsistency error: The listed function is not a method on export's procedural object interface specification.
solution: Contact Oracle Worldwide Support

message: The previous problem occurred when calling string . string . string
cause: The listed package provides export/import support for procedural
solution: Contact Oracle Worldwide Support. Most packages are supplied by Oracle internal cartridge or server development groups. The package name will help Support determine the correct owner of the problem.

message: Unexpected DbmsJava error number at step number
cause: The error was returned from a call to a DbmsJava procedure.
solution: Record the accompanying messages and report this as an Export internal error to customer support.

message: The previous problem occurred when calling string . string . string for object number
cause: The listed package provides export/import support for procedural objects, i.e, those whose DDL is supplied by stored procedures. The previously listed error occurred while calling the specified function.
solution: Contact Oracle Worldwide Support. Most packages are supplied by Oracle internal cartridge or server development groups. The package name will help Support determine the correct owner of the problem.

message: Primary key REFs in table " string "may not be valid on import
cause: The specified table contains primary key REFs which may not be valid in the import database.
solution: Do not use Export/Import to move Primary key REFs between databases having differing character sets.

message: Problem with internal hash table of schema/table names
cause: Most likely a problem with allocating memory for the hash table entries.
solution: Contact Oracle Worldwide Support

message: invalid FILE_FORMAT specification
cause: The FILE_FORMAT specification did not contain an instance of "%s". This wildcard string must be present.
solution: Correct the error and reenter the EXPORT command.

message: cannot pin type " string "." string "
cause: Export was unable to pin the specified type in the object cache. This is typically caused because a type could not be made valid (for example because of authorization violations in accessing subtypes).
solution: Fix the problem with the offending type until the type can be successfully compiled.

message: Exporting questionable statistics.
cause: Export was able export statistics, but the statistics may not be usuable. The statistics are questionable because one or more of the following happened during export: a row error occurred, client character set or NCHARSET does not match with the server, a query clause was specified on export, only certain partitions or subpartitions were exported, or a fatal error occurred while processing a table.
solution: To export non-questionable statistics, change the client character set or NCHARSET to match the server, export with no query clause, export complete tables. If desired, import parameters can be supplied so that only non-questionable statistics will be imported, and all questionable statistics will be recalculated.

message: Unable to set NLS_NUMERIC_CHARACTERS to required defaults.
cause: Export was unable to set NLS_NUMERIC_CHARACTERS to '.,'
solution: Record the accompanying messages and report this as an Export internal error to customer support.

message: Could not convert to server character set's handle
cause: Internal error.
solution: Contact Worldwide support.

message: Could not convert to server national character set's handle
cause: Internal error.
solution: Contact Worldwide support.

message: Flashback_time and Flashback_scn are not compatible
cause: Both flashback_time and flashback_scn paramerers were specified.
solution: Reissue command with only one flashback parameter.

message: Object type " string "." string " is not in a valid state, type will not be exported
cause: The object type's status is invalid which may be caused by a dependant type's modification (or removal) without cascading the change.
solution: The type must be recompiled using ALTER TYPE COMPILE.

message: Data in table has not been upgraded, table will not be exported
cause: Export is attempting to process a table containing references to a type which has evolved. In order for Export to process the table successfully, all data within each table must be upgraded to the latest revision of each referenced type.
solution: The table must be updated using ALTER TABLE UPGRADE DATA.

message: Table " string "." string " is not in a valid state, table will not be exported
cause: A table or one of its dependant types has modified without cascading the change. This left the table in an INVALID state.
solution: The table must be updated using ALTER TABLE UPDATE.

message: error converting an object type's hashcode to characters
cause: An invalid length of an object type identifier prevented its conversion.
solution: Contact Oracle Worldwide Support

message: Version 1 extensible index " string "." string " can not be included in Transportable Tablespace Export
cause: Transporable Tablespace extensible indexes must be at least version 2.
solution: Upgrade extensibile index implementation to version 2 specifications.

message: Resumable parameters ignored -- current session not resumable
cause: Current session is not resumable.
solution: Must specify RESUMABLE=Y to enable resumable session in order for the RESUMABLE_NAME and RESUMABLE_TIMEOUT parameters to take effect.

message: The FLASHBACK_TIME parameter was invalid
cause: FLASHBACK_TIME did not contain a valid timestamp or an expression that yields a valid timestamp.
solution: Specify a timestamp value in the format of YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI:SS or an expression that evaluates to a valid timestamp.

message: datatype ( string ) of column string in table string . string is not supported, table will not be exported
cause: The column is of a datatype which does not contain the required support. The table will not be exported.
solution: Use the Data Pump version of Export to export this table.

message: parameter string is not supported for this user
cause: The user attempted to specify either CONSISTENT or OBJECT_CONSISTENT when connected as sysdba.
solution: If a consistent export is needed, then connect as another user.

message: Invalid Database Link Passwords
cause: Invalid Encoded Password for Database Link
solution: Please drop the Database Link and recreate it after import.

message: Feature ( string ) of column string in table string . string is not supported. The table will not be exported.
cause: Export does not contain the required support for this feature. The table will not be exported.
solution: Use the Data Pump version of Export to export this table.

message: NULL lob fetched
cause: Internal error
solution: Contact Oracle Worldwide Support.

message: XSL delimiter not found
cause: Internal error
solution: Contact Oracle Worldwide Support.

message: Tablespace string is encrypted and will not be exported
cause: Encrypted Tablespace feature is not supported by classic export
solution: Use DATAPUMP Utility to export this tablespace.

message: Table string resides in an Encrypted Tablespace string and will not be exported
cause: Encrypted Tablespace feature is not supported by classic export
solution: Use DATAPUMP Utility to export this table.

message: Index string is of XMLType and could not be exported
cause: Export does not contain the required support for this feature. The index could not be exported.
solution: Use Oracle Data Pump Utility to export this index.

message: Feature string is unsupported. string string . string could not be exported
cause: Export does not contain the required support for this feature.
solution: Use Oracle Data Pump Utility

message: Length of string string is exceeding the maximum limit
cause: Provided length was more than the maximum limit allowed.
solution: Check the input value and provide the correct value.

message: Import terminated unsuccessfully
cause: Import encountered an Oracle error.
solution: Look up the accompanying Oracle message in the ORA message chapters of this manual, and take appropriate action.

message: respond with either string , string , RETURN or '.' to quit
cause: An invalid response was entered.
solution: Enter any of the responses shown in the message.

message: failed to open string for read
cause: Import failed to open the export file for reading. This message is usually followed by a device message from the operating system.
solution: Take appropriate action to restore the device.

message: ORACLE error number encountered
cause: Import encountered the referenced Oracle error.
solution: Look up the Oracle message in the ORA message chapters of this manual, and take appropriate action.

message: invalid username or password
cause: An invalid username or password was specified.
solution: Retry with a valid username and password.

message: all allowable logon attempts failed
cause: An attempt was repeatedly made to log on with an invalid username or password.
solution: Retry with valid username and password.

message: failed to allocate memory of size number
cause: Import failed to allocate the necessary memory.
solution: Decrease the import buffer size so that less memory is required, or increase the runtime memory size for Import.

message: must be a DBA to import objects to another user's account
cause: The privileges needed to import into another user's account do not exist. Only a database administrator can import into another user's account.
solution: Ask the database administrator to do the import.

message: unrecognized statement in the export file: string
cause: Import did not recognize a statement in the export file. Either the export file was corrupted, or an Import internal error has occurred.
solution: If the export file was corrupted, retry with a new export file. Otherwise, report this as an Import internal error and submit the export file to customer support.

message: abnormal end of export file
cause: The export file is probably from an aborted Export session.
solution: If so, retry the export and import. Otherwise, report this as an Import bug and submit the export file that caused this error to customer support.

message: not a valid export file, header failed verification
cause: Either the file was not generated by Export or it was corrupted.
solution: If the file was indeed generated by Export, report this an Import bug and submit the export file to customer support.

message: formatted table data not currently supported
cause: You tried to import an export file that contains formatted table data. Import only supports export files containing binary table data. wher
solution: Retry using an export file that contains only binary table data.

message: invalid export mode ( character ) in header
cause: The Export mode specified in the export file header is invalid.
solution: Check the export file to see if it was corrupted. If it was not, report this as an Import bug and submit the export file to customer support.

message: only a DBA can import a file exported by another DBA
cause: The privileges needed to Import an export file generated by a database administrator do not exist. Only a database administrator can import such files.
solution: Ask the database administrator to do the import.

message: option " string " is needed, but not present in database
cause: The command entered requires the specified option. Either that option is not installed, or the row describing the option is missing from table V$OPTION
solution: Reinstall Oracle with the option specified by the message.

message: following statement failed because the object already exists:
cause: Import failed to create an object because it already exists.
solution: Specify IGNORE=Y to ignore such errors and import rows even when tables are not created because they already exist.

message: required character set conversion (type number to number ) not supported
cause: Import could not convert the character format of the export file into the native character format.
solution: Change the user character set by setting the NLS_LANG environment variable to match the character set of the export file.

message: following statement failed with ORACLE error number :
cause: Import failed to execute the statement from the export file because of an Oracle error.
solution: Look up the accompanying Oracle message in the ORA message chapters of this manual and take appropriate action.

message: partial import of previous table completed: number rows imported
cause: A table was only partially imported because of an Oracle error.
solution: Look up the accompanying Oracle message in the ORA message chapters of this manual and take appropriate action.

message: row rejected due to ORACLE error number
cause: Import encountered the referenced Oracle error while trying to import a row.
solution: Look up the accompanying Oracle message in the ORA message chapters of this manual and take appropriate action.

message: long column too large for column buffer size ( number )
cause: The column buffer is too small. This usually occurs when importing LONG data.
