message: multiple records for default channel configuration for string found in repository
cause: Configuration for the channel was not consistent.
solution: Re-run CONFIGURE CHANNEL command to configure the channel.

message: configuration for string channel number is ignored
cause: This is an informational message only. Parallelism for the device is less than associated channel number.
solution: To use this configuration increase parallelism for this device. To clear this configuration use CONFIGURE CHANNEL... CLEAR command.

message: using channel string
cause: This is an informational message only.
solution: No action is required.

message: could not locate pieces of backup set key string
cause: Copies of the specified backup set key could not be accessed on any of the allocated channels.
solution: Allocate additional channels on other nodes of the cluster or, if the backup pieces has been deleted, use the CROSSCHECK BACKUP command to correct the recovery catalog or target database control file entries.

message: channel string disabled, job failed on it will be run on another channel
cause: This is an informational message displayed whenever a retryable error occurs for the job and there are channels available to run this step.
solution: No action is required.

message: continuing other job steps, job failed will not be re-run
cause: This is an informational message displayed whenever there is a non-retryable error occurred for the job.
solution: No action is required.

message: error on step filtered for normal output string
cause: This message is added when stacking errors for failed jobs after channel failover was performed. It will be filtered from normal output.
solution: No action is required.

message: abnormal termination of job step
cause: A job step encountered an error and could not recover. This error should be followed by other errors indicating the cause of the problem.
solution: Check the accompanying error.

message: target database not found in recovery catalog
cause: target database is not found in the recovery catalog
solution: make sure that the target database is registered in the recovery recovery catalog

message: target database already registered in recovery catalog
cause: target database is already registered in the recovery catalog
solution: if the target database is really registered, there is no need to register it again. Note that the recovery catalog enforces that all databases have a unique DBID. If the new database was created by copying files from an existing database, it will have the same DBID as the original database and cannot be registered in the same recovery catalog.

message: target database incarnation not found in recovery catalog
cause: RESETLOGS CHANGE# and/or time of the target database doesn't match any database incarnation in the recovery catalog.
solution: if target database was opened with RESETLOGS option then use 'reset database' to register the new incarnation.

message: target database name does not match name in recovery catalog
cause: name of the target database doesn't match the one stored in the recovery catalog
solution: This is an internal error.

message: target database name is ambiguous
cause: two or more databases in the recovery catalog match this name
solution: None

message: target database name is missing
cause: target database instance is not started or db_name initialization parameter is not set
solution: startup the instance and make sure that db_name parameter is set

message: database incarnation already registered
cause: this incarnation is already registered in the recovery catalog
solution: No action is required.

message: database incarnation not found
cause: database incarnation does not match any database incarnation in the recovery catalog
solution: specify a valid database incarnation key

message: target database incarnation is not current in recovery catalog
cause: the database incarnation that matches the RESETLOGS CHANGE# and time of the mounted target database control file is not the current incarnation of the database
solution: If 'reset database to incarnation <key>' was used to make an old incarnation current then restore the target database from a backup that matches the incarnation and mount it. You will need to do 'STARTUP NOMOUNT' before you can restore the control file using RMAN. Otherwise use 'reset database to incarnation <key>' make the intended incarnation current in the recovery catalog.

message: not authorized to register new database
cause: You attempted to register a new database with this recovery catalog, but you are using a virtual private catalog, and you have not been granted permission by the catalog administrator to register this database with this recovery catalog
solution: Ask the catalog administrator to grant permission for you to register this database.

message: error upgrading virtual private catalog
cause: An error occurred while automatically upgrading a virtual private catalog.
solution: Ensure that the virtual private catalog userid has all of the required privileges, such as being granted the RECOVERY_CATALOG_OWNER role.

message: virtual private catalog owner must be granted RECOVERY_CATALOG_OWNER role
cause: An attempt was made to establish a virtual private RMAN catalog in a schema that is not granted the RECOVERY_CATALOG_OWNER role.
solution: Grant RECOVERY_CATALOG_OWNER to the virtual private catalog owner.

message: not authorized to share this catalog
cause: You attempted to share a recovery catalog but were not authorized to do this by the catalog administrator.
solution: Ask the catalog administrator to grant permission for you to share this catalog.

message: virtual private catalog user cannot modify global scripts
cause: A virtual private catalog user attempted to create, delete, or modify a global script. Virtual private catalog users cannot modify global scripts.
solution: Connect to the catalog owner userid and retry the global script operation.

message: illegal script update operation
cause: An illegal script operation was performed.
solution: None

message: database not found in recovery catalog
cause: An attempt was made to grant or revoke catalog access to a database whose name was not registered in the recovery catalog.
solution: Correct the database name and re-issue the GRANT or REVOKE command. If this is an attempt to grant or revoke access to a database that is not yet registered, then re-issue the command using the database ID of the desired database.

message: database name not unique in recovery catalog
cause: An attempt was made to grant or revoke catalog access to a database whose name is not unique in the recovery catalog.
solution: Re-issue the command specifying the database ID of the desired database.

message: user not found
cause: An attempt was made to grant a privilege to a user that does not exist.
solution: Reissue the command specifying a user that exists.

message: cannot make a snapshot control file
cause: another operation that needs the snapshot control file is in progress
solution: try again later if necessary

message: resync in progress
cause: this procedure cannot be called while a resync is in progress
solution: This is an internal error.

message: resync not started
cause: this procedure can only be called in a resync
solution: This is an internal error.

message: checkpoint CHANGE# too low
cause: the checkpoint change# is less than the one of the previous resync or the checkpoint change# is null
solution: make sure that the right control file is used

message: control file SEQUENCE# too low
cause: the control file sequence is less than the one of the previous resync
solution: make sure that the right control file is used

message: resync not needed
cause: the control file has not changed since the previous resync
solution: nothing since the recovery catalog is in sync

message: must specify FORMAT for CONVERT command
cause: No FORMAT was specified when using CONVERT command.
solution: Resubmit the command using FORMAT clause.

message: format requires character when duplexing
cause: SET_DUPLEX=ON was specified, but %c was not part of the format.
solution: Include %c in format, or use %U.

message: must specify FORMAT for BACKUP INCREMENTAL FROM SCN command
cause: No FORMAT was specified when using BACKUP INCREMENTAL FROM SCN command.
solution: Resubmit the command using FORMAT clause.

message: full resync from primary database is not done
cause: Resync from standby detected that a full resync from primary database is required. One of the following events on primary database may have caused this error: 1) one or more tablespaces or datafiles were added 2) one or more tablespaces or datafiles were dropped 3) one or more datafiles status changed
solution: Perform full resync after connecting to primary database.

message: change stamp for the record
cause: A record with same recid and stamp is already known to catalog.
solution: None. This error is automatically handled by RMAN client by changing the stamp in control file during resync.

message: control file for remote database cannot be updated
cause: RESYNC CATALOG FROM DB_UNIQUE_NAME command was attempted, but the control file at the database with DB_UNIQUE_NAME needs to be resynced directly instead of through the current target.
solution: Directly connect as target to the remote database with the specified DB_UNIQUE_NAME and resync.

message: remote database has different database ID
cause: Command RESYNC CATALOG FROM DB_UNIQUE_NAME was executed and the database ID of the remote database was different than the connected target database.
solution: The remote database should have the same database ID as the database connected as the target database. Fix the connect identifier for the remote database and retry the command.

message: datafile not found in the recovery catalog
cause: The specified datafile is not found in the recovery catalog
solution: make sure that the datafile name is correct and that the recovery catalog is up-to-date

message: Tablespace not found in the recovery catalog
cause: the specified tablespace is not found in the recovery catalog
solution: make sure that the tablespace name is correct and that the recovery catalog is up-to-date

message: translation in progress
cause: this procedure can not be called when name translation is in progress
solution: This is an internal error.

message: translation not started
cause: GETDATAFILE procedure was called before TRANSLATETABLESPACE
solution: This is an internal error.

message: incomplete UNTIL clause
cause: The sequence# was NULL
solution: This is an internal error.

message: log sequence not found in the repository
cause: The specified log sequence does not exists in log history of the current database incarnation
solution: check the thread# and sequence#

message: UNTIL TIME or RECOVERY WINDOW is before RESETLOGS time
cause: UNTIL TIME and RECOVERY WINDOW cannot be less than the database creation time or RESETLOGS time.
solution: Check the UNTIL TIME or RECOVERY WINDOW. If the database needs to be restored to an old incarnation, use the RESET DATABASE TO INCARNATION command.

message: UNTIL CHANGE is before RESETLOGS change
cause: UNTIL CHANGE cannot be less than the database RESETLOGS change.
solution: Check the UNTIL CHANGE. If the database needs to be restored to an old incarnation, use the RESET DATABASE TO INCARNATION command.

message: duplicate datafile name
cause: Two datafiles have the same name
solution: This is an internal error.

message: FROM TIME is before RESETLOGS time
cause: FROM TIME cannot be less than the database creation time or RESETLOGS time.
solution: Check the FROM TIME. If the database needs to be restored to an old incarnation, use the RESET DATABASE TO INCARNATION command.

message: UNTIL CHANGE is an orphan incarnation
cause: Specified UNTIL CHANGE was an orphan incarnation.
solution: Check the UNTIL CHANGE or UNTIL RESTORE POINT. If the database needs to be restored or flashed back to an orphan incarnation, use the RESET DATABASE TO INCARNATION command.

message: backup set not found
cause: The specified backup set key was not found in the recovery catalog or target database control file.
solution: Specify a different backup set key.

message: datafile not part of the database
cause: the datafile does not exists or did not exist at until time/scn
solution: check the datafile name or number. This is an internal error. for restore database or tablespace.

message: datafile not found in repository
cause: This is an internal error.
solution: Contact Oracle Support Services.

message: control file copy not found in the repository
cause: The specified control file was not in the recovery catalog or target database control file or it was marked deleted.
solution: check the file name

message: ambiguous control file copy name
cause: more than one control file copy in the recovery catalog match the specified name.
solution: None

message: datafile name not found in recovery catalog or is ambiguous
cause: The specified datafile name is not the name of a datafile that is currently part of the target database, or an UNTIL clause has been specified and the file name was for a different datafile at the time specified by the UNTIL clause than it is now.
solution: Use a datafile number to specify the datafile you want to RESTORE or RECOVER.

message: DB_UNIQUE_NAME mismatch in snapshot control file
cause: The DB_UNIQUE_NAME value in the snapshot control file was incorrect. This error can occur in Oracle RAC when the snapshot control file location is not shared across nodes and virtual IPs are setup in the remote database from where resynchronization is done using RESYNC CATALOG FROM DB_UNIQUE_NAME commnad.
solution: To avoid this error, one of the following actions can be taken: 1) Share the control file snapshot location. The snapshot location can be displayed by executing SHOW SNAPSHOT CONTROLFILE NAME at the RMAN prompt. 2) Do not use Virtual IPs in the service name used to define the connect identifiers. The connect identifiers can be displayed using SHOW DB_UNIQUE_NAME command at the RMAN prompt.

message: datafile copy not found in the repository
cause: The specified datafile was not in the recovery catalog or target database control file or it was marked deleted.
solution: check the datafile copy name or key

message: ambiguous datafile copy name
cause: more than one control file copy in the recovery catalog match the specified name.
solution: use the datafile copy key to uniquely specify the datafile copy

message: archived log not found in the repository
cause: The specified archived log was not found in the recovery catalog or target database control file or it was marked deleted.
solution: check the archived log name or key

message: ambiguous archived log name
cause: more than one archived log in the recovery catalog match the specified name
solution: use the archived log key to uniquely specify the archived log

message: specification does not match any archived log in the repository
cause: No archived logs found that match specification in the recovery catalog or target database control file.
solution: check the archived log specifier

message: database db_unique_name is not known to the recovery catalog
cause: the user specified DB_UNIQUE_NAME not known to the recovery catalog.
solution: change the database DB_UNIQUE_NAME to a known database value. To display list of known db_unique_names execute LIST DB_UNIQUE_NAME OF DATABASE

message: can not change currently connected database db_unique_name
cause: the user specified currently connected DB_UNIQUE_NAME value to unregister.
solution: use the DB_UNIQUE_NAME other than connected target database's DB_UNIQUE_NAME value.

message: can not specify db_unique_name option in nocatalog mode
cause: the user specified DB_UNIQUE_NAME in nocatalog mode.
solution: remove the DB_UNIQUE_NAME option from the command.

message: new db_unique_name is already known to the recovery catalog
cause: the user specified known DB_UNIQUE_NAME value when renaming a DB_UNIQUE_NAME in the recovery catalog.
solution: change the database DB_UNIQUE_NAME to an known DB_UNIQUE_NAME value; or unregister the new DB_UNIQUE_NAME before renaming an old DB_UNIQUE_NAME value for a database. To display the list of all DB_UNIQUE_NAME for the databases LIST DB_UNIQUE_NAME OF DATABASE command can be executed.

message: specification does not match any foreign archived log in the repository
cause: No foreign archived logs found that match specification in the recovery catalog or target database control file.
solution: check the foreign archived log specifier

message: offline range not found in the repository
cause: The specified offline was not found in the recovery catalog or target database control file.
solution: check that recovery catalog is current

message: backup piece not found in the repository
cause: The specified backup piece was not in the recovery catalog or target database control file or it was marked deleted.
solution: check the backup piece handle or key

message: ambiguous backup piece handle
cause: more than one backup piece in the recovery catalog match the specified handle
solution: use the backup piece key to uniquely specify the backup piece

message: no parent backup found for the incremental backup
cause: no available backup or copy that could be used as the parent of the incremental backup was found in the recovery catalog.
solution: take a level 0 backup or copy of the datafile first

message: too many device types
cause: more than 8 device types were allocated
solution: make sure that the job allocates at most 8 different device types

message: DBMS_RCVCAT package not compatible with the recovery catalog
cause: The version of the recovery catalog tables does not work with this version of the DBMS_RCVCAT package.
solution: Check that the recovery catalog packages and schema are installed correctly. The UPGRADE CATALOG command can be used to upgrade the recovery catalog tables and packages to the most current version.

message: DBMS_RCVMAN package not compatible with the recovery catalog
cause: The version of the recovery catalog tables does not work with this version of the DBMS_RCVMAN package.
solution: Check that the recovery catalog packages and schema are installed correctly. The UPGRADE CATALOG command can be used to upgrade the recovery catalog tables and packages to the most current version.

message: proxy copy not found in the repository
cause: The specified proxy copy was not in the recovery catalog or target database control file or it was marked deleted.
solution: check the proxy copy handle or key

message: ambiguous proxy copy handle
cause: more than one proxy copy in the recovery catalog matches the specified handle
solution: use the proxy copy key to uniquely specify the proxy copy

message: script already exists
cause: a CREATE SCRIPT was issued, but a script with the specified name already exists.
solution: use a different name or use REPLACE SCRIPT.

message: redo logs from parent database incarnation cannot be applied
cause: A RESTORE or RECOVER of a datafile was requested, but recovery of the datafile would require applying redo logs that were generated before the most recent OPEN RESETLOGS.
solution: If a full backup or datafile copy from the current database incarnation exists, ensure that it is marked AVAILABLE, and that a channel of the correct device type is allocated. It may also be necessary to remove the FROM BACKUPSET or FROM DATAFILECOPY or FROM TAG operands if these have been specified.

message: DELETE EXPIRED cannot delete objects that exist - run CROSSCHECK
cause: A DELETE EXPIRED command was run, but the object was actually found to exist. This means the recovery catalog or target database control file is out of sync with reality.
solution: Run CROSSCHECK.

message: DELETE cannot delete expired objects - run CROSSCHECK or DELETE EXPIRED
cause: A DELETE command was run without EXPIRED option, but the object doesn't exist. This means the recovery catalog or target database control file is out of sync with reality.
solution: Run CROSSCHECK.

message: corruption list not found in recovery catalog
cause: corruption list is empty
solution: make sure that one or more blocks are marked corrupted in v$copy_corruption and v$backup_corruption and recovery catalog is up-to-date.

message: create datafile during recovery
cause: applying of archived log caused a create datafile redo-entry to to terminate recovery.
solution: none. This message is never displayed. RMAN automatically detects this case and creates the datafile.

message: no backup of archived log found
cause: during the recover process, no backup was found from which the archived logs could be restored.
solution: this message should be followed by a list of missing archived logs. Please make the necessary archived log backups available and try again.

message: some targets are remote - aborting restore
cause: during the restore process, one or more backup files were unavailable locally for the restore operation.
solution: This message should be accompanied with the list of remote backup files. Recall these backups from remote location and retry the RESTORE command.

message: temporary resource already in use
cause: Temporary resource that was allocated for IMPORT CATALOG command was already in use.
solution: Retry IMPORT CATALOG command.

message: temporary resource not found
cause: Temporary resource that was allocated for IMPORT CATALOG command was not found.
solution: Retry IMPORT CATALOG command.

message: database not found in source recovery catalog database
cause: Database that was specified in IMPORT CATALOG command was not found in the source recovery catalog database.
solution: Make sure that the database is registered in the source recovery catalog database.

message: database name is ambiguous in source recovery catalog database
cause: Two or more databases in the source recovery catalog database match this name.
solution: Use DBID option in IMPORT CATALOG command to specify the source database.

message: source database already registered in recovery catalog
cause: Source database was already registered in the recovery catalog.
solution: If the source database is really registered, there is no need to register it again. Note that the recovery catalog enforces that all databases have a unique DBID. If the new database was created by copying files from an existing database, it will have the same DBID as the original database and cannot be registered in the same recovery catalog.

message: feature requires Availability Machine recovery catalog
cause: The specified command required the Availability Machine recovery catalog.
solution: Connect to the Availability Machine recovery catalog and retry the command.

message: Operating system dependent operation: string failed with status: string
cause: There was an operating system call error.
solution: Contact Oracle Support Services.

message: Operating system failure message: string
cause: There was an operating system call error.
solution: Contact Oracle Support Services.

message: failure occurred at: string
cause: There was an operating system call error.
solution: Contact Oracle Support Services.

message: additional information: string
cause: There was an operating system call error.
solution: Contact Oracle Support Services.

message: Error acquiring ASM disk discovery string from Grid Plug and Play profile: call to [ string ] failed.
cause: Call to the Grid Plug and Play service to request disk discovery string failed.
solution: Ensure that the Grid Plug and Play component of Cluster Ready Services is available. If Grid Plug and Play is operational and command still fails, contact Oracle Support Services.

message: OS system dependent operation: string failed with status: string
cause: OS system call error
solution: contact Oracle Support

message: OS failure message: string
cause: OS system call error
solution: contact Oracle Support

message: failure occurred at: string
cause: OS system call error
solution: contact Oracle Support

message: additional information: string
cause: OS system call error
solution: contact Oracle Support

message: internal error [ number ]
cause: An internal error has occurred.
solution: Contact Oracle Support Services and report the error.

message: unknown parameter name ' string '
cause: The parameter name was misspelled.
solution: Spell the parameter name correctly.

message: ' string ' is not in the legal range for ' string '
cause: The value of the parameter is not within the legal range.
solution: Refer to the manual for the allowable values for this parameter.

message: ' string ' contains an illegal integer radix for ' string '
cause: An illegal integer radix specification was found.
solution: Only 'd', 'h', 'D', and 'H' may be used as radix specifications.

message: ' string ' is not a legal integer for ' string '
cause: The value is not a valid integer.
solution: Specify only valid integers for this parameter.

message: ' string ' is not a legal Boolean for ' string '
cause: The value is not a valid Boolean.
solution: Refer to the manual for allowable Boolean values.

message: out of memory
cause: The operating system has run out of memory.
solution: Take action to make more memory available to the program.

message: parameter name abbreviation ' string ' is not unique
cause: The given abbreviation was not unique.
solution: Use a longer abbreviation to make the parameter name unique.

message: invalid positional parameter value ' string '
cause: An invalid positional parameter value has been entered.
solution: Remove the invalid positional parameter.

message: could not open parameter file ' string '
cause: The parameter file does not exist.
solution: Create an appropriate parameter file.

message: syntax error at ' string '
cause: A syntax error was detected.
solution: Change the input so that the correct syntax is used.

message: no closing quote for value ' string '
cause: A quoted string was started but not finished.
solution: Put a closing quote in the proper location.

message: multiple values not allowed for parameter ' string '
cause: An attempt was made to specify multiple values for a parameter which can take only one value.
solution: Do not specify more than one value for this parameter.

message: error when processing file ' string '
cause: A problem occurred when processing this file.
solution: Examine the additional error messages and correct the problem.

message: error when processing from command line
cause: A problem occurred when processing the command line.
solution: Examine the additional error messages and correct the problem.

message: error when processing an environment variable
cause: A problem occurred when processing an environment variable.
solution: Examine the additional error messages and correct the problem.

message: syntax error at ' string ' following ' string '
cause: A syntax error was detected.
solution: Change the input so that the correct syntax is used.

message: syntax error at ' string ' at the start of input
cause: A syntax error was detected.
solution: Change the input so that the correct syntax is used.

message: syntax error at ' string ' at the end of input
cause: A syntax error was detected.
solution: Change the input so that the correct syntax is used.

message: unable to obtain a valid value for ' string '
cause: No valid value was obtained for this parameter.
solution: Rerun the application and enter a valid value.

message: ' string ' is not a legal Oracle number for ' string '
cause: The value is not a valid Oracle number.
solution: Refer to the manual for allowable Oracle number values.

message: ' string ' is not an allowable value for ' string '
cause: The value is not a legal value for this parameter.
solution: Refer to the manual for allowable values.

message: value ' string ' for ' string ' must be between ' number ' and ' number '
cause: The value of the parameter is not within the legal range.
solution: Specify a value that is within the legal range.

message: invalid character number found in the input file
cause: A character that is invalid was found in the input file.
solution: Specify an input file that contains only valid characters.

message: Out of memory. string
cause: The File IO package failed in trying to dynamically allocate memory. function name is used for additional comments to indicate where, when and why the error occured.
solution: Perform whatever actions necessary to make more memory available to the executing program.

message: Internal exception code. icode = [ string ], [ string ].
cause: Unknown - indicated by parameters. The first '%s' gives the internal exception code; the second is for any other additional comments.
solution: Report to the appropriate development group

message: Call to string failed.
cause: A function call has failed. This error is a generic message to show that the exception has occurred in a particular function function name. This allows the client to know the trace runtime calling sequence by examining the exception stack.
solution: See the accompanying error messages for more information.

message: Free some memory failed in string .
cause: A call to free some memory in function function name has failed.
solution: See the accompanying error messages for more information and contact Oracle Worldwide Support immediately.

message: Invalid parameter to function string .
cause: The function was called with an invalid parameter.
solution: Check the function call to make sure that the correct parameters are being passed.

message: NLSRTL's call failed. string .
cause: LX calls return failure
solution: Check if our parameters are correct. Contact the appropriate group immediately if we parameters are valid.

message: SLTS's initializing/terminating mutex failed for string .
cause: SLTS's call return failure in function '%s'.
solution: Contact the appropriate development group.

message: Unable to perform operation, file not opened in string .
cause: The file has not been successfully opened at the time the operation is attempted.
solution: Check to make sure that the file exists (for read) or that the program has access to the write a file (for write). It is also possible that the file was just never opened

message: Write failed, file cannot be written to.
cause: The buffer write operation failed. Possibly due to incorrect parameters being passed in.
solution: Check the underlying error for more information.

message: Unable to seek in sequentially accessed file.
cause: The file was opened with the flag LFILFA_SEQ for sequential file operations. Use seek only on files that are opened with the LFILFA_RANDOM flag for random access.
solution: Check to see how the file is being opened and accessed and make the two operations consistent (that is, make them both operations either sequential or random).

message: Seek operation failed.
cause: The buffer seek operation failed. Probably due to incorrect parameters or flags.
solution: Check syntax of the seek command and retry the operation.

message: Read operation failed.
cause: The buffer read operation failed. Probably due to incorrect parameters or flags.
solution: Check syntax of the read command and retry the operation.

message: Unable to add path.
cause: One of the following might have caused the error: the current path might not be in the proper format the directory might not be in the proper format the name object might not have been initialized properly
solution: Check the format of the current path and the new directory; check that the name object was initialized properly.

message: Path object holds more than one path.
cause: The path object passed to lfippth() holds more than one path.
solution: Make sure that the path object used in lfippth() holds only one path.

message: Open does not expect the file [ string ][ string ] to exist.
cause: The flags specified for the open indicate that the file does not exist. However, the file does exist.
solution: Check to make sure that the options that were specified for the file are correct and that you do not expect that the file should exist. If so then find out why the file does exist.

message: Open expect the file [ string ][ string ] to exist.
cause: The flags specified for the open indicate that the file the file to exist and it does not.
solution: Check to make sure that the options that were specified for the file are correct and that you expect that the file should exist. If so then find out why the file doesn't.

message: Unable to open file [ string ][ string ]. string .
cause: Either: the process does not have the proper access rights to open the file the file is already open
solution: Check to make sure the proper access permissions are assigned. If they are and the file still cannot be opened, then contact Oracle Worldwide Support.

message: Unable to initialize the Buffer Manager.
cause: The Buffer Manager initialization routine failed; probably because memory was exhausted.
solution: See the accompanying error messages for more information.

message: No other flags allowed in fixed length format.
cause: The function lfigfo() was called with an invalid File ID Descriptor. The valid File ID Descriptors are LFISTDIN, LFISTDOUT, and LFISTDERR.
solution: Check the call to lfigfo() to make sure it is correct.

message: Unable to initialize the Standard File object string .
cause: The call to open the standard file object failed.
solution: Check the underlying errors for more information.

message: Append is not allowed with string .
cause: Attempting to append using certain options.
solution: Check the flag options to verify its usage.

message: Buffer free failed.
cause: Probably do to the buffer flush failing.
solution: See the accompanying error messages for more information.

message: Unable to close file in operation string .
cause: The file close operation failed.
solution: See the accompanying error messages for more information.

message: Unable to rename file.
cause: The rename operation failed. Rename is called when we are protecting a file by operating on a temp file.
solution: Check to make sure that the process has the correct access rights to perform a rename.

message: Unable to change type to Unknown.
cause: The function lfichty() was called to change the file extension to LFIEXUNK (Unknown). This is not a valid operation.
solution: Check why you are doing this. If the extension is already unknown then you do not need to do this. If you just want no extension then use the extension type LFIEXNONE.

message: Unable to Abort an Unprotected file.
cause: The Abort function lfiabt() was called on a file that was not opened as a protected file. As such the abort operation is not valid.
solution: Check to see if you intended to open the file as a protected file.

message: Unable to parse root filename string .
cause: The root filename that was given to lfimknam() is not in a format that this platform understands.
solution: Check the format of the filename and retry the operation.

message: Only one of REPLACE, or PROT allowed for opty.
cause: Two or more of the following open type options were specified for the lfilini() function: LFILOPTY_REPLACE, or LFILOPTY_PROT.
solution: Remove one or more the of options such that you are only passing in one of the three.

message: Can only delete a file if we create it.
cause: The delete file flag was specified for a file that was not created by this file operation. The ability to delete a file is not portable. As such the only deletion that is allowed by this package is if we know we want to delete the file when we create it.
solution: You can only delete a file that you create. If you need to delete a file that you do not create then you will have to find another means of doing so.

message: Cannot access file Sequentially and Randomly.
cause: Both the LFILFA_SEQ (sequential) and LFILFA_RANDOM (random) flags were specified during the file object creation. This is not allowed. Only one of the two may be specified.
solution: Choose how you wish to access the file. If you choose random you can still access sequentially by just not using the repositioning functions.

message: No access mode was specified, default is sequential.
cause: Neither LFILFA_SEQ (sequential) or LFILFA_RANDOM (random) were specified during file object creation.
solution: The default is sequential but this should be explicitly set.

message: Random access only allowed on fixed length record files.
cause: The LFILFA_RANDOM flag was specified on a file that was not organized into fixed-length records. Random access is only allowed on fixed-length record files.
solution: Determine if the organization of your data needs to be in variable-length records and if you need to have random access to the file. If both conditions are true then you might need to buffer the entire file or enough of it to remove your need for random access. Another option is to close and rescan the file although this is not the optimal solution.

message: Record format can only be one of Fixed or Variable.
cause: Both LFILRF_FIXED (fixed) and LFILRF_VAR (variable) were specified during file object creation. Only one of the two is allowed for a given file.
solution: Determine how the file is organized and choose the option that matches.

message: No Record Format was specified, default is variable.
cause: Neither LFILRF_FIXED (fixed) or LFILRF_VAR (variable) were specified for record format. One of the two must be specified for each file.
solution: The default is LFILRF_VAR, but this should be explicitly set during file object creation.

message: Carriage Control is only valid for Standard file objects.
cause: The Carriage Control option is only valid for the standard file objects (LFISTDIN, LFISTDOUT, LFISTDERR). You may not specify this option for any other type of file.
solution: Choose between LFILRF_FIXED and LFILRF_VAR for the record format.

message: Invalid option string were specified on an input only file.
cause: The file was opened as input only but the output mode option LFILRF_WR_ASIS or delete option LFLOPTY_DELETE was specified.
solution: Check to see how you intend to open this file and make the necessary changes.

message: Input option specified on output only file.
cause: The file was opened as output only but one of the input mode options (LFILRF_READ_NL or LFILRF_FORCE_NL) or was specified.
solution: Check to see how you intend to open this file and make the necessary changes.

message: No open type specified.
cause: The file object was created without an open type (that is, LFILOPTY_INPUT, LFILOPTY_OUTPUT, etc.).
solution: Decide how the file should be accessed and specify one of the open types.

message: Record length string is greater than max length of string .
cause: The record length specified for the file is greater than the max supported by this platform.
solution: Decrease the record length.

message: Trying to create file string that already exists.
cause: The file object was initialized with LFILOPTY_OUTPUT and without LFILOPTY_REPLACE and yet a file by this name already exists.
solution: Check to make sure that you are creating the right file. If you intend to overwrite the file if it exists that specify the replace option LFILOPTY_REPLACE when initializing the file object.

message: Unable to protect a file for an append operation.
cause: The LFILOPTY_APPEND and LFILOPTY_PROT options were both specified for the file. This is currently not allowed because it would require copying the entire file at open time.
solution: Decide if you really need to protect the file for append. If so then think about making a copy of it before appending.

message: Unable to remove temporary file.
cause: A temporary file was created to protect a file and when the the tempfile was nolonger needed it LFI attempted to remove it and was unable to do so.
solution: Check the permissions and where the temp files are being created.

message: Unable to change type of open file.
cause: The function lfichty() was called on an opened file.
solution: This is a bug in the client code. lfichty() cannot be used in this case.

message: Unable to perform string on a file object that is string .
cause: Unable to perform an LFI operation on a file object for the given reason.
solution: Take the appropriate corrective measure. For example if a file is supposed to be opened before the operation can be performed, client code will need to open the file first.

message: Unable to perform string on a name object that is string .
cause: Unable to perform an LFI operation on a name object for the given reason.
solution: Take the appropriate corrective measure.

message: Option string cannot be used with option string in calling string .
cause: First option cannot be used with second option in such a function call.
solution: Re-examine code to determine which option is needed.

message: Invalid option string were specified on input-output file.
cause: The file was opened as input-output and one of the mode options (LFIOPTY_DELETE or non-LFIOPTY_RANDOM) was specified.
solution: Check to see how you intend to open this file and make the necessary changes.

message: Unable to abort file in operation string .
cause: The abort operation failed.
solution: Check the underlying errors for more information.

message: Unable to delete an existing file [ string ][ string ] not owned by Oracle.
cause: The file was not created by Oracle.
solution: Change owner of file to Oracle or give Oracle access privileges to delete it.

message: Unable to delete non-existent file string .
cause: The file to be deleted does not exist.
solution: Check the underlying errors for more information.

message: File [ string ][ string ] does not exist
cause: The file does not exist.
solution: Check to make sure the file exists and retry the operation.

message: User buffer too short.
cause: The buffer that was passed is not large enough.
solution: Allocate a larger buffer and retry the operation.

message: copy does not expect the file string . string to exist
cause: We are expecting the destination file not to exist and it does.
solution: Find out why the file does exist.

message: File string . string does not exist
cause: The file does not exist.
solution: Check to make sure the file exists and retry the operation.

message: string can be called only on files opened in byte mode
cause: A routine that should be used only for files in byte mode was called for a file that was opened in record mode
solution: In order to use this function, the file should be opened in byte mode.

message: Error on destroying hash table in function string
cause: We were expecting the cache path object and it does not.
solution: In order to use this function, the path object should be cache path object.

message: Error on creating hash table in function string
cause: routine failed to create path object hash table
solution: make sure that startsize <= LHTQMAXSLOTS

message: Error on inserting into hash table in function string
cause: routine failed to insert into hash table
solution: make sure there is enough memory for allocation and that the hash table exists.

message: Read operation (byte mode) failed.
cause: Byte mode read operation failed. Probably due to incorrect parameters or flags, or trying to read beyond end of file.
solution: Check syntax of the read command and size of file.

message: Unable to write line to file.
cause: The file being written to may no longer be open or we may have reached the end of the file.
solution: Examine underlying errors for more information.

message: Unable to write string bytes to file.
cause: The file being written to may no longer be open or we may have reached the end of the file.
solution: Examine underlying errors for more information.

message: Unable to read line from file.
cause: The file being read from may no longer be open.
solution: Examine underlying errors for more information.

message: Unable to read string bytes from file.
cause: The file being read from may no longer be open.
solution: See the accompanying error messages for more information.

message: Unable to empty buffer.
cause: The buffer manager is probably unable to write to the underlying file.
solution: Examine underlying errors for more information.

message: Unable to fill buffer.
cause: The buffer manager is probably unable to read from the underlying file.
solution: See the accompanying error messages for more information.

message: File ends in partial character in string .

solution: Examine underlying errors for more information.

cause: The length of the line exceeds the maximum length.

message: Max filename size exceeded generating filename.

cause: The ftell() function returned an error.

cause: Call to open() failed.

cause: The llseek() function returned an error.

message: bad bind variable ' string '
cause: The client (caller) of PL/SQL has parsed a bind variable that it has informed to be 'bad'.
solution: None

message: parser stack overflow because nesting is too deep
cause: The parser, which checks the syntax of PL/SQL statements, uses a data structure called a stack; the number of levels of nesting in the PL/SQL block exceeded the stack capacity.
solution: Reorganize the block structure to avoid nesting at too deep a level. For example, move the lowest-level sub-block to a higher level.

message: string
cause: This error message is from the parser. It found a token (language element) that is inappropriate in this context.
solution: Check previous tokens as well as the one given in the error message. The line and column numbers given in the error message refer to the end of the faulty language construct.

message: empty argument list in call of procedure ' string ' must be omitted
cause: In a subprogram call, the name of the subprogram was followed by an empty parameter list. For example, procedure P was called as P(). This is not allowed.
solution: Remove the empty parameter list. In the example, change the procedure call to P.

message: at most one forward declaration of type ' string ' is permitted
cause: More than one forward declaration of a type is redundant.
solution: Remove all but one forward declaration.

message: declarative units must be a single variable declaration
cause: While checking a declarative unit (a top-level declare block without the BEGIN...END), PL/SQL found that there was more than one item declared or that the item was not a variable declaration. A table is a common variable declaration at the unit level. To define a TABLE, compile a DECLARE compilation unit, but only one at a time is allowed.
solution: Declare variables in separate declarative units.

message: unknown exception name ' string ' in PRAGMA EXCEPTION_INIT
cause: No declaration for the exception name referenced in an EXCEPTION_INIT pragma was found within the scope of the pragma.
solution: Make sure the pragma follows the exception declaration and is within the same scope.

message: bind variable ' string ' not allowed in this context
cause: A bind variable, that is, an identifier prefixed with a colon, was found in an inappropriate context.
solution: Remove the colon or replace the bind variable with the appropriate object.

message: end-of-file in comment
cause: A Comment had a comment initiator (/*), but before the
solution: Remove the Comment initiator or add a comment terminator. The line and column numbers accompanying the error message refer to the beginning of the last legal token before the Comment initiator.

message: end-of-line in quoted identifier
cause: A quoted identifier had a beginning quote ("), but before the ending quote (") was found, an end-of-line marker was encountered.
solution: Remove the beginning quote or add the ending quote. The line and column numbers accompanying the error message refer to the beginning of the quoted identifier.

message: END identifier ' string ' must match ' string ' at line string , column string
cause: Following the keyword END, which terminates some language constructs (such as loops, blocks, functions, and procedures), you can optionally place the name of that construct. For example, at the end of the definition of loop L you might write END L. This error occurs when the optional name does not match the name given to the language construct. It is usually caused by a misspelled identifier or by faulty block structure.
solution: Make sure the spelling of the END identifier matches the name given to the language construct and that the block structure is correct.

message: identifier ' string ' too long
cause: The name of a PL/SQL variable is longer than 30 characters. Legal identifiers (including quoted identifiers) have a maximum length of 30 characters. A string literal might have been mistakenly enclosed in double quotes instead of single quotes, in which case PL/SQL considers it a quoted identifier.
solution: Shorten the identifier.

message: this PRAGMA must follow the declaration of ' string '
cause: The pragma refers to a PL/SQL object that was not declared or is not within the scope of the reference. Identifiers must be declared before they are used in a pragma; forward references are not allowed.
solution: Check the spelling and declaration of the identifier. Also confirm that the declaration is placed correctly in the block structure.

message: Duplicate where-clause in table expression
cause: Two or more WHERE clauses were found in a DELETE, SELECT, or UPDATE statement. The WHERE clause specifies a condition under which rows in a table are processed. The condition can contain several logical expressions connected by AND or OR, but a statement can contain only one WHERE clause.
solution: Remove one of the WHERE clauses and, if necessary, connect logical expressions by AND or OR

message: Duplicate connect-by clause in table expression
cause: Two or more CONNECT BY clauses were found in a SELECT statement. The CONNECT BY clause defines a relationship used to return rows in a hierarchical order. The relationship can contain two expressions separated by a relational operator (such as = or !=), but a statement can contain only one CONNECT BY clause.
solution: Remove one of the CONNECT BY clauses and, if necessary, separate expressions by a relational operator.

message: Duplicate group-by clause in table expression
cause: Two or more GROUP BY clauses were found in a SELECT statement. The GROUP BY clause lists column expressions used to form a summary row for each group of selected rows. The list can contain several column expressions separated by commas, but a statement can contain only one GROUP BY clause.
solution: Remove one of the GROUP BY clauses and, if necessary, separate column expressions by commas.

message: Duplicate having-clause in table expression
cause: Two or more HAVING clauses were found in a SELECT statement. The HAVING clause specifies a condition under which groups of rows (formed by the GROUP BY clause) are included in the result. The condition can include several logical expressions connected by AND or OR, but a statement can contain only one HAVING clause.
solution: Remove one of the HAVING clauses and, if necessary, connect logical expressions by AND or OR.

message: inappropriate argument in OPEN statement
cause: The asterisk (*) option was used in the argument list of a SQL group function other than COUNT. For example, the code might look like SELECT SUM(*) INTO emp_count FROM emp; -- should be COUNT(*) Only COUNT permits the use of the asterisk option, which returns the number of rows in a table.
solution: Remove the asterisk option from the argument list and replace it with an expression that refers to one or more database columns.

message: string as separator is allowed only with specific built-in functions
cause: A few built-in functions use keywords (instead of commas) as argument separators: Built-in function Argument separators --------------------------------------------- CHR, TRANSLATE USING CAST AS TRIM TRAILING, LEADING, BOTH, FROM A function different from one of these built-in functions is using a keyword as an argument separator.
solution: Correct the argument list or change the function name.

message: program too large ( string )
cause: PL/SQL was designed primarily for robust transaction processing. One consequence of the special-purpose design is that the PL/SQL compiler imposes a limit on block size. The limit depends on the mix of statements in the PL/SQL block. Blocks that exceed the limit cause this error.
solution: The best solution is to modularize the program by defining subprograms, which can be stored in an Oracle database. Another solution is to break the program into two sub-blocks. Have the first block INSERT any data the second block needs into a temporary database table. Then, have the second block SELECT the data from the table.

message: name of exception expected for first arg in exception_init pragma
cause: The first argument passed to the EXCEPTION_INIT pragma was something other than an exception name. The first argument must be the name of a legally declared exception.
solution: Replace the first argument with the name of a legally declared exception.

message: type name expected
cause: When a constant or variable was declared, its datatype was not specified. For example, the code might look like pi CONSTANT := 3.14159; -- should be CONSTANT REAL := 3.14159 Every constant and variable must have a datatype, which specifies a storage format, constraints, and valid range of values.
solution: Supply the type name

message: selector ALL is not allowed
cause: The ALL shortcut for specifying system privileges or statement options was used in a SQL statement. PL/SQL does not support the ALL shortcut.
solution: Remove the ALL shortcut from the SQL statement.

message: Pragma string is not a supported pragma
cause: The named pragma (compiler directive) is not among those supported by PL/SQL. The pragma name might be misspelled, or the pragma syntax might be faulty.
solution: Check the spelling of the pragma name, and make sure the proper syntax was used.

message: Illegal number of arguments for pragma string
cause: The number of arguments (actual parameters) passed to the named pragma (compiler directive) is incorrect. A required argument was omitted from the argument list, or the pragma syntax is faulty (for example, a comma might be missing between two parameters).
solution: Supply the missing argument, or correct the faulty syntax.

message: Pragma INTERFACE only supports C as its first argument
cause: The first parameter passed to pragma INTERFACE specified a host language other than C. Currently, C is the only host language supported. The parameter might be misspelled, or the pragma syntax might be faulty (for example, a comma might be missing between two parameters).
solution: Check the spelling of the first parameter, which should be C, and make sure the proper syntax was used.

message: Pragma string expects 1st argument to be a procedure/function/package/cursor
cause: The first argument (actual parameter) passed to the named pragma (compiler directive) was not the name of a subprogram, package, or cursor, as required. The parameter might be misspelled, or the pragma syntax might be faulty (for example, a comma might be missing between two parameters).
solution: Check the spelling of the first parameter, and make sure the proper syntax was used.

message: Pragma string expects 2nd argument to be a procedure/function
cause: The second argument (actual parameter) passed to the named pragma (compiler directive) was not the name of a procedure or function, as required. The parameter cannot be a non-static method. The parameter might be misspelled or the pragma syntax might be faulty (for example, a comma might be missing between two parameters).
solution: Check the spelling of the second parameter and make sure the proper syntax was used.

message: Pragma string does not support string
cause: One of the parameters passed to this pragma was not among the list of allowed values. The parameter might be misspelled, or the pragma syntax might be faulty (for example, a comma might be missing between two parameters).
solution: Check the spelling of all the parameters and make sure the proper syntax was used.

message: Pragma string expects 1st argument to be an identifier or string-literal
cause: The first argument (actual parameter) passed to the named pragma (compiler directive) was not an identifier or string literal, as required. The parameter might be misspelled, or the pragma syntax might be faulty (for example, a comma might be missing between two parameters).
solution: Check the spelling of the first parameter, and make sure the proper syntax was used.

message: Pragma string expects 2nd argument to be an identifier or string-literal
cause: The second argument (actual parameter) passed to the named pragma (compiler directive) was not an identifier or string literal, as required. The parameter might be misspelled, or the pragma syntax might be faulty (for example, a comma might be missing between two parameters).
solution: Check the spelling of the second parameter, and make sure the proper syntax was used.

message: Pragma string expects 3rd argument to be an identifier, string or numeric literal
cause: The fourth argument (actual parameter) passed to the named pragma (compiler directive) was not a numeric literal, as required. The parameter might be miscoded, or the pragma syntax might be faulty (for example, a comma might be missing between two parameters).
solution: Check the coding of the fourth parameter, and make sure the proper syntax was used.

message: Precision for a binary type must be one of 8, 16, or 32
cause: Invalid precision was specified for a signed or unsigned binary type.
solution: Specify precision as one of 8, 16, or 32.

message: duplicate external NAME specification in subprogram expression
cause: The subprogram was found to have two external NAME specifications.
solution: Remove one of the external NAME specifications.

message: duplicate external LIBRARY specification in subprogram expression
cause: The subprogram was found to have two external LIBRARY specifications.
solution: Remove one of the external LIBRARY specifications.

message: duplicate external PARAMETER STYLE specification in subprogram expression
cause: The subprogram was found to have two external PARAMETER STYLE specifications.
solution: Remove one of the external PARAMETER STYLE specifications.

message: duplicate external PARAMETER list specification in subprogram expression
cause: The subprogram was found to have two external PARAMETER STYLE specifications.
solution: Remove one of the external PARAMETER STYLE specifications.

message: duplicate external LANGUAGE specification in subprogram expression
cause: The subprogram was found to have two external LANGUAGE specifications.
solution: Remove one of the external LANGUAGE specifications.

message: duplicate external CALLING STANDARD specification in subprogram expression
cause: The subprogram was found to have two external CALLING STANDARD specifications.
solution: Remove one of the external CALLING STANDARD specifications.

message: duplicate external WITH CONTEXT specification in subprogram expression
cause: The subprogram was found to have two external WITH CONTEXT specifications.
solution: Remove one of the external WITH CONTEXT specifications.

message: duplicate external TRUSTED/UNTRUSTED specification in subprogram expression
cause: The subprogram was found to have two external TRUSTED/UNTRUSTED specifications.
solution: Remove one of the external external TRUSTED/UNTRUSTED specifications.

message: LIBRARY or ASSEMBLY file specification string is empty
cause: A zero-length string was found for the LIBRARY or ASSEMBLY file specification.
solution: Specify a non-zero length string for the LIBRARY or ASSEMBLY file specification.

message: Only 1 pragma of this type is allowed per subprogram
cause: The subprogram was found to have two PRAGMA RESTRICT_REFERENCES.
solution: Remove one of the PRAGMA RESTRICT_REFERENCES.

message: found: string but expected : INTEGER
cause: This error happens in the creation of a pl/sql external type: [SIGNED | UNSIGNED] BINARY INTEGER (<precision>). It may be referenced only in a create type statement. Such types are non-queryable. Something other than 'INTEGER' was supplied.
solution: None

message: Expression or Variable is an illegal type to PLS/QL: string
cause: A type was used which does not belong PL/SQL. This type can only be referenced in CREATE TYPE statements, and is a non-queryable data type.
solution: None

message: POINTER type may only reference an object type.
cause: A POINTER type which does not belong to PL/SQL can only refer to an object type. This type can only be referenced in CREATE TYPE statements, and is a non-queryable data type.
solution: None

message: A string type may only be used as an object type attribute.
cause: A POINTER or [SIGNED/UNSIGNED] BINARY INTEGER can only be used as attributes of object types. These types can only be referenced in CREATE TYPE statements, and are non-queryable data types. One of these external PL/SQL types outside of an object type.
solution: None

message: An object type may have only 1 MAP or 1 ORDER method.
cause: More than one map or order function was declared. An object type can have only one map function or one order function, but not both.
solution: None

message: Only a function may be a MAP, ORDER or CONSTRUCTOR method.
cause: A procedure was declared as a MAP, ORDER or CONSTRUCTOR method. Only functions can be MAP, ORDER or CONSTRUCTOR methods.
solution: None

message: Null constraints not supported for object attributes.
cause: A null constraint was specified for an attribute in an object. This is not supported.
solution: Remove the constraint.

message: AUTHID only allowed on schema-level programs
cause: An AUTHID clause was specified for a subprogram inside a package or type. These clauses are only supported for top-level stored procedures, packages, and types.
solution: Remove the clause

message: AUTHID must specify CURRENT_USER or DEFINER
cause: The only two allowed options for AUTHID are CURRENT_USER and DEFINER.
solution: Fix the AUTHID clause to specify CURRENT_USER or DEFINER

message: Pragma string expects 3rd argument to be an identifier or a string literal
cause: The third argument (actual parameter) passed to the named pragma (compiler directive) was not an identifier or a string literal when there is a fourth argument to the pragma. The parameter might be misspelled, or the pragma syntax might be faulty (for example, a comma might be missing between two parameters).
solution: Check the spelling of the third parameter, and make sure the proper syntax was used.

message: Pragma string expects 4th argument to be a positive integer literal
cause: The fourth argument (actual parameter) passed to the named pragma (compiler directive) was not a numeric literal, as required. The parameter might be misspelled, or the pragma syntax might be faulty (for example, a comma might be missing between two parameters).
solution: Check the spelling of the fourth parameter, and make sure the proper syntax was used.

message: cursor subqueries are not supported in this release
cause: This feature is not yet implemented.
solution: None

message: call statement is not supported in PL/SQL
cause: A CALL statement was found in PL/SQL source.
solution: Use an ordinary PL/SQL function or procedure call.

message: bad format for date, time, timestamp or interval literal
cause: The contents of the date, time, timestamp or interval literal did not match the expected format.
solution: Correct the format for the date, datetime, or interval literal.

message: keyword BULK is used in a wrong context
cause: keyword BULK is used illegally. For example, BULK is used without INTO clause
solution: remove the keyword BULK.

message: duplicate modifier specification ' string '
cause: A method or object type modifier was specified more than once.
solution: Remove all but one occurence of the duplicate modifier.

message: modifier ' string ' conflicts with prior ' string ' specification
cause: The method or object type modifier specified conflicts with an earlier modifier. For example, a FINAL modifier cannot be combined with a NOT FINAL modifier.
solution: Remove one of the conflicting modifiers.

message: the SQL statement in an OPEN statement or FOR loop must be a SELECT
cause: An OPEN cursor statement or cursor FOR loop can only invoke a SELECT statement, not an UPDATE, INSERT or DELETE.
solution: Use only SELECT statements in OPEN or cursor FOR loops

message: duplicate dedicated AGENT specification in subprogram expression
cause: The subprogram was found to have two dedicated AGENT specifications.
solution: Remove one of the dedicated AGENT specifications.

message: string literal too long
cause: The string literal was longer than 32767 bytes.
solution: Use a string literal of at most 32767 bytes.

message: SPACE, TAB or RETURN are disallowed as alternative quote delimiters
cause: SPACE, TAB or RETURN was used as alternative quote delimiter.
solution: Use a character other than SPACE, TAB or RETURN as the alternative quote delimiter.

message: a static boolean expression must be used
cause: The expression contained a syntax or semantic error, or it did not have a boolean type or its evaluation raised an exception.
solution: Write correct static boolean expression.

message: unexpected preprocessor token '$ string '
cause: A preprocessor token was used inappropriately.
solution: Remove the preprocessor token that is inappropriately used.

message: '$ string ' preprocessor directive does not end properly
cause: A preprocessor directive was not ended properly.
solution: Use $end to end the preprocessor directive properly.

message: a static character expression must be used
cause: The expression contained a syntax or semantic error, or it did not have a character type or its evaluation raised an exception.
solution: Write correct static character expression.

message: $ERROR: string
cause: $ERROR directive was used. This is an expected error message.
solution: NA

message: preprocessor directives are not supported in this context
cause: A preprocessor directive was used in a compilation unit for which conditional compilation is not supported.
solution: Do not use any preprocessor directives in this compilation unit.

message: unsupported preprocessor directive ' string '
cause: An unsupported preprocessor directive was used.
solution: Use a supported preprocessor directive.

message: Identifier cannot be an empty string
cause: Identifier was declared using an empty string,
solution: rename the identifier to a non empty string.

message: identifier ' string ' must be declared
cause: You tried to reference either an undeclared variable, exception, procedure, or other item, or an item to which no privilege was granted or an item to which privilege was granted only through a role.
solution: 1) Check your spelling and declaration of the referenced name. 2) Verify that the declaration for the referenced item is placed correctly in the block structure. 3) If the referenced item is indeed declared but you don't have privileges to refer to that item, for security reasons, you will be notified only that the item is not declared. 4) If the referenced item is indeed declared and you believe that you have privileges to refer to that item, check the privileges; if the privileges were granted only via a role, then this is expected and documented behavior. Stored objects (packages, procedures, functions, triggers, views) run in the security domain of the object owner with no roles enabled except PUBLIC. Again, you will be notified only that the item was not declared.

message: type ' string ' must be declared
cause: An attempt was made to reference an undefined type. Either the type specifier was not declared or it is not within the scope of the reference.
solution: Check the spelling and declaration of the type specifier. Also confirm that the declaration is placed correctly in the block structure.

message: function DECODE must be called with at least 3 non-boolean arguments
cause: Less than three arguments were passed to the built-in function DECODE. Though DECODE takes a variable number of (non-Boolean) arguments, at least three arguments must be passed.
solution: Call DECODE with three or more arguments

message: function or pseudo-column ' string ' may be used inside a SQL statement only
cause: A pseudocolumn or proscribed function was used in a procedural statement. The SQL pseudocolumns (LEVEL, ROWID, ROWNUM) can be used only in SQL statements. Likewise, certain functions such as DECODE, DUMP, and VSIZE and the SQL group functions (AVG, MIN, MAX, COUNT, SUM, STDDEV, VARIANCE) can be used only in SQL statements.
solution: Remove the pseudocolumn reference or function call from the procedural statement. Or, replace the procedural statement with a SELECT INTO statement; for example, replace bonus := DECODE(rating, 1, 5000, 2, 2500, ...); with the following statement: SELECT DECODE(rating, 1, 5000, 2, 2500, ...) INTO bonus FROM dual;

message: Aggregate not allowed here
cause: An aggregate, that is, a parenthesized list of values such as (7788, 'SCOTT', 20), was found in an inappropriate context.
solution: Remove or relocate the aggregate.

message: %TYPE must be applied to a variable, column, field or attribute, not to " string "
cause: The program object declared using the %TYPE datatype attribute is not of the appropriate class. It must be a variable, column, record component, subprogram formal parameter, or other object to which values can be assigned.
solution: Declare an object of the appropriate class or define the datatype in another way (for example, use %ROWTYPE).

message: identifier ' string ', applied to implicit cursor SQL, is not a legal cursor attribute
cause: An identifier that is not a cursor attribute was applied to the identifier SQL. For example, this error occurs if the cursor attribute is misspelled.
solution: Check the spelling of the cursor attribute name. Make sure the attribute is one of these: %NOTFOUND, %FOUND, %ROWCOUNT, %ISOPEN.

message: identifier ' string ' is not a legal cursor attribute
cause: An identifier not declared as a cursor attribute was applied to an identifier declared as a cursor. For example, this error occurs if the cursor attribute is misspelled.
solution: Check the spelling of the cursor attribute name. Make sure the attribute is one of these: %NOTFOUND, %FOUND, %ROWCOUNT, %ISOPEN.

message: table ' string ' is not in FROM clause
cause: In a query, a table referenced by the select list is not named in the FROM clause.
solution: Check the spelling of the table names, make sure each column in the select list refers to a table in the FROM clause, then re-execute the query.

message: an OTHERS clause is required in this CASE statement
cause: Unless the clauses of a CASE statement mention all values of the type of the selecting expression, an OTHERS clause must be provided as the last clause of the CASE statement. It is impossible to cover all values of type INTEGER (or NUMBER), so an OTHERS clause is always required when the expression following the keyword CASE is of type INTEGER (or NUMBER).
solution: None

message: CASE labels or ranges must not be duplicated in different WHEN clauses
cause: In this CASE statement, a value appears in more than one WHEN clause. A value may appear in at most one WHEN clause of a CASE statement.
solution: None

message: could not obtain enough memory to compile CASE statement
cause: The CASE statement is too big. The compiler did not have enough storage to process it.
solution: None

message: package STANDARD not accessible
cause: The PL/SQL compiler could not find package STANDARD in the current Oracle database. To compile a program, PL/SQL needs package STANDARD.
solution: Make sure that package STANDARD is available in the current Oracle database, then retry the operation.

message: BEGIN...END block nesting is too deep
cause: The number of levels of nesting in the PL/SQL block is too large. Blocks can be nested up to 255 levels deep, depending on the availability of system resources such as memory.
solution: Reorganize the block structure to avoid nesting at too deep a level. For example, move the lowest-level sub-block to a higher level.

message: String length constraints must be in range (1 .. 32767)
cause: When a character variable was declared, a length outside the legal range was specified. For example, the following declarations are illegal: flag CHAR(0); -- illegal; zero length name VARCHAR2(-10); -- illegal; negative length
solution: Change the length constraint, making sure that it lies in the range 1 .. 32767.

message: NUMBER precision constraint must be in range (1 .. 38)
cause: A NUMBER variable was declared with a precision that is outside the legal range. Declarations such as N NUMBER(800) or N NUMBER(123,10) are not supported.
solution: Change the illegal NUMBER precision constraint, making sure that it lies in the range 1 .. 38.

message: NUMBER scale constraint must be in range (-84 .. 127)
cause: A NUMBER variable was declared with a scale that is outside the legal range. Declarations such as N NUMBER(10,345) or N NUMBER(10,-100) are not supported.
solution: Change the illegal NUMBER scale constraint, making sure that it lies in the range -84 .. 127.

message: a variable declared NOT NULL must have an initialization assignment
cause: In general, variables that have no initialization clause in their declaration are automatically initialized to NULL. This is illogical for NOT NULL variables; therefore, an initialization clause is required.
solution: Add an initialization clause to the variable declaration. If the initilization is too complicated for the syntax, one can add a function call (in a later release).

message: label ' string ' reference is out of scope
cause: A block or loop label was used to qualify a variable (as in outer_block.date) that was not declared or is not within the scope of the label. The variable name might be misspelled, its declaration might be faulty, or the declaration might be placed incorrectly in the block structure.
solution: Check the spelling and declaration of the variable name. Also confirm that the declaration is placed correctly in the block structure.

message: simple name required in this context
cause: A qualified name such as A.B or A.B.C is not permitted here.
solution: Use a simple name such as A instead.

message: ' string ' is not a procedure or is undefined
cause: An identifier being referenced as a procedure was not declared or actually represents another object (for example, it might have been declared as a function).
solution: Check the spelling and declaration of the identifier. Also confirm that the declaration is placed correctly in the block structure.

message: no function with name ' string ' exists in this scope
cause: An identifier being referenced as a function was not declared or actually represents another object (for example, it might have been declared as a procedure).
solution: Check the spelling and declaration of the identifier. Also confirm that the declaration is placed correctly in the block structure.

message: paramaterless procedure ' string ' used as function
cause: An identifier being referenced as a parameterless function actually represents a procedure.
solution: Check the spelling and declaration of the identifier. Also confirm that the declaration is placed correctly in the block structure. If necessary, change the declaration of the identifier or change the reference so that it does not require a return value.

message: object ' string ' must be of type function or array to be used this way
cause: An identifier being referenced as a function or an array actually represents an object (a number or date, for example) that cannot be referenced in this way.
solution: Check the spelling and declaration of the identifier. Also confirm that the declaration is placed correctly in the block structure.

message: subprogram or cursor ' string ' reference is out of scope
cause: The prefix in a qualified name was a subprogram or cursor which was not in an enclosing scope; i.e., a subprogram or cursor name is being used as a scope qualifier for a reference to an entity (within that subprogram or cursor) that is not in scope. Example: declare x number; type t1 is record (a number); function f return t1 is a number; begin x := f.a; -- legal use of function "f" as a scope qualifier; -- resolves to local variable "a" in function "f". x := f().a; -- legal reference to component "a" of returned record end; begin x := f.a; -- illegal use of function "f" as a scope qualifier x := f().a; -- legal reference to component "a" of returned record end;
solution: a) if the intention was to refer to a local variable of a non-enclosing function, this is not allowed; remove the reference b) if this is a parameterless function, and the the intention was to access a field of the result of a call to this function, then use empty parentheses in the call.

message: package ' string ' used as variable reference
cause: A package was referenced in an expression as if it were a variable or function. Either the name of the variable or function is misspelled or the reference is not fully qualified. For example, to call the function my_function, which is stored in package my_package, dot notation must be used, as follows: ... my_package.my_function ...
solution: Correct the spelling of the variable or function name or use dot notation to reference the packaged variable or function.

message: subprogram 'in' formal string is not yet denotable
cause: When the formal parameters of a subprogram were declared, one parameter was used to initialize another, as in PROCEDURE my_proc (j NUMBER, k NUMBER := j) IS ... The first parameter has no value until run time, so it cannot be used to initialize another parameter.
solution: Remove the illegal formal parameter reference.

message: Illegal declaration of variable of type LONG
cause: The identifier is a formal parameter which is being used in the context of a default expression value for a formal parameter in the same formal parameter list. E.g.: procedure p(j number, k number := j).
solution: Remove the offending variable definition

message: Attribute expression within SQL expression
cause: An attribute expression, such as SQL%NOTFOUND, was used in a SQL statement, but attribute expressions are allowed only in procedural statements.
solution: To workaround this limitation, assign the value of the attribute expression to a variable, then use the variable in the SQL statement. For example, replace the statement INSERT INTO audits VALUES (c1%ROWCOUNT, ...); with the following statements: row_count := c1%ROWCOUNT; INSERT INTO audits VALUES (row_count, ...);

message: OUT and IN OUT formal parameters may not have default expressions
cause: When the formal parameters of a procedure were declared, an OUT or IN OUT parameter was initialized to a default value, as in PROCEDURE calc_bonus (bonus OUT REAL := 0, ...) IS ... However, only IN parameters can be initialized to default values.
solution: Remove the illegal default expression.

message: function ' string ' may not be used in SQL
cause: A proscribed function was used in a SQL statement. Certain functions such as SQLCODE and SQLERRM can be used only in procedural statements.
solution: Remove the function call from the SQL statement. Or, replace the function call with a local variable.
