message: Unexpected argument {0}.
cause: The command line argument reported in above error message is not expected the by tool
solution: Refer to the tool's inline help display or to the product documentation of the command line tool for valid options and arguments, and then rerun the tool.

message: The option {0} is required.
cause: The command line option reported by the above error message is a mandatory option required by the tool
solution: Review the tool's inline help display or to the product documentation of the command line tool for type of value required for this option. And then rerun the command specifying the above option in command line options.

message: The parameter {0} requires an argument.
cause: The command line parameter reported in error message needs a value.
solution: Review the tool's inline help display or to the product documentation of the command line tool for type of value required for this option. And then rerun the command specifying the above option in command line options.

message: Oracle Clusterware is not properly stopped and de-configured on node "{0}". The files "{1}" exist as configured.
cause: The files init.ohasd, or ocr.loc and/or directory scls_scr still exists on this node which makes the tool believe that the clusterware stack is not shutdown properly
solution: Run the Oracle clusterware deconfiguration utility to completely cleanup the configuration. The Clusterware deconfiguration tool is available in Oracle clusterware home and also on Oracle OTN (Technology Network) page.

message: Failed to stop Oracle Clusterware on nodes "{0}". Run the command "{1}" after fixing the problem.
cause: The clusterware deconfiguration tool has failed to stop Oracle clusterware stack. The reason for failure can be found browsing through clusterware alert logs found in log/<hostname>/alert<hostname>.log directory under Oracle clusterware.
solution: You should browse through deamon logs in log/<hostname> under Oracle clustereware home and manually correct the problem to stop clusterware stack. And then rerun the command specified in above error message.

message: Run the following command as the root user on node "{0}".
cause: The clusterware deconfiguration that is run as non-root user cannot automatically run the command specified in above message.
solution: You should login to another session as a privileged user and run the command specified in above message

message: Run the following command as administrator.
cause: The clusterware deconfiguration which is run as non-root user cannot automatically run the command specified in above message.
solution: You should login to another session as a privileged user and run the command specified in above message

message: As the privileged user, Execute "{0}" on every node in this cluster except for this node, and then execute "{1}" on this node to remove the configuration of the Oracle Clusterware and to completely remove the Oracle software
cause: This is the message reported by Oracle clusterware deconfiguration tool when it is run in non-interactive (or silent) mode.
solution: Execute the identified scripts as described. Deconfiguring Oracle Clusterware in silent mode requires one set of operations on all nodes but the last followed by a special set of operations on the last node.

message: Oracle Clusterware is not stopped and de-configured on node "{0}" due to error "{1}"
cause: The tool failed to deconfigure Oracle clusterware stack on the node because of errors reported in the above message
solution: You should review the error messages reported in above message to perform corrective actions and then rerun the tool

message: The stopping and de-configuring of Oracle Clusterware failed on some nodes. Fix the problem and rerun this tool to completely remove the Oracle Clusterware configuration and the software
cause: This is a message reported by the tool to inform you that the Oracle clusterware deconfiguration did not happen on some of the nodes in the cluster.
solution: You should review the error messages reported by the tool for failing to deconfigure clusterware stack on each node, perform corrective actions after reviewing the error messages, and rerun the tool to completely deconfigure Oracle clusterware stack

message: You must delete or downgrade Clusterware-managed Oracle databases and de-install Clusterware-managed Oracle homes before attempting to remove the Oracle Clusterware home.
cause: An attempt was made to deconfigure the Oracle Clusterware when one or more Clusterware-managed Oracle databases still exist.
solution: Run the Oracle Clusterware deconfiguration tool from Clusterware-managed Oracle homes to delete, deconfigure or downgrade Oracle database and then run the same tool from Oracle Clusterware home to deconfigure Clusterware.

message: The node "{0}" is currently not responding.
cause: The host reported in the above message may have rebooted or hung
solution: Login to the host if possible and review system logs, correct the problem

message: The stopping and de-configuring of Oracle Restart failed. Fix the problem and rerun this tool to completely remove the Oracle Restart configuration and the software
cause: The Oracle Restart stack couldn't be stopped cleanly before de-configuring.
solution: Review the error messages reported by the tool for failing to deconfigure Oracle Restart stack, perform corrective actions after reviewing the error messages, and rerun the tool to completely deconfigure Oracle Restart stack.

message: The deinstall tool failed to create the script file "{0}" that needs to be run in silent mode due to error "{1}"
cause: The tool failed to create silent mode script file because of errors reported in the above message.
solution: You should review the error messages reported in above message to perform corrective actions and then rerun the tool.

message: As the privileged user, execute "{0}" and then execute "{1}" on this node to remove the configuration of the Oracle Restart and to completely remove the Oracle software
cause: This is the message reported by Oracle Restart deconfiguration tool when it is run in non-interactive (or silent) mode.
solution: Execute the identified scripts as described.

message: Can't deconfigure Oracle Restart before removing or downgrading managed Oracle databases.
cause: A request to deconfigure Oracle Restart found one or more managed Oracle database homes, so the request was rejected.
solution: Run the Oracle deconfiguration tool from Oracle database homes to delete, deconfigure or downgrade Oracle database and then run the same tool from Oracle Restart home to deconfigure the Oracle Restart stack.

message: The home being deconfigured is NOT a configured Grid Infrastructure home ({0})
cause: The home that was deconfigured has a different path from the configured Infrastructure home.
solution: If it is required to deconfigure the active CRS home, specify the configured CRS home in the deinstall command argument, or run deinstall from the configured CRS home.

message: Current user "{0}" is not the oracle owner user "{1}" of oracle home "{2}"
cause: The command was run as a different user than the owner user of the oracle home path.
solution: Retry the command as the user who owns the specified oracle home.

message: Failed to get CSS mode

solution: Correct the problem indicated by the accompanying messages, if possible. Otherwise. contact Oracle Support Services.

solution: Contact Oracle Support Services.

message: Communications error
cause: CSS daemon is not running on the local node or unable to authenticate with CSS daemon
solution: Use 'crsctl check css' to ensure that CSS daemon is running. If CSS daemon is not running, execute 'crsctl start crs' command.

message: Oracle Cluster Registry error
cause: OCR returned an error while processing a CSS request
solution: Ensure that CRSD daemon is running e.g. with crsctl check clusterware

message: Unexpected CSS error

message: Check for node with node number 0 failed.
cause: CSS daemon is not running on local node or unable to authenticate with CSS daemon.
solution: Use 'crsctl check css' to ensure that CSS daemon is running. If CSS daemon is not running, execute 'crsctl start crs' command.

message: OCR error returned from an internal interface
cause: An internal interface encountered an error in OCR processing. This message may be accompanied by others identifying the specific problem.

message: Unexpected error ({0}) returned from an internal interface
cause: An internal error occurred.
solution: Contact Oracle Support Services.

message: GSD already exists
cause: An attempt was made to create the Global Services Daemon (GSD) application while there was a running GSD application.
solution: Stop and remove the GSD and create the GSD application again using 'srvctl add nodeapps'.

message: Listener already exists
cause: An attempt was made to create a Listener application while there was a running Listener application.
solution: Stop and remove the running Listener and create the Listener application again using 'srvctl add nodeapps'.

message: EM Agent already exists
cause: An attempt was made to create an Agent application while there was a running Agent application.
solution: Stop the running Agent and create the Agent application again using 'srvctl add nodeapps'.

message: Netmasks are different for starting and ending IP addresses
cause: An invalid range of VIP addresses was specified for the cluster
solution: Check if the starting and ending addresses in the VIP range belong to the same netmask.

message: No active nodes detected in the cluster
cause: The active node list of the cluster could not be retrieved. This could occur if the operating system dependent clusterware was not functioning properly in one or more nodes in the cluster, or because there was no clusterware installed on the system.
solution: Check the state of the cluster by running 'lsnodes' binary from your ORACLE_HOME/bin and see if it prints the node list correctly.

message: Error submitting commands in the buffer
cause: This is an internal error.
solution: Contact Oracle Support Services.

message: All the submitted commands did not execute successfully
cause: Either a node failed in the middle of a manageability operation, or the communication between nodes was disrupted.
solution: Check the state of your cluster by running 'lsnodes' binary from your ORACLE_HOME/bin and see if it prints the node list correctly.

message: Problem in copying file to nodes
cause: Attempted file copy operation(s) from the local node to one or more nodes in the cluster and one or multiple of those copy file operations failed. Possible causes: 1) One or more file copy operations to nodes in the cluster failed. 2) The destination directory did not have write permission for the user on one or more of the nodes .the source file did not exist. 3) The 'rcp' command to one or more nodes failed on UNIX platforms.
solution: 1) Check that the source file exists. 2) Check that all nodes in the cluster are up. 3) Check that destination directory has write permission for the user. 4) On UNIX based platforms check that user can do 'rcp' to all the nodes.

message: Problem in removing file from nodes
cause: Attempted file remove operation(s) from the local node to one or more nodes in the cluster and one or multiple of those file remove operations failed. Possible causes: 1) One or more nodes failed during the operation. 2) The destination directory did not have write permission for the user on one or more of the nodes. 3) The source file did not exist. 4) The 'rcp' command to one or more nodes failed on UNIX platforms.
solution: Check the accompanying error messages for details.

message: Problem in moving file to nodes
cause: Attempted file move operation(s) from the local node to one or more nodes in the cluster and one or multiple of those move file operations failed. Possible causes: 1) One or more nodes failed during the operation. 2) The destination directory did not have write permission for the user on one or more of the nodes. 3) The source file did not exist. 4) The 'rcp' command to one or more nodes failed on UNIX platforms.
solution: Check the accompanying error messages for details.

message: Problem in creating directories on the nodes
cause: Attempted directory create operation(s) from the local node to one or more nodes in the cluster and one or multiple of those directory create operations failed. Possible causes: 1) One or more nodes failed during the operation. 2) The destination directory did not have write permission for the user on one or more of the nodes. 3) The 'rcp' command to one or more nodes failed on UNIX platforms.
solution: Check the accompanying error messages for details.

message: Failed to start the service on all nodes
cause: The service failed to start on one or more nodes of the cluster.
solution: Check if all the nodes in cluster are up and look in the clusterware alert log.

message: Failed to stop the service on all nodes
cause: The service failed to stop on one or more nodes of the cluster.
solution: Check if all the nodes in cluster are up and service is still up on failed nodes. Look in the clusterware alert log.

message: Failed to delete the service from all nodes
cause: The service failed to be deleted on one or more nodes of the cluster.
solution: Check if all the nodes in cluster are up and service is still registered. Look in the clusterware alert log.

message: Failed to create the service on all nodes
cause: The service failed to be created on one or more nodes of the cluster.
solution: Check if all the nodes in cluster are up. Look in the clusterware alert log.

message: Failed to retrieve value of the enviornment variable "{0}", {1}
cause: Attempted to retrieve value of an environment variable which was not defined.
solution: Define the environment variable.

message: Problem restarting GSD
cause: GSD (Global Services Daemon) could not be started on the local node. This could occur if the operating system dependent clusterware was not functioning properly or there is already a running GSD.
solution: Check the state of your clusterware by running 'lsnodes' from ORACLE_HOME/bin. It should list the nodes in the cluster. Try 'gsdctl stop' and then 'gsdctl start' again.

message: Error getting coordinator node
cause: This could occur if the operating system dependent clusterware was not functioning properly.
solution: Use 'gsdctl stop' on each node to stop the GSDs. Use 'gsdctl start' on each node in the cluster.

message: Error creating handle to GSD daemon on the node {0}
cause: Global Services Daemon was not running on the node.
solution: Use 'gsdctl stat' to check the status of the daemon. Use 'gsdctl start' to start it.

message: Exception while executing the operation on the remote node {0}
cause: Attempted to execute an operation on the remote node when the Global Services Daemon was not up on the remote node {0}.
solution: Start the Global Services Daemon on the remote node using 'gsdctl start'.

message: Problem in the clusterware
cause: The operating system dependent clusterware could not be contacted. This could occur because the operating system dependent clusterware was not functioning properly.
solution: Check the state of the operating system dependent clusterware.

message: Could not get node name for node {0} in {1}
cause: The operating system dependent clusterware could not be contacted. This could occur because the operating system dependent clusterware was not functioning properly.
solution: Check the state of the operating system dependent clusterware using 'lsnodes -n'.

message: Failed to create a file under the filepath {0} because the filepath is not executable or writable
cause: The directory of the specified filepath did not have execute or write permission. So the temporary file could not be created to test whether the filepath was shared among nodes.
solution: Make the directory of the specified filepath executable and writable.

message: Oracle Restart is not supported in version {0}. It is supported from version {1} onwards
cause: This is an internal error.
solution: Contact Oracle Support Services.

message: File "{0}" not found.
cause: The file was not found in the file system.
solution: Make sure that the file exists in the file system.

message: Failed to get host name for the local computer
cause: An error occurred while attempting to retrieve the TCP/IP host name
solution: Correct the problem indicated by the accompanying error messages.

message: Failed to get OCR locations
cause: An error occurred while attempting to retrieve the OCR locations, possibly due to missing or incorrrect OCR locations file, or incomplete OCR configuration, or due to missing or incorrect SRVM shared libraries.
solution: Verify that the Clusterware has been correctly installed and configured. Verify that the ocr.loc file is present and readable in the appropriate location for your platform.

message: Failed to get drive letters used on following nodes: "{0}"
cause: An error occurred while attempting to retrieve used drive letters on one or more nodes.
solution: Look at the accompanying messages and fix the error(s). The messages typically relate to a node not being reachable, or the remote execution service not running on the node, or some permissions issue when attempting to use the remote execution service on the remote node.

message: The given path "{0}" does not exist
cause: The specified path may not have been created or an incorrect path has been specified.
solution: Make sure that the given path exists by specifying a correct existing path.

message: The specified path "{0}" is not a directory
cause: The specified path may be a file, not a directory, or an incorrect path may have been specified.
solution: Make sure to specify a path that is a valid directory path.

message: No directory is available on the remote node "{0}" to copy the binary RemoteExecService.exe
cause: Either the path defined by value of registry key HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE/System/CurrentControlSet/Services/OracleRemExecService is not available on the remote node, or the c:/temp/ directory is not available or not accessible on the specified remote node.
solution: Make sure that the required path is available on the remote node.

message: The node list provided had only one entry or had multiple entries that were duplicates of a single nodename entry
cause: The list of nodes provided for the shared path check was either only one node, or the list included entries that were duplicates of the same single node.
solution: Please provide the correct nodelist for the cluster on which the check is being called, making sure that there are at least two distinct entries.

message: Failed to validate raw device "{0}" -- Details: {1}
cause: The raw device was not an existing device that could be opened and recognized by the OS as a "raw/character" device type.
solution: Make sure the supplied value identifies a valid raw device that can be opened as a "raw/character" device type.

message: Failed to validate raw device "{0}"
cause: The raw device was not an existing device that could be opened and recognized by the OS as a "raw/character" device type.
solution: Make sure the supplied value identifies a valid raw device that can be opened as a "raw/character" device type.

message: Failed to validate raw device "{0}" -- Details: {1}
cause: The device was not an existing device that could be opened and recognized by the OS as either "raw/character" or a "block" device type.
solution: Make sure the supplied value identifies a valid device that can be opened as a "raw/character" or "block" device type.

message: Failed to validate device "{0}"
cause: The device was not an existing device that could be opened and recognized by the OS as either "raw/character" or a "block" device type.
solution: Make sure the supplied value identifies a valid device that can be opened as a "raw/character" or "block" device type.

message: Failed to retrieve the value of environment variable "{0}" on following nodes: "{1}", [{2}]
cause: An error occurred while attempting to retrieve value of environment variable on one or more nodes due to the node not being reachable, or the remote execution service not running on the node, or some permissions issue when attempting to use the remote execution service on the remote node.
solution: Look at the accompanying messages and respond accordingly.

message: Failed to retrieve the Windows domain on following nodes: "{0}"
cause: An error occurred while attempting to retrieve the Windows domain on one or more nodes. The possible causes include:" - A node is not reachable. - Remote execution service is not running on the node. - Permissions problems prevented use of remote execution service on a node.
solution: Look at the accompanying messages and respond accordingly.

message: "{0}" is not a file
cause: The indicated object was expected to be a file, but it was not.
solution: Make sure that the indicated object is a file and not a directory.

message: {0} Exception occurred while determining validity of storage type.
cause: An error occurred while getting storage type of the given path. Null arguments might have been passed.
solution: Make sure that the native api is passing non null arguments.

message: invalid command or arguments
cause: This is an internal error.
solution: Contact Oracle Support Services.

message: Failed to set up Windows service OracleRemoteExecService on node '{0}'
cause: An error occurred while setting up OracleRemoteExecService on the specified nodes."
solution: Look at the accompanying messages and respond accordingly.

message: Storage is partially shared. Details: {0}
cause: A subset of the nodes provided shared the given filesystem path with the local node.
solution: Mount the NFS filesystem on the node(s) that do not share the filesystem path.

message: Failed to resolve the specified path "{0}" to its physical path on following nodes: "{1}", [{2}]
cause: An error occurred while attempting to resolve the path on one or more nodes due to the node not being reachable, the remote execution service not running on the node, or some permissions issue when attempting to use the remote execution service on the remote node.
solution: Look at the accompanying messages and respond accordingly.

message: Failed to get sub-keys of registry key {0}
cause: Could not find any sub-keys for the given registry key.
solution: Check manually via 'regedit' that the registry key exists and has sub keys under it. If so, retry. Otherwise, contact Oracle Support Services.

message: Failed to get list of active nodes from Clusterware
cause: Possible causes: 1) Not operating in cluster mode. 2) Failed to load SRVM libraries. 3) Failed to initialize clusterware context.
solution: Check for the health of clusterware using "lsnodes" utility to get the list of active nodes in the cluster. Also, check for the presence of srvm libraries in the load library path. If these two checks get cleared, please contact Oracle Support Services.

message: Failed to start GSD on local node
cause: GSD is already running on the local node, or GSD could not be started because of some other reason.
solution: Run "gsdctl stat" to check if a daemon is already running on the local node. If a daemon is not running on local node, please contact Oracle Support Services to check for the other reasons for failure.

message: Failed to stop GSD on local node
cause: GSD is not running on the local node, or GSD could not shut down gracefully.
solution: Run "gsdctl stat" to check if a GSD is running on the local node. If a GSD is running, please contact Oracle Support Services to check for other reasons for failure.

message: Failed to get status of GSD on local node
cause: Failure to get the list of active nodes from the cluster, or failure to query the list of live daemons from the clusterware.
solution: Run "lsnodes" to check the health of the clusterware. If the clusterware is working fine, check for the presence of SRVM libraries in the load library path. If the libraries are present, please contact Oracle Support Services for further assistance.

message: Failed to retrieve local host name
cause: An attempt to retrieve the local host name using Java network functions failed.
solution: Ensure that the 'localhost' entry exists in the hosts configuration file.

message: Error occured while reading input from Console
cause: An attempt to read input from console failed
solution: Use terminal windows like xterm or Windows console to run the command.

message: The following nodes do not share the filesystem path "{0}" with node {1}: {2}
cause: A subset of the nodes provided shared the given filesystem path with the local node.
solution: Mount the NFS filesystem on the node(s) that do not share the filesystem path.

message: Failed to retrieve IP address of host "{0}"
cause: An attempt to retrieve IP address for the host specified failed.
solution: Run 'nslookup' on the host name and make sure the name is resolved or add the host name to OS hosts file.

message: Host "{0}" is unreachable
cause: An attempt to reach the specified host via IP failed.
solution: Make sure that the host is up and there are no firewalls blocking connectivity between local node and remote host.

message: Windows registry key "{0}" not found on node "{1}"
cause: Could not find the specified Windows registry key on the identified node.
solution: Contact Oracle Support Services.

message: Unexpected command output on node {0}: "{1}"
cause: A remotely-executed command produced output when none was expected.
solution: Ensure that ssh or rsh is configured properly on the target node. If it is, contact Oracle Support Services for assistance.

message: The command "{0}" run on node "{1}" gave an unexpected output: "{2}"
cause: A remote-shell command produced an output when none was expected.
solution: Ensure that ssh or rsh is configured properly on the specified nodes. If it is, contact Oracle Support Services for assistance.

message: Failed to create directory "{0}" on node "{1}"
cause: The specified directory could not be created on the specified node.
solution: Ensure that the user is an administrator on the specified node, that the specified drive has default share configured on it, and that there is enough space in the specified location. Look at accompanying error messages and respond accordingly.

message: Failed to remove directory "{0}" on node "{1}"
cause: The specified directory could not be removed on the specified node.
solution: Ensure that the user is an administrator on the specified node, that the specified drive has default share configured on it. Look at accompanying error messages and respond accordingly.

message: Cannot retrive configuration for cluster database {0}
cause: The cluster database configuration could not be retrieved from the repository. This could occur either because the database was never registered, or because the repository itself had not been created.
solution: Check if the database has been configured by printing a list of all cluster databases using 'srvctl config'. If the repostitory has not been created, use 'srvconfig -init' to create it.

message: Error starting database instance {0} on node {1}
cause: The instance could not be started using the SQL*Plus startup command.
solution: Try starting the named instance manually using SQL*Plus to see why it failed and examine the database instance alert log.

message: Error stopping database instance {0} on node {1}
cause: The SQL*Plus shutdown command returned an error while stopping the instance.
solution: Try stopping the named instance manually using SQL*Plus to see why it failed and examine the database instance alert log.

message: Startup operation partially failed
cause: Some components of the cluster database could not be started.
solution: Check the accompanying error messages for details.

message: Shutdown operation partially failed
cause: Some components of the cluster database reported errors while being stopped.
solution: Check the accompanying error messages for details.

message: Failed to start up cluster database {0}
cause: The cluster database could not be started.
solution: Check the accompanying error messages for details.

message: Failed to shut down cluster database {0}
cause: The cluster database reported errors while being shut down.
solution: Check the accompanying error messages for details.

message: Failed to start all the listeners associated with all the instances of cluster database {0}
cause: Internal error.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: Failed to start listeners associated with instance {0} on node {1}
cause: Internal error.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: Failed to stop all the listeners associated with all the instances of cluster database {0}
cause: Either the listener name associated with an instance could not be determined, or 'lsnrctl stop' failed for a listener.
solution: Verify that listener.ora contains a SID_LIST entry for each instance of the named database, and that the 'lsnrctl stop' command succeeds for those listeners.

message: Failed to stop all the listeners associated with instance {0} on node {1}
cause: Either the listener name associated with an instance could not be determined, or 'lsnrctl stop' failed for a listener.
solution: Verify that listener.ora contains a SID_LIST entry for each instance of the named database, and that the 'lsnrctl stop' command succeeds for those listeners.

message: Failed to get all the listeners associated with instance {0} on node {1}
cause: The listener name associated with an instance could not be determined.
solution: Ensure that listener.ora contains a SID_LIST entry for the named instance.

message: Invalid environment variable {0} setting for cluster database {1}
cause: The argument to the -t option was not of the form <name>=<value> or it contained special characters.
solution: Ensure that the -t option has an argument of the form <name>=<value>. Enclose the argument to the -t flag in quotes.

message: {0}: undefined environment variable for cluster database {1}
cause: The named environment variable is not defined for the named cluster database
solution: Set a value for the variable with 'srvctl setenv'.

message: {0}: undefined environment variable for instance {1} of cluster database {2}
cause: The named environment variable is not defined for the given instance
solution: Set a value for the variable with 'srvctl setenv'.

message: {0}: undefined environment variable
cause: The named environment variable is not defined
solution: Set a value for the named environment variable with 'srvctl setenv'.

message: Database "{0}" cannot have more than "{1}" services
cause: Attempt to add a new service to database was rejected because database has already reached the maximum services limit.
solution: Retry after removing a service of this database via 'srvctl remove service' command, or contact Oracle Support Services.

message: Failed to retrieve configuration of cluster database {0}
cause: Attempt to retrieve configuration of cluster database failed. This failure is most likely due to user incorrectly using a tool, such as SRVCTL, that is of different version than that of database's configuration.
solution: If error is due to user using SRVCTL that is of different version than than of the database's, then run SRVCTL tool from the ORACLE_HOME reported in the error message. Otherwise, contact Oracle support services.

message: cluster database {0} does not exist
cause: The cluster database was never registered in the repository.
solution: Check if the database has been configured by printing a list of all cluster databases using 'srvctl config'.

message: cluster database {0} already exists
cause: An attempt was made to register a cluster database which already existed in the repository.
solution: Check if the database has already been configured by printing a list of all cluster databases using 'srvctl config'.

message: instance {0} does not exist
cause: The named instance was never registered in the repository.
solution: Use 'srvctl config instance' to check if the instance is registered in the repository.

message: adding of cluster database {0} configuration failed, {1}
cause: Internal error.
solution: Contact your customer support representative.

message: deleting of cluster database {0} configuration failed, {1}
cause: Internal error.
solution: Contact Oracle Support Services.

message: getting of cluster database {0} configuration failed, {1}
cause: Internal error.
solution: Contact Oracle Support Services.

message: adding of instance {0} on node {1} to cluster database {2} failed.
cause: Internal error.
solution: Contact Oracle Support Services.

message: deleting of instance {0} from cluster database {1} failed, {2}
cause: Internal error.
solution: Contact Oracle Support Services.

message: moving of instance {0} to node {1} of cluster database {2} failed.
cause: Internal error.
solution: Contact Oracle Support Services.

message: renaming of instance {0} to instance {1} of cluster database {2} failed, {3}
cause: Internal error.
solution: Contact Oracle Support Services.

message: error {0} while serializing configuration of cluster database {1}
cause: Internal error.
solution: Contact Oracle Support Services.

message: error {0} while deserializing configuration of cluster database {1}
cause: Internal error.
solution: Contact Oracle Support Services.

message: error {0} while serializing directory
cause: Internal error.
solution: Contact Oracle Support Services.

message: error {0} while deserializing directory
cause: Internal error.
solution: Contact Oracle Support Services.

message: reading of cluster database {0} configuration failed, {1}, {2}
cause: Internal error.
solution: Contact Oracle Support Services.

message: writing of cluster database {0} configuration failed, {1}, {2}
cause: Internal error.
solution: Contact Oracle Support Services.

message: reading of directory failed, {0}, {1}
cause: Internal error.
solution: Contact Oracle Support Services.

message: writing of directory failed, {0}, {1}
cause: Internal error.
solution: Contact Oracle Support Services.

message: reading of version information failed, {0}, {1}
cause: Internal error.
solution: Contact Oracle Support Services.

message: writing of version information failed, {0}, {1}
cause: Internal error.
solution: Contact Oracle Support Services.

message: Cluster registry {0} contains incompatible version, {1} != {2}
cause: Internal error.
solution: Contact Oracle Support Services.

message: file {0} does not exist
cause: The named file did not exist.
solution: Specify a file that exists.

message: file {0} does not have {1} permissions
cause: The named file did not have the specified permission.
solution: Try changing the permission on the file to the specified permission.

message: file {0} does not contain property {1}
cause: The file did not contain the specified property.
solution: Contact Oracle Support Services.

message: property {0} not set in file {1}
cause: The file did not contain the specified property.
solution: Contact Oracle Support Services.

message: failed to retrieve list of cluster databases
cause: Internal error.
solution: Contact Oracle Support Services.

message: Cluster registry {0} is invalid [HINT: initialize cluster registry by using "srvconfig" tool]
cause: The management repository was never initialized.
solution: Use 'srvconfig -init' to initialize the repository.

message: invalid option {0} specified
cause: The specified option was invalid.
solution: Check the command documentation or the inline help display for usage details.

message: missing <file> argument for {0} option
cause: The specified option was invalid for srvconfig.
solution: Check the command documentation or the inline help display for usage details.

message: file {0} creation in {1} directory failed
cause: Either the directory did not exist or it did not have the required permissions.
solution: Create the directory if it did not exist or change the permission of the directory.

message: file {0} does not contain an entry for dbname {1}
cause: Internal error.
solution: Contact Oracle Support Services.

message: file name {0} is not of <cluster database name>.conf form
cause: Internal error.
solution: Contact Oracle Support Services.

message: invalid range {0} specified in node_list = {1}
cause: Internal error.
solution: Contact Oracle Support Services.

message: invalid parameter {0} specified in inst_oracle_sid = {1}
cause: Internal error.
solution: Contact Oracle Support Services.

message: invalid extra arguments {0} specified to {1} option
cause: Provided invalid arguments to srvconfig.
solution: Check the command documentation or the inline help display for usage details.

message: invalid registry entry {0} found; should be of form {1}
cause: Internal error.
solution: Contact Oracle Support Services.

message: environment variable does not exist
cause: Attempted to retrieve non existing environment variable.
solution: Set the environment variable.

message: Database {0} of version {1} cannot be administered using current version of srvctl. Instead run srvctl from {2}
cause: An attempt was made to access configuration of database using srvctl that was of different version than that of the database.
solution: Perform the operation using srvctl from the ORACLE_HOME mentioned in the error message.

message: Failed to get OCR locations
cause: An error occurred while attempting to retrieve the OCR locations, possibly due to missing or incorrrect OCR locations file, or incomplete OCR configuration, or due to missing or incorrect SRVM shared libraries.
solution: Verify that the Clusterware has been correctly installed and configured. Verify that the ocr.loc file is present and readable in the appropriate location for your platform.

message: No option specified for "modify gns"
cause: No option was specified for the "modify gns" command.
solution: Specify at least one option.

message: The "-{0}" option requires the specification of the "-{1}" option.
cause: An option was specified which requires that another option to be specified at the same time.
solution: Specify the required option.

message: Invalid host name or address: "{0}".
cause: The host name or address specified for the address on which GNS is to listen was not valid.
solution: Specify a valid host name or IP address. If an IP address is used, it must be one of the following: 1. A valid IPv4 address (N.N.N.N); 2. A valid IPv6 address (N[:N]*).

message: The "-{0}" option may not be used with the "-{1}" option.
cause: The two options may not be used together.
solution: Run srvctl with each option specified separately.

message: No option was specified for the GNS "modify" command.
cause: An option was not specified for the modify command.
solution: Specify an option.

message: ASM not stopped: deprecated option '-i' is not allowed.
cause: An attempt to stop ASM using srvctl specified the '-i' option.
solution: Use the '-n' option to specify the node where ASM instance should be stopped.

message: The "-{0}" option requires the specification of either the "-{1}" or the "-{2}" option.
cause: An option was specified which requires that one of the other possible options to be specified at the same time.
solution: Specify the one of the other options.

message: Both "-{0}" and "-{1}" options may not be specified with the "-{2}" option.
cause: An invalid combination of options was specified.
solution: Specify only one of the other possible options.

message: No other option is allowed when the "-l" option is specified.
cause: If the "-l" option is specified, no other option may be given.
solution: Only specify the "-l" option.

message: Both "-g" and "-x" options are required to set server pool {0} for single instance database {1} on the cluster.
cause: Option "-x" is not specified in 'srvctl modify database' command for a single instance database on the cluster.
solution: Specify both -g and -x options in 'srvctl modify database' and retry.

message: The number of candidate servers {0} in server pool {1} should be one for single instance database {2}
cause: The server pool specified in 'srvctl modify database' command for a single instance database contains more than 1 candidate servers.
solution: Either modify the given server pool via 'srvctl modify srvpool' command to have only one candidate server specified via -x argument or specify another server pool that contains only one candidate server specified via -x argument.

message: Invalid command line syntax for a single instance database
cause: user specified invalid command line syntax.
solution: Look at the usage provided for this command and specify all mandatory options.

message: Invalid command line syntax
cause: The syntax of the command is incorrect.
solution: Look at the usage provided for this command and use the correct syntax.

message: Invalid command line option:
cause: Invalid command line option was specified.
solution: Check the value printed along with the exception and specify the correct value.

message: Invalid command line option value:
cause: Invalid command line option was specified.
solution: Check the value printed along with the exception and specify the correct value.

message: Repetition of command line option:
cause: The command line option printed along with the exception was repeated.
solution: Delete the repeated command line option and try the command again.

message: Failure in getting Cluster Database Configuration for:
cause: The specified database does not exist.
solution: Check the specified database name and try again.

message: Invalid node name: {0}
cause: Unable to get the hostname for the given node/machine name.
solution: Check the node name and try again.

message: Invalid instance name: {0}
cause: Unable to obtain the node name on which the instance name specified was running.
solution: Check the instance name specified and try again.

message: Invalid connect string:
cause: The connect string specified was not in the format username/password [as {SYSDBA|SYSOPER}]
solution: Check the connect string and try again.

message: Invalid name/value string: {0}
cause: The name value string should be of the form name = value
solution: check the input name/value pair and try again.

message: Invalid command specified on command line: {0}
cause: The <command> specified on the command line was not recognized.
solution: Valid commands are enable|disable|start|stop|relocate|status|add|remove|modify|getenv|setenv|unsetenv|config. Usage of srvctl is printed with this errori. Check the usage and specify a valid command.

message: Invalid object specified on command line: {0}
cause: The <object> specified on the command line was not recognized.
solution: Valid objects are database|instance|service|nodeapps|vip|network|asm|diskgroup|listener|srvpool|scan|scan_listener|oc4j|home|filesystem|gns|cvu. Srvctl usage is printed along with this exception. Check the usage printed with this error and use a valid object.

message: {0} object is not supported in Oracle Restart
cause: The <object> specified on the command line was not a valid object for the Oracle Restart mode.
solution: Valid objects for Oracle Restart mode are database|service|asm|diskgroup|listener|home|ons. Srvctl usage is printed along with this exception. Check the usage printed with this error and use a valid object.

message: {0} object is not supported in Oracle Clusterware
cause: The <object> specified on the command line was not a valid object for the Oracle Clusterware mode.
solution: Valid objects for Oracle Clusterware are database|instance|service|nodeapps|vip|network|asm|diskgroup|listener| srvpool|scan|scan_listener|oc4j|home|filesystem|gns|cvu. Srvctl usage is printed along with this exception. Check the usage printed with this error and use a valid object.

message: The -a option should be specified with -d <dbunique_name> for 'srvctl config database' command
cause: -a option was specified without the required -d option specifying for which database to retrieve configuration.
solution: To retrieve the full configuration of the database, specify both -d and -a option with the 'srvctl config database' command.

message: Database {0} has no services configured
cause: 'srvctl config database' request found no services configured for the database.
solution: Use 'srvctl add service' command to configure services for the database and then retry.

message: Service {0} does not exist for database {1}.
cause: The service being updated is not defined for the given database.
solution: If the service needs to be added don't use '-u' option in 'srvctl modify service' command. Option '-u' is for updating existing services.

message: No databases are configured
cause: No databases were configured.
solution: Use 'srvctl add database' command to configure databases.

message: Invalid name-value string: {0}
cause: The name=value string specified is not in valid format.
solution: The format for the string should be name=value. Check input and correct the error.

message: Error in enabling ASM instance on node {0}. {1}
cause: ASM could not be enabled.
solution: Make sure that the node name is correct and that ASM exists on the specified node and it is not already enabled on the node. The current state of the ASM can be found using 'srvctl status asm' command. To check if ASM is configured or not, use 'srvctl config asm' command.

message: Error in disabling ASM instance on node {0}. {1}
cause: ASM could not be disabled.
solution: Make sure that the node name is correct and that ASM exists on the specified node and it is not already disabled on the node. The current state of the ASM can be found using 'srvctl status asm' command. To check if ASM is configured or not, use 'srvctl config asm' command.

message: Invalid command line syntax, mandatory options are either {0} or {1}, but not both.
cause: The command requires exactly one set of mandatory command line options. But either some options in one set were missing or the options from both sets were specified.
solution: Check the command line options entered and make sure that all the mandatory options in one set are specified.

message: Error occured while checking dependent resources on network {0}. Network was not removed.
cause: An attempt made to check if any resources are dependent on the given network failed.
solution: Make sure that the network is up. Make sure that the user has sufficient permission to remove network. If force flag was not specified in the remove command then specify force flag and try the command again.

message: Scan name {0} cannot be the same as a cluster node name: {1}
cause: Scan name is same as a cluster node name.
solution: Choose a different scan name and issue the command.

message: Only one server pool should be provided for a single instance database on a cluster
cause: An attempt to create a single instance database failed because more than one server pool was specified.
solution: Provide only one server pool while creating the single instance database.

message: The size of server pool should be one for single instance database
cause: An attempt to create a single instance database failed because a server pool with more than one server was specified.
solution: Provide a server pool with only one server while creating a single instance database.

message: OC4J could not be created as it already exists
cause: A new OC4J instance could not be created, as there is an existing instance of OC4J.
solution: Only one instance of OC4J can exists at any given time.

message: OC4J creation failed
cause: A new OC4J instance could not be added because of OC4J exception.
solution: Resolve the OC4J exception and then try the OC4J addition again.

message: OC4J is not configured
cause: OC4J is not configured on the cluster.
solution: Check the exception printed with this message. If OC4J is not configured then OC4J instance can be created using 'srvctl add oc4j'. If there are other errors shown with this error then check the cause/action messages of underlying exception.

message: OC4J is still running. It must be stopped before removing.
cause: 'srvctl remove oc4j' was issued while OC4J instance was running.
solution: Stop the oc4j instance using 'srvctl stop oc4j' and then try removing.

message: OC4J could not be removed
cause: OC4J instance could not be removed because it does not exist.
solution: The current OC4J configuration can be checked using 'srvctl config oc4j' command. Make sure that OC4J instance is running on that port. If their are other underlying messages printed then check the cause/action for the underlying errors shown with this.

message: OC4J RMI port could not be modified
cause: OC4J RMI port could not be modified.
solution: Make sure that OC4J instance exists and port is not in use by using the command 'srvctl config oc4j' and try again.

message: OC4J could not be started
cause: The start of OC4J instance failed.
solution: Make sure that OC4J instance exists and is not already started.

message: OC4J failed to stop
cause: The OC4J instance could not be stopped.
solution: Make sure that OC4J instance exists and are not already stopped.

message: Missing mandatory option {0}
cause: The specified mandatory command option is missing.
solution: Use srvctl with the -h option to display option details for the command and make sure that all the mandatory options are specified.

message: OC4J could not be enabled
cause: OC4J instance could not be enabled.
solution: Make sure that node name is correct and that OC4J instance exists and is not already enabled. The current state of the OC4J instance can be found using 'srvctl status oc4j' command. To check if OC4J instance is configured or not use 'srvctl config oc4j' command.

message: OC4J could not be disabled
cause: OC4J instance could not be disabled.
solution: Make sure that Node name is correct and that OC4J instance exists and is not already disabled. The current state of the OC4J instance can be found using the srvtl status oc4j command. To check if OC4J instance is configured or not use 'srvctl config oc4j' command.

message: OC4J could not be relocated
cause: OC4J instance could not be relocated to given node.
solution: If the node name was passed in the command line make sure that the node name is valid. Also make sure that 0C4J instance exists on the cluster and is running.

message: Cannot update service {0} because {1} is not administrator-managed
cause: An attempt to update the service using "-u" option failed because this option can be used with administrator-managed databases only.
solution: Make sure that you provide correct options for 'srvctl add service' command.

message: Failed to create server pool {0}: {1}
cause: An attempt to create the specified server pool failed because of the reason provided by the accompanying error.
solution: Examine the accompanying error messages for details.

message: The '-a' and '-r' options cannot both be supplied with '-u'
cause: Command 'srvctl add service' with '-u' option failed because both options '-a' and '-r' were provided.
solution: Correct options and issue command again.

message: Option '-a' or '-r' should be supplied with '-u'
cause: Command 'srvctl add service' with option '-u' failed because both it requires options '-a' or '-r' to be provided.
solution: Correct options and issue command again.

message: Option '-g' cannot be used with option '-r','-a' or '-P'
cause: Incorrect usage of -g option.
solution: Correct options and issue command again.

message: There is no server pool associated with database {0}
cause: Command 'srvctl add service' failed because the given database doesn't have an associated server pool.
solution: Oracle internal error. Contact customer support.

message: Command line options '-i' and '-n' cannot be used at the same time
cause: Incorrect usage of -i and -n options.
solution: Correct options and issue command again.

message: Options '-e', '-i', or '-w' should be supplied with option '-c'
cause: Incorrect usage of -e, -i and -w options.
solution: Correct options and issue command again.

message: Option '-c' cannot be used to create services with administrator-managed database {0}
cause: Incorrect usage of -c option.
solution: Remove -c option and issue command again.

message: Invalid number {0} for command line option {1}
cause: Invalid value was specified for the command line option that requires a number in a certain range.
solution: Check the value printed and specify a number within the required range.

message: Options '-x' and '-y' cannot be used to create RAC One Node database {0}
cause: Incorrect usage of -x and -y options.
solution: Remove -x and -y options and issue command again.

message: OC4J is already disabled
cause: OC4J instance could not be disabled because it is already disabled.
solution: If this is the expected state then this is not an error. If it is not then enable OC4J instance by using the 'srvctl enable oc4j' command.

message: OC4J is already enabled
cause: OC4J instance could not be enabled because it is already enabled.
solution: If this is the expected state then this is not an error. If it is not then disable OC4J instance by using the 'srvctl disable oc4j' command.

message: Options '-g' and '-e' cannot be used together
cause: Options -g and -e were used incorrectly.
solution: Correct options and issue command again.

message: Options '-g' and '-i' cannot be used together
cause: Incorrect usage of -g and -i options.
solution: Correct options and issue command again.

message: Only one server pool can be specified with the -g option for a RAC One Node database
cause: Incorrect number of serverpools was supplied with the -g option.
solution: Specify one server pool with the -g option and issue command again.

message: Options '-x' and '-y' cannot be used to modify RAC One Node database
cause: Options -x and -y were used incorrectly.
solution: Remove -x and -y options and issue command again.

message: Options '-e' and '-w' cannot be used to modify a database that is not RAC One Node
cause: Options -e and -w were used incorrectly.
solution: Remove -e and -w options and issue command again.

message: Database type can only be 'RAC' or 'RACONENODE
cause: Incorrect database type was specified for 'srvctl convert database' command.
solution: Specify 'RAC' or 'RACONENODE' when running 'srvctl convert database' command.

message: Options '-n' and '-w' cannot both be used with options '-a' and '-r'
cause: Options -n, -w, -a and -r were used incorrectly.
solution: Correct options and issue command again.

message: Either option '-e' or '-g' must be supplied for adding RAC One Node database
cause: Options -e and -g were not specified when adding RAC One Node database.
solution: Use 'srvctl add database' command with either -e or -g option.

message: Specified cardinality {0} is not valid for policy-managed RAC One Node service {1}
cause: Given cardinality was not applicable to RAC One Node service.
solution: Use 'srvctl add service' command without the -c option or specify SINGLETON value for the -c option.

message: Online relocation timeout value {0} is not within the range of {1} and {2}
cause: Online relocation timeout value was not within the required range.
solution: Supply a value within the required range.

message: Supplied node {0} must be in the candidate list of the administrator-managed database {1}
cause: The supplied node name was not in the candidate list of the administrator-managed database.
solution: Supply a node in the candidate list of the database and rerun 'srvctl start database' command.

message: Supplied node {0} must be in the server pool of the policy-managed database {1}
cause: The supplied node name was not in the server pool of the policy-managed database.
solution: Supply a node from the server pool of the database and rerun 'srvctl start database' command.

message: Options '-g', '-r' and '-a' cannot be used to add services for RAC One Node database {0}
cause: Failed to add specified service because provided options cannot be used to add a service for RAC One Node database.
solution: Use 'srvctl add service' command without options -g, -r or -a.

message: Options '-g', '-r' and '-a' cannot be used to modify services for RAC One Node database {0}
cause: Failed to modify specified service because provided options cannot be used to modify a service for RAC One Node database.
solution: Use 'srvctl modify service' command without options -g, -r or -a.

message: 'srvctl add instance' command is not supported with RAC One Node databases
cause: The specified database does not support 'srvctl add instance' command.
solution: Convert the RAC One Node database to a RAC database by using the 'srvctl convert database' command and then rerun 'srvctl add instance' command.

message: 'srvctl remove instance' command is not supported with RAC One Node databases
cause: The one instance of the RAC One Node database cannot be removed by the 'srvctl remove instance' command.
solution: Run 'srvctl remove database' command.

message: 'srvctl start/stop/enable/disable/modify/status/setenv/getenv/unsetenv instance' commands are not supported with RAC One Node databases
cause: The supplied instance command is not supported with RAC One Node database.
solution: Perform srvctl operations on the 'database' noun instead of 'instance' with a RAC One Node database.

message: Option '-n' should not be supplied to convert policy-managed RAC One Node database to RAC database
cause: Failed to convert database because provided option cannot be used to convert policy-managed RAC One Node database.
solution: Use 'srvctl convert database' command without -n option.

message: Database {0} is not of RAC One Node database type
cause: The supplied database was not a RAC One Node database.
solution: Run 'srvctl convert database' command with database of type RAC One Node.

message: Supplied nodes {0} should contain node {1} where database {1} is already running on
cause: Supplied nodes did not include the node that the database was running on.
solution: Make sure given nodes include the node that the database is running on.

message: Option '-x' should be supplied when adding single instance database
cause: Option -x was not supplied when adding single instance database.
solution: Supply -x option and issue command again.

message: Option '-r' requires option '-a'
cause: Command 'srvctl relocate database' with option '-r' failed because it requires option '-a' to be provided.
solution: Correct options and issue command again.

message: Cannot start RAC One Node database when an online relocation request for the database is already active
cause: Unable to start the supplied RAC One Node database because it already has an active online relocation request.
solution: Specify another database to start.

message: Cannot stop RAC One Node database when an online relocation request for the database is already active
cause: Unable to stop the supplied RAC One Node database because it already has an active online relocation request.
solution: Either wait for the online relocation request to complete or specify another database to stop.

message: Option '-e' cannot be used with RAC One Node policy-managed database {0}
cause: The -e option was specified to modify the candidate server list for RAC One Node policy-managed database.
solution: Either use 'srvctl modify srvpool' to modify the candidate server list or specify -g with 'srvctl modify database' to modify the server pool.

message: 'srvctl remove instance' command is not supported with single instance databases
cause: The single instance database cannot be removed by the 'srvctl remove instance' command.
solution: Run 'srvctl remove database' command.

message: A 'srvctl add database' command specified the '-e', '-i' or '-w' option for a database that is not Oracle RAC One Node
cause: A 'srvctl add database' command was issued that included either the '-e', '-i' or '-w' option but did not include a '-c' option specifying that the database being added was Oracle RAC One Node.These options are permitted only for Oracle RAC One Node databases.
solution: Either remove the '-e', '-i' or '-w' option or specify '-c' option with type Oracle RAC One Node.

message: Option '-n' must be supplied when running 'srvctl relocate database' for administrator managed RAC One Node database
cause: Option -n was not specified when executing relocate on administrator managed RAC One Node database.
solution: Use 'srvctl relocate database' command with -n option.

message: Option '-i' cannot be used to modify instance name of a RAC database
cause: Option -i in "srvctl modify database" command can be used to modify the instance name of a single instance database or instance name prefix of a RAC One Node database.
solution: Try 'srvctl modify instance' command.

message: Instance name {0} is not valid
cause: The supplied instance name is not the correct format for RAC One Node database.
solution: Make sure that the instance name is of the format <instance_name_prefix>_1 or <instance_name_prefix>_2. Use 'crsctl modify resource' to correct the instance name.

message: Option '-i' should not specified to convert policy-managed RAC database to RAC One Node database
cause: Failed to convert database because the provided option can not be used to convert policy-managed RAC database to RAC One Node database.
solution: Use 'srvctl convert database' command without -i option.

message: Option '-n' should not be specified to convert a RAC database to RAC One Node database
cause: Failed to convert database because the provided option '-n' should not be supplied to convert RAC database to RAC One Node database.
solution: Use 'srvctl convert database' command without -n option.

message: Option '-i' should be specified to convert an administrator-managed RAC database to its equivalent RAC One Node database configuration
cause: Failed to convert database because the option '-i' was not specified to convert administrator-managed RAC database to its equivalent RAC One Node database configuration.
solution: Use 'srvctl convert database' command with -i option.

message: Option '-w' should not be specified to convert a RAC One Node database to its equivalent RAC database configuration
cause: Failed to convert database because option '-w' was specified to convert RAC One Node database to its equivalent RAC database configuration.
solution: Use 'srvctl convert database' command without -w option.

message: VIP does not exist on node(s) : {0}
cause: VIP was not configured on the nodes.
solution: Add VIP using 'srvctl add nodeapps' or 'srvctl add vip' and try this command again.

message: GSD does not exist on node(s): {0}
cause: GSD was not configured on the nodes
solution: Add GSD using 'srvctl add nodeapps' and try this command again.

message: VIP {0} does not exist.
cause: VIP with the specified name was not configured.
solution: Add VIP using 'srvctl add nodeapps' or 'srvctl add vip' and try this command again.

message: Node applications are still running on node:
cause: Node applications are still running on node when a remove was attempted.
solution: Stop the node applications before removing them or use force flag when attempting removal.

message: Some or all node applications are not removed successfully on node:
cause: Not all node applications were removed on the node.
solution: Make sure that all resources that depend on node applications are stopped before attempting to remove node applications. Also if force flag was not specified, reissue this command with the force flag specified.

message: Instance {0} is already a preferred instance for service {1}.
cause: Given instance is already a preferred instance for the service.
solution: Specify an instance other than the preferred instances of this service.

message: Instance {0} is already an available instance for service {1}.
cause: Given instance is already an available instance for the service.
solution: Specify an instance other than the available instances of this service.

message: Failed to remove service {0} because this is the last service of RAC One Node database {1}
cause: An attempt was made to remove the last service of a RAC One Node
solution: Add another service, for example by using 'srvctl add service' command, before removing the given service. Otherwise, if you are trying to deconfigure database, then remove the database directly, for example by using 'srvctl remove database' command.

message: ONS daemon does not exist on node(s): {0}
cause: ONS was not configured on the nodes.
solution: Add ONS using 'srvctl add nodeapps' command and try this command again.

message: eONS daemon does not exist on node(s): {0}
cause: eONS was not configured on the nodes.
solution: Add eONS using 'srvctl add nodeapps' command and try this command again.

message: Node applications run on default network only. The netmask given {0} doesn't match default networks netmask {1}
cause: The netmask given in the modify command doesn't match with default network's netmask.
solution: Modify the default network first using 'srvctl modify nodeapps -S <options>' and then try modifying the VIP.

message: Node applications run on default network only. The interface given {0} doesn't match default networks interface {1}
cause: The interface specified in the modify command doesn't match with default network's interface.
solution: Modify the default network's interface using 'srvctl modify nodeapps -S <options>' and then try modifying the VIP.

message: The new VIP address given is same as the current VIP address
cause: The VIP address given for modification is same as the current VIP. So there is nothing to modify.
solution: Check the VIP address you want to modify and specify the correct value.

message: The command line parameter host port list should be in the form <host>[:<port>][,<host>:[<port>]...]
cause: The command line parameter -t <host_port_list> was not in the format <host>[:<port>][,<host>:[<port>]...] with port being numeric.
solution: Check the input and correct any error and try the command again.

message: The network resource has been modified successfully. VIP and other resources that depend on it might not start up unless they are modified
cause: When underlying network resource has been modified the VIP should be updated to the new network resource. This is not a error and is just a status message.
solution: Use 'srvctl modify nodeapps -A <options>' to update the VIP to the new network.

message: All the node applications already exist. They were not recreated.
cause: 'srvctl add nodeapps' was attempted when all the node applications already existed.
solution: If you want to modify node applications you should use 'srvctl modify nodeapps' command.

message: VIP exists for node {0}, VIP name {1}
cause: The VIP being added already exists.
solution: Check the input and if VIP needs to be modified use 'srvctl modify VIP' command.

message: Invalid address string:
cause: VIP address being passed on the command line is not a valid address string.
solution: Address string should be of the format <name|ip>/<netmask>/[if1[|if2...]]. Check the usage and correct the address format.

message: Invalid interface specified on command line: {0}
cause: VIP address specification '-A <name|ip>/<netmask>[/if1[|if2|...]]' or the network address specification '-S <subnet>/<netmask>[/if1[|if2|...]]' on the command line contained interfaces names, none of which exist on current node.
solution: Check the interfaces listed in the address string and make sure that they are enabled and are up. Use network interface names on the command line if there is more than one interfaces that connect to the same network.

message: Warning:-{0} option has been deprecated and will be ignored.
cause: Deprecated option has been used in the command line. The option will be ignored.
solution: Check the documentation for the new syntax of the command.

message: {0} command has been deprecated and will be ignored.
cause: The command being executed has been deprecated and will not do any action.
solution: Check the documentation for the commands supported by srvctl.

message: {0} command is not supported for configuration using server pool.
cause: The given command failed because it isn't applicable to instances of policy managed-databases.
solution: Check the documentation on the commands that are applicable to policy-managed databases.

message: ASM listener was not found
cause: Check the reported message, ASM listener may not exist.
solution: Use "srvctl modify asm -l <lsnr_name>" to set the listener that ASM should register with.

message: Specified server pool {0} cannot be used to host single instance database {1}
cause: An attempt to create a single instance database failed because the specified server pool had no configured candidate server.
solution: Use 'srvctl modify srvpool' with -n option to configure a candidate server for the server pool. Make sure that the candidate server name specified with the -n option matches that of the -x option in 'srvctl add database' command.

message: Specified server pool {0} has more than one candidate server
cause: An attempt to create a single instance database failed because a server pool with more than one candidate server was specified.
solution: Provide a server pool with only one candidate server when creating a single instance database.

message: VIP does not exist on node {0}.
cause: VIP was not configured on that node on which modification was attempted.
solution: VIP must be added using 'srvctl add nodeapps' command, before it can be modified.

message: VIP {0} does not exist.
cause: An attempt was made to remove a VIP with the specified vipname. No such VIP was configured on the cluster.
solution: If this is the expected state then it is not an error. Check the status of VIPs using 'srvctl status vip' command. VIP must be added using 'srvctl add vip' command before it can be removed.

message: Target instance {0} already supports service {1}.
cause: Given database instance already provides the given service.
solution: Specify an instance that is not a preferred or available instance for this service.

message: ONS daemon does not exist.
cause: ONS daemon was not configured on this cluster.
solution: ONS daemon can be configured using the 'srvctl add nodeapps' command.

message: eONS daemon does not exist.
cause: eONS daemon was not configured on this cluster.
solution: eONS daemon can be configured using the 'srvctl add nodeapps' command.

message: eONS already uses {0} as listening port. Nothing to modify.
cause: The listening port specified in this command is already in use by eONS.
solution: Check the input and if the listening port needs to be changed then specify a different port.

message: VIP {0} is still running on node: {1}
cause: VIP to be removed is still running on a node.
solution: Stop the VIP before attempting to remove it or retry the command with force flag.

message: VIP {0} is not removed successfully:
cause: VIP remove action failed because VIP was running and force flag was not specified or an exception occurred during the removal.
solution: Make sure that any applications, like for example listener, that depend on VIP are down. Try using -f option to remove the VIP. If you use force option to remove VIP then any application that depends on this VIP will stop working. Look at the help message for the accompanying exception.

message: Network {0} is not removed successfully:
cause: Since there were no VIPs hosted on the network an attempt was made to remove the network and network removal failed.
solution: Make sure that all other applications that depend on default network are stopped. If force flag was not specified then specify force flag and try the command again.

message: The specified hostname or address {0} cannot be resolved.
cause: An invalid IP address or irresolvable hostname was specified.
solution: If IP address is specified then make sure that it is of legal length. If a host name is specified then make sure that the host name resolves to an IP address.

message: Netmask is missing in address string:
cause: NETMASK is missing in the VIP address that was passed in the command string.
solution: VIP address is of form <ip_or_name>/<netmask>[/<interface1>[|<interface2>...]]. Specify the netmask.

message: -n <node_name> option has been deprecated.
cause: -n <node_name> has been deprecated in this release.
solution: Try to remove the usage of -n <node_name> in the command.

message: Command line option {0} should be followed by a value.
cause: The value needs to be specified by the command line option.
solution: Look at the usage and of the command and specify an appropriate value.

message: Invalid command line options. Neither -A nor -n can be specified with -S.
cause: Invalid combination of options specified for add/modify node application command. -A is node-specific option and has to be used with -n option. -S option is a global option and it cannot be used with -A or -n option.
solution: Issue the command using either -A and -n together or -S without -A or -n.

message: -n <node_name> option has been deprecated and is ignored.
cause: -n <node_name> option has been deprecated and is ignored from this release. It has no effect on the command.
solution: Remove the usage of -n <node_name> from the command line.

message: Network resource {0},{1} already exists. Nothing to modify
cause: The subnet specified is already the default subnet.
solution: Check the input and if the subnet needs to be modified then specify a different subnet.

message: eONS already uses {0} as Multicast address. Nothing to modify.
cause: The Multicast address specified in this command is already in use by eONS.
solution: Check the input and if the Multicast address needs to be changed then specify a different address.

message: eONS already uses {0} as Multicast port. Nothing to modify.
cause: The Multicast port specified in this command is already in use by eONS.
solution: Check the input and if the Multicast port needs to be changed then specify a different port.

message: ONS already uses {0} as port for local connections. Nothing to modify.
cause: The modify node applications command failed because the ONS port for local connections is already used by ONS for local connections.
solution: Check the input and if the port used by ONS for local connections need to be modified specify a different address.

message: ONS already uses {0} as port for remote connections. Nothing to modify.
cause: The modify node applications command failed because the ONS port for remote connections is already used by ONS for remote connections.
solution: Check the input and if the port used by ONS for remote connections need to be modified specify a different address.

message: The list of remote host/port ONS pairs matches the current list : {0}. Nothing to modify.
cause: The modify node applications command failed because the remote host/port ONS pairs matches the current list.
solution: Check the input and if the remote host/port pairs need to be modified and specify a different host/port list.

message: Network resource does not exist on the cluster nodes.
cause: Network resource does not exist on the cluster nodes.
solution: Node applications can be added by using 'srvctl add nodeapps' command.

message: GSD is already disabled on node(s): {0}
cause: The disable node applications command failed because GSD was already disabled.
solution: If this is the expected state then this is not an error. If it is not then GSD can be enabled by 'srvctl enable nodeapps' command.

message: VIP is already disabled on node(s): {0}
cause: The disable node applications command failed because VIP was already disabled.
solution: If this is the expected state then this is not an error. If it is not then VIP can be enabled by 'srvctl enable nodeapps' command.

message: Network resource is already disabled.
cause: The disable node applications command failed because Network resource was already disabled.
solution: If this is the expected state then this is not an error. If it is not then Network resource can be enabled by 'srvctl enable nodeapps' command.

message: ONS is already disabled on node(s): {0}
cause: The disable node applications command failed because ONS was already disabled.
solution: If this is the expected state then this is not an error. If it is not then ONS can be enabled by 'srvctl enable nodeapps' command.

message: eONS is already disabled on node(s): {0}
cause: The disable node applications command failed because eONS was already disabled.
solution: If this is the expected state then this is not an error. If it is not then eONS can be enabled by 'srvctl enable nodeapps' command.

message: GSD is already enabled on node(s): {0}
cause: The enable node applications command failed because GSD is already enabled.
solution: If this is the expected state then this is not an error. If it is not then GSD can be disabled by 'srvctl disable nodeapps' command.

message: VIP is already enabled on node(s): {0}
cause: The enable node applications command failed because VIP is already enabled.
solution: If this is the expected state then this is not an error. If it is not then VIP can be disabled by 'srvctl disable nodeapps' command.

message: Network resource is already enabled.
cause: The enable node applications command failed because Network resource is already enabled.
solution: If this is the expected state then this is not an error. If it is not then Network resource can be disabled by 'srvctl disable nodeapps' command.

message: ONS is already enabled on node(s): {0}
cause: The enable node applications command failed because ONS is already enabled.
solution: If this is the expected state then this is not an error. If it is not then ONS can be disabled by 'srvctl disable nodeapps' command.

message: eONS is already enabled on node(s): {0}
cause: The enable node applications command failed because eONS is already enabled.
solution: If this is the expected state then this is not an error. If it is not then eONS can be disabled by 'srvctl disable nodeapps' command.

message: GSD is already started on node(s): {0}
cause: The start node applications command failed because GSD is already started.
solution: If this is the expected state then this is not an error. If it is not then GSD can be stopped by 'srvctl stop nodeapps' command.

message: VIP is already started on node(s): {0}
cause: The start node applications command failed because VIP is already started.
solution: If this is the expected state then this is not an error. If it is not then VIP can be stopped by 'srvctl stop nodeapps' command.

message: Network resource is already started on node(s): {0}
cause: The start node applications command failed because Network resource is already started.
solution: If this is the expected state then this is not an error. If it is not then Network resource can be stopped by 'srvctl stop nodeapps' command. Note that once started network resource cannot be stopped.

message: ONS is already started on node(s): {0}
cause: The start node applications command failed because ONS is already started.
solution: If this is the expected state then this is not an error. If it is not then ONS can be stopped by 'srvctl stop nodeapps' command.

message: eONS is already started on node(s): {0}
cause: The start node applications command failed because eONS is already started.
