solution: If this is the expected state then this is not an error. If it is not then eONS can be stopped by 'srvctl stop nodeapps' command.

message: GSD is already stopped on node(s): {0}
cause: The stop node applications command failed because GSD is already stopped.
solution: If this is the expected state then this is not an error. If it is not then GSD can be started by 'srvctl start nodeapps' command.

message: VIP is already stopped on node(s): {0}
cause: The stop node applications command failed because VIP is already stopped.
solution: If this is the expected state then this is not an error. If it is not then VIP can be started by 'srvctl start nodeapps' command.

message: ONS is already stopped on node(s): {0}
cause: The stop node applications command failed because ONS is already stopped.
solution: If this is the expected state then this is not an error. If it is not then ONS can be started by 'srvctl start nodeapps' command.

message: eONS is already stopped on node(s): {0}
cause: The stop node applications command failed because eONS is already stopped.
solution: If this is the expected state then this is not an error. If it is not then eONS can be started by 'srvctl start nodeapps' command.

message: VIP is running on the node {0} and cannot be modified.
cause: Modify nodeapps command failed because VIP being modified is running on a node.
solution: Stop the node application by issuing 'srvctl stop nodeapps' and retry the modify again.

message: -n <node_name> should be specified with -A <name|ip>/netmask[/if1[|if2]] for modifying VIP.
cause: If -n <node_name> option is specified then -A option should also be specified for modifying VIP.
solution: If you want to modify the VIP then use specifiy both the -n and -A options. Otherwise remove the -n <node_name> option and try command again.

message: -A <name|ip>/netmask[/if1[|if2] should be specified with -n <node_name> for modifying VIP.
cause: -A <options> has been specified for the modify nodeapps command without specifying which node VIP needs to be modified.
solution: Specify the node whose VIP needs to be modified by using -n option.

message: Warning: the -n option is obsolescent; 'srvctl remove vip' is preferred for removing per-node VIP resource
cause: A 'srvctl remove nodeapps' command was issued with the -n option specifying one or more nodes. Support for this option will be removed in a future release, at which time you must use the preferred command 'srvctl remove vip -i <vip_list>'.
solution: The command is processed normally and attempts to remove VIP resources for the specified node(s). This message is displayed only to alert you to a future change. Use 'srvctl remove nodeapps' to remove all node applications from the last node of the cluster.

message: Network resource does not exist.
cause: Network resource to be started/stopped/modified/enabled/disabled does not exist.
solution: Network resource can be created using 'srvctl add nodeapps' command.

message: VIP does not exist.
cause: VIP to be started/stopped/modified/enabled/disabled does not exist.
solution: VIP can be created using 'srvctl add nodeapps' command.

message: Network resource is already stopped.
cause: The stop node applications command failed because network resource was already stopped.
solution: If this is the expected state then this is not an error. If it is not then network resource can be started by 'srvctl start nodeapps' command.

message: ONS already exists
cause: A new instance of ONS daemon could not be created, as there is an existing instance of ONS.
solution: If this is the expected state then it is not an error. Use 'srvctl config ons' command to look at ONS daemon attributes and 'srvctl modify ons' command to modify ONS attributes.

message: eONS already exists
cause: A new instance of eONS daemon could not be created, as there is an existing instance of eONS.
solution: If this is the expected state then it is not an error. Use 'srvctl config eons' command to see if eONS daemon is configured. Use 'srvctl modify eons' command to modify eONS attributes.

message: ONS does not exist
cause: ONS daemon was not configured on this instance of Oracle Restart.
solution: Add ONS daemon using the 'srvctl add ons' command and try this command again.

message: eONS does not exist
cause: eONS daemon was not configured on this instance of Oracle Restart.
solution: Add eONS daemon using the command 'srvctl add eons' command and try this command again.

message: ONS does not exist.
cause: ONS daemon was not configured on this instance of Oracle Restart.
solution: ONS daemon can be configured using the 'srvctl add ons' command.

message: eONS daemon does not exist.
cause: eONS daemon was not configured on this instance of Oracle Restart.
solution: eONS daemon can be configured using the 'srvctl add eons' command.

message: ONS is already started.
cause: The 'srvctl start ons' command failed because the ONS daemon was already started.
solution: If this is the expected state then this is not an error. If it is not then ONS can be stopped by 'srvctl stop ons' command.

message: eONS is already started.
cause: The 'srvctl start eons' command failed because the eONS daemon was already started.
solution: If this is the expected state then this is not an error. If it is not then eONS can be stopped by 'srvctl stop eons' command.

message: ONS daemon is already stopped.
cause: The 'srvctl stop ons' command failed because the ONS daemon was already stopped.
solution: If this is the expected state then this is not an error. If it is not then ONS can be started by 'srvctl start ons' command.

message: eONS daemon is already stopped.
cause: The 'srvctl stop eons' command failed because the eONS daemon was already stopped.
solution: If this is the expected state then this is not an error. If it is not then eONS can be started by 'srvctl start eons' command.

message: ONS is already enabled.
cause: The 'srvctl enable ons' command failed because the ONS was already enabled.
solution: If this is the expected state then this is not an error. If it is not then ONS can be disabled by 'srvctl disable ons' command.

message: eONS is already enabled.
cause: The 'srvctl enable eons' command failed because the eONS was already enabled.
solution: If this is the expected state then this is not an error. If it is not then eONS can be disabled by 'srvctl disable eons' command.

message: ONS is already disabled.
cause: The 'srvctl disable ons' command failed because the ONS was already disabled.
solution: If this is the expected state then this is not an error. If it is not then ONS can be enabled by 'srvctl enable ons' command.

message: eONS is already disabled.
cause: The 'srvctl disable eons' command failed because the eONS was already disabled.
solution: If this is the expected state then this is not an error. If it is not then eONS can be enabled by 'srvctl enable eons' command.

message: ONS daemon could not be removed because it is still running.
cause: 'srvctl remove ons' command failed because ONS daemon was still running.
solution: Stop the ons daemon by using 'srvctl stop ons' command and then attempt to remove it. You can also use the force option to remove a running ons daemon.

message: eONS daemon could not be removed because it is still running.
cause: 'srvctl remove eons' command failed because eONS daemon was still running.
solution: Stop the ons daemon by using 'srvctl stop eons' command and then attempt to remove it. You can also use the force option to remove a running eons daemon.

message: None of the ONS daemon parameters were modified.
cause: The configuration of the ONS daemon has remained the same after the 'srvctl modify ons' command.
solution: Make sure that at least one of the optional modification parameters was specified on the command line. The current values of parameters of the ONS daemon can be found by using 'srvctl config ons' command. Specify at least one value different then current value while issuing the 'srvctl modify ons' command.

message: None of the eONS daemon parameters were modified.
cause: The configuration of the eONS daemon has remained the same after the 'srvctl modify eons' command.
solution: Make sure that at least one of the optional modification parameters was specified on the command line. The current values of parameters of the eONS daemon can be found by using 'srvctl config eons' command. Specify at least one value different then current value while issuing the 'srvctl modify eons' command.

message: enable of GNS failed.
cause: Enabling the GNS server failed.
solution: Examine the accompanying exception for details.

message: modify of GNS failed.
cause: Modification the GNS server failed.
solution: Examine the accompanying exception for details.

message: disable of GNS failed.
cause: Disabling the GNS server failed.
solution: Examine the accompanying exception for details.

message: relocation of GNS failed.
cause: Relocation of the GNS server failed.
solution: Examine the accompanying exception for details.

message: removal of GNS failed.
cause: Removal of the GNS server failed.
solution: Examine the accompanying exception for details.

message: addition of GNS failed.
cause: The addition of the GNS server failed.
solution: Examine the accompanying exception for details.

message: GNS is already running
cause: The GNS server is already running.
solution: Remove the GNS server first before trying to add it.

message: GNS VIP does not exist. Specify the {0} option to create one.
cause: The attempt to add GNS failed because the VIP associated with it does not exist.
solution: Create the VIP.

message: The '-x <node>' option cannot be used to create RAC database {0}
cause: The '-x' option was supplied to create a single-instance database, along with '-c RAC' requesting a RAC database.
solution: Specify '-c SINGLE' with '-x <node>'

message: The CVU resource is not configured
cause: The CVU resource was not configured on the cluster or an unexpected error occurred while querying Clusterware for the CVU resource.
solution: If the CVU resource was not configured then a new resource can be created using 'srvctl add cvu' command. If the resource was configured, look at any accompanying error messages.

message: CVU is already disabled
cause: CVU resource could not be disabled because it is already disabled.
solution: If this is the expected state then this is not an error.

message: CVU is already enabled
cause: CVU resource could not be enabled because it is already enabled.
solution: If this is the expected state then this is not an error.

message: CVU resource must be stopped before removing
cause: 'srvctl remove cvu' was issued while CVU instance was running.
solution: Stop the CVU resource using 'srvctl stop cvu' and then try removing.

message: Unable to convert RAC One Node database because it has an active online relocation request
cause: Failed to convert RAC One Node database to RAC database because there was an active online relocation request for the database.
solution: Wait for the online relocation request to complete and then run 'srvctl convert database'.

message: Unable to convert RAC One Node database because it has a failed online relocation request
cause: Failed to convert RAC One Node database to RAC database because there was a failed online relocation request for the database.
solution: Use 'srvctl status database' command to show the target node of the failed online relocation request process. Either run 'srvctl relocate database' with -a option or with -n option with the correct target node. Then run 'srvctl convert database'.

message: Option '-n' cannot be used to start RAC database {0}
cause: The -n option was specified to start RAC database, but -n is only applicable to RAC One Node databases.
solution: Either use 'srvctl start instance' to start RAC database instance on the given node or use 'srvctl start database' without -n option to start the RAC database.

message: Only one instance can be listed in -i <inst_name_list> when -n option is specified
cause: More than one instance was specified for -i option when both -i and -n options were used.
solution: Supply one instance name for -i option when using both -i and -n option.

message: Server pool {0} already exists
cause: Command 'srvctl add serverpool' failed because the given server pool already exists.
solution: Make sure that the name of server pool is correct and a server pool with the given name doesn't exist.

message: Invalid instance name(s): {0}
cause: Some of the supplied instance names do not exist in the database configuration.
solution: Please supply valid instance names and retry.

message: Failed to remove database {0}:
cause: Failed to remove the database.
solution: Examine the accompanying message(s) for details of the error, and respond accordingly.

message: No such environment variable setting: {0}
cause: The environment variable(s) does not exist for the specified resource.
solution: Supply a valid environment variable.

message: Volume device: {0}
cause: Volume device label
solution: None

message: Mountpoint path: {0}
cause: Mountpoint path label
solution: None

message: User: {0}
cause: User label
solution: None

message: Administrator-managed database {1} can not support policy-managed service {0}.
cause: The specified database does not support policy-managed services.
solution: Provide a database which supports policy-managed services.

message: Policy-managed database {1} can not support administrator-managed service {0}.
cause: The specified database does not support administrator-managed services.
solution: Provide a database which supports administrator-managed services.

message: -P option cannot be used with policy-managed service {0}.
cause: The -P option was specified for a policy-managed service.
solution: Use the -m option to specify failover processing for a policy-managed service.

message: '-g' or '-r' option should be provided
cause: one of specified options should be provided.
solution: make sure that one of specified options is incuded into the command line.

message: Service {0} already exists in database {1}
cause: The service being added already exists.
solution: If the service needs to be modified use 'srvctl modify service' command.

message: Failed to check if service {0} exists: {1}
cause: Failed to get the servcie data.
solution: Make sure that Oracle Clusterware is active.

message: Database {0} cannot be started since it has no configured instances.
cause: The specified database is an administrator-managed database and it cannot be started because no instances were configured.
solution: Use srvctl add instance command to configure the instance and then retry.

message: Database {0} cannot be stopped since it has no configured instances.
cause: The specified database is an administrator-managed database and it could not be stopped because no instances were configured.
solution: Use srvctl add instance command to configure the instance and then retry.

message: -i option or -n option is required for starting an instance on the administrator-managed database {0}.
cause: The specified database is an administrator-managed database and the srvctl start instance command requires the instance name or nodename to be specified.
solution: Use srvctl start instance command with either the -i or -n option to start the instance.

message: -i option or -n option is required for stopping an instance of database {0}
cause: Neither the instance name nor the nodename was provided during 'srvctl stop instance' command invocation.
solution: Use 'srvctl stop instance' command with either the -i or -n option to specify which instance to stop.

message: Invalid value {0} for command line option {1}
cause: Invalid value was specified for the command line option.
solution: Check the value printed and specify the correct value.

message: Invalid GNS logging level: "{0}"
cause: The level of logging specified was not a positive integer.
solution: Specify a positive integer.

message: Unable to add database because the resource for diskgroup {0} could not be found. {1}
cause: The resource for the specified disk group could not be found. Either the diskgroup name was misspelled or the diskgroup has not been mounted.
solution: Correct the diskgroup spelling or use sqlplus to create the diskgroup.

message: Unable to modify database because the resource for diskgroup {0} could not be found. {1}
cause: The resource for the specified disk group could not be found. Either the diskgroup name was misspelled or the diskgroup has not been mounted.
solution: Correct the diskgroup spelling or use sqlplus to create the diskgroup.

message: Server pool {0} is internally managed as part of administrator-managed database configuration and therefore cannot be modified directly via srvpool object.
cause: An attempt was made to alter configuration of an internally managed server pool that is hosting an administrator-managed configuration.
solution: Do not modify this server pool via srvpool object directly. Instead use srvctl add/remove instance or srvctl modify database/service to alter this server pool's configuration.

message: -i option or -n option is required for checking the status of an instance of database {0}
cause: Neither the instance name nor the nodename was provided during 'srvctl status instance' command invocation.
solution: Use 'srvctl status instance' command with either the -i or -n option to check the status of the instance.

message: Database {0} has no instance on node {1}
cause: Instance was not configured on the specified node.
solution: Both 'srvctl add instance' or 'srvctl modify instance' command can also be used to change inst-node mapping in administrator-managed db's. For policy-managed database, use either 'srvctl start instance' command with -n option to start the instance on the specified node or use 'srvctl modify instance' command to configure an instance for that node.

message: -n option cannot be specified in conjunction with -z option
cause: -n and -z options were both provided during 'srvctl modify instance' command invocation.
solution: Use 'srvctl modify instance' command with either the -n or -z option to modify the node instance mapping of the database instance.

message: -z option cannot be used with administrator-managed database {0}
cause: The -z option was specified in an attempt to remove node to instance mapping of administrator-managed database.
solution: Use 'srvctl remove instance' command to remove node instance mapping of administrator-managed database.

message: Option '-c' cannot be used with administrator-managed service {0}
cause: The -c option was specified for administrator-managed service.
solution: Reissue the command without the -c option.

message: Node {0} does not belong to server pool {1} which defines nodes for service {2}
cause: Node doesn't belong to the server pool which defines nodes which can be used to run the specified service.
solution: Supply a node which belongs to specified server pool.

message: Options '-i' and '-t' cannot be used with policy-managed service {0}
cause: The -i and -t options were specified to relocate a policy-managed service.
solution: Use options -c and -n to relocate a service.

message: Options '-c' and '-n' cannot be used with administrator-managed service {0}
cause: The -c and -n options were specified to relocate an administrator-managed service.
solution: Use options -i and -t to relocate a service.

message: Database {0} could not be removed because it was running
cause: The 'srvctl remove database' command failed because the database was running.
solution: Stop the database by using 'srvctl stop database' command and then attempt to remove it. You can also use the force option to remove the running database.

message: Option '-i' cannot be used to enable/disable services for policy-managed database {0}
cause: Policy-managed database services can only be enabled or disabled by node, not by instance.
solution: Use option -n <node> to specify nodes on which to enable or disable services for this policy-managed database.

message: Options '-i', '-r', '-n' and '-a' cannot be used to modify policy-managed service {0}
cause: Options -i, -r, -n and -a can be used to modify administrator-managed service only.
solution: Make sure that the service you are going to modify is an administrator-managed service.

message: Option '-a' requires options '-n' and '-i' to be provided
cause: Option -a can not be used without options -n and -i.
solution: Make sure that options -n, -i and -a are provided according to 'srvctl modify service' syntax.

message: Option '-i' requires one of the options '-t', '-r' or '-n' to be set
cause: Option -i can not be used without additional options.
solution: Make sure that required option is provided according to 'srvctl modify service' syntax.

message: Option '-i' is not provided
cause: Options -t,-r, and -n requires option -i to be set.
solution: Make sure that required option is provided according to 'srvctl modify service' syntax.

message: Instance {0} cannot be removed because it is the only preferred instance for service(s) {1} for database {2}
cause: An attempt was made to remove the instance which is the only preferred instance for specified services.
solution: Make sure that specified services have more than one preferred instance or modify services to not have the instance as a preferred instance.

message: Instance {0} does not support service {1}.
cause: The given database instance is not defined as a preferred or available instance for the given service.
solution: Specify an instance that is defined as preferred or available instance for the given service.

message: The candidate server {0} of server pool {1} is different from the server {2} specified with the '-x' option
cause: Specified server must be the candidate server of the specified server pool.
solution: Make sure that the server specified with '-x' option is the same as the candidate server of the given server pool.

message: The server pool(s) {0} specified with the '-g' cannot be used to add an administrator-managed database
cause: A request to add an administrator-managed database specified the -g option.
solution: Use 'srvctl add database' without the '-g' option to add an administrator-managed database.

message: Option '-g' cannot have more than one specified server pool when converting an administrator-managed database to a policy-managed database
cause: An attempt was made to convert an administrator-managed database to a policy-managed database by specifying more than one server pool.
solution: Make sure to specify only one server pool with the '-g' option when converting an administrator-managed database to a policy-managed database.

message: The server pool(s) {0} specified with the '-g' option are subpools of Generic and therefore cannot be used to modify the server pool value of a policy-managed database
cause: The supplied server pools are meant for managing administrator-managed databases because they are subpools of Generic.
solution: Make sure that none of the supplied server pools are meant for managing administrator-managed database. Only supply server pools meant for managing policy-managed databases to the -g option of 'srvctl modify database' command. Use 'srvctl config srvpool' command to list the qualified server pools meant for managing policy managed databases.

message: -i option and/or -n option is required for starting an instance on the policy-managed database {0}.
cause: The specified database is a policy-managed database and the 'srvctl start instance' command requires the instance name and/or nodename to be specified.
solution: Use 'srvctl start instance' command with either the -i or -n option or both -i and -n options to start the instance.

message: Both -i and -n options are specified for starting an instance on the administrator-managed database {0}.
cause: The specified database is an administrator-managed database and the 'srvctl start instance' command requires either the instance name or nodename to be specified but not both.
solution: Use 'srvctl start instance' command with either the -i or -n option to start the instance.

message: Can not start the instance {0} on the specified node {1} because the node is assigned to another user configured instance {2}
cause: The database specified on 'srvctl start instance' is policy managed and has another instance already configured on the nodename specified with the -n option.
solution: Either reformulate the 'srvctl start instance' command so that there is no conflict with configured instances' nodes, or use 'srvctl modify instance' to change configured instances' nodes.

message: Server pool {0} is internally managed as part of administrator-managed database configuration and therefore cannot be queried directly via srvpool object.
cause: An attempt was made to query configuration of an internally managed server pool that is hosting an administrator-managed configuration.
solution: Do not query this server pool via srvpool object directly. Instead use srvctl config/status database/service command to query servers that are part of this pool's configuration.

message: Server pool {0} is internally managed as part of administrator-managed database configuration and therefore cannot be removed directly via srvpool object.
cause: An attempt was made to remove configuration of an internally managed server pool that is hosting an administrator-managed configuration.
solution: Do not remove this server pool via srvpool object directly. Instead use srvctl remove service/database command to remove this server pool and any service/database hosted by the server pool.

message: The actions setenv, getenv, and unsetenv are not suppported for Single Client Access Name listener {0}
cause: Failed to use srvctl setenv, getenv, and unsetenv listener command for specified Single Client Access Name Listener. The environment variables for Single Client Access Name Listener cannot be changed.
solution: Do not set, get, and unset environment variables for Single Client Access Name Listener.

message: Options '-u', '-r', '-a', '-g' and '-c' cannot be used to add service {0} for single instance database {1}
cause: Failed to add specified service because provided options can not be used to add a service for single instance database.
solution: use 'srvctl add service' command without options -u, -r, -a, -g or -c.

message: Options '-r', '-f', '-n', '-i', '-t', '-a', '-c' and '-x' cannot be used to modify service {0} for single instance database {1}
cause: Failed to modify specified service because provided options can not be used to modify a service for single instance database.
solution: Use 'srvctl modify service' command without options -r, -f, -n, -i, -t, -a, -c or -x.

message: Service {0} is defined for single instance database {1} and therefore cannot be relocated
cause: Failed to relocate specified service because provided options can not be used to relocate a service for single instance database.
solution: Make sure that you issue 'srvctl relocate service' command for the service which is not defined for a single instance database.

message: Invalid GNS parameter: "{0}"
cause: An invalid parameter value was specified.
solution: A parameter value must have the following format: <name>:<value>. The name may not contain a colon (":"). The value may not contain a comma (",").

message: EONS has been deprecated and ONS should be used to set and modify the local port for Enterprise Manager.
cause: The command being executed has been deprecated and will not do any action.
solution: Use online help 'srvctl -h' or check the documentation for the commands supported by srvctl.

message: 'srvctl relocate service' command is not supported on RAC One Node database service {0}
cause: An attempt was made to relocate a RAC One Node database service using 'srvctl relocate service' command.
solution: Use 'srvctl relocate database' command to relocate the RAC One Node database and its services to the target server.

message: TAF policy 'PRECONNECT' cannot be used to add a service for single instance database {0}
cause: Failed to add specified service because provided TAF specification can not be used with a single instance database.
solution: Use 'srvctl add service' command without 'PRECONNECT' TAF policy.

message: Option '-g' cannot be used with administrator-managed service {0}
cause: An attempt to change the server pool of service was rejected because the -g option cannot be used with administrator-managed service.
solution: Change the preferred and available instances of the service via 'srvctl modify service' command to manage placement of administrator-managed service.

message: Upgrade from version {0} to version {1} using 'srvctl upgrade model' command of version {2} is not supported
cause: A 'srvctl upgrade model' command was issued for a version change that is other than an increase in patch set level.
solution: Check that the versions provided are correct.

message: Option '-i' cannot be used to enable or disable service(s) {0} for single instance database {1}
cause: Failed to enable/disable specified service because its database is a single instance database.
solution: Make sure that you issue 'srvctl enable/disable service' command without option -i.

message: The '-o <oracle_home>' option value "{0}" corresponds to a pathname that does not exist or is not a directory
cause: The '-o <oracle_home>' option value did not resolve to an existing directory pathname.
solution: Ensure that the '-o <oracle_home>' option value correponds to an existing directory pathname.

message: The '-s <state_file>' option value "{0}" is a directory
cause: The '-s <state_file>' option value resolved to an existing directory pathname instead of a file pathname.
solution: Ensure that the '-s <state_file>' option value correponds to file.

message: The '-s <state_file>' option value "{0}" is a file under a non-writable directory
cause: The '-s <state_file>' option value resolved to a non-writable pathname.
solution: Ensure that the state file parent directory has write permissions.

message: The '-s <state_file>' option value "{0}" already exists
cause: The '-s <state_file>' option value resolved to an existing file pathname.
solution: Ensure that the '-s <state_file>' option value corresponds to a non-existing file pathname.

message: Cannot determine the canonical path to the state file "{0}"
cause: The '-s <state_file>' option value specified a pathname for which the canonical path cannot be retrieved.
solution: Provide the absolute pathname for '-s <state_file>' option value.

message: The '-s <state_file>' option value "{0}" does not exist or cannot be read
cause: The '-s <state_file>' option value mapped to a non-existing or non-readable file pathname.
solution: Ensure that the '-s <state_file>' option value corresponds to an existing readable file pathname.

message: Failed to add service {0} with PRECONNECT TAF policy because PRECONNECT TAF policy requires at least one available instance
cause: Attempt to add a service with PRECONNECT TAF policy was rejected because no available instance was specified.
solution: Specify at least one available instance using -a option of 'srvctl add service' command if the service TAF policy is to be PRECONNECT.

message: Failed to relocate as relocation is not supported in Oracle Restart mode
cause: Attempt to relocate failed as relocation is unsupported in Oracle Restart.
solution: Ensure you are in a cluster environment to relocate managed entities.

message: Failed to convert as convert action is not supported in Oracle Restart Mode
cause: Attempt to convert failed as convert action is unsupported in Oracle Restart.
solution: Ensure you are in a cluster environment to convert managed entities.

message: An attempt to modify the OC4J port failed because OC4J is running. Use -f to force stop and restart of OC4J.
cause: A request to modify the port number of OC4J was rejected because such modification requires OC4J to be stopped and restarted.
solution: Use '-f' option to force restart of OC4J.

message: Invalid command line options for listener. '-a' can not be specified with '-l'.
cause: Invalid combination of options specified for listener command.
solution: Issue the command using either '-l <listener_name>' or '-a'.

message: Single Client Access Name must start with a letter unless it is an IP address
cause: A SCAN was supplied which did not begin with a letter, however SCAN names must begin with a letter.
solution: Supply a SCAN name that begins with a letter.

message: Invalid upgrade phase ''{0}'' for upgrade model command
cause: An invalid value was specified for upgrade phase.
solution: Upgrade phase must be either 'first' or 'last'.

message: Invalid network server type ''{0}''
cause: An invalid value was specified for network server type.
solution: Network server type must be 'static' or 'dhcp' or 'mixed'.

message: Invalid port number {0}
cause: A supplied port number was not in the valid, non-privileged range 1024-65535.
solution: Specify a port number that is bigger than 1023.

message: Could not retrieve static nodelist. Verification cannot proceed
cause: Error running lsnodes/olsnodes.
solution: Ensure that the executable exists and that it is executable by your OS userid.

message: Could not retrieve local nodename
cause: Unable to determine local host name using Java network functions.
solution: Ensure that hostname is defined correctly using the 'hostname' command.

message: Unable to check the existence of Oracle Home "{0}"
cause: Could not verify the existence of the Oracle Home specified.
solution: Ensure that the Oracle Home location exists and is writeable by your user ID.

message: "{0}" is not writeable
cause: The path specified is not writeable.
solution: Ensure that write access exists for the specified path.

message: The Remote Shell "{0}" requested by the client does not exist
cause: Could not locate remote shell requested by the user.
solution: Ensure that the remote shell exists on all the nodes participating in the operation.

message: The Remote shell "{0}" requested by the client is not an executable file
cause: The remote shell requested by the user is not a file.
solution: Ensure that the remote shell exists on all the nodes participating in the operation and that it is a file with execute permissions.

message: The Remote Copy command "{0}" requested by the client does not exist
cause: Cannot locate remote copy command requested by the user.
solution: Ensure that the remote copy command exists on all the nodes participating in the operation.

message: The Secure Shell "{0}" requested by the client does not exist
cause: Could not locate the secure shell executable specified.
solution: Ensure that the executable file specified exists.

message: The Secure Copy command "{0}" requested by the client does not exist
cause: Could not locate the secure copy executable specified.
solution: Ensure that the executable file specified exists.

message: Unable to execute the Secure Shell "{0}" requested by the client
cause: Could not execute the secure shell specified.
solution: Ensure that the secure shell specified allows execute access for the current user ID.

message: Unable to execute the Secure Copy command "{0}" requested by the client
cause: Could not execute the secure copy specified.
solution: Ensure that the secure copy specified allows execute access for the current user ID.

message: The Remote Copy command "{0}" requested by the client is not an executable file
cause: The remote copy command requested by the user was not an executable file.
solution: Ensure that the remote copy command exists on all the nodes participating in the operation and that it is a file with execute permissions.

message: Unable to find oifcfg executable file in directory "{0}"
cause: An attempt to locate oifcfg executable file in specified directory failed.
solution: This is an internal error. Contact Oracle Support Services.

message: User "{0}" does not have sufficient authorization to run this command
cause: An attempt to run the CVU command failed because the user does not have sufficient authority to run it.
solution: The commands can only be run as root user(uid=0). Make sure that you run these commands as appropriate user.

message: User "{0}" does not have sufficient authorization to run this command
cause: An attempt to run the CVU command failed because the user does not have sufficient authority to run it.
solution: The command can be run only by the Oracle installation owner. Make sure that you run these commands as appropriate user.

message: The device file "{0}" does not exist on node "{1}"
cause: The expected device file could not be found.
solution: To enable asynchronous input-output operations using the asynchronous device driver, create the device file.

message: The device file "{0}" does not exist on nodes:
cause: The expected device file could not be found.
solution: To enable asynchronous input-output operations using the asynchronous device driver, create the device file.

message: The file "{0}" is not a device file on nodes:
cause: The file was not a device file.
solution: Ensure that the correct path and filename specified for the device file.

message: The file "{0}" is not a device file on node "{1}"
cause: The file was not a device file.
solution: Ensure that the correct path and filename are specified for the device file.

message: Failed to retrieve details of the device file "{0}" on nodes:
cause: An attempt to retrieve the attributes of a device file failed.
solution: Ensure that the file exists on the system and user has correct permissions to retrieve the details of specified device file.

message: Failed to retrieve details of the device file "{0}" on node "{1}"
cause: An attempt to retrieve the attributes of a device file failed.
solution: Ensure that the file exists on the system and user has correct permissions to retrieve the details of specified device file.

message: The minor number of device file "{0}" is incorrect on the nodes:
cause: The minor number of a device file was found incorrect as per the requirement.
solution: The third least significant bit (the 0x4 bit hexadecimal) of the minor number must be set.

message: The minor number of device file "{0}" is incorrect on the node "{1}"
cause: The minor number of a device file was found incorrect as per the requirement.
solution: The third least significant bit (the 0x4 bit hexadecimal) of the minor number must be set.

message: Failed to retrieve the ID for device file "{0}" on the node "{1}"
cause: Device file ID could not be retrieved on the node.
solution: Ensure that the device file exists at the specified path and is set to correct device ID.

message: Failed to retrieve minor number value for the device file "{0}" on the node "{1}"
cause: The device file ID does not contain the correct minor number.
solution: Ensure the value of the minor number of the device file is correct.

message: Length of value of environment variable "{0}" exceeds the maximum recommended length of "{1}" on the nodes:
cause: Length of the value of environment variable exceeds the recommended length.
solution: Ensure that the value of the environment variable does not exceed the standard operating system specified limit.

message: Length of value of environment variable "{0}" exceeds the maximum recommended length of "{1}" on the node "{2}"
cause: Length of the value of environment variable exceeds the recommended length.
solution: Ensure that the value of the environment variable does not exceed the standard operating system specified limit. Restart the installer after changing the setting for environment variable.

message: Environment variable name "{0}" is set on nodes:
cause: The environment variable was set on the nodes indicated.
solution: Ensure that the environment variable is not set to any value.

message: Environment variable name "{0}" is set on node "{1}"
cause: The environment variable was set on the node indicated.
solution: Ensure that the environment variable is not set to any value. Restart the installer after changing the setting for environment variable.

message: Environment variable name "{0}" is not set on nodes:
cause: Environment variable value could not be determined.
solution: Ensure that the environment variable is set and access permissions for the Oracle user allow access to read the environment variables.

message: Environment variable name "{0}" is not set on node "{1}"
cause: Environment variable value could not be determined.
solution: Ensure that the environment variable is set and access permissions for the Oracle user allow access to read the environment variables. Restart the installer after changing the setting for environment variable.

message: Environment variable check for variable "{0}" cannot be performed on nodes:
cause: Environment Variable value could not be determined.
solution: Ensure that the environment variable is set in either system or user environment and access permissions for the Oracle user allow access to read the environment variables.

message: Can not read environment variable "{0}" from node "{1}"
cause: Environment variable value could not be determined.
solution: Check user equivalence and whether the user has administrative privileges on the node.

message: Failed to retrieve value of environment variable "{0}"
cause: Environment variable value could not be determined.
solution: Check user equivalence and whether the user has administrative privileges on the node.

message: Environment variable name "{0}" is invalid for this operating system.
cause: Environment variable name does not meet operating system standards.
solution: Ensure that the environment variable name is as per the operating system standards. Restart the installer after changing the setting for environment variable.

message: Environment variable name not specified.
cause: Environment variable name was not specified.
solution: Ensure that a valid environment variable name is specified.

message: Adding the Oracle binary location to the PATH environment variable will exceed the OS length limit of [ "{0}" ], The maximum allowed length for PATH environment variable is ["{1}"] on the nodes:
cause: The environment variable PATH needs to be updated to include the value "%ORACLE_HOME%/bin;". However, doing so will cause PATH to exceed the maximum allowable length that this operating system allows.
solution: Ensure that the length of your current PATH environment variable is less than that of specified maximum allowed length, so that adding of "%ORACLE_HOME%/bin;" does not exceed the operating system's environment variable length limit.

message: Adding the Oracle binary location to the PATH environment variable will exceed the OS length limit of [ "{0}" ], The maximum allowed length for PATH environment variable is ["{1}"] on the node "{2}"
cause: The installer needs to update the PATH environment variable to include the value "%ORACLE_HOME%/bin;". However, doing so will cause PATH to exceed the maximum allowable length that this operating system allows.
solution: Ensure that the length of your current PATH environment variable is less than that of specified maximum allowed length, so that adding of "%ORACLE_HOME%/bin;" does not exceed the system's environment variable length limit. Restart the installer after changing the setting for environment variable.

message: Check: Space available on "{0}"
cause: Could not determine mount point for location specified.
solution: Ensure that the location specified is available.

message: User equivalence check failed for user "{0}"
cause: User equivalence for the specified user did not exist amoung all the nodes participating in the operation.
solution: Verify user equivalence on all the nodes participating in the operation, see "Enabling SSH User Equivalency on Cluster Member Nodes" documentation.

message: User equivalence unavailable on all the specified nodes
cause: User equivalence doesn't exist between the local node and the remote node(s).
solution: Ensure that user equivalence exists on all the nodes specified.

message: Inconsistent group IDs found for group "{0}"
cause: The group ID for the specified group is not the same across all the nodes.
solution: Make sure that the group has the same group ID across all the nodes.

message: Inventory configuration file "{0}" does not exist
cause: Cannot locate the inventory configuration file specified.
solution: Ensure that the correct inventory location was supplied and that the inventory file is there.

message: CRS is not installed on any of the nodes
cause: Could not identify a CRS installation on any node.
solution: Ensure that CRS is installed on all the nodes participating in the operation.

message: CRS is not installed on nodes:
cause: An attempt to identify Oracle Clusterware installation failed on specified nodes.
solution: Ensure that Oracle Clusterware is installed on all the nodes participating in the operation.

message: CSS is probably working with a non-clustered, local-only configuration on all the nodes
cause: Oracle CSS was found to be configured to run in a local-only (non-clustered) environment on all the nodes.
solution: Ensure that cluster setup is correct and reconfigure Cluster Synchronization Services (CSS) as necessary on the nodes that are supposed to be executing in a clustered environment. See Oracle Cluster Synchronization Services documentation for further information.

message: CSS is probably working with a non-clustered, local-only configuration on nodes:
cause: Oracle CSS was found to be configured to run in a local-only (non-clustered) environment on the nodes specified.
solution: Ensure that cluster setup is correct and reconfigure CSS as necessary on the nodes that are supposed to be executing in a clustered environment, see documentation regarding usage of the 'localconfig' script.

message: Unable to obtain OCR integrity details from any of the nodes
cause: OCR was not found to be in a healthy state on any of the nodes.
solution: Verify the state of OCR on each of the nodes using 'ocrcheck'.

message: Unable to obtain OCR integrity details from nodes:
cause: OCR was not found to be in a healthy state on some of the nodes.
solution: Verify the state of OCR on each of the nodes identified using 'ocrcheck'.

message: OCR ID is inconsistent among the nodes
cause: Multiple OCR ID's found across the cluster nodes specified.
solution: Verify Oracle Clusterware configuration and setup with 'ocrcheck' on each node specified. See 'ocrcheck' documentation for further information.

message: Version of OCR found "{0}", expected version of OCR for this release is "{1}"
cause: An incorrect version of OCR was found running on all the nodes.
solution: Verify version of OCR running on all the nodes using 'ocrcheck'.

message: OCR version is inconsistent amongst the nodes
cause: Found different version of OCR running on the cluster nodes.
solution: Ensure that the correct version of OCR is running on all the nodes using 'ocrcheck'.

message: Total space in OCR device is inconsistent amongst the nodes
cause: Found possible different devices in use across the nodes.
solution: Verify that the same OCR devices are used across the cluster nodes using 'ocrcheck'.

message: OCR integrity is invalid
cause: Cluster registry integrity check failed.
solution: Verify state of cluster registry using ocrcheck on the nodes participating in the verification operation.

message: OCR integrity results are inconsistent amongst the nodes
cause: Cluster registry integrity check failed on some of the nodes.
solution: Verify state of cluster registry using ocrcheck on the nodes participating in the verification operation.

message: Unable to retrieve storage information
cause: Internal error encountered while trying to retrieve storage information.
solution: If problem persists report issue to Oracle support and provide trace files generated when the cluvfy command is executed. Trace files should be located under <CRSHOME>/cv/log.

message: The number of addresses does not match the number of node
cause: Cannot determine IP address for every node.
solution: Verify each node in the cluster has a valid IP address.

message: Network interface information cannot be obtained from any of the node
cause: Could not find any network interface on any node in the cluster.
solution: Verify network interface(s) operational status on the cluster nodes.

message: Node reachability check failed from node "{0}"
cause: Network link to target node could not be verified using PING.
solution: Verify network link to target node using the PING utility.

message: Make sure IP address "{0}" is up and is a valid IP address on node "{1}"
cause: The network interface, IP address and subnet identified as "<network interface> : <IP address> [<subnet>]" is not available or is not functioning correctly.
solution: Please verify that the network interface identified is functioning as intended.

message: Node connectivity check failed
cause: Encountered errors attempting to verify node connectivity using the "OS ping" utility.
solution: Ensure that the IP addresses that failed can be reached using the OS ping utility and resolve any issues found with those IP addresses/interfaces.

message: Node connectivity failed for interface "{0}"
cause: Unable to verify connectivity to the interface indicated using the "OS ping" utility.
solution: Verify that the interface indicated is available.

message: Unable to reach any of the nodes
cause: Unable to reach any of the nodes using the OS ping command.
solution: Ensure that the nodes specified are accessible.

message: Node "{0}" is not reachable
cause: Unable to reach the node specified using the OS ping command.
solution: Ensure that the node specified is accessible.

message: User equivalence not found for node "{0}"
cause: Cannot access node specified using user equivalence.
solution: Ensure that user equivalence is setup between the local node and the node specified.

message: Could not find a suitable set of interfaces for VIPs
cause: Could not find a set of network interface adapters suitable for Virtual IP communication in the cluster .
solution: Ensure that the network interface adapters are installed and configured correctly on each node in the cluster and that each interface can communicate with a network gateway.

message: Could not find a suitable set of interfaces for the private interconnect
cause: Could not find a set of network interface adapters suitable for Private communication in the cluster.
solution: Ensure that the network interface adapters are installed and configured correctly on each node in the cluster according to RFC 1918, or that the interfaces are not accessible from the public network.

message: Source node "{0}" is not reachable from local node
cause: Unable to reach the source node specified using the OS ping command.
solution: Ensure that the source node specified is accessible.

message: User equivalence not found for source node "{0}"
cause: Cannot access source node specified using user equivalence.
solution: Ensure that user equivalence is setup between the local node and the source node specified.

message: Cannot identify Oracle Restart installation
cause: Cannot determine location of Oracle Restart installation.
solution: Ensure that the Oracle Restart environment is setup correctly.

message: Unable to obtain OLR integrity details from the local node
cause: Could not verify the state of OLR on the local node.
solution: Check the status of OLR on the local node using the command 'ocrcheck -local'.

message: Unable to obtain Oracle Restart integrity details from the local node
cause: Encountered an error when trying to run 'crsctl check has', or OHASD was found to be offline.
solution: Check the status of Oracle Restart using the 'crsctl check has' command on the local node.

message: Inconsistent user IDs found for user "{0}"
cause: The user ID for the specified user is not the same across all the nodes.
solution: Make sure that the user has the same user ID across all the nodes.

message: Failed to retrieve storage type for "{0}"
cause: The storage location specified may be non-existent or invalid or the user running the check may not have permissions to access the specified storage.
solution: Specify a valid existing location, and ensure that the user running the check has valid read permissions to this location.

message: Global failure for all nodes during execution of space check command
cause: CVU's attempt to execute the space check command on all nodes had a total failure.
solution: Make sure that the location specified is a valid location and available on all nodes.

message: Unable to obtain OLR location
cause: Could not verify the state of OLR.
solution: Check the status of OLR using the command 'ocrcheck -config -local'.

message: Multiple users "{0}" with UID "{1}" exist on "{2}".
cause: More than one user is found to have the same user ID as specified in the message.
solution: Ensure that no two users share the same UID.

message: Media Sensing of TCP/IP is enabled on the nodes:
cause: Media Sensing setting for TCP/IP is enabled.
solution: To disable Media Sensing for TCP/IP, add the REG_DWORD registry entry by name 'DisableDHCPMediaSense' and value 1 to the 'HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE/System/CurrentControlSet/Services/Tcpip/Parameters' subkey. It is recommended to backup the Windows Registry before proceeding with any changes, Restart your system to make your changes effective after changing the registry.

message: Media Sensing status check for TCP/IP cannot be performed on nodes:
cause: Media Sensing status could not be determined.
solution: Ensure that the access permissions for the Oracle user allow access to the Windows Registry and Registry has the REG_WORD entry named 'DisableDHCPMediaSense' with value 1 under 'HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE/System/CurrentControlSet/Services/Tcpip/Parameters' sub key on the node. It is recommended to backup the Windows Registry before proceeding with any changes, Restart your system to make your changes effective after changing the registry.

message: Error reading Registry sub key 'HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE/System/CurrentControlSet/Services/Tcpip/Parameters' from Windows Registry
cause: Windows Registry sub key 'HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE/System/CurrentControlSet/Services/Tcpip/Parameters' could not be read.
solution: Ensure that the access permissions for the Oracle user allow access to the Windows Registry.

message: Error reading Registry sub key 'HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE/Cluster/Parameters' from Windows Registry
cause: Windows Registry sub key 'HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE/Cluster/Parameters' could not be read.
solution: Ensure that the access permissions for the Oracle user allow access to the Windows Registry.

message: Error reading Registry value 'DisableDHCPMediaSense' for Windows Media Sensing
cause: Could not read Windows Registry value 'DisableDHCPMediaSense' under 'HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE/System/CurrentControlSet/Services/Tcpip/Parameters' sub key.
solution: Ensure that the access permissions for the Oracle user allow access to the Windows Registry and the Registry value 'DisableDHCPMediaSense' under 'HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE/System/CurrentControlSet/Services/Tcpip/Parameters' sub key is present on the node.

message: Error reading Registry value 'DisableClusSvcMediaSense' for Windows Media Sensing
cause: Could not read Windows Registry value 'DisableClusSvcMediaSense' under 'HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE/Cluster/Parameters' sub key.
solution: Ensure that the access permissions for the Oracle user allow access to the Windows Registry and the Registry value 'DisableClusSvcMediaSense' under 'HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE/Cluster/Parameters' sub key is present on the node.

message: Found different access permissions for the above storage location across the nodes specified
cause: The access permissions for the path specified (i.e. read, write, execute) are different, or could not be determined, across the nodes specified.
solution: Ensure that the access permissions allow access for the Oracle user on all the nodes specified.

message: The access permissions for the above storage location do not allow the user access across the nodes specified
cause: The access permissions for the path specified (i.e. read, write, execute) do not allow the user access.
solution: Ensure that the access permissions allow access for the Oracle user on all the nodes specified.

message: Size of the OCR location "{0}" does not meet the requirement. [Expected="{1}" ; Found="{2}"]
cause: Size of the ocr device does not meet the requirement
solution: Increase the size of the ocr device

message: Verification of the hosts config file failed
cause: The '/etc/hosts' file(s) contain incorrect, or incomplete, network host information.
solution: Review the contents of the node's '/etc/hosts' file and ensure that each entry contains a valid IP address and a canonical host name for the specified IP address.

message: Encountered error while trying to check hosts file
cause: Could not verify the contents of the '/etc/hosts' file.
solution: Review the node's 'hosts' file and ensure that it exists, has necessary permissions and each entry contains at least an IP address and a host name for the IP address specified.

message: The specified OCR location "{0}" is not a partition
cause: The location specified should be a disk partition rather than the disk itself.
solution: Specify a disk partition as the OCR storage.

message: The specified Voting Disk location "{0}" is not a partition
cause: The location specified should be a disk partition rather than the disk itself.
solution: Specify a disk partition as the Voting Disk storage.

message: Encountered issues with the following OCR Device/Files
cause: 'ocrcheck' returned failure, or warning, messages with the Device(s)/File(s) listed.
solution: Run 'ocrcheck' and resolve issues reported.

message: CRS integrity check passed, but encountered some warnings
cause: Some warnings were encountered while verifying CRS integrity.
solution: Review warnings and make modifications as necessary.

message: The effective group id "{0}" differs from the primary group id "{1}" of user "{2}"
cause: The user is currently logged into a group that is not user's primary group.
solution: Invoke the application after logging in to the primary group (using command 'newgrp <primary group>').

message: There is no primary group on this Operating System
cause: An attempt was made to check users primary group on an Operating System where there are no primary groups.
solution: This is an internal error; contact Oracle Support.

message: User "{0}" is part of group "{1}". Check failed
cause: The user who was executing this check was found to be part of root group.
solution: Use the 'id' command to check if the user is part of root group. Remove the user from root group using the 'usermod' command and try again.

message: Checking that user "{0}" is not part of "{1}" group could not be performed on node "{2}"
cause: A node specific error occurred while checking if user is not part of root group.
solution: Check that the node is accessible and user equivalence exists between the node on which command was executed and the node on which the check failed.

message: Proper soft limit for resource "{0}" not found on node "{1}" [Expected = "{2}" ; Found = "{3}"]
cause: Soft limit for the resource does not meet the requirement on the specified node.
solution: Modify the resource limits to meet the requirement.

message: Proper hard limit for resource "{0}" not found on node "{1}" [Expected = "{2}" ; Found = "{3}"]
cause: Hard limit for the resource does not meet the requirement on the specified node.
solution: Modify the resource limits to meet the requirement.

message: Resource soft limit check for "{0}" failed on node "{1}"
cause: Soft limit of the resource could not be determined.
solution: Ensure that the resource limit configuration is accessible.

message: Resource hard limit check for "{0}" failed on node "{1}"
cause: Hard limit of the resource could not be determined.
solution: Ensure that the resource limit configuration is accessible.

message: Persistent configuration check for cluster nodes failed
cause: The nodes IP address configuration was not found to be persistent.
solution: Make the nodes IP address configuration persistent using the 'crsctl pin css' command, see Oracle documentation 'Pinning Cluster Nodes for Oracle Database Release' for further information."

message: Check for existence of config file "{0}" could not be performed on node "{1}".
cause: Could not verify existence of configuration file specified.
solution: Verify access to node indicated and that the config file exists.

message: Host-guid of node "{0}" is not unique
cause: The system guid value is not unique across all the cluster nodes.
solution: Ensure that the guid value is unique across all cluster nodes using 'ocrcheck'.

message: OCFS is not configured in runlevel 3,4 and 5 on the node
cause: Runlevel was not configured with levels 3,4 and 5 all being on.
solution: Check OCFS configuration and ensure the run levels indicated are on.

message: Unable to retrieve {0} resource name from node {1}.
cause: Could not identify node application resource name specified on the node specified.
solution: Ensure that the node application resource name specified is available for the node specified.

message: Node application "{0}" does not exist on node "{1}"
cause: Could not identify resource specified on the node specified.
solution: Ensure that the resource specified is available for the node specified.

message: Failed to check existence of node application "{0}" on node "{1}"
cause: Could not verify existence of the nodeapp identified on the node specified .
solution: Ensure that the resource specified is available on the node specified, see 'srvctl add nodeapps' for further information.

message: Failed to check existence of VIP node application on nodes "{0}"
cause: An attempt to verify existence of the VIP on the nodes specified failed.
solution: Look at the accompanying messages for details on the cause of failure.

message: Failed to check existence of NETWORK node application on nodes "{0}"
cause: An attempt to verify existence of the NETWORK node application on the nodes specified failed.
solution: Look at the accompanying messages for details on the cause of failure.

message: Failed to check existence of GSD node application on nodes "{0}"
cause: An attempt to verify existence of the GSD node application on the nodes specified failed.
solution: Look at the accompanying messages for details on the cause of failure.

message: Failed to check existence of ONS node application on nodes "{0}"
cause: An attempt to verify existence of the ONS node application on the nodes specified failed.
solution: Look at the accompanying messages for details on the cause of failure.

message: Failed to check existence of node applications on nodes "{0}"
cause: An attempt to verify existence of node applications on the nodes specified failed.
solution: Look at the accompanying messages for details on the cause of failure.

message: An error occurred while parsing the output of the command "{0}" for node application resource "{1}". The output is: "{2}"
cause: An error occurred while parsing output of the command listed for the resource listed.
solution: This is an internal error. Contact Oracle Support Services.

message: Node applications do not exist on any node of the cluster
cause: Node applications were not configured on the cluster nodes.
solution: Node applications are created when root scripts are run. They can be also be created using the command 'srvctl add nodeapps'.

message: User equivalence not found for reference node "{0}"
cause: Cannot access reference node using user equivalence.
solution: Ensure that user equivalence is configured between the local node and the node specified. See Enabling SSH User Equivalency on Cluster Member Nodes documentation for further information.

message: Name resolution setup check for "{0}" (IP address: {1}) failed
cause: Inconsistent IP address definitions found for the SCAN name identified using DNS and configured name resolution mechanism(s).
solution: Look up the SCAN name with nslookup, and make sure the returned IP addresses are consistent with those defined in NIS and /etc/hosts as configured in /etc/nsswitch.conf by reconfiguring the latter. Check the Name Service Cache Daemon (/usr/sbin/nscd) by clearing its cache and restarting it.

message: Found inconsistent 'hosts' entry in /etc/nsswitch.conf on node {0}
cause: The 'hosts' specifications in the /etc/nsswitch.conf file is different the node specified.
solution: Ensure that the 'hosts' entries define the same lookup order in the /etc/nsswitch.conf file across all cluster nodes.

message: Found configuration issue with the 'hosts' entry in the /etc/nsswitch.conf file
cause: The 'hosts' specifications in the /etc/nsswitch.conf file should specify 'dns' before 'nis' to ensure proper IP address to name mapping.
solution: Ensure that the 'hosts' entries across the cluster nodes define 'dns' lookup before 'nis' lookup.

message: Found inconsistent name resolution entries for SCAN name "{0}"
cause: The nslookup utility and the configured name resolution mechanism(s), as defined in /etc/nsswitch.conf, returned inconsistent IP address information for the SCAN name identified.
solution: Check the Name Service Cache Daemon (/usr/sbin/nscd), the Domain Name Server (nslookup) and the /etc/hosts file to make sure the IP address for the SCAN names are registered correctly.

message: 'lsnodes' could not be executed on the node
cause: Error running 'lsnodes'.
solution: Ensure that the executable exists and that it is executable by your OS userid.

message: 'lsnodes' execution failed on the node
cause: Error running 'lsnodes'.
solution: Ensure that the executable <CRSHOME>/bin/lsnodes exists and that it is executable by your OS userid.

message: Multiple partitions found. Cluster is fragmented.
cause: An attempt to verify that the list of nodes that constitute the cluster is same on all nodes failed because different lists of cluster nodes were obtained on different nodes.
solution: Make sure that all nodes specified in the command belong to the same cluster. Make sure that all nodes share the same voting disk.

message: Location "{0}" not accessible on node(s) to be added.
cause: Location does not exist, or cannot be created, on node(s) to be added.
solution: Ensure location either exists or can be created on the node(s) to be added.

message: Path location check failed for: "{0}"
cause: Cannot write to path, or parent of path, specified.
solution: Verify access to entire path specified across cluster nodes(s).

message: Device location check failed for: "{0}"
cause: Cannot verify location specified.
solution: Verify location specified is accessible across cluster node(s).

message: Virtual IP (VIP) "{0}" found for node "{1}"
cause: The VIP node application identified was found on the node specified.
solution: Removed the specified VIP node application from the node specified.

message: Shared OCR location check failed
cause: Problem reading inventory file for CRS home location.
solution: Verify inventory file integrity.

message: Error checking Operating System Version compatibility for Universal Storage Manager on node "{0}"
cause: A remote operation to check Operating System version on the remote node failed.
solution: See the action for the additional error message displayed.

message: Version "{0}" is NOT supported for installing ACFS on node "{1}"
cause: The version of operating system on the node is not compatible for installing ACFS.
solution: Check documentation for compatible version and install compatible version.

message: Verification of SCAN VIP and Listener setup failed
cause: Could not identify any SCAN, or Scan Listener, resources on the cluster.
solution: Verify SCAN configuration using 'srvctl config scan'.

message: Scan Listener "{0}" not running
cause: The identified Listener was not in the running state.
solution: Start the identified Listener using 'srvctl start listener'.

message: Scan Listener port for listener "{0}" do not match other ports
cause: The port number used for the listener identified does not match those of all instances of the Listener started.
solution: Ensure that all the port numbers for the identified Listener match. See the commands 'srvctl config scan' and 'srvctl modify scan' for details on how to inspect and modify scan resource port numbers.

message: An error was encountered while verifying the SCAN configuration
cause: An error was encountered while obtaining SCAN information.
solution: Review additional messages displayed for details of the error that was encountered.

message: SCAN Listener processing error
cause: An error was encountered while obtaining SCAN Listener information.
solution: Review additional messages displayed for details of the error that was encountered.

message: SCAN VIP '"{0}"' not running
cause: The SCAN VIP resources is not in the 'running' state.
solution: Start the SCAN VIP resource using using 'srvctl start scan -i <num>'.

message: SCAN VIP "{0}" and Scan Listener "{1}" not running
cause: The SCAN VIP and SCAN Listener resources are not in the 'running' state.
solution: Start the SCAN VIP and SCAN Listener resources using 'srvctl'.

message: SCAN and Scan Listener may not function correctly
cause: The SCAN VIP and/or SCAN Listener are not in the 'Running' state, or the port numbers used for the Listeners do not match across the nodes.
solution: Start the SCAN VIP and/or SCAN Listener, or ensure that the port numbers used for the SCAN Listeners match across the nodes in the cluster.

message: Warning: all SCAN VIPs and SCAN Listeners are running on node "{0}"
cause: All the SCAN VIPs and SCAN Listeners were found to be running on specified node.
solution: Relocate scan using 'srvctl relocate scan' command to different nodes of the cluster.

message: TCP connectivity check for SCAN Listener "{0}" failed on node "{1}"
cause: An attempt to connect to SCAN Listener specified failed from the node specified.
solution: Examine the accompanying TNS error messages and respond accordingly.

message: ASM Running check failed. ASM is not running on all specified nodes
cause: ASM was not running on all the specified nodes.
solution: Ensure that ASM is running on all the nodes specified, see 'srvctl start asm' for further information.

message: ASM is not running on nodes: "{0}"
cause: ASM was not running on the cluster nodes specified.
solution: Ensure that ASM is running on all the cluster nodes.

message: Disk Group check failed. No Disk Groups configured
cause: No ASM disk groups were found configured on the ASM instance.
solution: Ensure that the necessary disk groups are configured in ASM.

message: Failure while checking ASM status on node "{0}"
cause: Could not verify ASM running on node specified.
solution: Ensure that ASM is running on the node specified.

message: ASM Disk group "{0}" is unavailable on nodes "{1}"
cause: Could not verify existence of ASM disk group specified on the nodes indicated.
solution: Verify existence of ASM group identified on the specified nodes, see 'asmcmd' for further information.

message: ASM Disk group "{0}" is unavailable on all nodes
cause: Could not verify existence of ASM disk group specified on all the nodes.
solution: Verify existence of ASM group identified on the cluster nodes.

message: Could not verify ASM group "{0}" for Voting Disk location "{1}"
cause: The ASM group specified was not found running on the system.
solution: Ensure that the ASM group is configured correctly and running, and ensure that the Voting Disk locations are configured correctly.

message: ACFS Driver version is not compatible with Operating System version on node "{0}"
cause: The version of ACFS driver is not compatible with the Operating system version on the node.
solution: Check documentation for compatible version and install compatible version.

message: Failed to retrieve ACFS driver version on node "{0}". Driver version compatibility check cannot be performed
cause: The version of the ACFS driver could not be retrieved from specified nodes.
solution: Make sure that ACFS driver is installed on these nodes.

message: Failed to retrieve Operating System version on the local node. ACFS driver version compatibility check will not be performed
cause: Operating system version on local node could not be determined.
solution: Look at the accompanying error messages displayed and fix the problems indicated.

message: Global failure when attempting to query ACFS driver state option "{0}" on all nodes
cause: ACFS driver state could not be obtained on all the nodes.
solution: Make sure that user executing this check has execute permissions on the usm_driver_state command.

message: Check of following Udev attributes of "{0}" failed: "{1}"
cause: Found incorrect attributes for the specified device.
solution: Ensure that the device attributes are set correctly. See Configurable Dynamic Device Naming documentation (udev) for further information.

message: No devices found matching discovery string "{0}"
cause: The specified device may not exist on the node being tested.
solution: Specify a correct discovery string that matches to existing devices on the node being tested.

message: No shared devices found
cause: No shared storage was found based on the discovery string used in the verification.
solution: A message should have been displayed for each shared storage check failure. For each such message, perform the suggested action for that message.

message: Failed to retrieve OCR locations
cause: An attempt to retrieve the OCR locations failed, possibly due to incorrect or incomplete Clusterware install, or due to incorrect configuration of the OCR, or due to invalid or incorrect OCR location file ocr.loc.
solution: Make sure that the Clusterware installation and Clusterware configuration has been correctly completed, and the ocr.loc file is present and accessible.

message: Failed to retrieve voting disk locations
cause: An attempt to retrieve the voting disk locations failed, possibly due to incorrect or incomplete Clusterware install, or due to incorrect configuration of the Clusterware.
solution: Make sure that the Clusterware installation and Clusterware configuration has been correctly completed.

message: GNS VIP resource configuration check failed.
cause: An error occurred while trying to obtain GNS VIP resource configuration information.
solution: Look at the accompanying messages for details on the cause of failure.

message: GNS resource is running on multiple nodes "{0}"
cause: GNS resource should be running on only one node in the cluster at any given time. It was found to be running on multiple nodes at the same time.
solution: Stop the GNS resources running on various nodes using 'srvctl stop gns' command and leave it running on just one node of the cluster.

message: GNS resource is not running on any node of the cluster
cause: GNS resource should be running on one node of the cluster. GNS resource wasn't running on any node.
solution: GNS can be configured using 'srvctl add gns' command. Use 'srvctl start gns' command to start GNS.

message: GNS resource configuration check failed
cause: An error occurred while trying to obtain GNS resource configuration information.
solution: Look at the accompanying messages for details on the cause of failure.

message: The following GNS resolved IP addresses for "{0}" are not reachable: "{1}"
cause: The listed IP addresses for the fully domain qualified name (FDQN) listed in the message and resolved by GNS were not reachable.
solution: Make sure that the configuration of GNS resource is proper using 'srvctl config gns' command. If GNS is configured correctly make sure that the network administrator has provided a set of IP addresses for the subdomain of the cluster and Domain Name Server (DNS) is forwarding requests for these to the GNS.

message: An error occurred while trying to look up IP address for "{0}"
cause: An error occurred while trying to translate the fully domain qualified name (FDQN), listed in the message, to IP addresses.
solution: These IP address requests should have been forwarded to GNS by the Domain Name Server (DNS). Check the configuration of GNS resource using 'srvctl config gns' command. If GNS is configured correctly make sure that the network administrator has provided a set of IP addresses for the subdomain of the cluster and DNS is forwarding requests for these to the GNS.

message: "{0}" did not resolve into any IP address
cause: The fully domain qualified name (FDQN) listed in the message did not resolve into any IP address.
solution: Make sure that the configuration of GNS resource is proper using 'srvctl config gns' command. If GNS is configured correctly make sure that the network administrator has provided a set of IP addresses for the subdomain of the cluster and Domain Name Server (DNS) is forwarding requests for these to the GNS.

message: GNS and GNS VIP resources are running on different nodes. GNS is running on nodes "{1}" while GNS VIP is running on "{0}".
cause: The GNS and GNS VIP resources were running on different nodes.
solution: If GNS should be running on one node of the cluster at any given point of time. Make sure that GNS is not running on multiple nodes of the cluster using 'srvctl config gns' command. If GNS is running on multiple nodes then shut down all but one using 'srvctl stop gns' command.

message: GNS VIP resource was not running on any node of the cluster
cause: The GNS VIP resource was not running on any nodes of the cluster.
solution: Make sure that the VIP name specified in 'srvctl add gns' command is an unused address belonging to one of the public networks of the cluster nodes.

message: The GNS subdomain name "{0}" is not a valid domain name
cause: The GNS domain name specified was not a valid domain name.
solution: A valid domain name starts with an alphabet and contain characters [A-Z], [a-z], [0-9], '.', '-'. Refer to RFC-1035 for more information.

message: GNS VIP "{0}" does not resolve to a valid IP address
cause: The specified GNS VIP does not resolve to an IP address.
solution: Make sure that the VIP name is spelled correctly. Make sure that the VIP name is registered with the DNS. Make sure that there are no firewalls between the cluster and the DNS server.

message: GNS VIP is active before Clusterware installation
cause: GNS VIP was found to be active on the public network before Clusterware installation.
solution: If you are upgrading an older release of Clusterware this is not an error. In case of new installation GNS VIP will be brought up by GNS resource after Clusterware installation. Make sure that GNS VIP is configured to be an unused IP address.

message: GNS VIP is inactive after Clusterware installation
cause: GNS VIP was not reachable after Clusterware installation.
solution: Bring the GNS resource online using 'srvctl start gns' command.

message: The GNS subdomain qualified host name "{0}" was resolved into an IP address
cause: The specified GNS subdomain qualified host name was resolved into an IP address before Clusterware installation.
solution: Ensure that the DNS is configured to forward (rather than resolve) names in the GNS subdomain.

message: There are no public networks that match the GNS VIP "{0}"
cause: GNS VIP subnet number did not match any of the public networks on the node.
