solution: Specify an address that matches the public subnet number for GNS VIP.

message: Command "{0}" executed to retrieve GPNP resource status failed on all of the nodes
cause: An attempt to execute the displayed command failed on all of the nodes.
solution: Make sure that the nodes of the cluster are accessible from the current node. Make sure that the user executing the check has permission to execute commands on nodes using 'ssh'.

message: Command "{0}" executed on node "{1}" produced no output
cause: An attempt to run the command listed on the node listed produced no output.
solution: This is an internal error. Contact Oracle support services.

message: The GPNP resource is not in ONLINE status on the following node(s): {0}
cause: The GPNP resource was found to be in OFFLINE or UNKNOWN state on the nodes listed.
solution: This is not an error if the GPNP resource was shutdown. If it is not the expected state then use the command 'crsctl start res ora.gpnpd -init' to start the GPNP resource.

message: Command "{0}" executed to retrieve the GPNP resource status failed on node(s): {1}
cause: An attempt to run the command listed failed on the node listed.
solution: Make sure that the nodes listed are accessible from the current node. Make sure that the user executing the check has permission to executed commands on the node(s) listed using 'ssh'.

message: Failed to retrieve active version for CRS on this node
cause: Could not identify location of CRS home.
solution: Ensure that correct installation of CRS exists.

message: Failed to locate CRS home
cause: Could not locate the CRS home.
solution: Ensure that the install of CRS has completed successfully and the CRS home is setup correctly.

message: Failed to execute the exectask command on node "{0}"
cause: Could not execute command specified on node listed.
solution: Verify command specified can be exectued on node listed.

message: The Oracle Clusterware is not healthy on node "{0}"
cause: An error was found with the Oracle Clusterware on the node specified.
solution: Review the error reported and resolve the issue specified.

message: Failed to retrieve Oracle Restart home
cause: Could not identify location of Oracle Restart home.
solution: Ensure that Oracle Local Repository (OLR) was created correctly. See Oracle Local Repository documentation for further information.

message: ohasd is either not running or could not be contacted on node "{0}"
cause: CRSCTL did not report that OHAS was online.
solution: Review the error information displayed and verify the state of OHAS on the node identified.

message: File "{0}" either does not exist or is not accessible on node "{1}".
cause: Cannot access the file specified.
solution: Verify that the specified file exists and can be access on the node identified.

message: No ohasd entry was found in /etc/inittab file
cause: Did not find 'respawn:/etc/init.d/init.ohasd' line in '/etc/inittab' file.
solution: Ensure that the OHASD environment has been setup correctly.

message: Failed to search for ohasd entry in /etc/inittab file on node "{0}"
cause: An error was encountered trying to search for OHASD information in /etc/inittab.
solution: Ensure that the OHASD environment has been setup correctly and that /etc/inittab is accessible on the specified node.

message: Could not find CRS, or Oracle Restart, installed on the local node
cause: Could not locate the CRS, or Oracle Restart, installation from the local node.
solution: Ensure that the install of CRS, or Oracle Restart, has completed successfully and the CRS, or Oracle Restart, home is setup correctly.

message: Failed to retrieve version of CRS installed on node "{0}"
cause: Could not identify location of CRS home.
solution: Verify installation of CRS on the identified node.

message: The Clusterware is currently being upgraded to version: "{0}". The following nodes have not been upgraded and are running Clusterware version: "{1}". "{2}"
cause: The CRS integrity may have discovered that your Oracle Clusterware stack is partially upgraded.
solution: Review warnings and make modifications as necessary. If the warning is due to partial upgrade of Oracle Clusterware stack then continue with upgrade and finish it.

message: No Oracle Restart is found configured on the local node
cause: Could not locate the Oracle Restart configuration on the specified node.
solution: Ensure that the install of Oracle Restart has completed successfully and the Oracle Restart home is set up correctly.

message: Oracle Cluster Synchronization Services do not appear to be online.
cause: An error was encountered when trying to verify the status of Oracle Cluster Synchronization Services.
solution: Verify the state of the Oracle Cluster Synchronization Services using 'crsctl check cluster'.

message: Failed to get the CRS or Oracle Restart home
cause: Could not locate the CRS, or Oracle Restart, home.
solution: Ensure that the install of CRS, or Oracle Restart, has completed successfully and the CRS, or Oracle Restart, home is setup correctly.

message: Failed to get the CRS user name for CRS home "{0}"
cause: An attempt to obtain the Clusterware owner information from CRS home failed.
solution: Ensure that the user executing the CVU check has read permission for CRS or Oracle Restart home.

message: Failed to get information for file "{0}"
cause: An attempt to read information for a file failed.
solution: Make sure that the user executing the CVU check has read permission for the file and the file exists in the specified path.

message: Could not find CRS installed on the node "{0}"
cause: Could not locate the CRS installation on the specified node.
solution: Ensure that the install of CRS has completed successfully and the CRS home is setup correctly.

message: Failed to retrieve release version for Oracle Restart
cause: Could not get release version for Oracle Restart.
solution: Ensure that the install of Oracle Restart has completed successfully.

message: Clock synchronization check using Network Time Protocol(NTP) failed
cause: One or more of the Clock Synchronization checks failed.
solution: Correlate with the other failure messages displayed and fix those failures.

message: Warning: Could not find NTP configuration file "{0}" on node "{1}"
cause: NTP might not have been configured on the node, or NTP might have been configured with a configuration file different from the one indicated.
solution: Configure NTP on the node if not done so yet. Refer to your NTP vendor documentation for details.

message: Operation to check presence of NTP configuration file "{0}" failed on node "{1}"
cause: The operation to check NTP configuration file failed on node indicated. The failure is due to a reason like incorrect permissions on the configuration file, communications error with the node, missing or inaccessible remote execution binary on the node, etc.
solution: Review the error messages that follow this message and fix the problem(s) indicated.

message: The NTP configuration file "{0}" does not exist on all nodes
cause: The configuration file specified was not available or was inaccessible on the given nodes.
solution: If you want to use NTP for time synchronization, create this file and setup its configuration as described in your vendor's NTP document. If you plan to use CTSS for time synchronization then NTP configuration should be uninstalled on all nodes of the cluster. Refer to "Preparing Your Cluster" of "Oracle Database 2 Day + Real Application Clusters Guide".

message: NTP Configuration file Check failed
cause: Attempt to check presence of configuration file failed on one or more nodes.
solution: Look at the related error messages and fix them.

message: NTP Time Server "{0}" is common only to the following nodes "{1}"
cause: One or more nodes in the cluster do not synchronize with the NTP Time Server indicated.
solution: At least one common NTP Time Server is required for a successful Clock Synchronization check. If there are none, reconfigure all of the nodes in the cluster to synchronize with at least one common NTP Time Server.

message: Check of common NTP Time Server failed
cause: The NTP query command showed there is no common time server among all of the nodes in the cluster.
solution: At least one common NTP Time Server is required for a successful Clock Synchronization check. Reconfigure all of the nodes in the cluster to synchronize with at least one common NTP Time Server. If you plan to use CTSS for time synchronization then NTP configuration should be uninstalled on all nodes of the cluster. Refer to "Preparing Your Cluster" of "Oracle Database 2 Day+ Real Application Clusters Guide".

message: Query of NTP daemon failed on all nodes on which NTP daemon is running
cause: Attempt to query the NTP daemon failed on all of the nodes of the cluster because the 'ntpq' command could not be found.
solution: Make sure that the NTP query command 'ntpq' is available on all nodes and the user running the CVU check has execute privilege for it.

message: Node "{0}" has a time offset of {1} that is beyond permissible limit of {2} from NTP Time Server "{3}"
cause: The time offset for the given node clock with the specified NTP Time Server is beyond permissible limits, possibly due to a clock drift, or due to an incorrectly functioning time server.
solution: Make sure that the Time Server is functioning properly, and if yes, adjust the system clock so that the offset is within limits.

message: Check of NTP Config file failed on all nodes. Cannot proceed further for the NTP tests
cause: Attempt to check existence of config file failed on all nodes.
solution: Look at the individual error messages displayed for the respective nodes and the overall result message and take appropriate action.

message: Check to see if NTP daemon or service is running failed
cause: Attempt to check if the NTP daemon was running failed on nodes of the cluster.
solution: Look at the accompanying error messages for the nodes on which the check failed and fix the problem. If you plan to use CTSS for time synchronization then NTP configuration should be uninstalled on all nodes of the cluster. Refer to "Preparing Your Cluster" of "Oracle Database 2 Day+ Real Application Clusters Guide".

message: Query of NTP daemon failed on all nodes
cause: An attempt to query the NTP daemon using the 'ntpq' command failed on all nodes.
solution: Make sure that the NTP query command 'ntpq' is available on all nodes and make sure that user running the CVU check has permissions to execute it.

message: NTP configuration file check failed on the following nodes:
cause: Check of existence of NTP configuration file failed on nodes listed because NTP was not configured on those nodes.
solution: If you plan to use NTP for time synchronization across nodes of the cluster then configure NTP on all of the nodes. If you plan to use CTSS for time synchronization then NTP configuration should be uninstalled on all nodes of the cluster. Refer to "Preparing Your Cluster" of "Oracle Database 2 Day+ Real Application Clusters Guide".

message: Clock time offset check failed
cause: Offsets on all of the nodes in the cluster were not within limits for any Time Server.
solution: Look at the individual messages displayed and fix the problems indicated.

message: Network Time Protocol(NTP) configuration file not found on any of the nodes. Oracle Cluster Time Synchronization Service(CTSS) can be used instead of NTP for time synchronization on the cluster nodes
cause: NTP is not configured on the cluster nodes.
solution: This is not an error if the system administrator intended to use Oracle Cluster Time Synchronization Service (CTSS) for clock synchronization on the cluster. If not then install NTP on all nodes of the cluster according to your NTP vendor documentation.

message: Voting disk configuration does not meet Oracle's recommendation of three voting disk locations
cause: For high availability, Oracle recommends that you have a minimum of three voting disk locations.
solution: Add additional voting disk locations to meet the Oracle recommended amount of three voting disks.

message: Oracle Cluster Voting Disk configuration check failed
cause: The Voting Disk configuration does not meet Oracle's recommendations.
solution: Review Clusterware and Voting Disk configuration.

message: The current voting disk state is at high risk
cause: The current state of the voting disk locations is susceptible to the loss of one voting disk location resulting in failure of the cluster.
solution: Add additional voting disk locations, or bring existing locations online, to reduce the risk of losing one voting disk location.

message: Cannot identify the current CRS software version
cause: Unable to obtain CRS version from CRSCTL.
solution: Ensure that CRSCTL is accessible on the nodes being verified.

message: Voting disk configuration does not meet Oracle's recommendation
cause: For high availability, Oracle recommends that you have more than two voting disk locations.
solution: Add additional voting disk locations.

message: The NTP daemon running on one or more nodes lacks the slewing option "{0}"
cause: NTP daemon on one or more nodes lacked slewing option.
solution: Shut down and restart the NTP daemon after setting the slewing option as follows: For Linux, edit /etc/sysconfig/ntpd and add -x to the command line option. For SUSE Linux, edit /etc/sysconfig/ntp and add -x to the OPTIONS variable. For AIX, edit /etc/rc.tcpip and add -x to the command line option. For HP-UX, edit /etc/rc.config.d/netdaemons and add -x to the command line option. For Solaris release 10 or earlier, edit /etc/inet/ntp.conf and add 'slewalways yes' and 'disable pll' to the file. For Solaris release 11 and higher, logon as root user and issue command: /usr/sbin/svccfg -s svc:/network/ntp:default setprop config/slew_always = true to change the setting, then refresh the service by issuing: svcadm refresh svc:/network/ntp:default

message: NTP daemon does not have slewing option "{0}" set on node "{1}"
cause: NTP daemon on the specified node does not have the slewing option set.
solution: Shut down and restart the NTP daemon with the slewing option set. In each case add -x to the ntpd command line options.

message: NTP daemon slewing option "{0}" check could not be performed on node "{1}"
cause: An attempt to obtain the command line options for NTP daemon failed.
solution: Make sure that the NTP daemon is running on the node. Also look at other messages accompanying this message.

message: Could not obtain NTP daemon's command line on any node
cause: An attempt to obtain the command line options for the NTP daemon's failed on all nodes.
solution: Make sure that the NTP daemon is running on all the nodes. Make sure that slewing option is set on all the nodes of the cluster.

message: Could not verify sharedness of Oracle Cluster Voting Disk configuration
cause: Unabled to obtain list of nodes with CRS installed.
solution: Ensure that Clusterware is up and running and verify Voting Disk configuration.

message: Voting Disk location "{0}" is not shared across cluster nodes
cause: Voting Disk location specified is not shared across all cluster nodes.
solution: Verify Voting Disk configuration and ensure all Voting Disk locations are shared across all cluster nodes and are of the same storage type.

message: Check of Voting Disk location "{0}" failed on the following nodes:
cause: Voting Disk location specified is not accessible on the nodes identified.
solution: Verify the owner, group and permissions settings on the location indicated.

message: Constraint type does not match
cause: The specified constraint does not relate to space checks.
solution: Make sure that the space constraint data is well formed and consistent in the constratint xml.

message: Missing key data "{0}"
cause: The data required for constraint check is missing.
solution: Verify that the space constraint data is correctly specified in the constraint xml.

message: Missing key reference data "{0}"
cause: The reference data required for constraint check is missing.
solution: For a greater than/equal comparison, reference data is required.Verify that the space constraint check reference data is correctly specified in the constraint xml.

message: Invalid data set for "{0}", EXPECTED:"{1}", FOUND: "{2}"
cause: The specified data is invalid for the space constraint check being performed.
solution: Make sure that correct data is specified, using the values indicated in the message.

message: Qualifier "{0}" is not supported for "{1}"
cause: The indicated qualifier is not supported for the class indicated in the message.
solution: Make sure that the correct qualifier is specified.

message: Cannot apply invalid constraint
cause: The specified constraint is invalid.
solution: Specify the correct constraint.

message: Invalid constraint. Compatibility check cannot proceed
cause: The specified constraint is invalid.
solution: Specify the correct constraint for the compatibility check.

message: Encountered an invalid setting for internal variable "{0}"
cause: This is an internal error.
solution: Please contact Oracle Support.

message: The NTP daemon''s boot time configuration, in file "{0}", on one or more nodes lacks the slewing option "{1}"
cause: NTP daemon boot time configuration on one or more nodes lacked slewing option.
solution: Make sure that the slewing option is specified in the file listed. For a list of nodes on which this check failed look at the accompanying error messages.

message: NTP daemon''s boot time configuration does not have slewing option "{0}" set on node "{1}"
cause: NTP daemon boot time configuration on the specified node does not have the slewing option set.
solution: The NTP daemon's boot time configuration file is listed with the messages accompanying this message. Make sure that slewing option is set in configuration file. For more information on NTP daemon slewing option refer to NTP daemon's man pages.

message: NTP daemon''s boot time configuration check could not be performed on node "{0}"
cause: An attempt to obtain the NTP daemon's boot time configuration file failed on the node specified.
solution: Make sure that the NTP daemon is configured on the node and will be started when the node boots up. Make sure that the user running this check has access to the configuration file specified. Also look at other messages accompanying this message.

message: Could not obtain NTP daemon's boot time configuration on any node
cause: An attempt to obtain the command line options for the NTP daemon's failed on all nodes.
solution: Make sure that the NTP daemon is running on all the nodes. Make sure that slewing option is set on all the nodes of the cluster.

message: TZ value missing in configuration file "{0}" on node "{1}".
cause: Time Zone value is missing in specified configuration file.
solution: Enter appropriate Time Zone value in the specified configuration file on the indicated node.

message: Time zone is not the same on all cluster nodes.
cause: Nodes have different time zone settings.
solution: Ensure that time zone is same on all nodes.

message: The NTP daemon on the indicated nodes is not using UDP port 123
cause: The port 123 for udp is not opened for the NTP daemon or service.
solution: For Unix, edit the /etc/services file appropriately.

message: Warning: Could not find NTP Daemon or Service running on node "{0}".
cause: NTP Daemon may have aborted , shut down or may not have been installed.
solution: Restart NTP Daemon on the indicated node or install if necessary.

message: Operation to check presence of NTP Daemon or Service failed on node "{0}".
cause: The operation to check NTP Daemon or service failed on node indicated. The failure is due to a reason like incorrect setup, communications error with the node, missing or inaccessible remote execution binary on the node, etc.
solution: Review the error messages that follow this message and fix the problem(s) indicated.

message: The NTP Daemon or Service was not alive on all nodes
cause: The NTP Daemon was not alive on all the nodes.
solution: Examine the status of ntp on each of the nodes indicated after this message and restart the daemon or install the NTP software if necessary.

message: The Check for NTP Daemon or Service status failed on some nodes
cause: The NTP Daemon was not accessible or there was some unknown failure in the check.The failure is due to a reason like incorrect setup, communications error with the node, missing or inaccessible remote execution binary on the node, etc.
solution: Review the error that follow this message and fix the problem(s) in the indicated nodes.

message: Timezone file "{0}" missing on node "{1}".
cause: A check for the indicated timezone file did not find it on the node shown.
solution: Restore the file on the indicated node by reinstalling timezone patches for your operating system.

message: There are more than one NTP daemons or Services running on various nodes of the cluster
cause: An attempt to check if NTP daemons or Service were running on nodes of the cluster found that more than one NTP daemons or Services were active.
solution: The accompanying messages will list the NTP daemon or service names along with the nodes on which they are running. Make sure that only one time synchronization service is active on all nodes of the cluster at any given time by shutting down others.

message: The user "{0}" is currently logged in to the group "{1}" which is not the primary group for the user
cause: The user is currently logged into a group that is not user's primary group.
solution: Invoke the application after logging in to the primary group (using command newgrp <primary group>).

message: Current group ID check cannot be performed
cause: Attempt to check if the current group ID matches with primary group ID failed.
solution: Look at the accompanying error messages displayed and fix the problems indicated.

message: The NTP daemon on node "{0}" is not using UDP port 123
cause: The port 123 for UDP was not being used by the NTP daemon or service.
solution: For Unix, edit the /etc/services file appropriately.

message: Check for UDP port 123 being used by NTP daemon or service could not be performed on node "{0}"
cause: Attempt to check for UDP port 123 being used by NTP daemon or service failed.
solution: Look at the accompanying error messages displayed and fix the problems indicated.

message: NTP daemon or service is not running on any node but NTP configuration file exists on the following node(s):
cause: The configuration file was found on at least one node though no NTP daemon or service was running.
solution: If you plan to use CTSS for time synchronization then NTP configuration must be uninstalled on all nodes of the cluster.

message: NTP configuration file is present on at least one node on which NTP daemon or service is not running.
cause: An NTP configuration file was found on at least one node where the NTP daemon or service was not running.
solution: NTP configuration must be uninstalled on all nodes of the cluster.

message: Automount feature is disabled on nodes:
cause: Automount feature for new volumes was found disabled.
solution: To enable Automount feature for new volumes, use 'mountvol /e' or use the 'diskpart' utility's 'automount enable' command Restart your system to make your changes effective after enabling the Automount feature.

message: Automount feature is disabled on the node "{0}"
cause: Automount feature for new volumes was found disabled on specified node.
solution: To enable Automount feature for new volumes, use 'mountvol /e' or use the 'diskpart' utility's 'automount enable' command. Restart your system to make your changes effective after enabling the Automount feature.

message: Error reading Registry subkey "{0}" from Windows Registry on node "{1}"
cause: Windows Registry subkey 'HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\\System\\CurrentControlSet\\Services\\MountMgr' could not be read on specified node.
solution: Ensure that the specified subkey exists in registry and access permissions for the Oracle user allow access to the Windows Registry. Restart your system to make your changes effective after changing the registry.

message: Check for status of Automount feature cannot be performed on nodes:
cause: Windows Registry subkey 'HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\\System\\CurrentControlSet\\Services\\MountMgr' could not be read.
solution: Ensure that the specified subkey exists in registry and the access permissions for the Oracle user allow access to the Windows Registry. Restart your system to make your changes effective after changing the registry.

message: Failed to perform the Automount status verification.
cause: An error occurred while attempting to retrieve the information about Automount feature.
solution: Look at the accompanying messages and respond accordingly.

message: On node "{0}" The following lines in file "{1}" could not be parsed as they are not in proper format: {2}
cause: Invalid lines were found in the file resolv.conf at the location and on the node indicated.
solution: Correct the errors indicated. On UNIX the general format of file resolv.conf is "<keyword> <value(s)>". For more details refer to resolv.conf man page.

message: 'domain' entry does not exist in file "{0}" on nodes: "{1}"
cause: The 'domain' was not found in the resolv.conf file on nodes indicated while it was present in others.
solution: Look at the file specified on all nodes. Make sure that either 'domain' entry is defined on all nodes or is not defined on any nodes.

message: 'domain' entry in file "{0}" on node "{1}" is "{2}" which differs from reference node
cause: The 'domain' entry on the node specified was not the same as the reference node 'domain' option specified above.
solution: Make sure that all nodes of the cluster have same 'domain' entry in the file specified.

message: File "{0}" does not exist on following nodes: {1}
cause: File specified did not exist on the nodes listed, but exists on other nodes.
solution: Make sure that the file is either present on all nodes or is not present on any node.

message: The file "{0}" on following nodes have more than "{1}" 'nameserver' entries: {2}
cause: The file specified had more than allowed number of 'nameserver' entries.
solution: Reduce the number of 'nameserver' entries on the nodes specified to the allowed number.

message: The file "{0}" on the following nodes have more than one 'attempts' entry: {1}
cause: More than one 'option attempts:' entry was found on nodes specified.
solution: Make sure that there is only one 'option attempts:' entry in the file specified.

message: The following nodes have multiple 'domain' entries defined in file "{0}": {1}
cause: The nodes specified had multiple 'domain' entry defined in the file specified.
solution: Make sure that the file specified has only one 'domain' entry.

message: The file "{0}" on the following nodes have more than one 'search' entry: {1}
cause: More than one 'search' entry was found on nodes specified, in the file specified.
solution: Make sure that there is only one 'search' entry in the file specified. Multiple domains can be listed in the same search entry.

message: 'nameserver' entry does not exist in file "{0}" on nodes: "{1}"
cause: The 'nameserver' entry was not found on nodes indicated while it was present in others.
solution: Look at the file specified on all nodes. Make sure that either 'nameserver' entry is defined on all nodes or is not defined any nodes.

message: 'nameserver' entry in file "{0}" on node "{1}" is "{2}" which differs from reference node
cause: The 'nameserver' entry on the node specified was not the same as the reference node 'nameserver' option specified above.
solution: Make sure that all nodes of the cluster have same 'nameserver' entry in the file specified.

message: 'search' entry does not exist in file "{0}" on nodes: "{1}"
cause: The 'search' entry was not found on nodes indicated while it was present in others.
solution: Look at the file specified on all nodes. Make sure that either 'search' entry is defined on all nodes or is not defined any nodes.

message: 'search' entry in file "{0}" on node "{1}" is "{2}" which differs from reference node
cause: The 'search' entry on the node specified was not the same as the reference node 'search' option specified above.
solution: Make sure that all nodes of the cluster have same 'search' entry in the file specified.

message: Unable to read file "{0}" copied to local scratch area from node {1}
cause: An error occurred while trying to read file specified.
solution: Make sure that the CV_DESTLOC area was not being used by another process. Make sure that CV_DESTLOC has sufficient permissions. Also look for messages accompanying this message for details.

message: The DNS response time for an unreachable node exceeded "{0}" ms on following nodes: {1}
cause: The DNS response time for an unreachable node exceeded the value specified on nodes specified.
solution: Make sure that 'options timeout', 'options attempts' and 'nameserver' entries in file resolv.conf are proper. On HPUX these entries will be 'retrans', 'retry' and 'nameserver'. On Solaris these will be 'options retrans', 'options retry' and 'nameserver'. Make sure that the DNS server responds back to name lookup request within the specified time when looking up an unknown host name.

message: DNS response time could not be checked on following nodes: {0}
cause: An attempt to check DNS response time for unreachable node failed on nodes specified.
solution: Make sure that 'nslookup' command exists on the nodes listed and the user executing the CVU check has execute privileges for it.

message: Both 'search' and 'domain' entries are present in file "{0}" on the following nodes: {1}
cause: Both 'search' and 'domain' entries were found in resolv.conf file on the nodes specified.
solution: Make sure that only one of these entries exist in file resolv.conf. It is preferable to use entry 'search' in resolv.conf.

message: Unable to create the directory "{0}"
cause: An attempt to create the directory specified failed on local node.
solution: Make sure that the user running CVU has read and write permissions on directory specified or specify a different work area using CV_DESTLOC environment variable where user has write permission.

message: Unable to delete files from directory "{0}"
cause: An attempt to remove files from the directory specified failed.
solution: Make sure that the user running CVU has read and write permissions on directory specified or specify a different work area using CV_DESTLOC environment variable where user executing this check has write permission.

message: No DHCP server were discovered on the public network listening on port {0}
cause: No reply was received for the DHCP discover packets sent on the specified port.
solution: Contact the network administrator to make sure that DHCP servers exist on the network. If the DHCP servers are listening to a different port then specify it by using -port option.

message: DHCP server was not able to provide sufficient IP addresses (required "{1}" , provided "{0}")
cause: DHCP server was unable to provide sufficient number of IP address.
solution: An IP is required for each node VIP. Three IP addresses are needed for SCAN VIP. One IP address is required for each application VIP specified. Make sure that the DHCP server listening on port specified in above messages has sufficient number of IP addresses to give out.

message: DHCP server response time could not be measured
cause: An attempt to measure DHCP server response time using 'crsctl discover' command failed.
solution: Look at messages accompanying this message for more information.

message: Warning: The DHCP server response time of {0} seconds is greater than VIP resource's SCRIPT_TIMEOUT attribute of {1} seconds
cause: An attempt to obtain a DHCP lease took more time than VIP resource's SCRIPT_TIMEOUT attribute.
solution: This check is network load sensitive and can yield different result at different times. Make sure that the DHCP server and the network is not overloaded. Also consider a higher SCRIPT_TIMEOUT value.

message: Command "{0}" executed on node "{1}" produced no output
cause: An attempt to run the command listed on the node listed produced no output.
solution: This is an internal error. Contact Oracle Support Services.

message: An error occurred while parsing the output of the command "{0}". The output is: "{1}"
cause: An attempt to parse output of the command listed failed.
solution: This is an internal error. Contact Oracle Support Services.

message: The number of IP addresses assigned to the network interface "{0}" exceeds recommended value (recommended {1}, actual {2})
cause: Too many IP addresses were assigned to the specified interface.
solution: If there are IP addresses that are not needed stop them in the operating system specific way. If too many resources are running on this node then relocate them to other nodes of the cluster relocate using 'srvctl relocate' command.

message: Unable to obtain network interface details on local node
cause: An attempt to obtain network interface details on local node failed.
solution: Make sure that the user executing CVU has sufficient permissions to query network interfaces on the node. Also look at accompanying messages and take action as per those messages.

message: Command "{0}" failed to execute on node "{1}". The output produced by the command is: "{2}"
cause: An attempt to execute specified command on the node specified failed.
solution: Refer to the specified output and fix the error.

message: Failed to execute command "{0}" on all nodes
cause: CVU's attempt to execute the specified command failed on all of the nodes.
solution: Examine the messages displayed for each node and take action as per those messages.

message: An error occurred while starting the IP address "{0}" on node "{1}"
cause: An attempt to start the specified IP address on the node specified failed.
solution: Look at messages accompanying this message for more information.

message: Unable to start the test DNS server
cause: An attempt to start the test DNS server failed with errors.
solution: Look at messages accompanying this message for more information.

message: Unable to start the test DNS server on address: "{0}", listening on port: {1}
cause: An attempt to start the test DNS server failed with errors.
solution: Look at messages accompanying this message for more information.

message: Unable to stop the test DNS server on address: "{0}", listening on port: {1}
cause: An attempt to stop the test DNS server failed with errors.
solution: Look at messages accompanying this message for more information.

message: Unable to stop the IP address "{0}" on node "{1}"
cause: An attempt to stop the IP address specified on the node specified failed.
solution: Look at messages accompanying this message for more information.

message: Unable to reach the IP address "{0}" from local node
cause: An attempt to reach the specified IP address from current node failed.
solution: Make sure that the specified IP address is a valid IP address. Check messages of the 'cluvfy comp dns -server' instance to make sure that there are no errors. If the address has been started then make sure that there are no firewalls between the local node and node on which this IP address has been started.

message: Unable to query the test DNS server started on address "{0}", listening on port {1}
cause: An attempt to query the test DNS server, started on specified address and port, failed.
solution: Look at messages on the 'cluvfy comp dns -server' instance to make sure that the test DNS server was stared. Also look at any messages accompanying this message.

message: Failed to verify DNS delegation of the GNS subdomain "{0}"
cause: An attempt to perform name resolution for nodename.<gns_subdomain> failed as DNS did not forward requests to the test DNS server.
solution: Look at messages accompanying this message for more information. Also look at any messages from 'cluvfy comp dns -server' invocation for CVU.

message: Unable to reach the IP address "{0}" from local node
cause: An attempt to reach the specified IP address failed.
solution: Make sure that the specified IP address is a valid IP address and is assigned to an interface on the node on which 'cluvfy comp dns -server' was run. Make sure that there are no firewalls between local node and node on which specified IP address is assigned.

message: Name lookup for FDQN "{0}" failed with test DNS server running on address "{1}", listening on port {2}
cause: An attempt to query specified FDQN on the test DNS server running on specified address and port failed.
solution: Make sure that the specified address and port is correct. Make sure that there are no firewalls between the node on which 'cluvfy comp dns -server' was run and the node on which this command was run. Also look at any error messages on the node on which 'cluvfy comp dns -server' was run.

message: Name lookup for FDQN "{0}" failed
cause: An attempt to query DNS servers for FDQN specified failed.
solution: Make sure that there are no firewalls between the local node and the DNS. Make sure that there are no firewalls between DNS and the node on which 'cluvfy comp dns -server' was run. Make sure that GNS subdomain delegation was setup correctly in the DNS. Also look at any error messages on the node on which 'cluvfy comp dns -server' was run.

message: The domain name "{0}" is not valid
cause: The GNS domain name specified did not conform to the industry standard.
solution: A valid domain name starts with an alphabetic character and consists only of characters [A-Z], [a-z], [0-9], '.', '-'. Refer to the RFC-1035 standard for more information.

message: The response time for name lookup for name "{1}" exceeded {0} seconds
cause: The DNS response time for the name specified exceeded the value specified.
solution: On Linux and AIX make sure that 'options timeout', 'options attempts' and 'nameserver' entries in file resolv.conf are proper. On HPUX these entries will be 'retrans', 'retry' and 'nameserver'. On Solaris these will be 'options retrans', 'options retry' and 'nameserver'. On windows look at registry key 'HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\\System\\CurrentControlSet\\Services\\VxD\\MSTCP' for values 'BcastQueryTimeout' and 'MaxConnectRetries'.

message: Could not get required information about the interface "{0}"
cause: Could not get interface information for the interface specified.
solution: Ensure that the interface is installed and online on the nodes in the cluster.

message: Unable to get information about interface "{0}" on the following nodes:
cause: Could not get interface information for the interface specified on the nodes listed.
solution: Ensure that the interface is installed and online on the nodes specified.

message: Unable to get network information from node: {0}
cause: Could not obtain any network interface information from the node specified.
solution: Verify state of network interface adapters on the specified node.

message: Could not find a fully connected subnet that covers all the nodes
cause: Could not find a network interface adapter that exists in the same subnet on every node in the cluster .
solution: Ensure that the network interface adapters are installed and configured correctly on each node in the cluster.

message: Unable to reach any of the nodes
cause: Unable to reach any of the nodes using the OS ping command.
solution: Ensure that the nodes specified are accessible with the OS ping utility.

message: Network interface unavailable on node "{0}"
cause: Could not find any network interface on the node.
solution: Verify network interface(s) operational status on the node identified.

message: Interface subnet "{0}" does not have a gateway defined
cause: Could not identify the gateway for the subnet identified.
solution: Define a gateway for the specified subnet.

message: Different MTU values used across network interfaces in subnet "{0}"
cause: Different MTU values found for the network adapter used between cluster nodes across the specified subnet.
solution: Set the MTU value for that network adapter/subnet to be the same on each node in the cluster.

message: Core file name pattern is not same on all the nodes.
cause: The core file name pattern is not same on all the nodes.
solution: Ensure that the mechanism for core file naming works consistently on all the nodes. Typically for Linux, the elements to look into are the contents of two files /proc/sys/kernel/core_pattern or /proc/sys/kernel/core_uses_pid. Refer OS vendor documentation for platforms AIX, HP-UX, and Solaris.

message: Core file name pattern can not be obtained from nodes "{0}".
cause: Unable to execute commands on the nodes specified.
solution: Ensure the ability to communicate with, and execute commands on, nodes specified .

message: Package cvuqdisk not installed
cause: The required cvuqdisk package to perform this operation was found missing.
solution: Ensure that the required version of cvuqdisk package is installed on all the nodes participating in the operation.

message: OCFS file system does not exist on location "{0}"
cause: OCFS file system was not found on the specified location.
solution: Ensure that OCFS file system is correctly created on the specified location.

message: Unable to determine the shareability of device {0} on nodes:
cause: An attempt to retrieve devices' Universally Unique Identifier (UUID) failed, or UUID's do not match, on the nodes indicated.
solution: Ensure the devices UUID can be obtained, and that the UUID value matches across all the nodes indicated.

message: Reserve_policy setting prevents sharing of {0} on nodes:
cause: The reserve_policy setting for the device is preventing the device from being shared on the nodes indicated.
solution: Change the reserve_policy setting for the device. See the chdev command for further details.

message: Reserve_lock setting prevents sharing of {0} on nodes:
cause: The reserve_lock setting for the device is preventing the device from being shared on the nodes indicated.
solution: Change the reserve_lock setting for the device. See the chdev command for further details.

message: File system exists on location "{0}"
cause: Existing file system found on the specified location.
solution: Ensure that the specified location does not have an existing file system.

message: Sufficient space is not available at location "{0}" on node "{1}" [Required space = {2}]
cause: Not enough free space at location specified.
solution: Free up additional space or select another location.

message: Kernel version is not consistent across all the nodes.
cause: The operating system kernel versions do not match across cluster nodes.
solution: Update the kernel version where necessary to have all cluster nodes running the same kernel version.

message: Sufficient physical memory is not available on node "{0}" [Required physical memory = {1}]
cause: Amount of physical memory (RAM) found does not meet minimum memory requirements.
solution: Add physical memory (RAM) to the node specified.

message: Physical memory check cannot be performed on node "{0}"
cause: Could not perform check of physical memory on the node indicated.
solution: Ensure the ability to access the node specified and view memory information.

message: Package "{0}" is missing on node "{1}"
cause: A required package is either not installed or, if the package is a kernel module, is not loaded on the specified node.
solution: Ensure that the required package is installed and available.

message: Proper version of package "{0}" is not found on node "{1}" [Required = "{2}" ; Found = "{3}"].
cause: Package does not meet the requirement.
solution: Upgrade the package to meet the requirement.

message: Package check cannot be performed on node "{0}"
cause: Package configuration could not be determined.
solution: Ensure that the package configuration is accessible.

message: Proper architecture is not found on node "{0}" [Expected = "{1}" ; Found = "{2}"]
cause: System architecture does not meet the requirement.
solution: Ensure that the correct software bundle is being used.

message: Architecture check cannot be performed on node "{0}"
cause: System architecture could not be determined.
solution: Ensure that the correct software bundle is being used.

message: User "{0}" does not exist on node "{1}"
cause: The specified user does not exist on the specified node.
solution: Create the user on the specified node.

message: User existence check cannot be performed on node "{0}"
cause: Attempt to check the existence of user on the specified node failed.
solution: Look at the accompanying error messages displayed and fix the problems indicated.

message: Group "{0}" does not exist on node "{1}"
cause: The specified group does not exist on the specified node.
solution: Create the group on the specified node.

message: Group existence check cannot be performed on node "{0}"
cause: Attempt to check the existence of group on the specified node failed.
solution: Look at the accompanying error messages displayed and fix the problems indicated.

message: Kernel version check cannot be performed on node "{0}"
cause: Unable to execute commands on node specified.
solution: Ensure the ability to communicate with, and execute commands on, node specified .

message: OS Kernel parameter "{0}" does not have proper value on node "{1}" [Expected = "{2}" ; Found = "{3}"].
cause: Kernel parameter value does not meet the requirement.
solution: Modify the kernel parameter value to meet the requirement.

message: Check cannot be performed for kernel parameter "{0}" on node "{1}"
cause: Kernel parameter value could not be determined.
solution: Ensure that the correct software bundle is being used.

message: Sufficient available memory is not available on node "{0}" [Required available memory = {1}]
cause: Amount of available memory (RAM) does not meet minimum memory requirements.
solution: Add physical memory (RAM) to the node specified, or free memory being used.

message: Available memory check cannot be performed on node "{0}"
cause: Could not perform check of available memory on the node indicated.
solution: Ensure the ability to access the node specified and view memory information.

message: Incorrect run level set on node "{0}" [Required run level = {1}]
cause: Found incorrect runlevel on the node specified.
solution: Reboot the specified node with the correct runlevel.

message: Run level check cannot be performed on node "{0}"
cause: Encountered error when trying to determine runlevel.
solution: Ensure that runlevel value can be obtained on the specified node.

message: User "{0}" does not belong to group "{1}" on node "{2}"
cause: The specified user is not a member of the specified group on the specified node.
solution: Make the user a member of the group on the specified node.

message: Group "{0}" is not the primary group for user "{1}" on node "{2}"
cause: The specified group is not the primary group for the specified user.
solution: Make the specified group as the primary group for the user.

message: Check cannot be performed for membership of user "{0}" with group "{1}" on node "{2}"
cause: Attempt to check the group membership of the user on the specified node failed.
solution: Look at the accompanying error messages displayed and fix the problems indicated.

message: Process "{0}" not running on node "{1}"
cause: Required process not running on the specified node.
solution: Ensure that the identified process can be started on the node .

message: Process running check cannot be performed on node "{0}"
cause: Could not collect process information from the specified node.
solution: Ensure the access to node specified and ability to view process information.

message: Sufficient swap size is not available on node "{0}" [Required = {1} ; Found = {2}]
cause: The swap size found does not meet the minimum requirement.
solution: Increase swap size to at least meet the minimum swap space requirement.

message: Swap size check cannot be performed on node "{0}"
cause: Could not perform check of swap space on the node indicated.
solution: Ensure the ability to access the node specified and view swap space information.

message: Encountered an internal error. The range of reference data for verifying swap size has not been correctly defined
cause: Swap size could not be determined based on the physical memory available.
solution: This is an internal error that should be reported to Oracle.

message: Multiple versions of package "{0}" found on node {1}: {2}
cause: Multiple versions of the package were found when only one version was expected.
solution: Ensure that the specified package is installed correctly.

message: "{0}" is not running on node "{1}"
cause: The process identified is not running on the specified node.
solution: Ensure that the identified process is started and running on the specified node. If it is one of the Clusterware daemons then you can use 'crsctl check' command to check status.

message: Check cannot be performed for status of "{0}" on node "{1}"
cause: An error was encountered trying to determine if the identified process was running on the specified node.
solution: Ensure the ability to communicate with the specified node. The status of Clusterware daemons can be checked on this node using the 'crsctl check' command.

message: Space availability check for location "{0}" cannot be performed on node "{1}"
cause: Unable to determine amount of free space available for the specified location on the node identified.
solution: Ensure the ability to communicate with the specified node and the ability to access the location identified.

message: CRS is not found to be installed on node "{0}"
cause: Could not identify CRS installation on the specified node.
solution: Ensure that CRS is installed on the specified node.

message: {0} is running but is not working effectively on node "{1}"
cause: Could not communicate with the process specified on the node indicated.
solution: Verify state of CRS on the node indicated using the 'crsctl check' command.

message: CRS status check cannot be performed on node "{0}"
cause: Could not verify the status of CRS on the node indicated using 'crsctl check'.
solution: Ensure the ability to communicate with the specified node. Make sure that Clusterware daemons are running using 'ps' command. Make sure that the Clusterware stack is up.

message: CSS is probably working with a non-clustered, local-only configuration on node "{0}"
cause: Oracle CSS was found to be configured to run in a local-only (non-clustered) environment on the specified node.
solution: Ensure that cluster setup is correct and reconfigure Cluster Synchronization Services (CSS) as necessary on the nodes that are supposed to be executing in a clustered environment. See Oracle Cluster Synchronization Services documentation for further information.

message: Unable to obtain OCR integrity details from node "{0}"
cause: OCR was not found to be in a healthy state on the node specified.
solution: Verify the state of OCR on the node specified using 'ocrcheck'.

message: Cannot verify user equivalence/reachability on existing cluster nodes
cause: Attempts to verify user equivalence, or node reachability, failed for all the existing cluster nodes.
solution: Verify that all the cluster nodes have user equivalence and are reachable.

message: Proper user file creation mask (umask) for user "{0}" is not found on node "{1}" [Expected = "{2}" ; Found = "{3}"]
cause: The user's OS file creation mask (umask) was not the required setting.
solution: Set appropriate user file creation mask. Modify the users .profile or .cshrc or .bashrc to include the required umask.

message: User file creation mask check cannot be performed for user "{0}" on node "{1}"
cause: Attempt to check the file creation mask of user on the specified node failed.
solution: Look at the accompanying error messages displayed and fix the problems indicated.

message: Unable to obtain network interface list from Oracle Clusterware
cause: The oifcfg executable may have encountered issues
solution: Verify this with the "oifcfg getif" command

message: Node connectivity failed for subnet "{0}" between "{1}" and "{2}"
cause: Node connectivity for the mentioned <subnet> could not be verified between the two interfaces identified ( <node> - <interface> : <IP addr> ).
solution: Verify the interface configurations for the network interfaces identified on the nodes indicated using utilities like ipconfig or ping.

message: Node connectivity between "{0}" and "{1}" failed
cause: Node connectivity between the two interfaces identified ( <node> : <IP addr> ) could not be verified.
solution: Verify the interface configurations for the network interfaces identified on the nodes indicated using utilities like ipconfig or ping.

message: Remote execution files could not be copied to "{0}" on the following nodes:
cause: An attempt to copy files to the directory specified failed.
solution: Make sure that the user running CVU has read and write permissions on directory specified or specify a different work area using CV_DESTLOC environment variable where user executing this check has write permission.

message: Path for fixup root directory is either null or is an empty string
cause: Provided fixup root directory path is either null or an empty string.
solution: Provide appropriate and absolute path for fixup root directory.

message: Path "{0}" for fixup root directory is invalid. It must be specified as an absolute pathname
cause: Fixup root directory was not specified as an absolute pathname.
solution: Respecify fixup root directory as an absolute pathname.

message: The path "{0}" for fixup root directory is not a valid directory
cause: Fixup root directory path was not a valid directory.
solution: Respecify fixup root path as a valid directory where files can be created and executed from.

message: The fixup root directory "{0}" is not writeable
cause: Directory identified is not writeable.
solution: Verify write access to directory specified.

message: The fixup root directory "{0}" cannot be created
cause: Could not create fixup root directory specified.
solution: Ensure that write access exists for the path for the directory specified.

message: Directory "{0}" cannot be created
cause: Could not create directory specified.
solution: Ensure that write access exists for the path for the directory specified.

message: File "{0}" cannot be created
cause: Could not create file specified.
solution: Ensure that write access exists for file location.

message: File "{0}" cannot be copied to file "{1}" on node "{2}"
cause: Could not copy the source file specified to the target file specified on the identified node.
solution: Ensure that the node identified and the target location for the file specified can be accessed.

message: Invalid path has been specified for fixup root directory
cause: The path specified for the fixup root directory is not correct.
solution: Specify an absolute path for a directory that exists and is writeable by the user performing the verification.

message: Fixup cannot be generated for creating group "{0}" on node "{1}"
cause: Attempt to generate fixup for group creation on the specified node failed.
solution: Look at the accompanying error messages displayed and fix the problems indicated.

message: Fixup cannot be generated for creating user "{0}" on node "{1}"
cause: Attempt to generate fixup for user creation on the specified node failed.
solution: Look at the accompanying error messages displayed and fix the problems indicated.

message: Fixup cannot be generated for setting kernel param "{0}" on node "{1}"
cause: Attempt to generate fixup for kernel param on the specified node failed.
solution: Look at the accompanying error messages displayed and fix the problems indicated.

message: Fixup cannot be generated for setting soft limit for resource "{0}" on node "{1}"
cause: Attempt to generate fixup for resource soft limit on the specified node failed.
solution: Look at the accompanying error messages displayed and fix the problems indicated.

message: Fixup cannot be generated for setting hard limit for resource "{0}" on node "{1}"
cause: Attempt to generate fixup for resource hard limit on the specified node failed.
solution: Look at the accompanying error messages displayed and fix the problems indicated.

message: Fixup cannot be generated for setting runlevel "{0}" on node "{1}"
cause: Attempt to generate fixup for run level on the specified node failed.
solution: Look at the accompanying error messages displayed and fix the problems indicated.

message: Fixup cannot be generated for setting membership of user "{0}" with group "{1}" on node "{2}"
cause: Attempt to generate fixup for group membership on the specified node failed.
solution: Look at the accompanying error messages displayed and fix the problems indicated.

message: Could not access or create trace file path "{0}". Trace information could not be collected
cause: Trace file location could not be created, or is not writeable.
solution: Make sure user has write access to location specified, or specify a different location using the environmental variable CV_TRACELOC.

message: Fixup cannot be generated for user "{0}", group {1}, on node "{2}" because the user is not defined locally on the node
cause: Fixup for group membership could not be generated because user was not found to be locally defined on the specified node.
solution: The fixup will have to be done manually. The user could be a Network Information Service (NIS) or Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP) user. Based on where the user is defined use appropriate tools to modify the user account.

message: Fixup cannot be generated for user "{0}", group "{1}", on node "{2}" because the group is not defined locally on the node
cause: Fixup for group membership could not be generated because the group was not found to be locally defined on the specified node.
solution: The fixup will have to be done manually. The group could be a Network Information Service (NIS) or Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP) user. Based on where the group is defined use appropriate tools to modify the user account.

message: String has bad format: "{0}"
cause: A parsing exception has occurred, and the string displayed could not parsed.
solution: This message should be part of one or more other messages. Please look at those messages and take appropriate action.

message: Linux RPM package version found to be lower than minimum required version of <"{0}"> on nodes:
cause: Linux RPM package version found to be older than recommended version.
solution: Ensure that the Linux RPM package version installed on the system is version 4.4.2.3 or higher.

message: Linux RPM package version was lower than the expected value. [Expected = "{0}" ; Found = "{1}"] on node "{2}"
cause: Linux RPM package version found to be older than recommended version.
solution: Ensure that the Linux RPM package version installed on the system is version 4.4.2.3 or higher.

message: Could not retrieve the version of Linux RPM package on node:
cause: An error occurred while running rpm command on system to determine the current version of Linux RPM package.
solution: Ensure that the Linux RPM package is correctly installed and is accessible to current user.

message: Could not retrieve the version of Linux RPM package on node "{0}"
cause: An error occurred while running rpm command on system to determine the current version of Linux RPM package.
solution: Ensure that the Linux RPM package is correctly installed and is accessible to current user.

message: OCFS2 is not configured in runlevel 3,4 and 5 on all the nodes
cause: Runlevel was not configured with levels 3,4 and 5 all being on.
solution: Check OCFS2 configuration and ensure the run levels indicated are on.

message: Current installation user "{0}" is not the owner "{1}" of the existing CRS installation
cause: Current user was not found to be an owner of an existing CRS installation.
solution: Ensure that the user upgrading CRS installation is an owner of already existing installation.

message: Failed to get the CRS user name for an existing CRS installation
cause: An attempt to obtain the Clusterware owner information from an existing CRS installation failed.
solution: Ensure that the user executing the CVU check has read permission for CRS or Oracle Restart home.

message: Command "{0}" to check CTSS status failed on all of the nodes
cause: CVU attempts to execute the displayed command failed on all of the nodes.
solution: Examine the messages displayed for each node and take action as per those messages.

message: CTSS status check command "{0}" executed successfully on node "{1}", but there was a failure in retrieving the output of this command
cause: Reason for failure to retrieve output could be due to improper execution.
solution: Try the command manually on the node to verify proper execution, and fix any issues arising out of this.

message: Query of CTSS for time offset and reference produced invalid output on node "{0}" Output: "{1}"
cause: Failure to correctly parse output could be due to improper execution.
solution: Try the command manually on the node to verify proper execution, and fix any issues arising out of this.

message: The CTSS command to query time offset and reference failed on node "{0}" with error message "{1}"
cause: Reason for failure to retrieve output could have been be due to improper execution.
solution: Try the command manually on the node to verify proper execution, and fix any issues arising out of this.

message: The CTSS command "{0}" failed to execute correctly or failed to produce valid output on all of the nodes
cause: Reason for failure could be due to improper execution.
solution: Look at the individual messages for each node and take action as per those messages.

message: The time offset of "{1}" on node "{0}" against reference node "{3}" is NOT within specified limit of "{2}" milliseconds
cause: One of the clocks, either on the current node, or on the reference node has drifted beyond limits.
solution: Monitor the offset over a longer duration and verify if the offset reduces over this period and falls within the threshold limits. Oracle Time Synchronization Service does periodic adjustments of the clock to attempt to bring it within threshold limits. If the threshold does not fall within limits over a period of time possibly due to a large deviation or drift, it is recommended that the Oracle processes on this node be shutdown, and the clock be adjusted on the problematic node suitably. It is NOT recommended to set a clock backwards.

message: Time offset is greater than acceptable limit on node "{0}" [actual = "{1}", acceptable = "{2}" ]
cause: System clock has drifted from the clock on the reference node for the specified set of nodes.
solution: Look at the individual messages for each node and take action as per those messages.

message: CTSS is in an inconsistent state with some nodes in Observer state and some nodes in Active state. All nodes must be either in Observer state or in Active state. Nodes with CTSS in Active state:"{0}" Nodes with CTSS in Observer state: "{1}"
cause: Some nodes may have NTP configured and some other nodes may not have NTP configured, resulting in an inconsistent state of CTSS.
solution: Stop Oracle CTSS service on all nodes and restart. Ensure that NTP is either configured on all nodes or not configured on any node.

message: Check of Clusterware install failed on some nodes. Clock Synchronization check will proceed with remnaining nodes
cause: A valid CRSHome was not found on one or more nodes. The messages displayed prior to this message indicate the list of nodes where a valid Clusteerware install was not found.
solution: Specify the correct set of nodes that contain a valid Clusterware installation, or complete the Clusterware installation on those node(s) and repeat this CVU verification.

message: CTSS is in Observer state. Switching over to clock synchronization checks using NTP
cause: All of the nodes queried for CTSS state indicate they are in Observer state. In the Observer state, CTSS is not performing active clock synchronization adjustments, but letting the underlying NTP handle this action.
solution: None. This is a normal state.

message: CTSS is in Observer state. Switching over to Windows-specific time synchronization checks
cause: All of the nodes queried for CTSS state indicate they are in Observer state. In the Observer state, CTSS is not performing active clock synchronization adjustments, but letting the underlying Windows time synchronization mechanisms handle this action.
solution: Look at the results of the Windows time synchronization checks displayed following this message. If there are any errors reported, perform action suggested for those error messages.

message: Command "{0}" executed to retrieve CTSS resource status failed on all of the nodes
cause: CVU attempts to execute the displayed command failed on all of the nodes.
solution: Examine the messages displayed for each node and take action as per those messages.

message: Failure to query CTSS resource on all nodes in the cluster
cause: Attempt to query CTSS resource on all of the nodes in the cluster failed. Possibly because Clusterware may not be running on the nodes.
solution: Look at the specific error messages reported for each of the nodes and take action as per those messages.

message: Failure checking status of CTSS on node "{1}" using command "{0}"
cause: CTSS may not OFFLINE, or may not be running, or the remote node may not be accessible.
solution: Try running in the indicated command directly on the specified node and ensure it is up and running, check that the remote node, and check user equivalence.

message: CTSS on node "{1}" is not in ONLINE state, when checked with command "{0}"
cause: The CTSS daemon is not running on the node, it may have died or may have been stopped.
solution: Restart the CTSS daemon on the specified node.

message: All nodes for which CTSS state was checked failed the check: Nodes: "{0}"
cause: CTSS is not in ONLINE state on any of nodes, possibly due to node accessibility, or being stopped.
solution: Look at the indvidual messages displayed for each node and perform the suggested action for those messages.

message: Clusterware is not installed on all nodes checked : "{0}"
cause: A valid Clusterware installation was not found on these nodes.
solution: Make sure the correct nodes are being specified in this check, or make sure that Clusterware is fully installed on the nodes before running this check for those nodes.

message: Clock Synchronization check without Oracle Cluster Time Synchronization Service (CTSS) is not supported on this platform
cause: The command line parameter, '-noctss', was specified on the command line which indicates that Clock Synchronization check should be performed without Oracle Cluster Time Synchronization Service (CTSS). This is not supported on this platform.
solution: Run the Clock Synchronization check without the '-noctss' flag.

message: CRS Active version is less than 11.2, performing NTP checks
cause: CTSS is supported only from release 11.2 onwards. Therefore, the clocksync component check can only run NTP checks.
solution: None

message: Failed to determine operating system patch status on the node "{0}"
cause: Operating system patch status could not be determined.
solution: Ensure that the operating system configuration is accessible.

message: An exception occurred while attempting to determine storage type for location "{0}"
cause: The location indicated may not be available on the node, or may have insufficient permissions for access by the user running the CVU check.
solution: Make sure that the location is available on the node, and has the right permissions to allow the user running the CVU check to read its attributes.

message: The storage location "{0}" is not a device, and therefore invalid for running Udev permissions check
cause: UDev permissions check are valid only for storage devices, and not valid for any kind of file system.
solution: Make sure that a valid storage device location is specified. If the location is derived from an ASM discovery string, make sure that the discovery string specified points to one or more storage devices, and not filesystems.

message: Attempt to get udev info from node "{0}" failed
cause: Attempt to read the udev permissions file failed, probably due to missing permissions directory, missing or invalid permissions file, or permissions file not accessible to use account running the check.
solution: Make sure that the udev permissions directory is created, the udev permissions file is available, and it has correct read permissions for access by the user running the check.

message: Failed to get storage attributes to compare udev attributes against, udev attributes check aborted
cause: In order to compare Udev attributes for a given storage location, the expected storage attributes are required to compare against. There was a failure to get these attributes, possibly due to invalid on non-existing Clusterware installation.
solution: Make sure that a valid Clusterware install exists on the node.

message: Encountered an internal error. The range of reference data for verification of kernel param "{0}" has not been correctly defined for node "{1}"
cause: No reference range defined to be used to calculate expected value.
solution: Define a reference range.

message: Proper OS Patch is not found on node "{0}" [Expected = "{1}" ; Found = "{2}"]
cause: Required OS Patch is not applied.
solution: Apply the required OS Patch.

message: No prereq file defined
cause: Prereq file was not set.
solution: Set prereq file.

message: Reference data is not available for verifying prerequisites on this operating system distribution
cause: No reference data was found for this operating system distribution.
solution: Please check the documentation for a list of supported operating system distributions for this product.

message: Check of Clusterware install failed on some nodes. Oracle patch check will proceed with remaining nodes
cause: A valid CRS home was not found on one or more nodes. The messages displayed prior to this message indicate the list of nodes where a valid Clusteerware install was not found.
solution: Specify the correct set of nodes that contain a valid Clusterware installation, or complete the Clusterware installation on those node(s) and repeat this CVU verification.

message: Clusterware is not installed on the following nodes : "{0}"
cause: A valid Clusterware installation was not found on these nodes.
solution: Make sure the correct nodes are being specified, and that the Clusterware is fully installed on the nodes before running this check for those nodes.

message: Failed to query patch information from OPatch inventory
cause: The execution of opatch lsinventory command failed.
solution: Make sure that the install inventory is readable by the user.

message: Failed to query patch information from Oracle executable
cause: Oracle executable could not be queried for patch information.
solution: Make sure that Oracle executable is present and is readable by the user running CVU.

message: Patch information from OPatch did not match patch information from Oracle executable
cause: Bug information from OPatch inventory does not match patch information recorded with Oracle executable.
solution: Make sure that all patches are applied correctly, refer to the OPatch user guide for information on patch application. Make sure that Oracle executable is relinked, refer to the Oracle Administrator Guide for information on relinking executables.

message: Patch information is not consistent across nodes
cause: Bug information from OPatch do not match between the nodes.
solution: Make sure that all patches are applied correctly on all nodes, refer to the OPatch user guide for information on patch application.

message: Patch information from OPatch did not match patch information from Oracle executable on the following nodes:
cause: Bug information from OPatch inventory does not match patch information recorded with Oracle executable.
solution: Make sure that all patches are applied correctly, refer to the OPatch user guide for information on patch application. Make sure that Oracle executable is relinked, refer to the Oracle Administrator Guide for information on relinking executables.

message: bug list did not match across nodes for the following nodes
cause: Bug information from OPatch do not match between the nodes.
solution: Make sure that all patches are applied correctly on all nodes, refer to the OPatch user guide for information on patch application.

message: Antivirus software is running
cause: Antivirus software was detected to be running.
solution: Oracle recommends that the Antivirus software be disabled. Antivirus may introduce delays in processing that interfere with time-sensitive cluster operations.

message: Owner of device "{0}" did not match the expected owner. [Expected = "{1}"; Found = "{2}"] on nodes: {3}
cause: Owner of the device listed was different than required owner.
solution: Change the owner of the device listed or specify a different device.

message: Group of device "{0}" did not match the expected group. [Expected = "{1}"; Found = "{2}"] on nodes: {3}
cause: Group of the device listed was different than required group.
solution: Change the group of the device listed or specify a different device.

message: Permissions of device "{0}" did not match the expected permissions. [Expected = "{1}"; Found = "{2}"] on nodes: {3}
cause: Permissions of the device listed was different than the required permissions.
solution: Change the permissions on the device listed or specify a different device.

message: Owner, group, permission information could not be obtained for device(s) "{0}" on node "{1}"
cause: Owner, group and permission information could not be obtained for devices listed on the nodes listed.
solution: "Ensure that the correct devices were specified and that they are created on the indicated node. Make sure that the path exists and is accessible by the user.

message: Owner, group, permission information could not be obtained for all devices on node "{1}"
cause: Owner, group and permission information could not be obtained for all devices on the node listed.
solution: Make sure that the node is up. Make sure that user equivalence exists on the node listed.

message: User "{0}" could not be verified as a domain user, domain "{1}" is either an invalid domain or can not be contacted
cause: Current user could not be verified as domain user. The identified domain name was either an invalid domain name or the domain could not be contacted.
solution: Ensure that the Windows Domain Server is reachable; log in to the OS as a domain user.

message: Node "{0}" is not yet deleted from the Oracle inventory node list
cause: The indicated node still exists in the list of nodes for the CRS home in the Oracle inventory.
solution: Use 'runInstaller -updateNodeList' to remove the indicated node from the CRS home node list.

message: Clusterware home "{0}" is located under Oracle base directory "{1}" on nodes "{2}"
cause: Clusterware home directory was found to be located in a subdirectory of ORACLE_BASE.
solution: Choose a Clusterware home directory that is not a subdirectory of the ORACLE_BASE. After Clusterware installation the owner will be changed to root for all of the directories above Clusterware home.

message: Clusterware home "{0}" is located under Oracle base directory "{1}" on node "{2}"
cause: Clusterware home directory was found to be located in a subdirectory of ORACLE_BASE.
solution: Choose a Clusterware home directory that is not a subdirectory of the ORACLE_BASE. After Clusterware installation the owner will be changed to root for all of the directories above Clusterware home.

message: Unable to check for the locations of Clusterware home and Oracle Base directory on nodes "{0}"
cause: Clusterware home or Oracle Base is not accessible or do not exist.
solution: Ensure that Oracle Base and Clusterware home exist and are accessible.

message: Unable to check for the locations of Clusterware home and Oracle Base directory on node "{0}"
cause: Clusterware home or Oracle Base is not accessible or do not exist.
solution: Ensure that Oracle Base and Clusterware home exist and are accessible.

message: Clusterware home "{0}" is located under Oracle base directory "{1}"
cause: The Clusterware home directory was found to be a subdirectory of the Oracle base directory.
solution: Choose a Clusterware home directory that is not a subdirectory of the Oracle base directory. After Clusterware installation the owner will be changed to root for all of the directories above Clusterware home.

message: OCR location is not the same across the cluster nodes
cause: More than one OCR location was found across the cluster nodes.
solution: Ensure the OCR location is the same across the cluster nodes.

message: Failed to retrieve storage type for "{0}" on node "{1}"
cause: The storage location specified may be non-existent or invalid or the user running the check may not have permissions to access the specified storage.
solution: Specify a valid existing location, and ensure that the user running the check has valid read permissions to this location.

message: Could not find any OCR Locations
cause: OCR Locations were not passed to the check.
solution: Pass Oracle locations to the check.

message: ASMLib is not installed on the nodes:
cause: The ASMLib installation file /etc/init.d/oracleasm was not found or could not be accessed on one or more nodes.
solution: Ensure that the ASMLib is correctly installed on all the nodes, or is not installed on any node.

message: ASMLib is not installed on the node "{0}"
cause: The ASMLib installation file /etc/init.d/oracleasm was not found or could not be accessed on the indicated node.
solution: Ensure that the ASMLib is correctly installed on the specified node, or is not installed on any node.

message: Failed to retrieve ASMLib information on the nodes:
cause: The check for ASMLib installation was unable to retrieve the required information on one or more nodes.
solution: Ensure that the ASMLib is correctly installed on all the nodes and that the user has the necessary access privileges.

message: Failed to retrieve ASMLib information on the node "{0}"
cause: The check for ASMLib installation was unable to retrieve the required information on the indicated node.
solution: Ensure that the ASMLib is correctly installed on all the nodes and that the user has the necessary access privileges.

message: ASMLib is not configured correctly on the nodes:
cause: ASMLib was found configured on some nodes, but not on the listed nodes.
solution: Ensure that the ASMLib is configured correctly and enabled on all the nodes, or is not configured on any node.

message: ASMLib is not configured correctly on the node "{0}"
cause: ASMLib was found configured on some nodes, but not on the indicated node.
solution: Ensure that the ASMLib is configured correctly and enabled on all the nodes, or is not configured on any node.

message: ASMLib does not identify the disks "{0}" on the nodes:
cause: ASMLib could not list all the disks on one or more nodes.
