solution: Ensure that the ASMLib is configured correctly to list all the created disks, To refresh the list of disks execute "/etc/init.d/oracleasm scandisks".

message: ASMLib does not identify the disks "{0}" on the node "{1}"
cause: ASMLib could not list all the disks on the indicated node.
solution: Ensure that the ASMLib is configured correctly to list all the created disks, To refresh the list of disks execute "/etc/init.d/oracleasm scandisks".

message: Following error occurred during the VIP subnet configuration check
cause: An error occurred while performing the VIP subnet check.
solution: Look at the accompanying messages for details on the cause of failure.

message: VIPs "{0}" are active before Clusterware installation
cause: Node VIPs were found to be active on the network before Clusterware installation.
solution: If you are upgrading an older release of Clusterware this is not an error. In case of new installation, make sure that the IP addresses to be configured as VIPs are currently unused.

message: VIPs "{0}" are not active after Clusterware installation
cause: Node VIPs were found to be not active on the network after Clusterware installation.
solution: Please run the command 'srvctl start nodeapps' to bring up VIPs

message: Failed lookup of IP address for host "{0}"
cause: An error occurred while trying to get IP address of the node VIP name.
solution: Run 'nslookup' on the name and make sure the name is resolved or add the node VIP name into OS hosts file.

message: IPMI device driver does not exist on nodes {0}
cause: Open IPMI device driver is not installed on the nodes.
solution: Install Open IPMI device drivers.

message: Error occurred while retrieving IP address of IPMI device on nodes {0}
cause: An internally-issued 'crsctl get css ipmiaddr' on the nodes failed.
solution: Configure IPMI device over LAN and run command 'crsctl set css ipmiaddr' command on the nodes to set the IP address.

message: IPMI IP address {0} on node {1} is not reachable
cause: A timeout occurred while receiving IPMI ping response. Usually this results from having the wrong IP address.
solution: Run 'crsctl set css ipmiaddr' command to set the correct IP address.

message: Login to node {0} BMC device using stored credentials failed
cause: An attempt to login to BMC on the node using username and password present in IPMI wallet failed.
solution: Run 'crsctl set css ipmiadmin' command to set correct credentials.

message: Path "{0}" is not suitable for usage as RAC database software
cause: The specified path is not found suitable for usage as RAC database software
solution: Ensure that you have selected a path that is suitable for the desired usage.

message: Path "{0}" is not suitable for usage as RAC database file
cause: The specified path is not found suitable for usage as RAC database file
solution: Ensure that you have selected a path that is suitable for the desired usage.

message: Path "{0}" is not suitable for usage as Oracle Clusterware storage
cause: The specified path is not found suitable for usage as Oracle Clusterware storage(OCR or Voting Disk).
solution: Ensure that you have selected a path that is suitable for the desired usage.

message: Path "{0}" is not suitable for usage as Single Instance database software
cause: The specified path is not found suitable for usage as Single Instance database software
solution: Ensure that you have selected a path that is suitable for the desired usage.

message: Path "{0}" is not suitable for usage as Single Instance database file
cause: The specified path is not found suitable for usage as Single Instance database file
solution: Ensure that you have selected a path that is suitable for the desired usage.

message: Error occurred while opening configuration file "{0}"
cause: Configuration file could not be opened. It either does not exist or you are not allowed read access.
solution: Provide a usable configuration file.

message: Could not allocate new memory
cause: Could not allocation any new memory.
solution: Retry after make more memory available.

message: Network Security error code {0}
cause: Failed to perform the network security operation.
solution: Look at the network security error for the appropriate action.

message: Failed to do the cluster wallet operation {0}
cause: Failed to perform the cluster wallet operation.
solution: Look at the cluster wallet error for the appropriate action.

message: Could not open the wallet {0} due to error {1} : {2}
cause: Failed to open the cluster wallet.
solution: Look at the cluster wallet error for the appropriate action.

message: Wallet {1} did not exist due to error code {1}
cause: The cluster wallet did not exist.
solution: Need to create the cluster wallet.

message: Alias {0} in Wallet {1} did not exist
cause: The alias within the cluster wallet did not exist.
solution: Need to create the alias within the cluster wallet.

message: Alias {0} in Wallet {1} could not be read due to error {2}
cause: Could not read the alias within the cluster wallet.
solution: Look at the network security error for the appropriate action.

message: Alias {0} in Wallet {1} could not be written due to error code {2}
cause: Could not write the secret of the alias to the cluster wallet.
solution: Look at the network security error for the appropriate action.

message: Wallet {0} could not be saved due to error code {1}
cause: Could not save the cluster wallet.
solution: Look at the cluster wallet error for the appropriate action.

message: Wallet {0} could not be created due to error {1}: {2}
cause: Could not create the cluster wallet.
solution: Look at the cluster wallet error for the appropriate action.

message: Wallet {0} could not be accessed due to error code {1}
cause: Could not access the cluster wallet.
solution: Use the correct cluster wallet password.

message: Wallet {0} could not be deleted due to error code {1}
cause: Could not delete the cluster wallet.
solution: Look at the cluster wallet error for the appropriate action.

message: Failed to initialize cluster wallet context due to error code {0}
cause: Could not initialize the cluster wallet context.
solution: Look at the cluster wallet error for the appropriate action.

message: Failed to terminate cluster wallet context due to error code {0}
cause: Could not terminate the cluster wallet context.
solution: Look at the cluster wallet error for the appropriate action.

message: ASM Disk Group {0} does not exist
cause: An attempt failed to retrieve an ASM disk group that was not configured.
solution: Create the diskgroup using sqlplus if the specified diskgroup does not exist. Mount the diskgroup in ASM which registers the diskgroup with CRS.

message: ASM Disk Group resource does not exist
cause: There was no disk group resource registered with CRS.
solution: Create the diskgroup using sqlplus and mount the diskgroup in ASM which registers the diskgroup with CRS.

message: Failed to remove CRS resource {0} for ASM Disk Group {1}
cause: An attempt to remove the CRS resource for the specified ASM Disk Group failed.
solution: Examine the accompanying error messages for details.

message: Failed to create ASM {0} resource {1}
cause: An attempt to add the CRS resource for ASM failed.
solution: Ensure that the CRS stack is running, the user running srvctl add asm is also the owner of the CRS home, and examine the accompanying error message for details.

message: Failed to retrieve server parameter file of ASM {0}
cause: Cannot retrieve ASM server parameter file.
solution: Retry the request after ensuring that the CRS stack is running, the ASM resource has been configured, and the user has read permission on the ASM resource.

message: Failed to update server parameter file {0} of ASM {1}
cause: Unable to update the ASM server parameter file.
solution: Retry the request after ensuring that the CRS stack is running, the ASM resource has been configured, and the user has update permission on the ASM resource.

message: ASM {0} is not using initialization parameters: {1}
cause: The specified ASM instance does not use the initialization parameters shown.
solution: Examine the accompanying error messages for details.

message: Failed to remove ASM resource {0} for ASM instance {1}
cause: An attempt to remove the specified ASM configuration failed.
solution: Examine the accompanying error message for details.

message: ASM {0} does not exist
cause: ASM is not configured yet.
solution: Configure ASM and then retry.

message: Failed to retrieve ASM instance list for ASM {0}
cause: Failed to retrieve the list of ASM instances.
solution: Make sure that the crs stack is up and the ASM resource has been configured.

message: ASM {0} is not running
cause: The ASM resource does not have any running instances.
solution: Use 'srvctl start asm' command to start the asm resource.

message: Unable to create ACFS file system resource {0} for the volume device {1}
cause: The ACFS file system resource for the specified volume device path could not be created. Possible causes: 1) CRS stack was not available. 2) ASM instance was not running. 3) User was not running with an account with administrative access. (root, Administrator, etc) 4) Was unable to identify the mount point that the user requested the resource to use.
solution: 1) Verify that the CRS stack is available. ( 'crsctl check crs' ) 2) Verify that ASM is running. (srvctl status asm) 3) Verify that the user is running with administrative access. 4) Verify that the mount point given to the create resource command exists.

message: Unable to retrieve ACFS file system for the volume device {0}
cause: The ACFS file system resource for the specified volume device path could not be retrieved. Possible causes: 1) CRS stack was not available. 2) ASM instance was not running. 3) User was not running with an account with administrative access. (root, Administrator, etc) 4) Was unable to identify the mount point that the user requested the resource to use.
solution: 1) Verify that the CRS stack is available. ( 'crsctl check crs' ) 2) Verify that ASM is running. (srvctl status asm) 3) Verify that the user is running with administrative access. 4) Verify that the mount point given to the create resource command exists.

message: ACFS file system resource already exists for disk group {0} and volume {1}
cause: The ACFS file system resource had already been created for the specified disk group and volume names.
solution: 1) Supply a different volume device path to srvctl add filesystem to create a different ACFS file system resource. -or- 2) Delete the previous resource (' srvctl remove filesystem -d <volume device> ') and re-run the command.

message: Unable to add ACFS file system resource {0} for disk group {1} and volume {2}
cause: The ACFS file system resource for the specified volume device path could not be added. Possible causes: 1) CRS stack was not available. 2) ASM instance was not running. 3) User was not running with an account with administrative access. (root, Administrator, etc) 4) Was unable to identify the mount point that the user requested the resource to use.
solution: 1) Verify that the CRS stack is available. ( 'crsctl check crs' ) 2) Verify that ASM is running. ( 'srvctl status asm' ) 3) Verify that the user is running with administrative access. 4) Verify that the mount point given to the create resource command exists.

message: Unable to retrieve the volume for disk group {0} and volume {1}
cause: The ACFS file system resource for the specified volume device path was unable to be retrieved. Possible causes: 1) CRS stack was not available. 2) ASM instance was not running. 3) User was not running with an account with administrative access. (root, Administrator, etc)
solution: 1) Verify that the CRS stack is available. ( 'crsctl check crs' ) 2) Verify that ASM is running. ( 'srvctl status asm' ) 3) Verify that the user is running with administrative access.

message: Unable to retrieve the mountpoint path for disk group {0} and volume {1}
cause: The ACFS file system resource for the specified volume device path was unable to be retrieved. Possible causes: 1) CRS stack was not available. 2) ASM instance was not running. 3) User was not running with an account with administrative access. (root, Administrator, etc)
solution: 1) Verify that the CRS stack is available. ( 'crsctl check crs' ) 2) Verify that ASM is running. ( 'srvctl status asm' ) 3) Verify that the user is running with administrative access.

message: Unable to set the user of the ACFS file system for disk group {0} and volume {1}
cause: The user of the ACFS file system resource for the specified disk group and volume was unable to be modified. Possible causes: 1) CRS stack was not available. 2) ASM instance was not running. 3) User was not running with an account with administrative access. (root, Administrator, etc)
solution: 1) Verify that the CRS stack is available. ( 'crsctl check crs' ) 2) Verify that ASM is running. ( 'srvctl status asm' ) 3) Verify that the user is running with administrative access.

message: Failed to remove ACFS file system configuration for disk group {0} and volume {1}
cause: Cannot remove the ACFS file system configuration for the specified disk group and volume.
solution: 1) Verify that the CRS stack is available. ( 'crsctl check crs' ) 2) Verify that ASM is running. ( 'srvctl status asm' ) 3) Verify that the user is running with administrative access.

message: Failed to retrieve listener associated with ASM {0}
cause: Failed to retrieve listener associated with ASM.
solution: Ensure that user has read permissions on ASM resource and then retry. Also, ensure that listener specified in ASM resource's start dependencies exists.

message: Failed to associate listener {0} with ASM {1}
cause: Failed to associate given listener with ASM.
solution: Ensure that user has update permissions on ASM resource and then retry.

message: Failed to retrieve the diskgroup associated with the volume device {0}
cause: Unable to retrieve the diskgroup associated with the given volume device using "asmcmd volinfo -g <volume_name>" command.
solution: Make sure that the asm instance is running; the asmcmd utility exists and the underlying ofs devices are accessible.

message: Unable to retrieve the diskgroup {0} associated with the volume device {1}
cause: The ACFS file system resource for the specified volume device path was unable to be retrieved. Possible causes: 1) CRS stack was not available. 2) ASM instance was not running. 3) User was not running with an account with administrative access. (root, Administrator, etc) 4) Disk group is not mounted.
solution: 1) Verify that the CRS stack is available. ( 'crsctl check crs' ) 2) Verify that ASM is running. ( 'srvctl status asm' ) 3) Verify that the user is running with administrative access. 4) Verify that the disk group is mounted.

message: ASM listener {0} does not exist
cause: ASM listener is not registered with Oracle Clusterware.
solution: Run 'srvctl add listener -l <lsnr_name>' command with <lsnr_name> as in above error message, or if there is another listener registered with Oracle clusterware, then try 'srvctl modify asm -l <lsnr_name>'

message: ACFS file system resource does not exist for volume device {0}
cause: The ACFS file system resource with the specified volume device was not registered with the Oracle Clusterware.
solution: Use 'srvctl add filesystem' command to create an ACFS file system resource.

message: ACFS file system resource does not exist in Oracle Clusterware
cause: No ACFS file system resource was registered with the Oracle clusterware.
solution: Use 'srvctl add filesystem' command to create an ACFS file system resource.

message: Unable to determine the databases that use the disk group {0}
cause: Unable to retrieve databases that have dependencies on the disk group.
solution: Make sure that the crs stack is up; the user has read permissions on database CRS resources and then retry.

message: An Oracle Restart environment-specific API was invoked in an Oracle Clusterware environment.
cause: Internal error.
solution: Contact Oracle Support Services.

message: Failed to retrieve the diskgroup discovery string of ASM {0}
cause: An attempt to retrieve the diskgroup discovery string for ASM failed.
solution: Retry the request after ensuring that the CRS stack is running, the ASM resource has been configured, and the user has read permission on ASM resource.

message: Failed to update the diskgroup discovery string {0} of ASM {1}
cause: An attempt to update the diskgroup discovery string for ASM failed.
solution: Retry the request after ensuring that the CRS stack is running, the ASM resource has been configured, and the user has update permission on ASM resource.

message: Volume device {0} does not exist
cause: The supplied volume device does not exist.
solution: Use asmca to create the volume device and then run 'srvctl add filesystem' command again.

message: Failed to check the existence of volume device {0}
cause: Failed to execute acfsutil command to check for the existence of the supplied volume device.
solution: Review the underlying error messages that provide the details of why acfsutil execution failed. Resolve the reported problem and retry the command.

message: Failed to validate disk group {0} of volume device {1}
cause: Failed to execute acfsutil command to validate the disk group of the volume device.
solution: Review the underlying error messages that provide the details of why acfsutil execution failed. Resolve the reported problem and retry 'srvctl add filesystem' command.

message: Diskgroup {0} is not valid for volume device {1}
cause: The supplied diskgroup does not match the underlying diskgroup created for the supplied volume device.
solution: Execute 'srvctl add filesystem' command with the correct disk group value.

message: Failed to validate volume {0} of volume device {1}
cause: Failed to execute acfsutil command to validate the volume of the volume device.
solution: Review the underlying error messages that provide the details of why acfsutil execution failed. Resolve the reported problem and retry 'srvctl add filesystem' command.

message: Volume {0} is not valid for volume device {1}
cause: The supplied volume does not match the underlying volume created for the supplied volume device.
solution: Execute 'srvctl add filesystem' command with the correct volume value.

message: ACFS is not supported on this platform
cause: A filesystem operation was requested on an unsupported platform.
solution: Run srvctl filesystem command on a supported platform.

message: File system for volume device {0} exists in the ACFS registry
cause: File system for the specified volume device was registered in the ACFS registry. File system can either be in the ACFS registry or registered as a CRS resource, but not both.
solution: Either run 'acfsutil registry -d' to delete the volume device from the ACFS registry or run 'srvctl add filesystem' with a different volume device.

message: Unable to find ACFS file system resource for volume device {0} because of inability to get the canonical form of the volume device
cause: An internally-issued 'advmutil canonical' command failed and the volume device recorded in the ACFS file system resource did not match the specified volume device.
solution: Review the underlying error messages that provide the details of why advmutil execution failed. Resolve the reported problem and retry.

message: The user "{0}" could not be found on the cluster
cause: The user specified as the file system owner/user could not be found.
solution: Enter the name of an existing user or the owner of the specified file system.

message: Invalid mount point path {0} because specified mount point path was a remote path
cause: The specified mount point path was a remote path.
solution: Make sure that the mount point path was not a remote path.

message: Unable to retrieve the canonical form of the volume device for disk group {0} and volume {1}
cause: The ACFS file system resource for the specified canonical form of the volume device path was not retrieved.
solution: 1) Make sure that the CRS stack is available. ( 'crsctl check crs' ) 2) Review the accompanying error messages for details about the failure. Retry after resolving those issues.

message: Unable to upgrade ACFS from version {0} to version {1}
cause: Failed to upgrade ACFS from one version to another version.
solution: Review the accompanying error messages for details about the failure. Retry after resolving those issues.

message: Parameter {0} value is not valid
cause: This is an internal error. The value for the specified parameter is null or empty string.
solution: Contact Oracle Support Services.

message: Failed to retrieve install group: {0}
cause: An attempt to retrieve the install group failed.
solution: Examine the accompanying error messages for details.

message: Failed to update install group: {0}
cause: An attempt to set the install group failed.
solution: Examine the accompanying error messages for details.

message: Version for module {0} is not available
cause: An attempt to retrieve the version information for specified module failed.
solution: Examine the accompanying error messages for details.

message: Unknown identifier {0} specified for checking result of operation
cause: Failed to retrieve the result from the exception data using the specified identifier because the exception did not have the specified identifier.
solution: This is an internal error. Contact Oracle Support Services.

message: Parameter {0} is not an absolute path
cause: The specified parameter is not an absolute directory path.
solution: Provide an absolute directory path.

message: Path {0} is not a directory
cause: The specified path is not a directory.
solution: Provide a directory path.

message: Path {0} does not exist
cause: The specified path did not exist.

solution: Retry the operation after either including the current server where this database is running in the given candidate server list or stopping the database.

message: Failed to update candidate servers to {0} of the server pool hosting RAC One Node database {1}
cause: An attempt to update the candidate servers of the server pool hosting RAC One Node Database has failed.
solution: Review the accompanying error messages for details about failure. Retry after resolving those issues.

message: The database {0} is not hosted by a server pool
cause: An attempt to query the server pool for given database failed because this database is not hosted by a server pool. This is most likely due to a program calling cluster environment API in Oracle Restart environment.
solution: Examine the accompanying error messages for details and contact Oracle Support Services.

message: The {0} TAF policy is not valid for RAC One Node service {1}
cause: A TAF policy other than BASIC or NONE was specified for RAC One Node service.
solution: Specify BASIC or NONE TAF policy and retry the operation.

message: The cardinality of {0} is not valid for RAC One Node database or service {1}
cause: An invalid cardinality was specified for RAC One Node database or service.
solution: Specify a SINGLETON cardinality and retry the operation.

message: The {0} management policy is not valid for RAC One Node database {1}
cause: A management policy other than AUTOMATIC was specified for RAC One Node database.
solution: Specify AUTOMATIC management policy and retry the operation.

message: {0} API is not supported on RAC One Node database environment
cause: Internal error.
solution: Contact Oracle Support Services.

message: Database {0} is not a RAC One Node database
cause: The specified database is not a RAC One Node database.
solution: Provide database name for a RAC One Node database.

message: The server pool {0} of administrator-managed database {1} has no candidate servers
cause: Either no instance had been added to the database or this database's server pool was altered inapproprately.
solution: If no instance was added to the database yet, try to add an instance to this database, for example by using 'srvctl add instance' command, and then retry. Otherwise, contact Oracle Support Services.

message: Failed to convert the configuration of RAC One Node database {0} into its equivalent configuration for RAC database
cause: Internal error.
solution: Review the accompanying error messages and contact Oracle Support Services.

message: AUTOMATIC management policy cannot be used for the service {0} when the database {1} is not AUTOMATIC
cause: An attempt to create/modify a service failed because the management policy specified for the service is AUTOMATIC but the database's management policy is not AUTOMATIC.
solution: Make sure that the provided service's management policy is MANUAL or NORESTART when running 'srvctl add service' or 'srvctl modify service' command.

message: Failed to retrieve EDITION for service {0}
cause: An attempt to retrieve the EDITION attribute of the specified database failed.
solution: Examine the accompanying error messages for details.

message: Failed to convert the configuration of RAC One Node database {0} into its equivalent RAC database configuration because RAC One Node database is running on a different server {1} than the given target server {2}
cause: A target server was specified that was different from the server where the RAC One Node database is running.
solution: Either supply the server where RAC One Node Database is running now as target server or stop the database and retry.

message: Failed to update instance name {0} for database {1}
cause: An attempt to update instance name for the specified database failed.
solution: Examine the accompanying error messages for details.

message: Failed to convert the configuration of cluster database {0} into its equivalent RAC One Node database configuration
cause: An attempt to convert the specified cluster database to RAC One Node database failed.
solution: Review the accompanying error messages and retry after resolving these errors or contact Oracle Support Services.

message: Failed to convert the configuration of cluster database {0} into its equivalent RAC One Node database configuration because cluster database is running on more than one server {1}
cause: User attempted conversion of a cluster database to RAC One Node database that was running on more than one servers.
solution: Stop this database on all but one server and retry.

message: Failed to convert the configuration of cluster database {0} into its equivalent RAC One Node database configuration because cluster database has more than one server pool {1} to control its placement
cause: User attempted conversion of a cluster database that had more than one server pool to control its placement.
solution: Update configuration of this database by either 'srvctl modify database' or if this database has services that are in their own respective server pool, then removing all but one of its services via 'srvctl remove service' and then retry.

message: Failed to convert the configuration of cluster database {0} into its equivalent configuration for RAC One Node database due to its services {1} having {2} TAF policy
cause: This database has services that have TAF policy (e.g. PRECONNECT) that is not supported by RAC One Node Database.
solution: Either modify the TAF policy of these services to either BASIC or NONE using 'srvctl modify service' or remove these services using 'srvctl remove service' and then retry.

message: Failed to convert the configuration of cluster database {0} into its equivalent configuration for RAC One Node database because none of its services have {1} management policy
cause: An attempt to convert a cluster database configuration into its equivalent configuration for RAC One Node database was rejected because all services of the given database have MANUAL management policy.
solution: Modify the management policy of at least one of these services to AUTOMATIC using 'srvctl modify service ... -y AUTOMATIC' command and then retry.

message: Invalid database type {0}
cause: The database type supplied is not valid.
solution: Supply a valid database type.

message: Target node must be specified when initiating an online relocation of administrator managed RAC One Node database {0}
cause: The target node was not specified when requesting online relocation on administrator managed RAC One Node database.
solution: Use 'srvctl relocate database' command with -n option.

message: Online relocation request for RAC One Node database {0} was rejected because this database is not running
cause: RAC One Node database was not running.
solution: Start the database by issuing the 'srvctl start database' command and then retry.

message: Online relocation failed for RAC One Node database {0}
cause: Online relocation of the given database was unsuccessful.
solution: Either run 'srvctl relocate database -a' command to abort the online relocation or run 'srvctl relocate database -n' command to perform online relocation of the database to the given target node.

message: Invalid online relocation status {0}
cause: This is an internal error.
solution: Review the accompanying error messages and contact Oracle Support Services.

message: Failed to modify database {0}
cause: Failed to modify database.
solution: Make sure that the CRS stack is up and running and then retry.

message: An online relocation request for RAC One Node database {0} is already active
cause: The given database has an already active online relocation request.
solution: Either specify another database in the 'srvctl relocate database' command or abort the in-progress request with 'srvctl relocate database -a' command.

message: An online relocation request for RAC One Node database {0} has failed
cause: An online relocation request for the database has failed and the supplied target node was not the same as that in the failed request.
solution: Use 'srvctl status database' command to query the target node of the failed online relocation request. Either run 'srvctl relocate database -a' command to abort the failed request or 'srvctl relocate database -n' command with with the correct target node.

message: The supplied node {0} is not available in the {1} server pool
cause: Supplied node was not in the Free server pool.
solution: Supply node from the Free server pool.

message: Failed to determine the status of the online relocation request for RAC One Node database {0}
cause: Unable to determine the status of the online relocation request for given RAC One Node database.
solution: Examine the accompanying error messages for details.

message: Invalid online relocation state {0}
cause: This is an internal error.
solution: Review the accompanying error messages and contact Oracle Support Services.

message: Failed to abort the online relocation request for RAC One Node database {0}
cause: Failed to abort the online relocation of the RAC One Node database.
solution: Review the accompanying error messages for details about failure. Retry after resolving those issues.

message: A failed online relocation request for RAC One Node database {0} does not exist
cause: The supplied RAC One Node database does not have a failed online relocation request.
solution: Supply a RAC One Node database that has a failed online relocation request.

message: The online relocation timeout value {0} is not within the range of between {1} and {2}
cause: The specified online relocation timeout value was not within the required range.
solution: Supply a value within the required range.

message: Configuration of database {0} has already been upgraded to version {1}
cause: The supplied database was already upgraded.
solution: Supply a database of a lower version.

message: Failed to upgrade configuration of services {0} to version {1}
cause: Failed to upgrade the service configuration.
solution: Review the accompanying error messages. If you are unable to resolve the problem, contact Oracle Support Services.

message: Failed to upgrade configuration of database {0} to version {1}
cause: Failed to upgrade the database configuration.
solution: Review the accompanying error messages for details about failure. Retry after resolving those issues.

message: Failed to upgrade configuration of service type to version {0}
cause: Failed to upgrade the service type configuration.
solution: Review the accompanying error messages and contact Oracle Support Services.

message: Failed to upgrade configuration of database type to version {0}
cause: Failed to upgrade the database type configuration.
solution: Review the accompanying error messages for details about failure. Retry after resolving those issues.

message: Failed to retrieve service resource {0} for non cluster database {1}
cause: An attempt to get the specified service failed because the database provided is a single instance and not a cluster database.
solution: Make sure that Oracle Clusterware is configured, specify a service defined for cluster database, and then retry.

message: TAF policy 'PRECONNECT' cannot be used to add a service for single instance database {0}
cause: Failed to create a service because provided TAF specification can not be used with a single instance database.
solution: Retry after removing 'PRECONNECT' TAF policy.

message: Failed to enable or disable service {0} on particular nodes for non-cluster single instance database {1}
cause: An attempt to enable or disable the service on particular nodes for single instance database failed. Such enable or disable operations are not applicable to services defined for single instance databases in Oracle Restart.
solution: Specify a service defined for database which is running on cluster or do not specify nodes.

message: Failed to detect whether the standby database {0} supports the Data Guard protection mode
cause: An attempt has failed to determine whether the standby database supports the configured Data Guard protection mode.
solution: Review the accompanying error messages for details about the failure and retry the command after resolving those issues.

message: Cannot update server pool to {0} for RAC One Node database service {1}
cause: Attempt to update server pool of a RAC One Node database service was rejected because placement of this service is controlled by the server pool hosting the underlying database.
solution: Try updating the server pool controlling the placement of the database via 'srvctl modify database' command or its equivalent.

message: Cannot update server pool to {0} for single instance database service {1}
cause: Attempt to update server pool of a single instance (non-RAC) database service was rejected because placement of this service is controlled by the server pool hosting the underlying database.
solution: Try updating the server pool controlling the placement of the database via 'srvctl modify database' command or its equivalent.

message: Cannot update server pool to {0} for database service {1}
cause: Attempt to update server pool of database service was rejected because a subpool server pool was specified.
solution: Supply a first-level server pool that is not a subpool of any other server pool and retry the operation.

message: The cardinality {0} is not valid for single instance database service {1}
cause: An invalid cardinality was specified for single instance (non-RAC) database.
solution: Retry after specifying a SINGLETON cardinality in 'srvctl modify service' command or its equivalent.

message: Service {0} defined for RAC One Node database {1} cannot be started on more than one node
cause: An attempt to start the specified service failed because RAC One Node service cannot be started on more than one node.
solution: Retry after specifying one node to start the service on.

message: Failed to retrieve the version of database {0}
cause: An attempt to retrieve the VERSION resource attribute has failed.
solution: Review the accompanying error messages for details about failure. Retry after resolving those issues.

message: Option to remove the target node was not allowed for aborting online relocation of policy-managed RAC One Node database {0}
cause: Option -r was specified in a request to abort online relocation on policy managed RAC One Node database.
solution: Use 'srvctl relocate database -a' command without -r option.

message: 'PRECONNECT' TAF policy cannot be used to create service {0} on policy managed database {1}
cause: Failed to create a service because a policy managed database cannot have service with PRECONNECT TAF policy.
solution: Retry after supplying 'BASIC' or 'NONE' TAF policy.

message: The database {0} is policy-managed and an administrator-managed service {1} cannot be created on it
cause: The specified database does not support administrator-managed services.
solution: Provide a database which supports administrator-managed services.

message: Failed to add service {0} to database {1} because database is already at maximum services limit of {2}
cause: Attempt to add a new service to database was rejected because database has already reached the maximum services limit.
solution: Retry after removing a service from this database via 'srvctl remove service' command, or contact Oracle Support Services.

message: The stop request on instance {0} of standby database {1} was rejected to prevent termination of the primary database
cause: The attempt to stop this instance of the standby database was rejected because the configured Data Guard protection mode required this instance to be running to prevent termination of the primary database.
solution: Retry the stop request after stopping the primary database or downgrading the protection mode.

message: Configuration of database {0} has already been downgraded to version {1} for database {2}
cause: The supplied database was already downgraded.
solution: Supply a database of a higher version.

message: Downgrade from current version {0} to version {1} is not supported for database {2}
cause: An unsupported version was specified for downgrading the database.
solution: Check that the versions provided are correct.

message: Failed to downgrade configuration of services {0} to version {1}
cause: A request to downgrade the service configuration failed.
solution: Review the accompanying error messages. If you are unable to resolve the problem, contact Oracle Support Services.

message: Failed to downgrade configuration of database {0} to version {1}
cause: A request to downgrade the database configuration failed.
solution: Review the accompanying error messages for details about failure. Retry after resolving those issues.

message: Failed to update administrator-managed database {0} to use server pool {1}
cause: Attempt to update administrator-managed database was rejected because administrator-managed database cannot be moved to another subpool.
solution: Retry after supplying a first-level server pool in 'srvctl modify database' command to convert administrator-managed database to policy-managed database.

message: Failed to update policy-managed database {0} to use server pools {1}
cause: Attempt to update policy-managed database was rejected because specified server pools do not include all server pools hosting services of this database.
solution: Either include all server pools hosting services of this database in the supplied server pool list or specify one server pool to move all services into one server pool in 'srvctl modify database' command and retry.

message: Failed to retrieve preferred instance of service {0} of RAC One Node database {1}
cause: Attempt to retrieve preferred instance of service belonging to RAC One Node database failed because database is either in failed online relocation state or undergoing online relocation.
solution: Check the status of online relocation via 'srvctl status database' command. If online relocation status is reported as active, then retry after online relocation completes. If online relocation status is reported as failed, then repair the configuration via 'srvctl relocate database ... -a' command and then retry.

message: The start options {2} can not be used while starting service {0} and its database {1}
cause: An attempt to start the service was rejected because the specified start options can not be used with service when the databse is not running.
solution: Remove the specified start options and then retry.

message: The start options {1} can not be used while starting services for database {0}
cause: An attempt to start the services was rejected because the specified start options can not be used with services when the databse is not running.
solution: Remove the specified start options and then retry.

message: RAC One Node database {0} does not have enough servers in its server pool {1} to initiate an online relocation
cause: Online relocation request was rejected because there were less than two servers in the server pool of the specified RAC One Node database.
solution: Make sure that the minimum and maximum size of the server pool are set properly.

message: The service name {0} cannot be same as the database default service name {1}
cause: An attempt to create the service was rejected because the given service name is same as the database default service name.
solution: Retry after supplying a service name that is different than the database default service name.

message: Cannot start RAC One Node database {0} because a failure has occurred while trying to clean up an earlier failed online relocation
cause: An attempt to start a RAC One Node database was rejected because a failure has occurred while trying to clean up an earlier failed online relocation.
solution: Use 'srvctl status database' command to query the target node of the failed online relocation process. Either run 'srvctl relocate database' with -a option or with -n option with the target node thus discovered.

message: An instance with name "{0}" already exists on node {1}
cause: Unable to add an instance to the database on the specified node because an instance with the same name was found on another node.
solution: Use 'srvctl modify instance' command to change the name of the existing instance, or use a different instance name in the 'srvctl add instance -i <inst>' command.

message: Service {0} of database {1} is still running
cause: An attempt to remove RAC One Node service failed because the given service was still running.
solution: Stop the service and then retry the command.

message: Administrator-managed RAC database {0} has more than one instance
cause: Failed to convert RAC database to RAC One Node database because there was more than one instance.
solution: Use 'srvct remove instance' command to remove all but one instance and then run 'srvctl convert database -c RACONENODE'.

message: Unable to downgrade RAC One Node database {0}
cause: Failed to downgrade RAC One Node database to an earlier version because there was no RAC One Node specific configuration in the earlier version.
solution: None

message: Online relocation of database "{0}" failed but database was restored to its original state
cause: Online relocation of the given database was unsuccessful, therefore the database was restored to its original state.
solution: See accompanying messages for online relocation failure.

message: The service name {0} contains illegal characters {1}
cause: An attempt to create the service was rejected because the given service name contains illegal characters.
solution: Retry after supplying a service name that contains characters from its character set ({a-zA-Z0-9_} for the base name, and {a-zA-Z0-9_$#} for the domain name if needed)."

message: The {0} management policy is not valid for RAC One Node database service {1}
cause: A management policy other than AUTOMATIC was specified for RAC One Node database service.
solution: Either specify AUTOMATIC management policy for this service or modify management policy of another service of this database to AUTOMATIC, such as via 'srvctl modify service' command, and then retry the current operation.

message: An attempt to remove service {0} of database {1} was rejected because this is the last service with {2} management policy. A RAC One Node database must have at least one service with {2} management policy.
cause: An attempt was made to remove the last service of a RAC One Node database having AUTOMATIC management policy.
solution: Add another service with AUTOMATIC management policy, for example by using 'srvctl add service ... -y AUTOMATIC' command, or modify the management policy of an existing service to AUTOMATIC, using 'srvctl modify service' command, before removing the given service.

message: Failed to retrieve ASM Cluster Filesystem resource {0} for database {1}.
cause: The ASM Cluster Filesystem resource was not registered in Oracle Clusterware.
solution: Create the ASM Cluster Filesystem resource using 'srvctl add filesystem' command and then retry.

message: Failed to retrieve ASM Cluster Filesystem list for database {0}.
cause: Failed to retrieve the ASM Cluster Filesystems of the specified database.
solution: Review the accompanying error messages for details about failure. Retry after resolving those issues.

message: Failed to convert administrator-managed RAC database {0} to RAC One Node database because the database had no instance added
cause: Attempt to convert RAC database to RAC One Node database was rejected because database did not have any instance added.
solution: Use 'srvct add instance' command to add an instance and then run 'srvctl convert database -c RACONENODE'.

message: An attempt to access configuration of database {0} was rejected because its version {1} differs from the program version {2}. Instead run the program from {3}.
cause: An attempt was made to access configuration of database that is of different version than that of the program.
solution: Make sure that database configuration version and the program version are same and then retry. For example, try the operation using srvctl from the ORACLE_HOME mentioned in the error message.

message: Failed to modify database {0} to use server pool {1}
cause: An attempt to modify the database to use the given server pool has failed.
solution: Review the accompanying error messages for details about the failure. For example, a failure could happen if the database owner does not have execute permissions on the given server pool. In this case, use 'srvctl config database -d <db_unqiue_name>' command to find out the database owner's username, create a server pool as that user, and then supply that server pool as argument when retrying the command.

message: Failed to upgrade configuration of database {0} to version {1} in new Oracle home {2}
cause: Failed to upgrade the database configuration.
solution: Review the accompanying error messages for details about failure. Retry after resolving those issues.

message: Failed to upgrade configuration of database {0} because database version {1} is an unsupported version for upgrade
cause: Version of the database was not supported for upgrade.
solution: None

message: Failed to downgrade configuration of database {0} to version {1} in new Oracle home {2}
cause: Failed to downgrade the database configuration.
solution: Review the accompanying error messages for details about failure. Retry after resolving those issues.

message: Failed to downgrade configuration of database {0} to version {1} because the specified version is unsupported for downgrade
cause: Specified version was not supported for downgrade.
solution: Specify a version that is 10.1 or later.

message: Unable to downgrade configuration of single instance database {0} to version {1}
cause: Single instance database was specified.
solution: Remove the single instance database configuration. 11.2 Clusterware cannot manage pre-11.2 single instance databases.

message: Unable to downgrade configuration of RAC One Node database {0} to version {1}
cause: RAC One Node database was specified.
solution: Convert the administrator-managed RAC One Node database to an administrator-managed RAC database using 'srvctl convert database' command and then retry.

message: Unable to downgrade configuration of policy-managed RAC database {0} to version {1}
cause: Policy-managed RAC database was specified.
solution: Remove the 11.2 database configuration and use pre-11.2 srvctl to re-create the configuration.

message: Failed to get attributes for database {0}
cause: Failed to get attributes for the database.
solution: Make sure that the CRS stack is up and running and then retry.

message: Failed to downgrade configuration of database {0} to version {1} because the database has dependency on ASM Cluster File System
cause: Specified database was dependent on ASM Cluster File System.
solution: None

message: Unable to downgrade configuration of database {0} because its database role of {1} is not supported in version {2}
cause: Database role of specified database was not supported in the specified version.
solution: Modify the database role using 'srvctl modify database' command and then retry this command.

message: Failed to upgrade configuration of database {0} to version {1} in new Oracle home {2}. Also failed to remove the internal server pool configuration.
cause: Failed to upgrade the database configuration.
solution: Review the accompanying error messages for details about failure. Retry after resolving those issues.

message: Unable to convert RAC database {0} to RAC One Node database because the database had no service added
cause: Attempt to convert RAC database to RAC One Node database was rejected because the database did not have any service configured. A RAC One Node database must always have one service.
solution: Use 'srvct add service' command to add a service and then run 'srvctl convert database -c RACONENODE'.

message: Failed to start instance {0} of database {1} because an instance having same name was already running on node {2}
cause: An attempt to start an instance with the given name was rejected because another instance with same name was already running on another node.
solution: Either supply a different instance name or stop the running instance with the same name and then retry.

message: Failed to start service {0} of RAC One Node database {1} on the given node {2} because the database was running on node {3}
cause: An attempt to start the specified service on the given node was rejected because RAC One Node database is running on a node different than the given node.
solution: Either omit the node option or supply the node where the database is running.

message: Addition of database version {0} is not allowed using srvctl version {1}
cause: The versions of srvctl used and database to be created did not match.
solution: Use the same version of srvctl as database.

message: Online relocation of RAC One Node Data Guard standby database "{0}" was rejected because the database is in Data Guard maximum protection mode
cause: An online relocation request was rejected because the specified database is operating in Data Guard maximum protection mode.
solution: Downgrade the protection mode to maximum availability and retry the online relocation.

message: Failed to stop resources running from Oracle home {0}
cause: Attempt to stop one or more resources in the specified Oracle home failed.
solution: for the individual resource stop failure and perform the steps for each resource that failed to stop.

message: Failed to start resources in Oracle home {0}
cause: Attempt to start one or more resources in the specified Oracle home failed.
solution: for the individual resource start failure and perform the steps for each resource that failed to start.

message: Failed to stop resources running from CRS home {0}
cause: Attempt to stop one or more resources in the specified CRS home failed.
solution: for the individual resource stop failure and perform the steps for each resource that failed to stop.

message: Failed to start resources in CRS home {0}
cause: Attempt to start one or more resources in the specified CRS home failed.
solution: for the individual resource start failure and perform the steps for each resource that failed to start.

message: Failed to stop service
cause: Attempt to stop a Service resource in the specified oracle home failed.
solution: Review the error messages for possible reasons and if needed, use 'srvctl stop service -d <db_unique_name>' to stop the service.

message: Failed to stop database
cause: Attempt to stop the database resource in the specified oracle home failed.
solution: Review the error messages for possible reasons, correct the error and use 'srvctl stop database -d <db_unique_name>' to stop the database.

cause: Attempt to stop the Listener resource in the specified oracle home failed.
solution: Review the error messages for possible reasons, correct the error and use 'srvctl stop listener' to stop the Listener.

message: Failed to stop Listener
cause: Attempt to stop the Listener resource in CRS home failed.
solution: Review the error messages for possible reasons, correct the error and use 'srvctl stop listener' to stop the Listener.

message: Failed to start service
cause: Attempt to start a Service resource in the specified oracle home failed.
solution: Review the error messages for possible reasons, correct the error and use 'srvctl start service -d <db_unique_name>' to start the service.

message: Failed to start database
cause: Attempt to start the database resource in the specified oracle home failed.
solution: Review the error messages for possible reasons, correct the error and use 'srvctl start database -d <db_unique_name>' to start the database.

message: Failed to start Listener
cause: Attempt to start the Listener resource in the specified Oracle home failed.
solution: Review the error messages for possible reasons, correct the error and use 'srvctl start listener' to start the Listener.

message: Failed to start Listener
cause: Attempt to start the Listener resource in the specified CRS home failed.
solution: Review the error messages for possible reasons, correct the error and use 'srvctl start listener' to start the Listener.

message: Failed to stop EONS
cause: Attempt to stop the EONS resource in the specified CRS home failed.
solution: Review the error messages for possible reasons, correct the error and use 'srvctl stop nodeapps' to stop the EONS resource.

message: Failed to start EONS
cause: Attempt to start the EONS resource in the specified CRS home failed.
solution: Review the error messages for possible reasons, correct the error and use 'srvctl start nodeapps' to start the EONS resource.

message: Failed to stop ONS
cause: Attempt to stop the ONS resource in the specified CRS home failed.
solution: Review the error messages for possible reasons, correct the error and use 'srvctl stop nodeapps' to stop the ONS resource.

message: Failed to start ONS
cause: Attempt to start the ONS resource in the specified CRS home failed.
solution: Review the error messages for possible reasons, correct the error and use 'srvctl start nodeapps' to start the ONS resource.

message: Failed to stop GSD resource
cause: Attempt to stop the GSD resource in the specified CRS home failed.
solution: Review the error messages for possible reasons, correct the error and use 'srvctl stop nodeapps' to stop the GSD resource.

message: Failed to start GSD resource
cause: Attempt to start the GSD resource in the specified CRS home failed.
solution: Review the error messages for possible reasons, correct the error and use 'srvctl start nodeapps' to start the GSD resource.

message: Failed to stop VIP resource
cause: Attempt to stop the VIP resource in the specified CRS home failed.
solution: Review the error messages for possible reasons, correct the error and use 'srvctl stop vip -n <node_name>' to stop the VIP resource.

message: Failed to start VIP resource
cause: Attempt to start the VIP resource in the specified CRS home failed.
solution: Review the error messages for possible reasons, correct the error and use 'srvctl start vip -n <node_name>' to start the VIP resource.

message: Failed to stop Network resource
cause: Attempt to stop the Network resource in the specified CRS home failed.
solution: Review the error messages for possible reasons, correct the error and use 'srvctl stop nodeapps' to stop the Network resource.

message: Failed to start Network resource
cause: Attempt to start the Network resource in the specified CRS home failed.
solution: Review the error messages for possible reasons, correct the error and use 'srvctl start nodeapps' to start the Network resource.

message: Failed to stop SCAN VIP resource
cause: Attempt to stop the SCAN VIP resource in the specified CRS home failed.
solution: Review the error messages for possible reasons, correct the error and use 'srvctl stop scan' to stop the SCAN VIP resource.

message: Failed to start SCAN VIP resource
cause: Attempt to start the SCAN VIP resource in the specified CRS home failed.
solution: Review the error messages for possible reasons, correct the error and use 'srvctl start scan' to start the SCAN VIP resource.

message: Failed to stop SCAN Listener resource
cause: Attempt to stop the SCAN Listener resource in the specified CRS home failed.
solution: Review the error messages for possible reasons, correct the error and use 'srvctl stop scan_listener' to stop the SCAN Listener resource.

solution: If wild card causes the problem, provide interface name and subnet without wild card.

solution: Delete the interface with invalid key using 'oifcfg delif -global <if_name> [-force]'. Reset the interface using 'oifcfg setif -global <if_name>/<subnet>:<if_type>'.

message: Failed to retrieve the OCR registry key [ string ] for interface string on node string
cause: An attempt to get the registry key for the specified interface from OCR failed.
solution: Delete the interface with invalid key using 'oifcfg delif -node <nodename> <if_name> [-force]'. Reset the interface using 'oifcfg setif -node <nodename> <if_name>/<subnet>:<if_type>'.

message: Failed to initialize the cluster registry
cause: The Oracle Cluster Registry could not be accessed. The possible causes are: 1. The cluster registry has not been formatted. 2. The cluster registry location is not accessible. 3. The cluster registry location has incorrect permissions. 4. Oracle Clusterware is not running.
solution: 1. Run the 'ocrcheck' command to confirm that the OCR is formatted and usable. 2. Run 'ocrcheck -config' command to retrieve the configured locations, and verify that each location is accessible and has the correct permissions via native platform or OS methods. If a location is an ASM disk group, verify that the disk group exists and is mounted. 3. Run 'crsctl check crs' command to verify that Oracle Clusterware is running.

cause: The Oracle Cluster Registry could not be accessed. The possible causes are: 1. The cluster registry has not been formatted. 2. The cluster registry location is not accessible. 3. The cluster registry location has incorrect permissions. 4. Oracle Clusterware is not running.
solution: 1. Run the 'ocrcheck' command to confirm that the OCR is formatted and usable. 2. In case the cluster registry is already configured, execute the 'ocrcheck' command to retrieve the total size, and ensure that the size of the device to be added is large enough for use by cluster registry.

solution: Install and configure Oracle Clusterware.

message: Oracle Cluster Registry configurations are not compatible
cause: Cluster registry configuration on this node did not match with another node in the cluster.
solution: Retrieve the cluster registry configuration using 'ocrcheck -config' command on all nodes in the cluster. Fix the configuration on this node and make it consistent using 'ocrconfig -repair' command.

solution: Change the configuration of the cluster registry to a supported storage type. Refer to Oracle documentation for an exhaustive list for each platform.

message: Requested block number is not allocated from Oracle Cluster Registry
cause: The requested block number is not allocated from Oracle Cluster Registry.
solution: Retry the operation with another block number.

message: Requested block has an invalid header
