message: Cannot proceed while the Cluster Ready Service is running
cause: The Cluster Ready Service was running.
solution: Use the 'crsctl stop crs' command to shutdown the Cluster Ready Service on the local node.

message: Insufficient permission to proceed. Require privileged user
cause: User was not a privileged user.
solution: Run the command again using a privileged user.

message: Invalid parameter
cause: Input parameter was not valid.
solution: Check log file for more information.

message: Storage too small
cause: Specified storage was too small to mirror OCR content.
solution: Execute the 'ocrcheck' command to retrieve the total size, and ensure that the size of the device to be added is large enough for use by cluster registry.

message: Failed to backup OCR
cause: Unable to take a backup of OCR.
solution: Check availability of the cluster registry and the available free space on the file system where the manual backup will be stored. Use ocrconfig -backuploc to specify a new backup location if necessary. Check the CRS log file for more information.

message: Auto backups for the Oracle Cluster Registry are not available
cause: Auto backups for the Oracle Cluster Registry were not yet created. They are created once every four hours.
solution: No action required.

message: Manual backups for the Oracle Cluster Registry are not available
cause: Manual backups for the Oracle Cluster Registry were not yet created.
solution: Manual backups can be created using 'ocrconfig -manualbackup' command.

message: Oracle Cluster Registry backup locations were retrieved from a local copy
cause: The Oracle Cluster Registry files were not accessible. Information about the cluster registry backups is also maintained in the Oracle Local Registry. The information displayed has been retrieved from the Oracle Local Registry. This information may be outdated.
solution: Run 'ocrconfig -showbackup' command from another node in the cluster. Compare the output of the 'ocrconfig -showbackup' on this node with output of the same command from other nodes in the cluster to determine the latest backup copy.

message: Cannot configure another Oracle Cluster Registry location because the maximum number of Oracle Cluster Registry locations (5) have been configured
cause: The maximum number of Oracle Cluster Registry locations (5) had been configured.
solution: (Optional) Verify the configuration using the 'ocrcheck -config' command. Delete an Oracle Cluster Registry device by executing 'ocrconfig -delete <existing location>' command, and retry the operation.

message: Cannot delete or replace the only configured Oracle Cluster Registry location
cause: A delete or replace operation was performed when there was only 1 configured Oracle Cluster Registry location. The above listed operation can only be performed when there are at least 2 configured Oracle Cluster Registry locations.
solution: Execute 'ocrconfig -add <new location>' to add the new Oracle Cluster Registry location followed by 'ocrconfig -delete <existing location>' command.

message: The Oracle Cluster Registry location is already configured
cause: The location to be added was identical to a configured Oracle Cluster Registry location.
solution: Verify the configuration using the 'ocrcheck -config' command. Ensure that the location to be added is not already configured.

message: The Oracle Cluster Registry location to be added is not usable
cause: The Oracle Cluster Registry location to be added did not exist, wasn't mounted correctly, did not have the required permissions, or did not have the sufficient disk space.
solution: Ensure that the location exists, that it is mounted correctly and visible to all nodes in the cluster, that its permissions are correct, and that it has sufficient disk space. If trying to add an ASM Oracle Cluster Registry location, check for related entries in the ASM alert log file for more details.

message: The Oracle Cluster Registry location to be added is an ASM disk
cause: The Oracle Cluster Registry location to be added is already in use by ASM.
solution: Specify a Oracle Cluster Registry location that is not currently in use. Use the 'crsctl query css votedisk' command to get the list of voting files used by CSS. Use the 'asmcmd lsdsk --member' command to get the list of disks used by ASM. Specify a location that is not in either list.

message: The Oracle Cluster Registry location to be added is a CSS voting file
cause: The Oracle Cluster Registry location to be added is already configured as a CSS voting file.
solution: Specify a Oracle Cluster Registry location that is not currently in use. Use the 'crsctl query css votedisk' command to get the list of voting files used by CSS. Use the 'asmcmd lsdsk --member' command to get the list of disks used by ASM. Specify a location that is not in either list.

message: Oracle High Availability Services on the local node is not running
cause: Oracle High Availability Services on the local node was not running
solution: Run 'crsctl start crs' command to start the Oracle High Availability Services on the local node.

message: The Oracle Cluster Registry location to be deleted is not configured
cause: The location to be deleted was not already configured as an Oracle Cluster Registry location.
solution: Run 'ocrcheck -config' command to get the list of configured Oracle Cluster Registry locations. Ensure that the location to be deleted is already configured.

message: The configured OCR locations are not accessible.
cause: The configured Oracle Cluster Registry (OCR) locations did not exist, were not mounted correctly, did not have the required permissions, or did not have sufficient disk space.
solution: Ensure that the locations exist, that they are mounted correctly and visible to all nodes in the cluster, that their permissions are correct, and that they have sufficient disk space. If using an Oracle Automatic Storage Management (Oracle ASM) OCR location, check for entries in the Oracle ASM alert log file for more details.

message: Duplicate or previously used Oracle Cluster Registry location string cannot be added
cause: The Oracle Cluster Registry location to be added had the same contents as that of currently configured locations. This might be due to the location to be added was either duplicate of one of the currently configured locations with a different path or previously used.
solution: Make sure that the location to be added is not currently configured with a different path. If the location was previously configured as an Oracle Cluster Registry location, ensure that the contents are erased before adding it again.

message: The Oracle Cluster Registry location string cannot be deleted because it is required for the OCR to be available
cause: A delete operation was requested when there were minimum configured Oracle Cluster Registry locations available. The above listed operation can only be performed when a majority of configured Oracle Cluster Registry locations are accessible and online.
solution: Run 'ocrcheck' command to get the current status of the configured Oracle Cluster Registry locations. Execute 'ocrconfig -add <new location>' to add the new Oracle Cluster Registry location followed by 'ocrconfig -delete <existing location>' command.

message: The Oracle Cluster Registry location cannot be added because location string is offline
cause: An add or replace operation was requested when there was at least one configured Oracle Cluster Registry location which was not accessible or online. The above listed operation can only be performed when the inaccessible Oracle Cluster Registry location has been deleted or replaced.
solution: Run 'ocrcheck' command to get the current status of the configured Oracle Cluster Registry locations. Execute 'ocrconfig -delete <offline location>' command to delete the inaccessible Oracle Cluster Registry location followed by 'ocrconfig -add <new location>' command.

message: The specified file ' string ' has an invalid format
cause: The specified file was not a valid Oracle Cluster Registry export/import file.
solution: Specify a valid Oracle Cluster Registry file which was created using the 'ocrconfig -export' command.

message: The specified file ' string ' has an invalid format
cause: The specified file was not a valid Oracle Cluster Registry backup file.
solution: Use the 'ocrconfig -showbackup' command to list all available backups. Specify a valid Oracle Cluster Registry backup file listed by the above command.

message: The specified backup location ' string ' is not accessible
cause: The backup location did not exist or the required permissions were not granted.
solution: Ensure that the location exists and the required file creation permissions are granted.

message: The specified backup location ' string ' is not a directory or an ASM disk group
cause: The specified backup location was not a directory or an ASM disk group.
solution: Specify a directory or an ASM disk group.

message: Cannot change the Oracle Cluster Registry backup location to an ASM disk group.
cause: An attempt was made to change the Oracle Cluster Registry backup location to an ASM disk group when the Oracle Cluster Registry was not configured on ASM.
solution: Migrate the Oracle Cluster Registry to ASM before changing the Oracle Cluster Registry backup location to an ASM disk group.

message: The specified Oracle Cluster Registry backup location string is inaccessible.
cause: Oracle Cluster Registry backup location did not exist, was not mounted correctly, or did not have the required permissions.
solution: Ensure that the backup location exists, that it is mounted correctly, and that its permissions are correct. Check the entries in the ASM alert log file for more details.

message: Failed to repair the Oracle Cluster Registry configuration while adding the location ' string ' on the local node.
cause: The Oracle Cluster Registry location to be added did not exist, was not mounted correctly, did not have the required permissions, or the OCR file in the disk group did not exist.
solution: Ensure that the location exists with appropriate permissions. If the location is an ASM disk group, then the OCR file in the disk group must already exist, the disk group must be mounted correctly; also check the entries in the ASM alert log file for more details.

message: Cannot change the Oracle Cluster Registry backup location to the specified ASM disk group string .
cause: An attempt was made to change the Oracle Cluster Registry backup location to an ASM disk group which was the same as the only configured ASM Oracle Cluster Registry location.
solution: Add another ASM Oracle Cluster Registry location before changing the Oracle Cluster Registry backup location to the specified ASM disk group or specify a different ASM disk group for the Oracle Cluster Registry backup location.

message: The Oracle Cluster Registry (OCR) integrity check failed.
cause: The integrity check failed for one or more of the configured Oracle Cluster Registry locations.
solution: Use 'ocrcheck' command to validate the block integrity of the configured Oracle Cluster Registry locations. Delete the corrupt locations using the command 'ocrconfig -delete <corrupt location>'. If all configured Oracle Cluster Registry locations are corrupted, check the availability of backups using the 'ocrconfig -showbackup' command and restore a compatible backup. If you are not able to resolve the problem, contact Oracle Support Services.

message: * Use option '-local' to indicate that the operation is to be performed on the Oracle Local Registry.
cause: ocrconfig called with incorrect or missing options.
solution: Use ocrconfig with correct options.

message: Dump is not feasible when clusterware is running
cause: Unable to dump cluster registry data when clusterware is running.
solution: Stop the clusterware before retrying ocrdump.

message: Failed to initialize ocrdump
cause: Unable to initialize and start ocrdump.
solution: Check log file for details about the failure.

message: Dump file already exists [ string ]
cause: Requested dump file exists in the given path.
solution: Change the location for the dump file or remove the old dump file.

message: Failed to create dump file [ string ]
cause: Unable to create or open file for dumping cluster registry data.
solution: Check access privilege or disk space of the requested path.

message: Failed to write to dump file [ string ]
cause: Unable to write to dump file while dumping cluster registry data.
solution: Check access privilege or disk space of the requested path.

message: Failed to retrieve cluster registry data
cause: Unable to read cluster registry data.
solution: Check log file for details about the failure.

message: The specified key does not exist in cluster registry
cause: Unable to retrieve the specified key from cluster registry.
solution: Check log file for the key name.

message: Failed to access the Oracle Cluster Registry backup file.
cause: The Oracle Cluster Registry backup file either did not exist or the user did not have the permission to open the file.
solution: Ensure that the file exists and its permissions are correct.

message: Use option '-local' to indicate that the operation is to be performed on the Oracle Local Registry.
cause: ocrdump called with incorrect or missing options.
solution: Use ocrdump with correct options.

message: Failed to initialize ocrcheck
cause: Unable to initialize and start ocrcheck.
solution: Check log file for details about the failure.

message: Failed to retrieve data from the cluster registry
cause: Unable to retrieve necessary information from the cluster registry.
solution: Check the availability of the cluster registry and the details of the failure from the log file.

message: Oracle Cluster Registry is logically corrupted
cause: A logical corruption was detected in the Oracle Cluster Registry.
solution: Check the log file for more information. Check availability of backups using 'ocrconfig -showbackup' command. Restore a compatible backup, and verify using ocrcheck.

message: Failed to retrieve the configured location(s) of the cluster registry.
cause: Unable to retrieve the configured location(s) of the cluster registry.
solution: Check log file for details about the failure.

message: Oracle Cluster Registry configuration is :
cause: ocrcheck called.
solution: None

message: when running this tool.
cause: ocrcheck called with incorrect or missing options.
solution: Use ocrcheck with correct options.

message: Not An Error
cause: Everything is working as it should.
solution: Don't worry: Be happy.

message: INTCTL: error while getting command line from the terminal
cause: Improper standard input connection from the terminal.
solution: Normally not visible to the user. Start the INTCTL program again. If error persists, contact Oracle Customer Support.

message: INTCTL: error while starting the Interchange
cause: of the problem. Be sure to turn tracing off when the problem has been rectified.
solution: Check the Interchange configuration files (INTCHG.ORA, TNSNET.ORA and TNSNAV.ORA) for errors and confirm that no other programs are using the ADDRESS(es) specified. If error continues, turn on tracing in the Interchange components and examine the trace files to determine the

message: INTCTL: error while sending request to the Interchange
cause: Improper command sent to the Interchange or the Interchange is not responding. Not normally visible to the user.
solution: Verify that the command sent to the Interchange is valid. Also check that the Interchange is running by using the INTCTL STATUS command. If necessary, start the Interchange using the INTCTL START command.

message: INTCTL: error while starting the Navigator
cause: The Navigator could not be started.
solution: Check to make sure that executables for the Navigator (navgatr) are present in the ORACLE executable directory on your platform. Check the configuration files TNSNET.ORA and TNSNAV.ORA for errors. If error continues, turn on tracing in the Interchange components and examine the trace files to determine the cause of the problem. Be sure to turn tracing off when the problem has been rectified.

message: INTCTL: error while sending request to the Navigator
cause: The Navigator is not responding. Either the Navigator is not running or another process is responding.
solution: Check that the Navigator is running by using the STATUS command of the Interchange Control Utility. Verify that the correct addresses are listed in the TNSNAMES.ORA, TNSNET.ORA, and TNSNAV.ORA configuration files.

message: INTCTL: HOST variable is not defined
cause: The HOST variable was not set.
solution: Set the variable HOST properly and restart the INTCTL program.

message: INTCTL: unknown host
cause: The pointer HOST is set to an unknown hostname.
solution: Set the pointer HOST properly and restart INTCTL program.

message: INTCTL: could not contact destination Navigator
cause: Connection could not be properly established to a Navigator. This may be because the Navigator specified is not running or the Navigator addresses are incorrect.
solution: Check that the Navigator is running by using the STATUS command of the Interchange Control Utility; if necessary, start the Navigator using the START command of the Interchange Control Utility. If it is running and the error persists, contact Oracle Customer Support.

message: INTCTL: could not contact destination Connection Manager
cause: Connection could not be properly established to a Connection Manager. This may be because the Connection Manager (Interchange) specified is not running or the Connection Manager addresses are incorrect.
solution: Make sure the Connection Manager is running by using the STATUS command of the Interchange Control Utility; if necessary, start the Connection Manager using the START command of the Interchange Control Utility. If it is running and the error persists, contact Oracle Customer Support.

message: Error while flushing NS context
cause: Internal NS error; connection may be lost.
solution: Make sure the connection is properly established. If the error persists, then contact Oracle Customer Support.

message: INTCTL: error while starting the Connection Manager
cause: The Connection Manager could not be started.
solution: Assure that the executable can be found in the standard Oracle executable area. Check the configuration file INTCHG.ORA for errors and confirm that no other process is using the ADDRESS(es) for this Connection Manager as specified in TNSNET.ORA. Tracing can also be turned on in the Connection Manager and detailed information about the reason for the error determined. Consult the MultiProtocol Interchange Administrator's Guide and Chapter 2 of this manual for how to turn on tracing.

message: INTCTL: error while processing Connection Manager request
cause: An improper command was sent to the Connection Manager or it is not responding. Not normally visible to the user.
solution: Verify that the correct addresses are listed in the TNSNAMES.ORA, TNSNET.ORA, and TNSNAV.ORA configuration files. Also check that the Connection Manager is running by using the STATUS command of the Interchange Control Utility. If the error persists, contact Oracle Customer Support.

message: INTCTL: error while performing NS disconnect command
cause: Internal NS error. Error in closing down connections.
solution: Make sure the networking protocol being used is properly installed on the machine. If the error persists contact Oracle Customer Support.

message: INTCTL: error while opening terminal input channel
cause: Could not open standard terminal input. Internal error.
solution: Normally not visible to the user. Restart the INTCTL program. If error persists, contact Oracle Customer Support.

message: INTCTL: error while closing terminal input channel
cause: Could not close terminal input channel. Internal error.
solution: Normally not visible to the user. Restart the INTCTL program. If error persists, contact Oracle Customer Support.

message: INTCTL: error while performing NS send command
cause: Internal NS error. Connection may be lost.
solution: If the error persists contact Oracle Customer Support.

message: INTCTL: error while performing NS receive command
cause: Internal NS error. Connection may be lost.
solution: If the error persists contact Oracle Customer Support.

message: INTCTL: TNS_ADMIN not defined
cause: The TNS_ADMIN pointer is improperly set.
solution: No action necessary; TNS_ADMIN need only be set if you want to use a different network environment.

message: INTCTL: error initializing the national language interface
cause: The message file could not be found.
solution: Make sure that the ORACLE environment is set and that the message file is in the correct place.

message: INTCTL: missing NAVIGATOR_DATA in TNSNAV.ORA
cause: TNSNAV.ORA does not contain the NAVIGATOR_DATA component.
solution: Define the ADDRESS(es) for the Navigator, then restart the INTCTL program.

message: INTCTL: missing INTERCHANGE_DATA in INTCHG.ORA
cause: INTCHG.ORA does not contain an INTERCHANGE_DATA component.
solution: Define the correct data for the Connection Manager, then restart the INTCTL program.

message: INTCTL: missing CMANAGER_NAME in INTCHG.ORA
cause: INTCHG.ORA does not contain a CMANAGER_NAME component.
solution: Define the correct name for the CMANAGER_NAME, then restart the INTCTL program.

message: INTCTL: missing ADDRESS(es) in config files
cause: Configuration files do not contain an ADDRESS/ADDRESS_LIST component.
solution: Define the Connection Manager ADDRESS(es) in the TNSNET.ORA file and check the Navigator ADDRESS(es) in the TNSNAV.ORA file, then restart the INTCTL program.

message: INTCTL: Unable to contact Navigator to obtain Connection Manager address
cause: The Navigator is not running.
solution: Verify that the Navigator is running by doing a status request on the Navigator (use the Interchange Control Utility command STATUS). If necessaary, start the Navigator using the Interchange Control Utility. Verify that the network is properly configured; if the error persists, contact Worldwide Customer Support.

message: INTCTL: The ORACLE environment is not set up correctly
cause: The ORACLE environment is incorrectly set up.
solution: Refer to the Oracle operating system specific documentation for your platform for information on how the ORACLE environment should be set. Correct it and rerun INTCTL. Make sure the ORACLE environment includes the correct directories.

message: INTCTL: TNS_ADMIN directory set, and is being used
cause: The TNS_ADMIN environment variable is set properly. INTCTL will use the TNS_ADMIN directory. This is only an informative message. If you do not want it to be used, and want the default directory to be used instead, then unset TNS_ADMIN and reexecute.
solution: None

message: INTCTL: Could not resolve Navigator's name/address
cause: The Navigator's name to address definition is missing.
solution: Check TNSNAMES.ORA file and make sure to include a definition for the name specified.

message: INTCTL: Could not resolve Connection Manager's name/address
cause: The Connection Manager's name does not have a definition that the Navigator knows about, nor is the name/address available in the TNSNAMES.ORA file. The name may also be incorrect in the INTCHG.ORA file.
solution: Verify that the Connection Manager's name is in the TNSNET.ORA file read by the Navigator or in the TNSNAMES.ORA file. Be sure that INTCHG.ORA is correct.

message: INTCTL: internal NT error
cause: Problem interfacing to the protocol adapters installed.
solution: Normally not visible to the user. Try starting INTCTL again. If the error persists, check the product installation. If it is correct, contact Oracle Customer Support.

message: INTCTL: internal NS error
cause: Problem interfacing with TNS.
solution: Normally not visible to the user. Try starting INTCTL again. If the error persists, check the product installation. If it is correct, contact Oracle Customer Support.

message: INTCTL: internal NL error
cause: Problem with internal TNS module NL.
solution: Normally not visible to the user. Try starting INTCTL again. If the error persists, check the product installation. If it is correct, contact Oracle Customer Support.

message: INTCTL: internal NR error
cause: Problem with internal Interchange routines.
solution: Normally not visible to the user. Try starting INTCTL again. If the error persists, check the product installation. If it is correct, contact Oracle Customer Support.

message: INTCTL: error while constructing full file name
cause: Problem while constructing the full path for a file name because the path name to the file or the environment variables are incorrect. Files looked up include TNSNAMES.ORA, TNSNAV.ORA, INTCHG.ORA and the error files for the Navigator and Connection Manager.
solution: Check that all environment variables are defined correctly and that all configuration files exist in their correct places.

message: INTCTL: error reading from Navigator or Connection Manager error files
cause: Problem while reading from Navigator or Connection Manager error files generated by the Navigator or Connection Manager when they fail to start.
solution: Check that a standard Network Error directory exists and that all privileges on the directory are appropriate.

message: INTCTL: error opening Navigator or Connection Manager error files
cause: Failed to open Navigator or Connection Manager error files when they have failed to start.
solution: Check that a Network Error directory exists and that all privileges on the directory are appropriate.

message: INTCTL: Poorly formed address or command string
cause: An unacceptable string was encountered while attempting to send a message to either the Navigator or Connection Manager. The addresses provided for either the Navigator or Connection Manager may be incorrectly constructed.
solution: Check all address strings in configuration files (TNSNAMES.ORA, TNSNAV.ORA or TNSNET.ORA) and assure that they are properly formed. Regenerate the files, if possible. If all is correct, please contact Worldwide Customer Support.

message: INTCTL: error while spawning a process
cause: An error was encountered while spawning a process due to an internal operating system dependent problem. Machine resources may be limited.
solution: Retry command. Check permissions on Interchange executables and the current setting of the search path. If necessary, terminate other applications to free up machine resources. If the error persists, contact Oracle Customer Support.

message: INTCTL: failed to initialize trace context- Continuing anyway
cause: Problem while opening specified trace file because of errors in INTCHG.ORA or because the user has incorrect privileges, or the file does not exist.
solution: Check the privileges on the configuration files and ensure that all of them exist in their proper locations.

message: INTCTL: Navigator already running. Start operation cancelled
cause: There is a Navigator already running and listening on the same addresses.
solution: None; the Navigator is already running.

message: INTCTL: CMANAGER already running. Start operation cancelled
cause: There is a Connection Manager already running and listening on the same addresses.
solution: None; the Connection Manager is already running.

message: The CMANAGER has active connections, do you still want to stop it (y/n)?
cause: The CMANAGER that is being stopped has active connections going through. This is the confirmation message.
solution: Respond by pressing y or n. Answering y will cause the active database connection to be dropped; this is not generally recommended.

message: INTCTL: You must have an INTCHG.ORA file to contact the Connection Manager
cause: There was an attempt to contact a default Connection Manager (Interchange) where there was no INTCHG.ORA present in the correct directory.
solution: Create an INTCHG.ORA file. Make sure it is placed in the correct directory and includes the correct name for the Connection Manager you wish to contact.

message: INTCTL: Could not contact the Navigator on address
cause: There was an attempt to contact a Navigator on a specific address which is not responding.
solution: Check the TNSNAV.ORA file for that address. Or check that the Navigator is actually listening on that address.

message: INTCTL: Could not contact the CMANAGER on address
cause: There was an attempt to contact a CMANAGER on a specific address which is not responding.
solution: Verify that the TNSNET.ORA file contains that address. Also check that the CMANAGER is actually listening on that address by using the INTCTL STATUS command. If necessary, start the Connection Manager using the INTCTL START command.

message: INTCTL: Bad command: only the STATUS command can be used on remote Interchanges
cause: The user entered a command that does not exist, or the user tried to make a request other than STATUS to a remote Interchange.
solution: Check the MultiProtocol Interchange Administrator's Guide for a list of INTCTL commands or type HELP for a list of valid commands.

message: INTCTL: Bad command or syntax error: You must specify a trace level
cause: The user did not specify a trace level.
solution: Specify a trace level and retry command.

message: INTCTL: Bad command or syntax error: For help type help/h/?
cause: The user entered an invalid command.
solution: Check the MultiProtocol Interchange Administrator's Guide or type HELP for a list of valid commands.

message: INTCTL: Failed to allocate memory for buffers
cause: INTCTL was unable to allocate memory for internal buffers.
solution: Check the amount of available memory on your machine to ensure that there is enough memory to run this executable. If necessary, free up memory by running fewer programs, then try again.

message: INTCTL: Failed to find CMANAGER_NAME in INTCHG.ORA
cause: INTCTL was unable to find the CMANAGER_NAME parameter in INTCHG.ORA.
solution: Check that the INTCHG.ORA file is properly constructed.

message: INTCTL: Command cannot be executed remotely
cause: A command other than status and version has been attempted remotely.
solution: If you desire execute any command other than status and version, you must run intctl on the interchange machine.

message: Unable to allocate memory
cause: Out of memory on the machine.
solution: Add more memory or run fewer processes.

message: File operation error
cause: Error in accessing reading or writing a particular file.
solution: Check existence of or operating system access to the log and trace file locations.

message: Keyword-Value binding operation error
cause: Not normally visible to the user. May indicate a shortage of memory.
solution: If error persists contact Oracle Customer Support.

message: Parameter file load error
cause: Parameter file process failed.
solution: Check to make sure that all parameter files necessary for the Interchange are present (TNSNAV.ORA, TNSNET.ORA and INTCHG.ORA). If these files are present and properly configured, turn on tracing and repeat the operation. Turn off tracing when the trace is complete. Look in the trace file for errors in the parameter loading process. If error persists contact Oracle Customer Support.

message: Data stream open/access error
cause: Unable to open or access data stream for either log or trace files for the Interchange.
solution: Check read/write permissions on Oracle files and directories.

message: Could not initialize tracing
cause: The INTCHG.ORA file is improperly configured. Verify the trace parameters specified.
solution: If error persists contact Oracle Customer Support.

message: Failed to open log file
cause: Unable to access or obtain write permission to create log file.
solution: Check existence of or access to log file directory.

message: Unable to initialize TNS global data
cause: Not normally visible to the user.
solution: If error persists contact Oracle Customer Support.

message: TNS_ADMIN not defined
cause: TNS_ADMIN pointer is not set.
solution: Set the TNS_ADMIN pointer before running application

message: Message could not be printed; not enough memory
cause: Printing of message failed due to lack of memory. Not normally visible to user.
solution: Increase the resources on your machine. If error persists contact Oracle Customer Support.

message: Could not initialize network from file TNSNET.ORA
cause: Poorly formed network information in network file.
solution: Fix network configuration data to assure that at least one Interchange is defined in TNSNET.ORA.

message: Failed to get configuration data from file
cause: Poorly formed configuration information in network files TNSNET.ORA or TNSNAV.ORA.
solution: Check TNSNET.ORA and TNSNAV.ORA and confirm that they are correct.

message: Failed to find configuration file name
cause: Name specified for configuration file was incorrect.
solution: Check for presence of the configuration file.

message: Failed to open error log file
cause: Could not open log file during startup of Navigator or Connection Manager due to read or write permission problems or non-existent error directory.
solution: Create the standard error directory or assure that if one is present the Interchange executables can write to it.

message: Internal error- Allocation of addresses not performed
cause: Internal error. Should not normally occur.
solution: Contact Oracle Customer Support.

message: Could not allocate pump global buffers
cause: Not enough memory to allocate pump buffers.
solution: Decrease the number of PUMP_BUFFERS in INTCHG.ORA.

message: Pump failed during initial bequeath
cause: d by insufficient machine resources.
solution: Attempt the connection again. The pump should recover from such a failure. If machine resources appear to be the problem, add more resources // or shut down some active applications. If problem persists, contact Oracle Customer Support.

message: Internal error- No data passed through pump
cause: Internal error. Data expected has not arrived yet.
solution: If error persists, contact Oracle Customer Support.

message: Missing PUMP_CONNECTIONS in INTCHG.ORA
cause: No PUMP_CONNECTIONS parameter specified in INTCHG.ORA.
solution: Add PUMP_CONNECTIONS parameter to INTCHG.ORA.

message: Missing PUMPS in INTCHG.ORA
cause: No PUMPS parameter specified.
solution: Add an appropriate number of PUMPS to INTCHG.ORA.

message: Missing CMANAGER_NAME in INTCHG.ORA
cause: No CMANAGER_NAME parameter specified.
solution: Define the CMANAGER_NAME parameter in INTCHG.ORA; it must match the CMANAGER_NAME parameter used in TNSNET.ORA for that Interchange.

message: Missing ADDRESS(es) in TNSNET.ORA file
cause: No ADDRESS or ADDRESS_LIST parameter specified in TNSNET.ORA.
solution: Define a valid set of ADDRESSes for the Connection Manager in the TNSNET.ORA file.

message: Unable to perform a listen on configured ADDRESS(es)
cause: Another process is already listening on this address or the ADDRESS is incorrectly defined.
solution: Check the ADDRESS(es) defined in TNSNET.ORA (for the Connection Manager) for errors. Verify that another program is not using them.

message: Internal error - Unable to create empty address
cause: - Internal error. Should not normally occur.
solution: If problem persists contact Oracle Customer Support.

message: Failed to get number of Interchanges in TNSNET.ORA
cause: Error in the TNSNET.ORA file.
solution: Check the contents of TNSNET.ORA and eliminate errors. Regenerate the configuration files.

message: Missing Connection Manager name and address in TNSNET.ORA
cause: The Interchange name specified in INTCHG.ORA is not defined in the TNSNET.ORA file.
solution: Define one Connection Manager name and set of addresses for each Interchange in the network. Regenerate the configuration files.

message: Missing Connection Manager name in TNSNET.ORA
cause: One or more Connection Manager names are missing.
solution: Ensure that each Connection Manager name is defined in TNSNET.ORA. Regenerate TNSNET.ORA.

message: Missing COMMUNITY in TNSNET.ORA
cause: One or more ADDRESSes does not have a COMMUNITY assigned.
solution: Ensure that all addresses have a COMMUNITY defined in TNSNET.ORA.

message: Internal error - Failed to create new community
cause: Internal Error. Should not normally occur. There may be a resource limitation problem on the machine.
solution: Stop and restart Interchange. If possible, make more memory available on the machine. If problem persists, contact Oracle Customer Support.

message: Failed to create Interchange's internal address
cause: There is an error in one of the addresses listed in TNSNET.ORA.
solution: Check the file for errors in defining Interchanges.

message: Missing COMMUNITY in COMMUNITY_COST_LIST in TNSNET.ORA
cause: A COMMUNITY keyword-value pair is missing within the COMMUNITY_COST_LIST in TNSNET.ORA.
solution: Define the communities with a COMMUNITY name and associated COST in COMMUNITY_COST_LIST.

message: COST value must be an integer greater than 0
cause: A community has been defined in TNSNET.ORA with a COST of 0.
solution: Assign an alternate value that is greater than 0.

message: Missing LOCAL_COMMUNITIES field in TNSNAV.ORA
cause: Improperly configured TNSNAV.ORA file.
solution: Define the LOCAL_COMMUNITIES fields correctly in TNSNAV.ORA.

message: Missing COMMUNITY component in addresses for the Navigator in TNSNAV.ORA
cause: The addresses specified for the Navigator have no COMMUNITY name.
solution: Ensure that all addresses in the NAVIGATOR_ADDRESSES field have a COMMUNITY entry in the TNSNAV.ORA file.

message: Missing TNS error message file
cause: No error message file present.
solution: Ensure that the ORACLE environment is correctly set for your platform and that there is a message directory that contains the correct error message file.

message: Did not register product/facility for TNS error message
cause: Error message file error.
solution: Ensure that the ORACLE environment is correctly set for your platform and that there is a message directory that contains the correct error message file.

message: Failed to get TNS error message file entry
cause: No TNS error message file present.
solution: Ensure that the ORACLE environment is correctly set for your platform and that there is a message directory that contains the correct error message file.

message: Failed to find ORACLE executable directory
cause: The ORACLE environment is not correctly set.
solution: Ensure that the ORACLE environment is correctly set and the error messages file is in the correct place.

message: Internal - Data passed from the Interchange listener is poorly formed
cause: Internal error in Interchange.
solution: Check that you are using compatible components of the Interchange product, using the INTCTL VERSION command. If problem persists call Oracle Customer Support.

message: Interchange specified was not found in network tables
cause: Could not find the Interchange specified in a control request.
solution: Check that the Interchange specified is indeed in TNSNET.ORA.

message: Failed to get file stream information
cause: Error in the file stream package.
solution: None

message: Community mismatch in TNSNAV.ORA
cause: The communities in the LOCAL_COMMUNITIES entry in TNSNAV.ORA do not correspond with all the communities in the NAVIGATOR_ADDRESSES entry.
solution: Assure that all communities in the NAVIGATOR_ADDRESSES correspond to those in the LOCAL_COMMUNITIES component.

message: Illegal PREFERRED_CMANAGERS entry in TNSNAV.ORA
cause: PREFERRED_CMANAGERS entry in the TNSNAV.ORA used by the Connection Manager. There should only be a PREFERRED_NAVIGATORS entry in the TNSNAV.ORA on an Interchange.
solution: Remove the PREFERRED_CMANAGERS entry from TNSNAV.ORA and assure that either no PREFERRED_NAVIGATORS entry is present or that it is correct.

message: PUMP_CONNECTIONS value in INTCHG.ORA is too large.
cause: The number of PUMP_CONNECTIONS specified in INTCHG.ORA is too large to be supported on this platform.
solution: Consult the Oracle operating system specific manual for the maximum value for the number of PUMP_CONNECTIONS.

message: PUMPS value in INTCHG.ORA is too large.
cause: The number of PUMPS specified in INTCHG.ORA is too large to be supported on this platform.
solution: Consult the Oracle operating system specific manual for the maximum value for the number of PUMPS.

message: Internal-- Retry data request withing pump.
cause: The data space provided in order to receive data from the pump is to small.
solution: Operation must be retried with a larger buffer.

message: Failed to start a pre-spawned pump.
cause: The Connection Manager was unable to start a pump during startup.
solution: Check all configuration parameters and assure that they are correct. Turn on tracing to determine the area that the failure ocurred in.

message: Unable to do nsanswer on context result= string

solution: Try making the connection again. If the problem persists call Oracle Customer Support.

solution: If problem persists, check the application using the Interchange (it may be closing down or crashing). Call Oracle Customer Support if the problem cannot be located.

message: Failed to contact Connection Manager
cause: Connection Manager is not running.
solution: Start the Connection Manager and retry

message: Cannot allocate memory
cause: Sufficient memory could not be allocated to perform the desired activity.
solution: Either free some resource for TNS or add more memory to the machine. For further details, turn on tracing and reexecute the operation.

message: Invalid argument
cause: An internal function received an invalid parameter.
solution: Not normally visible to the user. For further details, turn on tracing and reexecute the operation. If error persists, contact Oracle Customer Support.

message: Illegal ADDRESS parameters
cause: An illegal set of protocol adapter parameters was specified.
solution: Check the parameters within the ADDRESS section of the TNSNAMES.ORA file. It may be helpful to turn on tracing and look at the addresses specified in the trace file, checking for spelling or other errors. Be sure to turn tracing off when the trace is complete.

message: Operation not supported
cause: An internal function received a request to perform an operation that is not supported (on this machine).
solution: Not normally visible to the user. For further details, turn on tracing and reexecute the operation. If error persists, contact Oracle Customer Support.

message: Operation timed out
cause: The requested operation could not be completed within the timeout period.
solution: For further details, turn on tracing and reexecute the operation.

message: Operation would block
cause: An internal operation did not commence because to do so would block the current process and the user has requested that operations be non-blocking.
solution: None needed; this is an information message.

message: Connection closed
cause: Normal "end of file" condition has been reached; partner has disconnected.
solution: None needed; this is an information message.

message: No such protocol adapter
cause: The protocol adapter requested for this connection does not exist.
solution: Install the protocol adapter or use one that is available. Be sure that the correct protocols are listed in the configuration files.

message: Buffer overflow
cause: Too much data for buffer.
solution: Reexecute with larger receive buffer or smaller send buffer.

message: Internal limit restriction exceeded
cause: Too many files or sockets open simultaneously (or some other resource has been depleted).
solution: For further details, trace the operation for protocol details.

message: No listener
cause: The connect request could not be completed because no application is listening on the address specified, or the application is unable to service the connect request in a sufficiently timely manner.
solution: Ensure that the supplied destination address matches one of the addresses used by the listener - compare the TNSNAMES.ORA entry with appropriate LISTENER.ORA file (or TNSNAV.ORA if the connection is to go by way of an Interchange. Start the listener on the remote machine.

message: Address already in use
cause: Specified listener address is already being used.
solution: Start your listener with an unused address.

message: Destination host unreachable
cause: Contact cannot be made with remote party.
solution: Make sure the network driver is functioning and the network is up.

message: Contexts have different wait/test functions
cause: Two protocol adapters have conflicting wait/test functions.
solution: Not normally visible to the user. For further details, turn on tracing and reexecute the operation. If error persists, contact Oracle Customer Support.

message: Connect failed because target host or object does not exist
cause: The address specified is not valid, or the program being connected to does not exist.
solution: Ensure the ADDRESS parameters have been entered correctly; the most likely incorrect parameter is the node name. Ensure that the executable for the server exists (perhaps "oracle" is missing.)

message: Permission denied
cause: User has insufficient privileges to perform the requested operation.
solution: Acquire necessary privileges and try again.

message: Lost contact
cause: Partner has unexpectedly gone away.
solution: Investigate partner application for abnormal termination.

message: Incomplete read or write
cause: A data send or receive failed.
solution: Not normally visible to the user. For further details, turn on tracing and reexecute the operation. If error persists, contact Oracle Customer Support.

message: Operating system resource quota exceeded
cause: The current user has exceeded the allotted resource assigned in the operating system.
solution: Acquire more operating system resource, or perform a different function.

message: Syntax error
cause: The supplied connect descriptor contains illegal syntax.
solution: Check the syntax of the connect descriptor for correct syntax.

message: Missing keyword
cause: The supplied connect descriptor is missing one or more TNS keywords.
solution: Check the syntax, and ensure all required keywords are present.

message: Operation was interrupted
cause: An internal operation was interrupted and could not complete.
solution: Not normally visible to the user. For further details, turn on tracing and reexecute the operation. If error persists, contact Oracle Customer Support.

message: Previous operation was busy
cause: Operation tried could not be successfully completed because the requested resource was busy.
solution: Attempt the operation again. If error persists, contact Oracle Customer Support.

message: Current operation is still in progress
cause: Internal operation is still in progress but will complete.
solution: None; wait for operation to complete.

message: Insufficient privilege for operation
cause: Operating system failed to complete operation because user lacked sufficient privileges.
solution: Check your platform-specific privileges.

message: No caller (false async event)
cause: Internal error.
solution: For further details, turn on tracing and reexecute the operation.

message: Protocol Adapter not loadable
cause: On some platforms (for example OS/2) protocol adapters are loaded at run-time. If the shared library (or DLL) for the protocol adapter is missing or one of its supporting libraries is missing, then this error is returned.
solution: For further details, turn on tracing and reexecute the operation. The trace file will have the name of the shared library (or DLL) that could not be loaded.

message: Protocol Adapter not loaded
cause: On some platforms (for example OS/2) protocol adapters are loaded at run-time. If the shared library (or DLL) for the protocol adapter has not been loaded, then this error is returned.
solution: For further details, turn on tracing and reexecute the operation. The trace file will have the name of the shared library (or DLL) that has not been loaded.

message: Protocol adapter error

solution: For further details, turn on tracing and reexecute the operation.

message: No previous async operation to wait on

message: Connection dissolved or not yet made

solution: For further details, turn on tracing and reexecute the operation. If error persists, contact Oracle Customer Support.

message: Connection entered inappropriate state

message: Index into protocol adapter table is out of legal range

message: SSL protocol adapter failure
cause: The SSL protocol adapter encountered an error.
solution: In most cases, this error should only be pair with a more meaningful ORA- error.

message: underlying transport does not exist.
cause: The SSL protocol adapter was unable to locate an adapter for the protocol that it is going to use as the data transport.
solution: In most cases, the underlying transport is TCP. Make sure that the Oracle Net TCP/IP adapter was installed.

message: SSL Handshake failed
cause: The SSL protocol adapter was unable to connect to another process.
solution: This error can be caused by a variety of problems including the termination of the peer process. Enable Oracle Net tracing and attempt the connection again. The trace file should give some clues as to what the exact problem is.

message: internal error
cause: The SSL protocol adapter encountered an unexpected error.
solution: This error is not normally visible to users. Enable Oracle Net tracing and attempt to reproduce the error. If it occurs, contact Oracle customer support.

message: unsupported operation
cause: The SSL adapter could not perform a given command.
solution: This error is not normally visible to users. Enable Oracle Net tracing and attempt to reproduce the error. If it occurs, contact Oracle customer support.

message: parameter retrieval failure
cause: The SSL protocol adapter was not able to retrieve a configuration parameter for some reason.
solution: This error is not normally visible to users. Enable Oracle Net tracing and attempt to reproduce the error. If it occurs, contact Oracle customer support.

message: control failure
cause: The SSL protocol adapter was unable to perform a command.
solution: This error is not normally visible to users. Enable Oracle Net tracing and attempt to reproduce the error. If it occurs, contact Oracle customer support.

message: user information retrieval failed
cause: The SSL protocol adapter was unable to retrieve information about the remote user.
solution: Examine the first error in the error stack. It should describe the error in more detail.

message: value specified for client authentication parameter is not boolean
cause: The value specified for the parameter that specifies that SSL client authentication is to be used was not boolean.
solution: Specify a correct value for the parameter.

message: value specified for the SSL version is not valid
cause: The value specified for the SSL version is not valid.
solution: Specify a valid value for the SSL version.

message: disconnection error
cause: The SSL protocol adapter encountered an error when the underlying transport disconnected.
solution: This error is not normally visible to users. Enable Oracle Net tracing and attempt to reproduce the error. If it occurs, contact Oracle customer support.

message: underlying transport connection failed
cause: The underlying transport adapter used by the SSL adapter failed to connect.
solution: Enable Oracle Net tracing and try the connection again. If the connection fails, examine the trace file to determine the cause.

message: no valid cipher suites were specified
cause: SSL cipher specs were specified, but none were valid.
solution: Specify correct cipher suites.

message: read failed
cause: The SSL adapter failed to read data from its connection.
solution: Examine the contents of sqlnet.log for more information. Enable Oracle Net tracing and try the connection again. If the connection fails, examine the trace file to determine the cause.

message: write failed
cause: The SSL adapter failed to send data over its connection.
solution: Examine the contents of sqlnet.log for more information. Enable Oracle Net tracing and try the connection again. If the connection fails, examine the trace file to determine the cause.

message: no directory specified for wallet resource locator
cause: It was specified that a file was to be used from which to retrieve a wallet, but no directory was specified for the wallet.
solution: Specify the directory where the wallet is located.

message: no method specified for wallet retrieval
cause: A wallet resource locator was specified, but no method was given for the retrieval of the wallet.
solution: Specify the method by which the method is to be retrieved.

message: unsupported wallet retrieval method
cause: The method specified for wallet retrieval is not supported. Currently, only files are supported for wallet retrieval.
solution: Specify "FILE" as the wallet retrieval method.

message: Entrust login failed
cause: Entrust failed to authenticate the username, password, and/or profile name that was presented.
solution: Specify correct values for the username, password or profile name. If no data was prompted for, contact Oracle support.

message: load of Entrust certificate failed
cause: An error occurred while attempting to validate the provided Entrust certificate.
solution: This error is not normally visible to users. Enable Oracle Net tracing and attempt to reproduce the error. If it occurs, contact Oracle customer support.

message: extraction of name from Entrust certificate failed
cause: An error occurred while attempting to extract a name from an Entrust certificate.
solution: This error is not normally visible to users. Enable Oracle Net tracing and attempt to reproduce the error. If it occurs, contact Oracle customer support.

message: Read failed due to closed or invalid transport connection
cause: Read attempt was made on a transport connection which was previously terminated or is somehow deemed to be invalid.
solution: Indicates a substantial transport level failure. Check the O/S configuration for the particular transport or contact the transport provider. For further details, turn on tracing and reexecute the operation.

message: Send failed due to timeout
cause: The send operation did not complete within the allowed time interval.
solution: Error is informational. Note, repeated receipt of this error could indicate an attempted Denial-Of-Service attack. Also, if the receipt of this error interferes w/ a customer's normal operations, the customer may wish to lengthen the timeout.

message: Receive failed due to timeout
cause: The receive operation did not complete within the allowed time interval.
solution: Error is informational. Note, repeated receipt of this error could indicate an attempted Denial-Of-Service attack. Also, if the receipt of this error interferes w/ a customer's normal operations, the customer may wish to lengthen the timeout.

message: Valid node checking: unable to parse configuration parameters
cause: Valid node checking was unable to parse the configuration due to syntactical errors.
solution: Ensure that the configuration syntax matches the Oracle reference manual documented syntax. For further details, turn on tracing and reexecute the operation.

message: Valid node checking configuration error
cause: Valid node checking specific Oracle Net configuration is invalid.
solution: Ensure the hosts specified in the "invited_nodes" and "excluded_nodes" are valid. For further details, turn on tracing and reexecute the operation.

message: TNS returned error number when attempting to start the listener
cause: d by the fact that the TNSLSNR executable cannot be found in the place expected in your platform's ORACLE environment. Verify that the full pathname of the TNSLSNR executable as displayed by LSNRCTL is correct.
solution: If NS error code 12538 is also returned then the BEQ driver is not installed; call Oracle Worldwide Support as the BEQ driver should always be installed. If this is not the problem then the error is probably

message: Could not find service name string
cause: The ervice name could not be resolved by name-lookup.
solution: Verify that the listener name or service name specified to LSNRCTL has the correct name and address defined in LISTENER.ORA or in TNSNAMES.ORA.

message: TNS application contacted was not the listener
cause: Another TNS application such as the Interchange was listening at the address contacted. There may be another TNS application listening at the address contacted and the data returned is not in the appropriate format.
solution: Verify that the listener name or service name specified to LSNRCTL has the correct name and address defined in LISTENER.ORA or in TNSNAMES.ORA.

message: Protocol specific component of the address is incorrectly specified
cause: The ADDRESS used to contact the listener is not correctly specified. This error occurs because the address fails to specify the destination of the listener. The address is well formed (for example, there are no missing parentheses) but it is missing a protocol specific component. For example, this is the error returned when the HOST component is missing from a TCP/IP address string.
solution: Edit the ADDRESS in LISTENER.ORA to include the required protocol-specific keywords. For more information about the keywords required by different protocol adapters, see the Oracle operating system specific documentation for your platform.

message: Listener using listener name string has already been started
cause: Another listener is already listening on one of the ADDRESSes specified.
solution: Shutdown the previous listener specified by the listener name before starting this one.

message: A valid trace level was not specified
cause: Failed to specify a valid trace level for the LSNRCTL trace command.
solution: Specify one of OFF, USER, ADMIN, or SUPPORT. Type "LSNRCTL help trace" for more information or consult Chapter 2 of this manual for an introduction to the concepts of tracing.

message: Listener password prompt failed
cause: Password not entered via tty
solution: Enter the listener password on a tty device

message: Listener password encryption failed
cause: Possibly garbled password entered
solution: Re-enter the listener password, using valid ASCII characters. If problem persists, contact Oracle Customer Support.

message: Mismatch - password unchanged
cause: New password and reentered new password are different"
solution: Re-enter the listener password, make sure that New password and reentered new password are the same

message: Log status can either be ON or OFF
cause: Failed to specify a log status value for the LSNRCTL log_status command.
solution: Specify one of ON or OFF. Type "LSNRCTL help set log_status" for more information or consult Chapter 2 of this manual for an introduction to the concepts of logging.

message: Plug and play can either be ON or OFF
cause: Failed to specify a valid value for the LSNRCTL use_plugandplay command.
solution: Specify one of ON or OFF. Type "LSNRCTL help set use_plugandplay" for more information.

message: save_config_on_stop can either be ON or OFF
cause: Failed to specify a valid value for the LSNRCTL save_config_on_stop command.
solution: Specify one of ON or OFF. Type "LSNRCTL help set save_config_on_stop" for more information.

message: LSNRCTL could not perform local OS authentication with the listener
cause: LSNRCTL failed to obtain system resources (heap memory, or shared memory) needed to perform local OS authentication with the listener.
solution: Make sure that system resources like shared memory and heap memory are available for LSNRCTL tool to execute properly.

message: OS error string creating shared memory segment of string bytes with key string
cause: The shared memory segment could not be created as requested. For example, a segment with the provided key may already exist, or the size may be outside of system allowed range.
solution: Use the error code to determine the exact cause of the problem. In certain cases the problem may be resolved by adjusting the system-imposed limits such as the maximum number of allowed shared memory segments, or their maximum and minimum sizes. In other cases, resources need to be freed up first for the operation to succeed.

message: Listener alias name given as connect identifier is too long
cause: The listener alias name you were attempting to resolve was too long.
solution: The maximum length of a listener alias name is 255 bytes; this limit has been exceeded. Use a smaller listener alias name.

message: The address of the specified listener name is incorrect
cause: The address on which the listener attempted to listen contains a syntax error.
solution: For the listener name or service name specified to LSNRCTL, check that the address or connect descriptor is well-formed. You can find the listener name in LISTENER.ORA, or you can access the listener through the service name is TNSNAMES.ORA.

message: Missing listener name, string , in LISTENER.ORA
cause: The listener could not find the listener name specified.
solution: Make sure valid addresses on which to listen are specified for the listener name in LISTENER.ORA.

message: All addresses specified for the listener name, string , failed
cause: The listener failed to listen on any of the specified addresses.
solution: Make sure that another application is not listening on the addresses specified or check that the appropriate protocol adapters are installed. Turn on tracing and execute again for more information.

message: Failed to process string: string
cause: The string specified is not well-formed.
solution: Not normally visible to the user. For further details, turn on tracing and reexecute the operation. If error persists, contact Oracle Customer Support.

message: SID detected in old format that is no longer supported
cause: One of the SIDs was specified in an obsolete format.
solution: Check LISTENER.ORA for a line of the form: <sid> = (SID=(ORACLE_HOME=<oracle_home>)) OR <sid> = (SID_DESC=(ORACLE_HOME=<oracle_home>)) The above format is no longer supported and SID_LIST_<listener_name> format described in the Oracle9i Net Services Reference Guide should be used. For example, SID_LIST_LISTENER = (SID_LIST=(SID_DESC=(SID_NAME=<sid>)(ORACLE_HOME=<oracle_home>)))

message: Incorrectly specified SID_LIST_ string parameter in LISTENER.ORA
cause: SID_LIST_<listener_name> in LISTENER.ORA has an error in it.
solution: Be sure this parameter is specified as described in the Oracle9i Net Services Reference Guide. For example, SID_LIST_LISTENER = (SID_LIST=(SID_DESC=(SID_NAME=<sid>)(ORACLE_HOME=<oracle_home>)))

message: Missing or inappropriate PROTOCOL, TIMEOUT or POOL_SIZE parameter from PRESPAWN_DESC
cause: PRESPAWN_DESC in each SID_DESC does not have required fields.
solution: Be sure the parameters required for PRESPAWN_DESC are specified in each SID_DESC. For example, SID_LIST_LISTENER = (SID_LIST=(SID_DESC=(SID_NAME=<sid>)(PRESPAWN_MAX=5)(ORACLE_HOME=<oracle_home>)(PRESPAWN_DESC=(PROTOCOL=tcp)(POOL_SIZE=10)(TIMEOUT=30)))) Add or correct these parameters in the LISTENER.ORA file

message: Can only listen on number addresses - ignoring string
cause: Too many addresses were given to listen on.
solution: Reduce the number of addresses to listen on and use another listener to listen on the remaining addresses.

message: Internal connection limit reached, preventing dispatcher from connecting
cause: The internal Oracle Net connection list is full. Too many dispatchers are connected to the listener; therefore, no more dispatchers are allowed to connect.
solution: For further details, turn on tracing and reexecute the operation. If error persists, contact Oracle Customer Support.

message: Internal connection limit has been reached; listener has shut down
cause: The internal Oracle Net connection list is full. The listener is configured to use too many Oracle Net connections.
solution: Reduce the number of listen addresses or services connected to the listener. For further details, turn on tracing and reexecute the operation. If error persists, contact Oracle Customer Support.

message: Trace level was not specified
cause: Failed to specify a trace level for the trace command.
solution: Specify one of OFF, USER, ADMIN, or SUPPORT. Users should not see this error if LSNRCTL is being used.

message: Spawn alias string was not found. Check listener parameter file
cause: The alias specified to spawn a program was not found in LISTENER.ORA.
solution: This is not seen in normal use of Oracle Net.

message: Syntax error in the address resolved from the spawn alias: string
cause: The alias specified to spawn a program was not a valid NVstring.
solution: This is not seen in normal use of Oracle Net.

message: Failed to spawn process: string
cause: The process failed to start correctly.
solution: This is not seen in normal use of Oracle Net.

message: No spawn alias sent to listener
cause: The spawn command was issued without an alias.
solution: This is not seen in normal use of Oracle Net.

message: Spawn alias has no program name set in it
cause: The spawn alias in LISTENER.ORA is incorrectly specified.
solution: This is not seen in normal use of Oracle Net.

message: The command string is not supported by the listener contacted
cause: The listener does not recognize the command.
solution: This is caused when a newer version of LSNRCTL contacts an old listener. Upgrade listener if executing this command is important.

message: Cannot allocate memory
cause: Sufficient memory could not be allocated to perform the desired activity.
solution: Either free some resource for TNS, or add more memory to the machine. For further details, turn on tracing and reexecute the operation.

message: The listener has not recognized the password
cause: The listener has the password security mechanism enabled and requires the correct password to execute any command other than VERSION. The user attempted to issue one of the privileged administrative commands, but could not be successfully authenticated with the password provided.
solution: If an authorized user is attempting the command, then use the SET PASSWORD command at the LSNRCTL prompt with the listener password. If you do not know the password, then you are trying to execute an inappropriate command.

message: Event detection broke for address: string
cause: The event detection mechanism for the address specified returned an error.
solution: Future attempts to detect events on this address will fail. The listener will deallocate the listen address and connections will no long be accepted for this address. This error is not normally visible to the user. For further details, turn on tracing and reexecute the operation. If error persists, contact Oracle Customer Support.

message: Event detection broke for dispatcher: string
cause: The event detection mechanism for the dispatcher specified returned an error.
solution: Future attempts to detect events on this dispatcher will fail. The listener will deallocate the dispatcher and connections will no long be redirected to this dispatcher. This error is not normally visible to the user. For further details, turn on tracing and reexecute the operation. If error persists, contact Oracle Customer Support.

message: Listener has shut down since all listen addresses have been deallocated
cause: The event detection mechanism broke and caused all listen addresses to be removed.
solution: Error 1170 has occured and caused all the listen addresses to be deallocated. Since all the listen addresses have been removed, no more connections can be established to this listener so it shuts itself down. This error is not normally visible to the user. For further details, turn on tracing and reexecute the operation. If error persists, contact Oracle Customer Support.

message: Missing or inappropriate PRESPAWN_MAX parameter from SID_DESC
cause: PRESPAWN_MAX in each SID_DESC does not have required fields.
solution: Be sure the parameters required for PRESPAWN_DESC are specified in each SID_DESC. For example, SID_LIST_LISTENER = (SID_LIST=(SID_DESC=(SID_NAME=<sid>)(PRESPAWN_MAX=15)(ORACLE_HOME=<oracle_home>)(PRESPAWN_DESC=(PROTOCOL=tcp)(POOL_SIZE=10)(TIMEOUT=30)))) Add or correct these parameters in the LISTENER.ORA file

message: The sum of the POOL_SIZEs from each PRESPAWN_DESC is greater than the PRESPAWN_MAX
cause: The minimum value for PRESPAWN_MAX should be the sum of the POOL_SIZEs.
solution: Be sure the parameters required for PRESPAWN_DESC are specified in each SID_DESC. For example, SID_LIST_LISTENER = (SID_LIST=(SID_DESC=(SID_NAME=<sid>)(PRESPAWN_MAX=15)(ORACLE_HOME=<oracle_home>)(PRESPAWN_DESC=(PROTOCOL=tcp)(POOL_SIZE=10)(TIMEOUT=30))(PRESPAWN_DESC=(PROTOCOL=ipc)(POOL_SIZE=5)(TIMEOUT=15)))) Add or correct these parameters in the LISTENER.ORA file

message: Password unchanged
cause: Unable to set the new password
solution: Be sure to see that the new password has legal ASCII characters. Try to set the password again.

message: Error in loading the new parameter value
cause: Illegal values given for the parameters
solution: Make sure that the parameter values are valid refer to the manual for the legal values for paramters

message: Log Status is OFF. Log file/directory unchanged
cause: Log status needs to be set ON for changing the log file
solution: use command set log_status ON to set the log status of the listener ON.

message: Trace Level is 0. Trace file/directory unchanged
cause: Trace Level needs to be set for changing the trace file/directory
solution: use command set trc_level ON to set the trace level

message: Listener cannot load instance class " string "
cause: Instance tried to register as a class unknown to listener.
solution: check LISTENER.ORA and/or instance configuration, and reference platform documentation to find the instance classes available for the listener on this platform.

message: Missing listener object string in Directory Server
cause: The listener could not find the listener object specified.
solution: Make sure the listener object is present in the Directory Server.

message: Internal registration connection limit reached
cause: The number of registration connections has reached the maximum. No more registrations are allowed until some of the existing registration connections are completed.
solution: Disconnect existing registration connections if they are no longer needed.

message: Listener rejected registration of service " string "
cause: Received registration information could not be processed because it was invalid, or an internal error occurred.
solution: Not normally visible to the user. For further details, turn on tracing and restart the instance. If error persists, contact Oracle Customer Support.

message: Listener rejected registration or update of instance " string "
cause: Received registration or update information could not be processed because it was invalid, or an internal error occurred.
solution: Not normally visible to the user. For further details, turn on tracing and restart the instance. If error persists, contact Oracle Customer Support.

message: Listener rejected registration or update of service handler " string "
cause: Received registration or update information could not be processed because it was invalid, or an internal error occurred.
solution: Not normally visible to the user. For further details, turn on tracing and restart the instance. If error persists, contact Oracle Customer Support.

message: Registration attempted from a remote node
cause: It was determined that the registering instance is not located on the same node as the listener. It is required that the instance be colocated with the listener for this type of service registration.
solution: Check the configuration of the registering instance. Ensure that local_listener parameter specifies only local listeners. Use remote_listener parameter to specify remote listeners.

message: Client connection was dropped based on a filtering rule
cause: Listener was configured with a filtering rule which explicitly specified that the client connection should be terminated without returning an error to the client.
solution: Modify the filtering rules if the client should be allowed access to the requested service.

message: No proxy service handler available
cause: One of the following conditions has occurred: - the proxy service was not registered - the proxy service was registered, but was blocking new connections - all of the registered proxy service handlers were blocking new connections
solution: If the proxy service is not registered it may need to be restarted. If the proxy service handlers are busy and not accepting new connections more of them may need to be started to handle the load.

message: Listener cannot operate with incompatible transport protocols
cause: Listener was configured with multiple listening addresses with different and incompatible transport protocols. Listener cannot operate efficiently in such configuration.
solution: Modify the existing listener configuration by removing the listening address that caused the error. Configure a separate listener to listen on this address.

message: The listener could not authenticate the user
cause: The user attempted to issue a privileged administrative command, but could not be successfully authenticated by the listener using the local OS authentication mechanism. This may occur due to one of the following reasons: 1. The user is running a version of LSNRCTL that is lower than the version of the listener. 2. The user is attempting to administer the listener from a remote node. 3. The listener could not obtain the system resources needed to perform the authentication. 4. The local network connection between the listener and LSNRCTL was terminated unexpectedly during authentication message exchange, such as if LSNRCTL program was suddenly aborted. 5. The communication between the listener and LSNRCTL is being intercepted by a malicious user. 6. The software that the user is running is not following the authentication protocol, indicating a malicious user.
solution: Make sure that administrative commands are issued using the LSNRCTL tool that is of a version equal or greater than the version of the listener, and that the tool and the listener are running on the same node. You can issue the VERSION command to find out the version of the listener. If a malicious user is suspected, use the information provided in the listener log file to determine the source and nature of the requests. Enable listener tracing for more information. If the error persists, contact Oracle Support Services.

message: The user is not authorized to execute the requested listener command
cause: Most of the listener administrative commands are only intended to be issued by privileged users, for example DBAs or system administrators. If the listener password is not set, then the listener only accepts administrative requests from LSNRCTL running with the same OS credentials, or running as a local administrator (also referred to as super user).
solution: If an authorized user is attempting the command, then make sure that LSNRCTL is executed with the same OS user credentials as the running listener, or as a local administrator.

message: Failed to initialize the local OS authentication subsystem
cause: Initialization of the security subsystem failed during listener startup or reload. The listener could not obtain system resources (memory, or file descriptors) needed for local OS authentication security mechanism.
solution: Make sure that system resources like shared memory and heap memory are available for listener to execute properly. For further details, turn on tracing and execute the operation again. If the error persists, contact Oracle Support Services.

message: Missing SID_LIST_ value left of equation for SID description in LISTENER.ORA
cause: SID description in LISTENER.ORA had an error in it.
solution: Make sure the lines of code in LISTENER.ORA containing SID_DESC or SID begin with SID_LIST_<listener_name> on the left side of the equation. For example, SID_LIST_LISTENER =(SID_LIST=(SID_DESC=(SID_NAME=<sid>)(ORACLE_HOME=<oracle_home>)))

message: Listener cannot operate with specified secure transport
cause: Listener was configured with transport protocols which are either invalid or none of the secure transport protocols are present in listening addresses.
solution: Modify the existing listener configuration by specifying a valid tranport protocol in secure transport list.

message: The listener command did not arrive in a secure transport
cause: Most of the listener administrative commands are only intended to be issued in a secure transport, which are configured in secure_control_ parameter. If the parameter is set, then the listener accepts administrative requests only on those secure transports.
solution: Make sure the command is issued using a transport specified in secure transport list.

message: Listener failed to initialize valid node list
cause: VNCR options are not properly initialized in listener.ora or OS API failed.
solution: Check VNCR options i.e. valid_node_checking_for_regisrtation, registration_invited_nodes, registation_excluded_nodes in listener.ora For further details, turn on tracing.

message: Listener failed to create the end point
cause: Internal error. Unable to get subnet mask for the ip address.
solution: OS failure. Turn on tracing for further details

message: The listener must be suid root
cause: The ownership privileges of the TNSLSNR executable are incorrect.
solution: Contact your DBA or system administrator to change the ownership of the file to be suid root and restart the listener. This action is necessary because the user that started the process should claim ownership.

message: Listener cannot find executable string for SID string
cause: The executable for the Oracle dedicated server process cannot be found.
solution: Check the appropriate SID_DESC in LISTENER.ORA to make sure that the ORACLE_HOME component is pointing to a valid location. If this component is not set, then check the value of the ORACLE_HOME environment variable.

message: Missing the dba group ( string ) specified by DBA_GROUP in SID_DESC
cause: The dba group specified is missing from /ETC/GROUP.
solution: Check the DBA_GROUP parameter in the SID_DESC in LISTENER.ORA and verify it has a valid entry in /ETC/GROUP.

message: Missing the account ( string ) specified by DEFAULT_USER_ACCOUNT in SID_DESC
cause: The unprivileged OS account is missing from /etc/passwd.
solution: Check the DEFAULT_USER_ACCOUNT parameter in the SID_DESC in LISTENER.ORA and verify it has a valid entry in /etc/passwd. This is the account that the Oracle shadow process will be started with if the the connecting client has database privileges or does not exist on this machine.

message: Unprivileged account ( string ) is in dba group ( string )
cause: The unprivileged account has DBA privileges. The unprivileged account specified by DEFAULT_USER_ACCOUNT in the SID_DESC in LISTENER.ORA is a member of the dba group specified by DBA_GROUP in SID_DESC. The unprivileged account cannot belong to the dba group because this would be a security violation with OPS$ logins.
solution: Remove the unprivileged account from the dba group.
